name: 4ocean
fact: 4ocean is a company founded in 2017 that pays crews to collect rubbish from oceans and coasts and sells bracelets made from recycled material.

name: A Coruña
fact: A Coruña's Tower of Hercules is the oldest Roman lighthouse still in use, guiding ships on Spain's Atlantic coast.

name: Aba aba
fact: The aba aba swims forwards and backwards with equal ease and senses its surroundings with a weak electric field.

name: Abalone
fact: Abalone shells are lined with iridescent mother-of-pearl and have a row of holes through which the animal breathes.

name: Abel Tasman
fact: Abel Tasman was a Dutch navigator who in 1642 became the first European to reach Tasmania and New Zealand.

name: Abidjan
fact: Abidjan, Ivory Coast's economic capital, became a major Atlantic port in the early 1950s when the Vridi Canal was cut through to its lagoon.

name: Abrolhos Bank
fact: The Abrolhos Bank off Brazil holds the largest coral reefs in the South Atlantic, built into mushroom-shaped pillars found nowhere else.

name: Abu Dhabi
fact: Abu Dhabi, the capital of the United Arab Emirates, is built on an island in the Persian Gulf.

name: Abu Nuhas
fact: Abu Nuhas is a Red Sea reef at the mouth of the Gulf of Suez on which several ships have been wrecked.

name: Abyssal grenadier
fact: The abyssal grenadier roams abyssal plains worldwide between about 2,000 and 5,000 metres, following its nose to carcasses that sink from above.

name: Abyssobrotula
fact: Abyssobrotula galatheae is a pale cusk-eel with tiny eyes, recorded from 8,370 metres in the Puerto Rico Trench in 1970, a depth record that stood for decades.

name: Acanthephyra shrimp
fact: Deep-sea Acanthephyra shrimp are blood-red, which looks black in the depths, and spit a cloud of glowing blue liquid into a predator's face.

name: Acapulco
fact: Acapulco in Mexico was the Pacific terminus of the Manila galleon trade route, which ran from 1565 to 1815.

name: Acapulco Trench
fact: The Acapulco Trench is the section of the Middle America Trench off the Pacific coast of Mexico near Acapulco.

name: Achille Lauro
fact: The Achille Lauro was an Italian cruise ship hijacked by terrorists in 1985, and she sank in 1994 after a fire.

name: Achilles tang
fact: The Achilles tang is a black surgeonfish with a teardrop of bright orange around its tail blade, living in the surge zone of Pacific reefs.

name: Acropora
fact: Acropora is the largest genus of reef-building corals, including the staghorn and table corals, and is among the first to bleach when the water warms.

name: Adélie penguin
fact: Adélie penguins eat mostly krill, and the pink stains of their guano show up from space, letting scientists count colonies by satellite.

name: Aden
fact: Aden in Yemen is built inside the crater of an extinct volcano and was a British-ruled port from 1839 to 1967.

name: Admiral Graf Spee
fact: The German pocket battleship Admiral Graf Spee was scuttled by its own crew off Montevideo in December 1939 after the Battle of the River Plate.

name: Adriatic Sea
fact: The Adriatic Sea separates Italy from the Balkans and is the arm of the Mediterranean on which Venice was built.

name: Adriatic trout
fact: The Adriatic, or softmouth, trout of the Balkans has a soft fleshy snout unlike any other trout and lives in a few rivers draining to the Adriatic.

name: Aegean Sea
fact: The Aegean Sea between Greece and Turkey is scattered with hundreds of islands, and its ancient trade routes made it the cradle of Greek civilisation.

name: Aegina
fact: Aegina is a Greek island in the Saronic Gulf known for its pistachios and the ancient Temple of Aphaia.

name: Aegir
fact: Aegir is the Norse giant and god of the sea, who was said to hold great feasts for the gods in his undersea hall.

name: Common grey sea slug
fact: The common grey sea slug eats sea anemones and stores their stinging cells in the tips of its gills.

name: African arowana
fact: The African arowana is a large, air-gulping fish of West and Central African rivers and floodplains.

name: African knifefish
fact: The African knifefish swims by rippling a long fin along its belly and can breathe air at the surface.

name: African lungfish
fact: When its pool dries up the African lungfish burrows into mud, wraps itself in a mucus cocoon and breathes air for months, even years, until rain returns.

name: African moony
fact: The African moony is a silvery, disc-shaped fish of West African estuaries and rivers that can live in fresh or brackish water.

name: African penguin
fact: The African penguin of South Africa and Namibia was declared critically endangered in 2024 as its sardine and anchovy prey dwindled.

name: African pike
fact: The African pike is a fast, toothy predator of African rivers that guards its nest of foam-bubbles.

name: African sharptooth catfish
fact: The African sharptooth catfish can breathe air and crawl between pools, and is farmed widely across Africa and Asia as a cheap protein.

name: African tigerfish
fact: The African tigerfish has been filmed leaping from the water to snatch swallows out of the air, the first freshwater fish confirmed to catch birds in flight.

name: Aft
fact: Aft means towards the back or stern of a ship.

name: Agadir
fact: Agadir is a Moroccan port city on the Atlantic coast, rebuilt after the great earthquake of 1960.

name: Aggregating anemone
fact: Aggregating anemones clone themselves by splitting in two, forming dense carpets where rival clone armies fight along their borders.

name: Agulhas Current
fact: The Agulhas Current races south along the east coast of South Africa and, meeting opposing winds, produces some of the world's most dangerous rogue waves.

name: Agulhas Return Current
fact: The Agulhas Return Current is the eastward flow formed when the Agulhas Current turns back on itself south of Africa.

name: Ahmed Gabr
fact: Egyptian diver Ahmed Gabr set the scuba depth record in 2014, descending to 332.35 metres in the Red Sea off Dahab.

name: Ahoy
fact: Ahoy is a sailor's call to attract attention or hail another ship, and Alexander Graham Bell suggested it as a telephone greeting.

name: Aircraft carrier
fact: An aircraft carrier is a warship with a long flight deck that serves as a floating airbase for the fleet's aircraft.

name: Automatic identification system
fact: The automatic identification system broadcasts a ship's name, position and course so that other vessels and coastal stations can track it.

name: Ajaccio
fact: Ajaccio on Corsica was the birthplace of Napoleon Bonaparte in 1769.

name: Akademik Mstislav Keldysh
fact: The Russian research ship Akademik Mstislav Keldysh carries the Mir submersibles and appears as itself in the opening scenes of the film Titanic.

name: Akagi
fact: The Japanese carrier Akagi, flagship of the Pearl Harbor attack, was sunk at Midway in 1942 and found in 2019 more than 5,000 metres down.

name: Akiami paste shrimp
fact: The thumbnail-sized Akiami paste shrimp is caught in bigger tonnages than any other shrimp species, mostly for shrimp paste and dried shrimp in Asia.

name: Alacranes Reef
fact: Alacranes Reef, off Mexico's Yucatan coast, is the largest coral reef system in the Gulf of Mexico.

name: Alaska Current
fact: The Alaska Current carries relatively warm water anticlockwise around the Gulf of Alaska, keeping the coast of the Alaska panhandle milder and wetter.

name: Alaska pollock
fact: Alaska pollock is the most-caught fish in the United States and the fish inside most fish fingers, fast-food fish sandwiches and surimi crab sticks.

name: Alaska SeaLife Center
fact: The Alaska SeaLife Center in Seward opened in 1998, funded partly by settlement money from the Exxon Valdez oil spill.

name: Albacore
fact: Albacore, the 'white tuna' of canned tuna, has the longest pectoral fins of any tuna and is served as shiro maguro in sushi bars.

name: Albatross
fact: Albatrosses lock their wings open with a special shoulder tendon and can glide for hours over the ocean without a single flap.

name: Alboran Sea
fact: The Alboran Sea is the westernmost part of the Mediterranean, just inside the Strait of Gibraltar, where Atlantic water first flows in.

name: Aldabra Atoll
fact: Aldabra Atoll in the Seychelles is one of the largest raised coral atolls in the world and home to about 100,000 giant tortoises.

name: Aleksandr Kolchak
fact: Aleksandr Kolchak was a Russian admiral and polar explorer who led the anti-Bolshevik White forces in Siberia and was shot in 1920.

name: Aleutian Islands
fact: The Aleutian Islands are a chain of volcanic islands stretching about 1,900 kilometres west from Alaska towards Russia.

name: Aleutian Trench
fact: The Aleutian Trench curves for about 3,400 kilometres south of Alaska's Aleutian Islands and reaches more than 7,600 metres deep.

name: Alewife
fact: The alewife is a small herring that migrates from the sea into rivers to spawn, and landlocked populations invaded the Great Lakes through canals.

name: Alexandria
fact: Alexandria in Egypt was founded by Alexander the Great in 331 BC and was once home to the Pharos lighthouse.

name: Alexandrium
fact: Alexandrium is a dinoflagellate genus whose blooms make saxitoxin, causing paralytic shellfish poisoning.

name: Algae octopus
fact: The algae octopus disguises itself as a shell overgrown with weed and can walk away on two arms while holding the other six in a ball.

name: Algal bloom
fact: An algal bloom is a rapid growth of algae or phytoplankton in the water, sometimes visible from space.

name: Algiers
fact: Algiers, the capital of Algeria, has a historic Casbah that is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

name: Aliwal Shoal
fact: Aliwal Shoal off South Africa's KwaZulu-Natal coast is famous for baited dives with tiger sharks and the winter gathering of ragged-tooth sharks.

name: All Is Lost
fact: All Is Lost is J. C. Chandor's 2013 film in which Robert Redford plays a lone sailor with almost no dialogue, whose yacht is wrecked in the Indian Ocean.

name: Allard's clownfish
fact: Allard's clownfish is a dark anemonefish with two white bars and a yellow tail found only off East Africa, from Kenya to South Africa.

name: Alligator gar
fact: The alligator gar can grow well over 2 metres long and gulps air at the surface through a swim bladder that works like a lung.

name: Alligator pipefish
fact: The alligator pipefish drifts among seagrass and floating weed in the Indo-Pacific and has a prehensile tail with no tail fin at all.

name: Allure of the Seas
fact: Allure of the Seas is the 2010 sister ship of Oasis of the Seas, with a central park of real trees running through the ship.

name: Aluminaut
fact: Aluminaut was a research submarine built with an aluminium hull in 1964 that helped search for a lost hydrogen bomb off Spain in 1966.

name: Alvaro de Bazan
fact: Alvaro de Bazan, Marquis of Santa Cruz, helped win Lepanto and was to lead the Spanish Armada but died in 1588 before it sailed.

name: Alvin
fact: Alvin is the US deep-diving submersible that explored the wreck of the Titanic in 1986 and found the first hydrothermal vent communities in 1977.

name: Alvinella caudata
fact: Alvinella caudata is a close relative of the Pompeii worm that lives on the chimney walls of East Pacific Rise vents.

name: Alvinocaris shrimp
fact: Alvinocaris shrimp were among the first animals described from the Galápagos Rift vents after their discovery in 1977, scavenging among tube worms and clams.

name: Ama diver
fact: Ama are Japanese women, historically, who free-dive without breathing apparatus to gather shellfish, seaweed and pearl oysters, a tradition that has lasted for well over a thousand years.

name: Amago salmon
fact: The amago is a subspecies of masu salmon that lives in the rivers of western Japan and carries red spots along its flanks.

name: Amano shrimp
fact: The Amano shrimp is a small freshwater shrimp of Japan that is kept in aquariums for eating algae.

name: Amazon leaffish
fact: The Amazon leaffish drifts in the water like a dead leaf, then snaps up small fish that come close.

name: Amazon Reef
fact: The Amazon Reef was only fully described in 2016, a reef system hidden under the muddy plume of the Amazon River where few thought reefs could grow.

name: Amazon river dolphin
fact: The Amazon river dolphin turns pink with age and has an unfused neck that lets it turn its head to hunt among flooded trees.

name: Amazonian manatee
fact: The Amazonian manatee is the only manatee that lives entirely in fresh water.

name: Ambracian Gulf
fact: The Ambracian Gulf on Greece's west coast lies beside Actium, where Octavian's fleet defeated Mark Antony in 31 BC.

name: American bullfrog
fact: The American bullfrog, farmed for frogs' legs, has invaded ponds across Europe, Asia and the western USA, eating anything that fits in its mouth.

name: American crocodile
fact: American crocodiles live in coastal mangroves and lagoons from Florida to Peru and have salt glands that let them tolerate the sea.

name: American eel
fact: The American eel grows up in rivers from Greenland to Brazil and returns to the Sargasso Sea to spawn, like its European cousin.

name: American lobster
fact: The American lobster is the heaviest crustacean ever recorded, with a 20-kilogram giant caught off Nova Scotia in 1977.

name: American plaice
fact: The American plaice, called the long rough dab in Europe, is a cold-water flatfish with a large mouth that lives on both sides of the North Atlantic.

name: American shad
fact: American shad live at sea and surge up east-coast rivers each spring to spawn, and the shad is the official state fish of Connecticut.

name: Ammonite
fact: Ammonites were coiled-shelled relatives of squid that filled the seas for over 300 million years and vanished with the dinosaurs.

name: Amok trey
fact: Amok trey is a Cambodian steamed fish curry in coconut milk and kroeung paste, traditionally served in banana leaves.

name: Amphibious assault ship
fact: An amphibious assault ship carries troops, landing craft and helicopters so a force can be put ashore from the sea.

name: Amphipod
fact: Scavenging amphipods swarm onto any bait lowered to the floor of the Mariana Trench within minutes, even at the very bottom of the Challenger Deep.

name: Amphitrite
fact: Amphitrite was a Greek sea goddess, one of the Nereids, who became the wife of Poseidon.

name: Amsterdam Island
fact: Amsterdam Island is a remote French volcanic island in the southern Indian Ocean and the only home of the Amsterdam albatross.

name: Amundsen Sea
fact: The Amundsen Sea off West Antarctica is named after the Norwegian explorer Roald Amundsen and is where the fast-melting Thwaites Glacier flows into the sea.

name: Amur catfish
fact: The Amur catfish is a whiskered East Asian predatory catfish that lives in rivers and lakes of Japan, Korea and China.

name: Anchor
fact: An anchor is a heavy hook-shaped weight lowered to the seabed to hold a ship in place.

name: Anchovy
fact: Anchovies swim with their mouths wide open to sieve plankton with their gill rakers, and the Peruvian anchoveta is the most heavily fished species on Earth.

name: Andaman Islands
fact: The Andaman Islands are an Indian archipelago in the Bay of Bengal, and on North Sentinel Island people live in isolation from the outside world.

name: Andrea Doria
fact: The Italian liner Andrea Doria sank in 1956 after colliding with the Stockholm off Nantucket, and its wreck at about 73 metres is called the Mount Everest of wreck diving.

name: Andrea Doria (admiral)
fact: Andrea Doria was a Genoese admiral of the sixteenth century who ruled the seas for Genoa and served Emperor Charles V.

name: Andrew Cunningham
fact: Andrew Cunningham led the Mediterranean Fleet in the Second World War and won the Battle of Cape Matapan in 1941.

name: Andrews' beaked whale
fact: Andrews' beaked whale is known almost entirely from strandings in Australia and New Zealand and is named after explorer Roy Chapman Andrews.

name: Andros Barrier Reef
fact: The Andros Barrier Reef in the Bahamas runs about 190 kilometres and drops away into the Tongue of the Ocean, a deep ocean trench.

name: Anegada
fact: Anegada is a flat coral island, unlike the other volcanic British Virgin Islands, and is ringed by Horseshoe Reef, where many ships have wrecked.

name: Anemometer
fact: An anemometer measures wind speed, and sailors use it to judge how much sail to carry.

name: Anemone porcelain crab
fact: The spotted porcelain crab lives among the tentacles of large sea anemones, filtering plankton from the water with its feathery mouthparts.

name: Anemone shrimp
fact: The glass anemone shrimp is transparent apart from a few white and orange spots, and lives unharmed among the stinging tentacles of its host anemone.

name: Angel shark
fact: The angel shark is a flattened ambush predator that buries itself in sand for days, then snaps up passing fish in a tenth of a second.

name: Angel skin coral
fact: Angel skin coral is a pale pink precious coral harvested for jewellery and related to red coral.

name: Angelfish
fact: Marine angelfish are among the most colourful reef fish, and many change their pattern completely as they grow from juvenile to adult.

name: Angelwing
fact: The angelwing is a bivalve whose long white shell resembles a pair of wings and which bores into mud and clay.

name: Anglerfish
fact: The female deep-sea anglerfish dangles a glowing lure of bacteria in front of her mouth, and in some species the tiny male fuses onto her body for life.

name: Angola
fact: Angola has a long Atlantic coastline, and its capital, Luanda, is a major port.

name: Angola Current
fact: The Angola Current is a warm current flowing south along the coast of Angola until it meets the cold Benguela Current.

name: Anguilla
fact: Anguilla is a long, thin, flat coral island whose name is generally said to come from the word for eel.

name: Angular roughshark
fact: The angular roughshark has tall sail-like dorsal fins and a stocky, triangular body, and lives on muddy slopes down to around 700 metres.

name: Anjouan
fact: Anjouan is a volcanic island of the Comoros that is steep and green and is known for growing ylang-ylang.

name: Annaba
fact: Annaba in Algeria lies beside the ruins of Roman Hippo Regius, where Saint Augustine served as bishop.

name: Anne Bonny
fact: Anne Bonny was an Irish-born pirate who sailed with Calico Jack Rackham and was captured in 1720 alongside Mary Read.

name: Annulated sea snake
fact: The annulated sea snake can take in oxygen through a network of blood vessels on top of its head, which works a little like a snorkel.

name: Anomalocaris
fact: Anomalocaris was the top predator of the Cambrian seas about 500 million years ago, a metre-long hunter with grasping front limbs and a circular mouth.

name: Anse Lazio
fact: Anse Lazio on Praslin in the Seychelles is a granite-flanked beach regularly named among the best in the world.

name: Anse Source d'Argent
fact: Anse Source d'Argent on La Digue in the Seychelles is lined with smooth granite boulders and is among the most photographed beaches on Earth.

name: Anson's circumnavigation
fact: George Anson's voyage of 1740 to 1744 captured a Spanish treasure galleon and returned with only a fraction of his original crews.

name: Antalya
fact: Antalya on Turkey's southern coast has an old harbour and Hadrian's Gate, built in AD 130 to honour a visit by the emperor.

name: Antarctic blue whale
fact: The Antarctic blue whale is the largest subspecies of the blue whale and was hunted to a tiny fraction of its former numbers.

name: Antarctic Circumpolar Current
fact: The Antarctic Circumpolar Current circles the whole of Antarctica unbroken by land and is the largest ocean current on Earth, carrying more water than any other.

name: Antarctic fur seal
fact: Antarctic fur seals were nearly wiped out by 19th-century sealers but now breed by the millions on South Georgia.

name: Antarctic giant isopod
fact: The Antarctic giant isopod is a relative of the woodlouse that crawls the cold seabed and can grow to about 20 centimetres.

name: Antarctic limpet
fact: The Antarctic limpet is the commonest limpet on Antarctic shores and grazes algae from rocks.

name: Antarctic minke whale
fact: Antarctic minke whales live among the pack ice and were the main target of Japan's so-called scientific whaling in the Southern Ocean.

name: Antarctic petrel
fact: The Antarctic petrel breeds in huge colonies on inland Antarctic mountains, some about 200 kilometres from the open sea.

name: Antarctic prion
fact: The Antarctic prion filters krill through comb-like plates in its bill, like a tiny flying baleen whale, which is why sailors called prions whalebirds.

name: Antarctic scallop
fact: The Antarctic scallop lives on the seabed beneath the ice and can swim by clapping its shell valves.

name: Antarctic sea star
fact: The Antarctic sea star is one of the commonest seabed animals around Antarctica, scavenging and hunting on the cold shelf.

name: Convention for the Conservation of Antarctic Seals
fact: The 1972 Convention for the Conservation of Antarctic Seals limits the killing of seals south of 60 degrees south, and no commercial sealing has been carried out under it.

name: Antarctic silverfish
fact: The Antarctic silverfish is the key fish of the Antarctic food web, eating krill and copepods and in turn feeding penguins, seals and toothfish.

name: Antarctic tern
fact: The Antarctic tern nests on coasts around Antarctica and nearby islands and dives for small fish and krill.

name: Antarctic toothfish
fact: The Antarctic toothfish grows to 2 metres in the Ross Sea, and its blood carries antifreeze proteins that stop ice crystals forming.

name: Antarctic Treaty
fact: The Antarctic Treaty of 1959 reserves Antarctica for peace and science and banned military activity south of 60 degrees south.

name: Anthias
fact: Anthias are the small orange fish that shimmer in clouds above Indo-Pacific reefs, each male guarding a harem of females.

name: Antigua
fact: Antigua is home to Nelson's Dockyard, an eighteenth-century Royal Navy base that is a World Heritage Site.

name: Antigua and Barbuda
fact: Antigua and Barbuda is a twin-island nation lying where the Atlantic Ocean meets the Caribbean Sea.

name: Antilles Current
fact: The Antilles Current flows north-west along the outer edge of the Caribbean islands and joins the Florida Current to form the Gulf Stream.

name: Antofagasta
fact: Antofagasta in northern Chile is a major port for exporting copper from the Atacama Desert mines.

name: Apache trout
fact: The Apache trout is found only in the White Mountains of Arizona and is the official state fish of Arizona.

name: Apia
fact: Apia on the island of Upolu is the capital of Samoa, and the writer Robert Louis Stevenson spent his final years nearby.

name: Apo Reef
fact: Apo Reef off Mindoro in the Philippines is the largest atoll-like reef in the country and is often described as the second-largest contiguous coral reef in the world.

name: Apolemia
fact: Apolemia is a stringy siphonophore colony that can stretch to about 30 metres, making it one of the longest animals known.

name: Aqaba
fact: Aqaba at the head of the Gulf of Aqaba is Jordan's only seaport.

name: AquaDom
fact: The AquaDom in Berlin was a cylindrical aquarium about 25 metres tall that burst in December 2022.

name: AquaRio
fact: AquaRio in the port of Rio de Janeiro opened in 2016 and is the largest marine aquarium in South America.

name: Aquarium Barcelona
fact: Aquarium Barcelona at Port Vell opened in 1995 and has an 80-metre underwater tunnel.

name: Aquarium of the Bay
fact: Aquarium of the Bay at Pier 39 in San Francisco has underwater tunnels that show the marine life of San Francisco Bay.

name: Aquarium of the Pacific
fact: The Aquarium of the Pacific in Long Beach, California, opened in 1998 and focuses on the Pacific Ocean and its wildlife.

name: AQWA
fact: AQWA, the Aquarium of Western Australia, opened in 1988 at Hillarys Boat Harbour near Perth and is known for its underwater tunnel.

name: Ar-Men Lighthouse
fact: Ar-Men Lighthouse stands on a tiny rock off Brittany and took 14 years to build, from 1867 to 1881, earning the nickname Hell of Hells.

name: ARA San Juan
fact: The Argentine submarine ARA San Juan vanished in November 2017 with 44 crew and was found a year later about 900 metres down in the South Atlantic.

name: Arabian Gulf sea snake
fact: The Arabian Gulf sea snake lives in the shallow waters of the Persian Gulf and nearby seas and bears live young in the water.

name: Arabian Picasso triggerfish
fact: The Arabian Picasso triggerfish, with its painted-on stripes, is found only in the Red Sea and the seas around Arabia.

name: Arafura Sea
fact: The Arafura Sea is a shallow sea between northern Australia and New Guinea.

name: Araguaian river dolphin
fact: The Araguaian river dolphin of Brazil was described in 2014, the first new river dolphin species recognised in almost a century.

name: Arame
fact: Arame is a brown kelp harvested in Japan and eaten shredded after soaking and boiling.

name: Arapaima
fact: The arapaima of the Amazon must surface regularly to gulp air and has been verified at just over 3 metres long.

name: Araucanian herring
fact: The Araucanian herring is a small schooling fish of the Chilean coast that supports a large fishery.

name: Archelon
fact: Archelon was the largest turtle ever, about 4 metres long, and swam the inland sea of Cretaceous North America.

name: Archerfish
fact: Archerfish shoot down insects with a jet of water spat from the mouth, correcting for the bending of light at the surface, and will also leap out to grab prey.

name: Archimède
fact: The French bathyscaphe Archimède dived to about 9,500 metres in the Kuril Trench in 1962 and later explored the Mid-Atlantic Ridge in Project FAMOUS.

name: Arctic char
fact: Arctic char live further north than any other freshwater fish, and sea-run char feed in Arctic coastal waters each summer.

name: Arctic cod
fact: Arctic cod carry antifreeze proteins in their blood and live right under the sea ice, feeding seals, whales and seabirds.

name: Arctic skate
fact: The Arctic skate lives on deep, cold seabeds across the Arctic basin and lays its eggs in tough leathery cases.

name: Arctic tern
fact: The Arctic tern flies from the Arctic to the Antarctic and back each year, the longest migration of any animal, around 70,000 kilometres or more.

name: Ardnamurchan Lighthouse
fact: Ardnamurchan Lighthouse, built by Alan Stevenson and lit in 1849, marks the most westerly point of mainland Britain.

name: Argentina
fact: Argentina's Atlantic coast runs for thousands of kilometres from the Río de la Plata south to Tierra del Fuego.

name: Argentine anchovy
fact: The Argentine anchovy schools in vast numbers off Argentina, Uruguay and southern Brazil.

name: Argentine hake
fact: The Argentine hake is the most important fish of Argentina's fisheries, trawled over the Patagonian shelf.

name: Argentine shortfin squid
fact: Hundreds of jigging boats light up the night off Argentina to catch this squid, one of the most heavily fished squid species on Earth.

name: Argo float
fact: Argo floats are robotic probes that drift with ocean currents, rising and sinking to measure temperature and salinity worldwide.

name: Argonaut
fact: The female argonaut, an octopus, secretes a thin, papery shell that she uses as a floating egg case and buoyancy aid.

name: Arica
fact: Arica in northern Chile belonged to Peru until the War of the Pacific, and today is a port serving Bolivia's trade.

name: Ark shell
fact: The ark shell, called akagai in Japan, is a red-fleshed clam served as sushi, its colour coming from haemoglobin in its blood.

name: Armoured cruiser
fact: Armoured cruisers were cruisers with side armour like a battleship's, and they were built in the late nineteenth and early twentieth centuries.

name: Arnoux's beaked whale
fact: Arnoux's beaked whale lives in the cold Southern Ocean and has been seen diving beneath Antarctic sea ice.

name: Arowana
fact: Arowanas can breathe air using their swim bladder and are famous for leaping out of the water to snatch insects from overhanging branches.

name: Giant South American river turtle
fact: The giant South American river turtle is the largest river turtle in the region, and females gather in large numbers to nest on sandbanks.

name: Arrow crab
fact: The arrow crab of Caribbean reefs has spindly legs and a pointed head, and is kept in aquariums to eat bristle worms.

name: Arrow worm
fact: Arrow worms are glassy, torpedo-shaped predators of the plankton that grab copepods with hooked spines and a venom like that of pufferfish.

name: Arrowtooth flounder
fact: The arrowtooth flounder is the most abundant groundfish in the Gulf of Alaska, but an enzyme turns its flesh to mush when cooked, so it was long discarded.

name: Aruba
fact: Aruba lies about 29 kilometres off the coast of Venezuela and is one of the Dutch Caribbean's ABC islands.

name: Arugam Bay
fact: Arugam Bay on Sri Lanka's east coast is known for a long right-hand point break and a surf season from April to September.

name: Ascension Island
fact: Ascension Island is a volcanic island in the mid-Atlantic to which green turtles swim about 2,000 kilometres from Brazil to nest on its beaches.

name: Asian carp
fact: Asian carp, a group of imported Chinese carp species, have overrun the Mississippi basin, and electric barriers try to keep them out of the Great Lakes.

name: Asian clam
fact: The Asian clam has spread through rivers across North America, South America and Europe and fouls the cooling systems of power stations.

name: Asian shore crab
fact: The Asian shore crab turned up in New Jersey in 1988 and is now the most common crab on many rocky shores from Maine to North Carolina.

name: Asian stinging catfish
fact: The Asian stinging catfish has a long air-breathing sac and venomous pectoral spines that can give a painful sting.

name: Asian tiger shrimp
fact: The Asian tiger shrimp, a farmed prawn up to 30 centimetres long, has escaped into the Gulf of Mexico and the south-eastern US coast.

name: Asiatic mangrove
fact: The Asiatic mangrove props itself on stilt roots and drops long, pencil-shaped seedlings that are already germinated.

name: Aspidochelone
fact: The aspidochelone is a giant sea creature of medieval bestiaries, a turtle or whale so huge that sailors landed on it, thinking it an island.

name: Astrolabe
fact: The mariner's astrolabe was a simple brass instrument used from the fifteenth century to measure the height of the sun or stars at sea.

name: Atacama snailfish
fact: The Atacama snailfish lives in the Atacama Trench off Peru and Chile, thousands of metres deeper than most fish can survive.

name: Atlantic blue tang
fact: The Atlantic blue tang is a Caribbean surgeonfish that is bright yellow as a juvenile and turns deep blue as it grows.

name: Atlantic bonito
fact: The Atlantic bonito is a fast, striped, tuna-like schooling fish of the Atlantic and Mediterranean, eaten salted or grilled in Turkey as palamut.

name: Atlantic brief squid
fact: The Atlantic brief squid is a small squid of the western Atlantic that can tolerate the low salt levels of estuaries.

name: Atlantic chub mackerel
fact: The Atlantic chub mackerel forms big schools in the Atlantic and Mediterranean and is caught for food.

name: Atlantic croaker
fact: The Atlantic croaker croaks by rapidly contracting muscles against its swim bladder, loudly enough to be heard when it is hauled into a boat.

name: Atlantic gray whale
fact: The Atlantic gray whale once lived on both sides of the North Atlantic and was hunted to extinction by about the 1700s.

name: Atlantic halibut
fact: Atlantic halibut can live for 50 years and females take about 10 years to mature, so the species is easily overfished.

name: Atlantic horse mackerel
fact: The Atlantic horse mackerel is a schooling jack of the North Sea and eastern Atlantic with a line of bony scutes along its side.

name: Atlantic humpback dolphin
fact: The Atlantic humpback dolphin lives in estuaries and shallow coasts of West Africa and is critically endangered, with fewer than 3,000 left.

name: Atlantic longarm octopus
fact: The Atlantic longarm octopus can mimic a swimming flatfish as it glides over sandy seabeds.

name: Atlantic mackerel
fact: Atlantic mackerel feed on copepods and krill as they swim constantly to breathe, and are the species the British fleet catches in the largest quantity.

name: Atlantic pomfret
fact: The Atlantic pomfret is an open-ocean fish that migrates over long distances through the North Atlantic.

name: Atlantic puffin
fact: Atlantic puffins can carry a dozen or more small fish crosswise in their beaks at once and spend the winter alone far out at sea.

name: Atlantic pygmy octopus
fact: The Atlantic pygmy octopus is small enough to live inside an empty clam shell, which it pulls shut around itself with its suckers.

name: Atlantic rock crab
fact: The Atlantic rock crab lives along the shores of eastern North America and crushes small shellfish in its strong claws.

name: Atlantic salmon
fact: Atlantic salmon return from the sea to the river where they hatched, and unlike Pacific salmon some survive spawning and go back to sea to spawn again.

name: Atlantic sea scallop
fact: The Atlantic sea scallop supports a major fishery off the north-eastern United States.

name: Atlantic sharpnose shark
fact: The Atlantic sharpnose shark is a small, common shark of the US Atlantic and Gulf coasts, often the first shark a beach angler catches.

name: Atlantic silverside
fact: The Atlantic silverside is a small schooling fish of US Atlantic estuaries whose sex is decided by the water temperature its eggs develop in.

name: Atlantic spotted dolphin
fact: Atlantic spotted dolphins are born spotless and gain more spots with age, and the Bahamas population has been studied for over 30 years.

name: Atlantic stingray
fact: The Atlantic stingray tolerates fresh water and has a permanent population in Florida's St Johns River.

name: Atlantic sturgeon
fact: The Atlantic sturgeon lives in coastal seas and swims up rivers to spawn, and in the past grew to more than 4 metres long.

name: Atlantic thread herring
fact: The Atlantic thread herring, named for a long trailing ray on its dorsal fin, schools along the Gulf of Mexico coast and is netted for bait.

name: Atlantic tomcod
fact: The Atlantic tomcod is a small cod of North American estuaries; those in the Hudson River evolved resistance to PCB pollution in just a few decades.

name: Atlantic torpedo
fact: The Atlantic torpedo is the largest electric ray, up to about 1.8 metres and 90 kilograms, and delivers shocks of around 220 volts.

name: Atlantic white-sided dolphin
fact: The Atlantic white-sided dolphin has a bold yellow-ochre streak on its tail stock and lives in cool North Atlantic waters.

name: Atlantis
fact: Atlantis is the Woods Hole research ship that serves as the mothership for the submersible Alvin.

name: Atlantis II
fact: Atlantis II was a Woods Hole research ship that served as Alvin's mother ship for decades.

name: Atolla jellyfish
fact: When attacked, the Atolla jellyfish flashes a swirling ring of blue light, a burglar alarm that may attract predators of its attacker.

name: Auckland
fact: Auckland sits on a narrow isthmus between two harbours, one opening to the Pacific and one to the Tasman Sea.

name: Aquarium of the Americas
fact: The Aquarium of the Americas in New Orleans opened in 1990 on the banks of the Mississippi River.

name: Auguste Piccard
fact: Auguste Piccard invented the bathyscaphe, a free-diving deep submersible, after first setting altitude records in a stratospheric balloon.

name: Austinograea williamsi
fact: Austinograea williamsi is a crab of hydrothermal vents in the western Pacific.

name: Australasian gannet
fact: Australasian gannets breed in large colonies such as the one at Cape Kidnappers on New Zealand's North Island.

name: Australasian snapper
fact: The Australasian snapper, simply called snapper in New Zealand, is a pinkish sea bream that is one of the most popular fish there to catch and eat.

name: Australia
fact: Australia has coastlines on both the Pacific and Indian oceans, and the Great Barrier Reef lies off its Pacific coast.

name: Australian bonito
fact: The Australian bonito is a small tuna-like fish of southern Australian and New Zealand waters, sought by anglers.

name: Australian fur seal
fact: The Australian fur seal breeds on rocky islands in Bass Strait, between the Australian mainland and Tasmania.

name: Australian humpback dolphin
fact: The Australian humpback dolphin was described in 2014 and lives in shallow coastal waters and estuaries of northern Australia and New Guinea.

name: Australian longfin eel
fact: The Australian longfin eel lives in the rivers of eastern Australia and is thought to migrate to the Coral Sea to spawn.

name: Australian lungfish
fact: The Australian lungfish has a single lung and surfaces to gulp air when its river water runs low in oxygen.

name: Australian salmon
fact: Despite its name, the Australian salmon is not a true salmon but a schooling fish of the southern Australian coast.

name: Australian sea lion
fact: The Australian sea lion is one of the rarest sea lions and has an unusual 17- to 18-month breeding cycle.

name: Australian snubfin dolphin
fact: The Australian snubfin dolphin was only recognised as a species in 2005 and spits water to herd fish in northern Australia's estuaries.

name: Australian spotted mackerel
fact: The Australian spotted mackerel is a fast mackerel of northern Australian waters, valued by anglers and commercial fishers.

name: Auxiliary cruiser
fact: An auxiliary cruiser was a merchant ship converted to carry guns for raiding or patrolling, a common German tactic in both world wars.

name: Avast
fact: Avast is a sailor's command to stop or hold still, and it comes from the Dutch word houd vast.

name: Ayu
fact: The ayu, or sweetfish, hatches in Japanese rivers, spends the winter at sea, and returns to the river to graze algae from the rocks.

name: Azores
fact: The Azores are nine volcanic Portuguese islands in the mid-Atlantic, about 1,500 kilometres west of Lisbon, and a famous whale-watching spot.

name: Azores Current
fact: The Azores Current is an eastward branch of the Gulf Stream system that crosses the Atlantic near the Azores.

name: Azure damselfish
fact: The azure damselfish has a vivid blue body with a yellow tail and a small size of about 7 centimetres.

name: Azure vase sponge
fact: The azure vase sponge forms blue-lilac vase-shaped tubes on Caribbean reefs and filters plankton from the water.

name: Bab-el-Mandeb
fact: The Bab-el-Mandeb, whose name means Gate of Tears, joins the Red Sea to the Gulf of Aden between Yemen and Djibouti.

name: Bacalhau a Bras
fact: Bacalhau a Bras is a Portuguese dish of shredded salt cod, fried potato and scrambled egg.

name: Backstaff
fact: The backstaff let navigators measure the sun's height with their back to it, so they did not have to look into its glare.

name: Baffin Bay
fact: Baffin Bay between Greenland and Baffin Island is named after William Baffin, the English navigator who explored it in 1616.

name: Bagoong
fact: Bagoong is a Filipino paste of fermented fish or shrimp that is used as a seasoning or dip.

name: Bahamas
fact: The Bahamas are about 700 islands and cays on shallow banks in the Atlantic, where Columbus made his first landfall in 1492.

name: Bahrain
fact: Bahrain is an island nation of more than 30 islands in the Persian Gulf.

name: Baiji
fact: The baiji of the Yangtze was declared functionally extinct in 2006 after a survey failed to find a single animal.

name: Baikal seal
fact: The Baikal seal lives only in Lake Baikal in Siberia and is the only seal that spends its whole life in fresh water.

name: Baird's beaked whale
fact: Baird's beaked whale is the largest beaked whale, up to about 13 metres, and is still hunted off Japan in small numbers.

name: Baking
fact: Baking cooks fish in the dry heat of an oven, often wrapped or with a little liquid to keep it moist.

name: Bald eagle
fact: Bald eagles snatch fish from the surface with their talons and gather by the hundred on Alaskan coasts when salmon and herring run.

name: Balearic Sea
fact: The Balearic Sea lies between the east coast of Spain and the Balearic Islands of Majorca, Minorca and Ibiza.

name: Baleen whale
fact: Baleen whales have no teeth; instead they strain krill and small fish from mouthfuls of water through fringed plates of baleen.

name: Bali
fact: Bali is a mainly Hindu island in Indonesia, a country with a Muslim majority, and lies just east of Java.

name: Ballan wrasse
fact: The ballan wrasse is the largest wrasse in British waters, used in salmon farms to eat sea lice off the salmon.

name: Ballistic missile submarine
fact: A ballistic missile submarine is a nuclear-powered vessel that carries long-range nuclear missiles and is meant to stay hidden at sea.

name: Balos
fact: Balos on the north-west tip of Crete is a shallow lagoon beach reached by a long dirt track or by boat from Kissamos.

name: Baltic Sea
fact: The Baltic Sea is a brackish arm of the Atlantic so diluted by rivers that parts of it freeze over every winter.

name: Bamboo coral
fact: Bamboo corals of the deep sea have skeletons of limestone segments joined by dark, flexible nodes, like a bamboo stem.

name: Bamboo shark
fact: Bamboo sharks are small, slender reef sharks that lay eggs, and their egg cases are a staple of public and home aquariums.

name: Banana prawn
fact: Banana prawns take their name from their yellowish colour and are a main catch of prawn trawlers in northern Australia.

name: Banco Chinchorro
fact: Banco Chinchorro is a large Mexican coral atoll off the Yucatan coast and a biosphere reserve littered with shipwrecks.

name: Banda Aceh
fact: Banda Aceh at the northern tip of Sumatra was devastated by the Indian Ocean tsunami of 26 December 2004.

name: Banda Sea
fact: The Banda Sea in eastern Indonesia is a deep basin surrounding the Banda Islands, the original source of nutmeg and mace.

name: Bandar Abbas
fact: Bandar Abbas in Iran stands on the Strait of Hormuz and is the country's main port for container traffic.

name: Banded butterflyfish
fact: The banded butterflyfish is a Caribbean butterflyfish with black bars that often swims in pairs.

name: Banded coral shrimp
fact: The banded coral shrimp waves long white antennae from reef crevices to attract fish, which it then cleans of parasites.

name: Banded pipefish
fact: The banded pipefish has red and white rings and a paddle-shaped tail, and pairs of them work as cleaner fish on Indo-Pacific reefs.

name: Banded sea krait
fact: Banded sea kraits hunt eels on reefs but return to land to digest their meals, shed their skins and lay eggs.

name: Banded snake eel
fact: The banded snake eel mimics the venomous banded sea krait in colour and pattern, and burrows tail-first into sand.

name: Banded stingaree
fact: The banded stingaree is a small, round-bodied ray of southern Australia with a pattern of dark bands across its back.

name: Banded wobbegong
fact: Banded wobbegongs lie camouflaged on the seabed of southern Australia and ambush fish that wander within reach.

name: Banggai cardinalfish
fact: The male Banggai cardinalfish broods the eggs and then the hatched young in his mouth for weeks, so the species never has a drifting larval stage.

name: Bangladesh
fact: Bangladesh sits on the Bay of Bengal at the delta of the Ganges, Brahmaputra and Meghna rivers.

name: Banjo catfish
fact: The banjo catfish is a flat, lumpy South American catfish shaped like a banjo that lies buried in sand and leaf litter by day.

name: Banjul
fact: Banjul is the capital of The Gambia, on an island where the Gambia River meets the Atlantic.

name: Bantry Bay
fact: Bantry Bay is a long, deep inlet on Ireland's south-west coast, where a French invasion fleet failed to land in 1796.

name: Banzai Pipeline
fact: Pipeline on Oahu's North Shore breaks in hollow barrels over a shallow reef and hosts the Pipe Masters contest every December.

name: Bar-tailed godwit
fact: In 2022 a young bar-tailed godwit flew non-stop from Alaska to Tasmania, 13,560 kilometres in 11 days, the longest non-stop flight ever recorded for a bird.

name: Barbados
fact: Barbados is the most easterly of the Caribbean islands and is built largely of coral limestone rather than volcanic rock.

name: Barbecuing
fact: Barbecuing cooks fish over hot coals or a flame, and whole fish are often held in a hinged basket so they do not break up.

name: Barbel
fact: The barbel is a bottom-feeding fish of fast European rivers, named for the four whiskers around its mouth.

name: Barbour's seahorse
fact: Barbour's seahorse is a spiny Southeast Asian seahorse named for the American zoologist Thomas Barbour.

name: Barbuda
fact: Barbuda is the smaller island of Antigua and Barbuda and has a large frigatebird colony at Codrington Lagoon.

name: Barcelona
fact: Barcelona's port, crowned by a monument to Columbus, is one of the busiest cruise ports in Europe.

name: Barcelona Convention
aliases: Convention for the Protection of the Mediterranean Sea
fact: The Barcelona Convention of 1976 is the regional treaty for protecting the Mediterranean Sea from pollution.

name: Barents Sea
fact: The Barents Sea north of Norway and Russia is named after the Dutch navigator Willem Barentsz, who died there in 1597 after wintering on Novaya Zemlya.

name: Barentsz's voyages
fact: Willem Barentsz led Dutch Arctic expeditions in the 1590s, and his crew survived the winter of 1596 and 1597 on Novaya Zemlya.

name: Bargibant's pygmy seahorse
fact: Bargibant's pygmy seahorse grows to about 2 centimetres and lives only on Muricella sea fans, matching their colour and knobbly texture so well it was found by accident in 1969.

name: Bari
fact: Bari in Apulia holds the relics of Saint Nicholas, brought there by sailors in 1087.

name: Barnacle
fact: Barnacles are crustaceans, relatives of crabs, that glue their heads to rocks and build limestone shells around themselves.

name: Barndoor skate
fact: The barndoor skate is one of the largest skates of the north-west Atlantic, reaching 1.5 metres, and was nearly wiped out as bycatch.

name: Barometer
fact: A barometer measures air pressure, and a falling reading warns sailors that a storm may be coming.

name: Barque
fact: A barque is a sailing ship of three or more masts, square-rigged on all but the last mast.

name: Barracuda
fact: The great barracuda is a torpedo-shaped reef predator with fang-like teeth that hunts in sudden short bursts of speed.

name: Barramundi
fact: Barramundi hatch in estuaries, grow up in fresh water and return to the sea to spawn, with most starting life as males and later changing into females.

name: Barred sand bass
fact: The barred sand bass is a California sea bass popular with anglers and known for gathering to spawn each summer.

name: Barrel jellyfish
fact: The barrel jellyfish, the largest jellyfish in British waters, can reach the size of a dustbin lid and is harmless enough to be food for leatherback turtles.

name: Barreleye
fact: The barreleye has a transparent dome over its head and tubular green eyes that rotate inside it to look up through its own skull.

name: Barrier Reef anemonefish
fact: The Barrier Reef anemonefish lives in sea anemones on Australia's reefs and is a close relative of the orange clownfish.

name: Bartholomew Sharp
fact: Bartholomew Sharp was an English buccaneer who raided the Pacific coast of Spanish America in 1680 and captured a Spanish book of sea charts.

name: Basilosaurus
fact: Basilosaurus was an early whale about 18 metres long with tiny hind legs, and its name means 'king lizard' because it was first mistaken for a reptile.

name: Basket star
fact: A basket star is a brittle star whose arms branch again and again into a tangled net that it spreads at night to catch plankton.

name: Basking shark
fact: The basking shark is the second-largest fish and filters plankton through a gaping mouth as it cruises slowly along.

name: Bass
fact: Bass is a name shared by many unrelated fish, from the sea bass of European coasts to the largemouth bass of North American lakes.

name: Bass Strait
fact: Bass Strait separates Tasmania from mainland Australia and is named after George Bass, the ship's surgeon who proved Tasmania was an island in 1798.

name: Bat ray
fact: Bat rays flap over the sandy bottoms of California bays, digging up clams with their wings, and can span nearly 2 metres.

name: Bat star
fact: The bat star has webbing between its arms like a bat's wing and comes in almost every colour from red to purple to mottled.

name: Batavia
fact: The Dutch East India Company ship Batavia was wrecked on a reef off Western Australia in 1629, and a bloody mutiny followed among the survivors.

name: Bath sponge
fact: The soft, springy skeleton of the bath sponge has been harvested from the Mediterranean for thousands of years for washing.

name: Bathycallisoma
fact: Bathycallisoma schellenbergi is a large scavenging amphipod of the deepest Pacific trenches.

name: Bathykermadeca hadalis
fact: Bathykermadeca hadalis is an isopod first found in the Kermadec Trench, living deeper than 6,000 metres.

name: Bathysaurus
fact: Bathysaurus is a genus of large deep-sea lizardfish that wait on the seabed to ambush prey.

name: Bathysphere
fact: The bathysphere was a steel ball on a cable in which William Beebe and Otis Barton descended to about 920 metres off Bermuda in 1934, a record that stood for 15 years.

name: Bathythermograph
fact: A bathythermograph records the temperature of seawater at different depths as it descends.

name: Battle of Actium
fact: At Actium in 31 BC Octavian's fleet defeated Mark Antony and Cleopatra, clearing his way to become the first Roman emperor.

name: Battle of Aegospotami
fact: At Aegospotami in 405 BC the Spartan Lysander destroyed the Athenian fleet, effectively ending the Peloponnesian War.

name: Battle of Arginusae
fact: Arginusae in 406 BC was an Athenian naval victory, after which Athens controversially executed generals who failed to rescue survivors.

name: Battle of Beachy Head
fact: Beachy Head in 1690 was a French victory over a combined English and Dutch fleet in the English Channel.

name: Battle of Camperdown
fact: Camperdown in 1797 was a British victory over the Dutch fleet off the Netherlands under Admiral Duncan.

name: Battle of Cape Matapan
fact: At Cape Matapan in March 1941 Admiral Cunningham's fleet sank three Italian heavy cruisers off southern Greece.

name: Battle of Cape St Vincent
fact: At Cape St Vincent in 1797 Commodore Nelson left the line without orders to capture two Spanish ships and helped win the battle.

name: Battle of Chesma
fact: At Chesma in 1770 the Russian fleet used fireships to burn the Ottoman fleet in a Turkish bay.

name: Battle of Copenhagen
fact: At Copenhagen in 1801 Nelson is said to have raised his telescope to his blind eye to ignore a signal to retreat.

name: Battle of Coronel
fact: At Coronel off Chile in November 1914 von Spee's squadron sank two British cruisers, the Royal Navy's first defeat in a fleet action for over a century.

name: Battle of Dan-no-ura
fact: At Dan-no-ura in 1185 the Minamoto destroyed the Taira fleet in the Shimonoseki Strait, and the child emperor Antoku drowned.

name: Battle of Dogger Bank (1915)
fact: At Dogger Bank in January 1915 British battlecruisers sank the German armoured cruiser Blucher in the North Sea.

name: Battle of Gangut
fact: Gangut in 1714 was the first major Russian naval victory, won over the Swedes in the Baltic with Peter the Great taking part.

name: Battle of Hampton Roads
fact: Hampton Roads in March 1862 saw the first duel between ironclad warships, USS Monitor against CSS Virginia.

name: Battle of Heligoland Bight
fact: Heligoland Bight in August 1914 was the first major naval action of the First World War, and the British sank three German cruisers.

name: Battle of Jutland
fact: Jutland in 1916 was the largest naval battle of the First World War, between the British Grand Fleet and the German High Seas Fleet.

name: Battle of La Hogue
fact: La Hogue in 1692 saw the Anglo-Dutch fleet destroy French ships that were meant to cover an invasion of England.

name: Battle of Lake Erie
fact: At Lake Erie in 1813 Oliver Hazard Perry's American squadron captured a whole British fleet, and he reported that the enemy was ours.

name: Battle of Lepanto
fact: Lepanto in 1571, in which the Holy League beat the Ottoman fleet, was one of the last great battles fought mainly by oared galleys.

name: Battle of Leyte Gulf
fact: Leyte Gulf in October 1944 is often described as the largest naval battle in history, fought around the Philippines.

name: Battle of Lissa
fact: At Lissa in 1866 the Austrian fleet under Tegetthoff rammed and sank Italian ironclads in a famous clash of early armoured ships.

name: Battle of Lowestoft
fact: Lowestoft in 1665 was a major English victory over the Dutch in the Second Anglo-Dutch War.

name: Battle of Manila Bay
fact: At Manila Bay in May 1898 Commodore Dewey destroyed the Spanish Pacific squadron with very few American casualties.

name: Battle of Midway
fact: At Midway in June 1942 American aircraft sank four Japanese aircraft carriers, a turning point in the Pacific War.

name: Battle of Mylae
fact: At Mylae in 260 BC the Romans beat Carthage using boarding bridges called corvus, their first major naval victory.

name: Battle of Navarino
fact: Navarino in 1827 saw British, French and Russian ships destroy an Ottoman and Egyptian fleet, and it was the last major battle fought between sailing fleets.

name: Battle of Quiberon Bay
fact: At Quiberon Bay in 1759 Admiral Hawke chased the French fleet onto a rocky coast in a gale and wrecked its invasion plans.

name: Battle of Salamis
fact: At Salamis in 480 BC a smaller Greek fleet lured the Persians into a narrow strait and won a decisive victory.

name: Battle of Savo Island
fact: At Savo Island in August 1942 a Japanese night attack sank four Allied heavy cruisers in one of the worst American naval defeats.

name: Battle of Sinop
fact: At Sinop in 1853 a Russian squadron destroyed an Ottoman fleet in harbour, helping bring Britain and France into the Crimean War.

name: Battle of Sluys
fact: At Sluys in 1340 Edward III's English fleet destroyed a French fleet in the early years of the Hundred Years' War.

name: Battle of Solebay
fact: At Solebay in 1672 de Ruyter surprised the Anglo-French fleet at anchor off the Suffolk coast.

name: Battle of Taranto
fact: At Taranto in November 1940 British Swordfish torpedo planes from the carrier Illustrious crippled the Italian battle fleet in harbour.

name: Battle of Texel
fact: Texel in 1673 was the last battle of the Third Anglo-Dutch War, in which de Ruyter prevented an Anglo-French landing in the Netherlands.

name: Battle of the Aegates Islands
fact: The Aegates Islands in 241 BC was the Roman naval victory over Carthage that ended the First Punic War.

name: Battle of the Atlantic
fact: The Battle of the Atlantic from 1939 to 1945 was the longest continuous campaign of the Second World War, fought over Allied shipping against German U-boats.

name: Battle of the Barents Sea
fact: The Barents Sea battle of December 1942 saw British destroyers drive off larger German warships attacking an Arctic convoy, which enraged Hitler.

name: Battle of the Bismarck Sea
fact: In the Bismarck Sea in March 1943 Allied aircraft sank most of a Japanese troop convoy heading for New Guinea.

name: Battle of the Coral Sea
fact: The Coral Sea in May 1942 was the first naval battle fought entirely by aircraft, with the opposing ships never in sight of each other.

name: Battle of the Denmark Strait
fact: In the Denmark Strait in May 1941 the German battleship Bismarck sank HMS Hood, leaving only three survivors.

name: Battle of the Falkland Islands
fact: At the Falkland Islands in December 1914 a British squadron destroyed Admiral von Spee's German East Asia Squadron.

name: Battle of the Nile
fact: At the Nile in 1798 Nelson destroyed most of the French fleet in Aboukir Bay, and the French flagship L'Orient blew up.

name: Battle of the North Cape
fact: At the North Cape in December 1943 a British force that included the battleship Duke of York sank the German battleship Scharnhorst.

name: Battle of the Philippine Sea
fact: The Philippine Sea in June 1944 became known as the Great Marianas Turkey Shoot because American pilots shot down hundreds of Japanese aircraft.

name: Battle of the River Plate
fact: At the River Plate in December 1939 three British cruisers damaged the German pocket battleship Admiral Graf Spee, which was then scuttled off Montevideo.

name: Battle of the Saintes
fact: At the Saintes in 1782 Admiral Rodney's fleet broke the French line in the Caribbean and defeated Admiral de Grasse.

name: Battle of the Yalu River
fact: At the Yalu River in 1894 the Japanese fleet defeated the Chinese Beiyang Fleet in the first big clash of modern steam warships.

name: Battle of Trafalgar
fact: At Trafalgar in 1805 Nelson's fleet destroyed a larger French and Spanish force off the coast of Spain, though Nelson himself was killed.

name: Battle of Tsushima
fact: At Tsushima in May 1905 Admiral Togo's Japanese fleet destroyed the Russian Baltic Fleet after its long voyage around the world.

name: Battlecruiser
fact: Battlecruisers had the guns of a battleship but thinner armour in exchange for greater speed, and three exploded at Jutland.

name: Battleship
fact: Battleships were heavily armoured warships with the biggest guns afloat, and the last ones were retired by the early 1990s.

name: Bay anchovy
fact: The bay anchovy is probably the most abundant fish on the US Atlantic and Gulf of Mexico coasts, yet few people have ever seen one.

name: Bay of All Saints
fact: The Bay of All Saints at Salvador is the largest bay in Brazil and was named by Portuguese explorers who arrived on All Saints' Day in 1501.

name: Bay of Biscay
fact: The Bay of Biscay, between France and Spain, is notorious among sailors for its violent Atlantic storms.

name: Bay of Campeche
fact: The Bay of Campeche is the southern bight of the Gulf of Mexico, site of the huge Cantarell oil field and part of the Chicxulub impact crater.

name: Bay of Fundy
fact: The Bay of Fundy between Nova Scotia and New Brunswick has the highest tides in the world, rising and falling by as much as 16 metres.

name: Bay of Haifa
fact: The Bay of Haifa is the Mediterranean bay in northern Israel on which the port of Haifa sits.

name: Bay of Kotor
fact: The Bay of Kotor in Montenegro is a winding, fjord-like inlet of the Adriatic ringed by steep mountains.

name: Bay of Pigs
fact: The Bay of Pigs is an inlet on Cuba's southern Caribbean coast, famous for the failed 1961 invasion by CIA-trained Cuban exiles.

name: Bay of Plenty
fact: The Bay of Plenty on New Zealand's North Island was named by Captain Cook in 1769 for the friendly welcome and abundant supplies he found there.

name: Bay pipefish
fact: The bay pipefish hides upright among eelgrass blades along North America's Pacific coast, from Alaska to Baja California.

name: Bay scallop
fact: Bay scallops have dozens of tiny blue eyes along their mantle and swim by snapping their shells shut.

name: Bazaruto
fact: Bazaruto is an island archipelago off Mozambique that is a national park and a refuge for dugongs.

name: Beadlet anemone
fact: The beadlet anemone of British rock pools is a red blob at low tide, and fights its neighbours with a ring of blue stinging beads under its tentacles.

name: Beagle Channel
fact: The Beagle Channel in Tierra del Fuego is named after HMS Beagle and is a route to the port of Ushuaia.

name: Beaked sea snake
fact: The beaked sea snake causes most sea snake bites and deaths, especially among fishermen pulling nets in South and Southeast Asia.

name: Beaked whale
fact: Beaked whales are deep-diving, elusive whales with just one or two pairs of teeth, and some species are known only from stranded animals.

name: Bear paw clam
fact: The bear paw clam is a giant clam with a thick, ridged shell that gets part of its food from algae living in its tissues.

name: Bearded seal
fact: Bearded seals have long white whiskers for finding clams and crabs on the Arctic seabed, and males sing long trilling songs under the ice.

name: Beaufort Gyre
fact: The Beaufort Gyre is a wind-driven clockwise circulation in the Arctic Ocean north of Alaska that stores a huge volume of fresh water from melting ice.

name: Beaufort scale
fact: The Beaufort scale rates wind strength from calm to hurricane, from 0 to 12, based on the effect on the sea and on sails.

name: Beaufort Sea
fact: The Beaufort Sea north of Alaska and Canada is named after Sir Francis Beaufort, the British admiral who devised the Beaufort wind scale.

name: Beaugregory
fact: The beaugregory is a Caribbean damselfish, yellow below and blue above as a juvenile, that fiercely defends a small patch of reef.

name: Beira
fact: Beira in Mozambique is a port at the mouth of the Pungwe River that serves the inland countries of southern Africa.

name: Beirut
fact: Beirut's port was the site of a huge explosion on 4 August 2020 that devastated much of the city.

name: Belcher's sea snake
fact: Belcher's sea snake is often wrongly called the world's most venomous snake; its venom is potent, but it is docile and rarely bites.

name: Belemnite
fact: Belemnites were squid-like animals with an internal bullet-shaped shell, and their fossils were once thought to be thunderbolts.

name: Belgica
fact: The Belgica carried the Belgian Antarctic Expedition of 1897 to 1899, the first to spend a winter trapped in Antarctic pack ice.

name: Belgica expedition
fact: The Belgica expedition of 1897 to 1899 was the first to winter in the Antarctic, when its ship became trapped in ice.

name: Belize Barrier Reef
fact: The Belize Barrier Reef runs about 300 kilometres along the coast of Belize and is the largest section of the Mesoamerican Reef.

name: Bell Rock Lighthouse
fact: Bell Rock Lighthouse off Angus in Scotland, built by Robert Stevenson and finished in 1810, is the oldest surviving sea-washed lighthouse in the world.

name: Bellingshausen Sea
fact: The Bellingshausen Sea off Antarctica is named after Fabian Gottlieb von Bellingshausen, the Russian officer whose expedition sighted the continent in 1820.

name: Bells Beach
fact: Bells Beach in Victoria, Australia, hosts the Rip Curl Pro, one of the longest-running contests in surfing.

name: Beluga sturgeon
fact: The beluga sturgeon of the Caspian and Black Seas can live for more than 100 years and is the source of the most expensive caviar.

name: Beluga whale
fact: Belugas are nicknamed sea canaries for their chirps and whistles, and they can turn their heads because their neck bones are not fused.

name: Belyaev's snailfish
fact: Belyaev's snailfish is a hadal snailfish of the trenches of the north-west Pacific.

name: Ben Franklin
fact: In 1969 the submersible Ben Franklin drifted silently for 30 days inside the Gulf Stream with six men aboard, a mission NASA studied as a model for long space flights.

name: Bengal tiger
fact: Bengal tigers of the Sundarbans, the world's largest mangrove forest, swim between islands and hunt along the tidal creeks.

name: Benghazi
fact: Benghazi is the second-largest city in Libya and its main port on the Gulf of Sidra.

name: Benguela Current
fact: The Benguela Current carries cold, nutrient-rich water north along the coast of Namibia and South Africa, supporting vast shoals of sardines and the Namib coast's fogs.

name: Benin
fact: Benin has roughly 120 kilometres of coastline on the Gulf of Guinea.

name: Benjamin Hornigold
fact: Benjamin Hornigold was a leading Bahamas pirate who mentored Blackbeard and later accepted a pardon to hunt other pirates.

name: Benthesicymus
fact: The prawn Benthesicymus crenatus was filmed in the Kermadec and Japan trenches at about 7,700 metres, the first decapod seen in the hadal zone.

name: Bequia
fact: Bequia is the largest of the Grenadines that belong to Saint Vincent and the Grenadines and is known for traditional wooden boat-building.

name: Berbera
fact: Berbera on the Gulf of Aden is the main port of Somaliland.

name: Bergen
fact: Bergen is a Norwegian port on the North Sea coast, with the old Hanseatic wharf of Bryggen.

name: Bergen Aquarium
fact: Bergen Aquarium in Norway opened in 1960 and sits on the Nordnes peninsula.

name: Berghia
fact: Berghia sea slugs eat glass anemones, and aquarists keep them to control those pests.

name: Bering Sea
fact: The Bering Sea separates Alaska from Siberia and is named after Vitus Bering, the Danish navigator who sailed through it for Russia in 1728.

name: Bering Sea beaked whale
fact: The Bering Sea beaked whale lives in the cold North Pacific and is rarely seen at sea.

name: Bering Strait
fact: The Bering Strait, named after the Danish navigator Vitus Bering, separates Russia from Alaska by about 82 kilometres and links the Pacific to the Arctic.

name: Bermuda
fact: Bermuda is a lone group of islands in the North Atlantic about 1,000 kilometres from the US coast, with the most northerly coral reefs in the world.

name: Bermuda fireworm
fact: Bermuda fireworms rise to the surface a few nights after each summer full moon and spin in glowing green circles to mate, a display Columbus may have seen in 1492.

name: Bermuda petrel
fact: The Bermuda petrel, or cahow, was thought extinct for about three centuries until a few nesting pairs were rediscovered in 1951.

name: Beroe comb jelly
fact: Beroe is a sack-shaped comb jelly with no tentacles that swallows other comb jellies whole.

name: Bertram Ramsay
fact: Bertram Ramsay planned the evacuation of Dunkirk in 1940 and later the naval side of the Normandy landings.

name: Betta
fact: Bettas have a labyrinth organ above the gills that lets them gulp air at the surface, which is why they survive in still, oxygen-poor water.

name: Bichir
fact: Bichirs have paired lungs and can breathe air, and young bichirs even have external gills like a salamander larva.

name: Bicolor angelfish
fact: The bicolor angelfish is a small dwarf angelfish, half yellow and half blue, that lives in harems.

name: Bicolor damselfish
fact: The bicolor damselfish of the Caribbean is dark in front and pale behind, and tends algae gardens that it guards from other grazers.

name: Bicolor parrotfish
fact: The bicolor parrotfish changes from a pale juvenile to a green and pink adult, and big males grow a bump on the forehead.

name: Big-belly seahorse
fact: The big-belly seahorse of Australia and New Zealand is one of the largest seahorses, reaching about 35 centimetres, and the male's pouch swells hugely with eggs.

name: Big red jellyfish
fact: Big red is a metre-wide deep-sea jellyfish discovered in 2003 that has no tentacles at all, feeding instead with four to seven thick fleshy arms.

name: Big skate
fact: The big skate of the north-east Pacific carries a pair of large eye-like spots on its wings and can grow over two metres long.

name: Big wave surfing
fact: Big wave surfing is riding waves that reach several metres, such as those at Nazare in Portugal and Mavericks in California.

name: Bigeye sixgill shark
fact: Bigeye sixgill sharks have large eyes suited to the dim deep sea and, like their cousins, six pairs of gill slits.

name: Bigeye thresher shark
fact: The bigeye thresher has huge upward-facing eyes for hunting in dim water hundreds of metres down, where it spends its days.

name: Bigeye tuna
fact: The bigeye tuna, with large eyes for hunting in dim deep water, is a major catch for longline fleets and is sold as sashimi-grade ahi in Hawaii.

name: Bigfin reef squid
fact: Bigfin reef squid have one of the fastest growth rates of any large invertebrate, reaching well over half a kilogram within about four months.

name: Bigfin squid
fact: Bigfin squid dangle ten thin, elbowed arms that stretch to a total length of about 8 metres, and one was filmed 6,212 metres down in the Philippine Trench.

name: Bighead carp
fact: The bighead carp is farmed in huge quantities in China, where its large head is prized for soups.

name: Bight of Benin
fact: The Bight of Benin is a bay in the Gulf of Guinea whose shore was once known as the Slave Coast.

name: Bight of Biafra
fact: The Bight of Biafra, now officially the Bight of Bonny, is the easternmost corner of the Gulf of Guinea, off Nigeria and Cameroon.

name: Bignose shark
fact: The bignose shark is a large requiem shark with a long, rounded snout, usually found near the seabed on continental slopes.

name: Bigtooth river stingray
fact: The bigtooth river stingray is a freshwater ray found in the Tocantins-Araguaia river basin of Brazil.

name: Bikini Atoll
fact: Bikini Atoll's reef was blasted by 23 nuclear tests between 1946 and 1958, yet its corals have since grown back vigorously.

name: Bilbao
fact: Bilbao's port on the Bay of Biscay is one of Spain's busiest, and the city was reinvented by the Guggenheim museum in 1997.

name: Bilge
fact: The bilge is the lowest part of a ship's interior, where water collects, and it is the source of the slang word for nonsense.

name: Billy Budd
fact: Billy Budd is Herman Melville's novella about a young sailor on a warship, left unfinished at his death in 1891 and published in 1924.

name: Binnacle
fact: A binnacle is the stand that holds a ship's compass near the helm.

name: Binoculars
fact: Binoculars are a pair of linked telescopes that sailors use to spot buoys, coastlines and other ships.

name: Bioko
fact: Bioko is a volcanic island in the Gulf of Guinea that holds Malabo, the capital of Equatorial Guinea, far from the country's mainland.

name: Bioluminescence
fact: Bioluminescence is light produced by living organisms, and it makes the sea glow where plankton like dinoflagellates are disturbed.

name: Birch Aquarium
fact: Birch Aquarium in La Jolla, California, is the public face of the Scripps Institution of Oceanography.

name: Bird wrasse
fact: The bird wrasse has a long, curved beak-like snout that it uses to pluck small animals from crevices on Indo-Pacific reefs.

name: Birdbeak dogfish
fact: The birdbeak dogfish has an extremely long, flattened snout and lives on continental slopes down to around 1,500 metres.

name: Bird's nest coral
fact: Bird's nest coral grows as thin, tightly branching colonies with pointed tips that resemble a tangled nest.

name: Bireme
fact: The bireme was an ancient oared warship with two banks of oars on each side, often fitted with a bronze ram.

name: Biscayne Bay
fact: Biscayne Bay is a shallow lagoon beside Miami in Florida, and much of it is protected as a national park.

name: Bishop Rock Lighthouse
fact: Bishop Rock off the Isles of Scilly is described as the smallest island in the world with a building on it, and its lighthouse is the outermost in England.

name: Bismarck
fact: The battleship Bismarck was sunk in May 1941 after a three-day chase, and Robert Ballard found the wreck in 1989 standing upright about 4,700 metres down.

name: Bismarck Sea
fact: The Bismarck Sea lies north-east of New Guinea and is named, like the Bismarck Archipelago, after the German chancellor Otto von Bismarck.

name: Biwa trout
fact: The biwa trout is a subspecies of masu salmon found only in Lake Biwa in Japan, from which it runs up streams to spawn.

name: Black-axil chromis
fact: The black-axil chromis is a green-blue damselfish that forms big plankton-feeding schools over Indo-Pacific reefs.

name: Black-banded sea krait
fact: The black-banded sea krait, or erabu, is caught and smoked in Okinawa to make a traditional soup called irabu-jiru.

name: Bartholomew Roberts
fact: Bartholomew Roberts, known as Black Bart, captured around 400 ships in a few years and was one of the most successful pirates of all time.

name: Black-blotched stingray
fact: The blotched fantail ray can grow nearly 2 metres across and is often seen at cleaning stations on Indo-Pacific reefs.

name: Black brittle star
fact: The black brittle star lives in dense beds on north-east Atlantic seabeds, lifting its arms into the current to catch food.

name: Black-browed albatross
fact: Black-browed albatrosses have a dark smudge over each eye and breed in huge colonies, mainly on the Falkland Islands.

name: Black caiman
fact: The black caiman is the largest predator of the Amazon basin and can grow to about 5 metres long.

name: Black coral
fact: Black coral has a dark, flexible skeleton that has been carved into jewellery, and some colonies are more than 4,000 years old.

name: Black crappie
fact: Crappie are schooling sunfish of North American lakes, and anglers catch them in numbers around sunken brush in spring.

name: Black dogfish
fact: The black dogfish is a small glowing shark of the deep North Atlantic that gathers in large schools on the continental slope.

name: Black drum
fact: Black drum make such loud, low booming calls while spawning that Florida residents have complained of a mysterious hum coming through their walls.

name: Black ghost knifefish
fact: The black ghost knifefish swims backwards as easily as forwards by rippling one long fin and senses its world with a weak electric field.

name: Black grouper
fact: The black grouper is a large grouper of the western Atlantic, growing to about 1.5 metres, with rectangular dark blotches on its sides.

name: Black guillemot
fact: The black guillemot is a black seabird with white wing patches and bright red feet that nests along rocky Arctic and subarctic coasts.

name: Black-headed sea snake
fact: The black-headed sea snake is a slender true sea snake of south-east Asian coastal waters.

name: Black leather chiton
fact: The black leather chiton has a tough dark girdle covering most of its eight plates and grazes seaweed on Pacific shores.

name: Black-lip pearl oyster
fact: The black-lip pearl oyster produces the dark pearls known as Tahitian pearls.

name: Black mangrove
fact: Black mangroves push pencil-like roots up out of the mud to breathe and get rid of salt through their leaves.

name: Black marlin
fact: The black marlin of the Indo-Pacific is often claimed to be the fastest fish of all, and its rigid pectoral fins cannot be folded flat against the body.

name: Black molly
fact: The black molly is a jet-black aquarium strain of a Central American livebearer that gives birth to free-swimming fry.

name: Black piranha
fact: The black piranha is among the largest piranhas and is a fierce predator of the Amazon and Orinoco basins.

name: Black Sails
fact: Black Sails is a television series that ran from 2014 to 2017 and serves as a prequel to Treasure Island, set among pirates of the Caribbean.

name: Black scabbardfish
fact: The black scabbardfish is a jet-black, eel-like deep-sea fish with fangs, hauled up from about 1,000 metres on long lines off Madeira, where it is served with banana.

name: Black Sea
fact: The Black Sea connects to the Mediterranean only through the Bosporus and Dardanelles, and below about 150 metres its water contains no oxygen at all.

name: Black sea bass
fact: The black sea bass of the US east coast starts life as a female and later changes into a male with a bright blue hump on its nape.

name: Black sea nettle
fact: The black sea nettle has a bell up to a metre across and oral arms about 8 metres long, yet it was not formally described until 1997.

name: Black seadevil
fact: Female black seadevils dangle a glowing lure in the dark depths and are far larger than the males.

name: Black skimmer
fact: The black skimmer flies low with its longer lower beak slicing the water, snapping shut the instant it touches a fish.

name: Black skipjack
fact: The black skipjack is a small tuna of the eastern Pacific, marked with dark stripes along its belly.

name: Black smoker
fact: A black smoker is a hydrothermal vent on the seabed that spews dark, mineral-rich water heated to hundreds of degrees Celsius.

name: Black swallower
fact: The black swallower can gulp down fish more than twice its own length, stretching its stomach so far that it sometimes bursts.

name: Black swan
fact: Black swans graze on algae and water plants, including seagrass in estuaries, and are native to Australia.

name: Black triggerfish
fact: The black triggerfish forms big groups that feed on plankton above tropical reefs in all oceans.

name: Black turban snail
fact: The black turban snail is a common grazer of Pacific tide pools whose empty shells are favourite homes for hermit crabs.

name: Blackbar devil
fact: The blackbar devil has a dark bar across its pale body, and it farms algae on the coral it defends.

name: Blackbeard
fact: Blackbeard, whose real name was probably Edward Teach, terrorised the Caribbean and American coast until he was killed off North Carolina in 1718.

name: Blackbelly lanternshark
fact: The blackbelly lanternshark is a small deep-water shark that glows faintly from light-producing organs on its dark belly.

name: Blackening
fact: Blackening coats fish in spices and sears it in a very hot pan, and Louisiana chef Paul Prudhomme made blackened redfish famous in the 1980s.

name: Blackfin tuna
fact: The blackfin tuna is the smallest of the true tunas, rarely over a metre long, and is found only in the western Atlantic.

name: Blackmouth catshark
fact: The blackmouth catshark has a dark lining inside its mouth and lives on muddy seabeds of the north-east Atlantic and Mediterranean.

name: Blacknose shark
fact: The small blacknose shark has a dark smudge on its snout tip and is common in the warm shallows of the western Atlantic.

name: Blacksmith
fact: The blacksmith is a blue-grey damselfish of California's kelp forests that shelters in rock crevices at night and feeds on plankton by day.

name: Blackspot shark
fact: The blackspot shark is a small requiem shark of Indian and western Pacific coasts, named for the dark mark on its second dorsal fin.

name: Blackspot tuskfish
fact: The blackspot tuskfish was filmed on the Great Barrier Reef smashing clams against a rock anvil, one of the first documented cases of tool use in a fish.

name: Blackspotted puffer
fact: The blackspotted puffer, nicknamed the dog-faced puffer, has a grey body with black spots and a muzzle like a puppy's.

name: Blackthroat seaperch
fact: The blackthroat seaperch, nodoguro in Japan, is a fatty deep-water fish prized for sushi and grilling, named for its black mouth lining.

name: Blacktip reef shark
fact: Blacktip reef sharks patrol reef flats so shallow that their black-tipped dorsal fins often poke above the surface.

name: Blacktip shark
fact: Blacktip sharks leap and spin out of the water when chasing fish and migrate along the Florida coast in large numbers each year.

name: Bladderwrack
fact: Bladderwrack is the brown seaweed with paired air bladders along its fronds, common on rocky shores and the original source of iodine.

name: Blainville's beaked whale
fact: Blainville's beaked whale has the densest bone known in any animal, in its beak, and is named after French zoologist Henri de Blainville.

name: Blanket octopus
fact: A female blanket octopus can be 2 metres long while the male is barely 2 centimetres, and they rip stinging tentacles from Portuguese man o' war to use as weapons.

name: Blenny
fact: Blennies are small scaleless fish that wedge themselves into cracks in rock pools, and some can hop between pools over wet rock.

name: Bligh's open boat voyage
