fact: Giant petrels are the vultures of the Southern Ocean, tearing into seal and penguin carcasses, but they also catch fish, squid and krill at sea.

name: Giant phantom jelly
fact: The giant phantom jelly is a rarely seen deep-sea jelly with four enormous ribbon-like arms that trail for several metres.

name: Giant river prawn
fact: The giant river prawn, with its long blue claws, is farmed in freshwater ponds across Asia and sold as scampi in India.

name: Giant sea bass
fact: The giant sea bass of California can reach over 2 metres and 250 kilograms, and nearly vanished before fishing for it was banned in 1982.

name: Giant sea spider
fact: Giant sea spiders of the deep and Antarctic seas can span about 70 centimetres, and pump blood with their guts rather than a strong heart.

name: Giant siphonophore
fact: The giant siphonophore Praya dubia can reach 40 to 50 metres long, among the longest animals on Earth, and its stinging tentacles glow when touched.

name: Giant snakehead
fact: The giant snakehead breathes air and can grow to more than a metre long, and the parents aggressively guard their bright red young.

name: Giant squid
fact: The giant squid has the largest eyes of any animal, about the size of a dinner plate, and was not filmed alive in the deep until 2012.

name: Giant trevally
fact: The giant trevally of Indian Ocean reefs has been filmed leaping to snatch terns out of the air, and anglers prize its brutal strength.

name: Giant tube worm
fact: The giant tube worm has no mouth or gut: bacteria inside it turn vent sulphide into food, letting it grow to 2 metres, nearly a metre of it in a single year.

name: Giant warty squid
fact: The giant warty squid of Antarctic waters can reach more than 2 metres in total length and is a food of sperm whales and other Southern Ocean predators.

name: Pilot gig racing
fact: Pilot gig racing is a rowing sport using six-oared Cornish pilot gigs, and the world championships are held at the Isles of Scilly.

name: Gigantopelta chessoia
fact: Gigantopelta chessoia is a large vent snail found at hydrothermal vents on the East Scotia Ridge in the Southern Ocean.

name: Giglio
fact: Giglio is a small Italian island off Tuscany where the cruise ship Costa Concordia capsized in 2012.

name: Gila trout
fact: The Gila trout survives in a handful of mountain streams in New Mexico and Arizona and was among the first fish listed as endangered in the United States.

name: Gilded catfish
fact: The gilded catfish, or dourada, makes one of the longest freshwater migrations known, swimming thousands of kilometres up the Amazon to spawn.

name: Gillaroo
fact: The gillaroo is an Irish lake trout with a thick, muscular stomach for crushing the snails and shrimps it eats.

name: Gioia Tauro
fact: Gioia Tauro in Calabria is Italy's largest container transshipment port, built in the 1990s.

name: Gizzard shad
fact: The gizzard shad, kohada, is the fish by which Tokyo sushi chefs are judged; it is salted and pickled in vinegar before serving.

name: Gjoa expedition
fact: Roald Amundsen's Gjoa expedition of 1903 to 1906 was the first to navigate the Northwest Passage by ship.

name: Gladstone
fact: Gladstone in Queensland is a deep-water port that ships coal and liquefied natural gas.

name: Glass catfish
fact: The glass catfish of Southeast Asia is so transparent you can see its bones and organs, and it turns milky white when it dies.

name: Glass eel
fact: Young eels arriving at European and American coasts after drifting from the Sargasso Sea are called glass eels because their bodies are completely transparent.

name: Glass octopus
fact: The glass octopus is almost completely transparent; only its eyes, optic nerves and digestive tract show as it drifts through the open ocean.

name: Glass sea slug
fact: The glass sea slug is a transparent, free-swimming sea slug that drifts in open water and glows when disturbed.

name: Glass sponge
fact: Glass sponges build skeletons of silica glass fibres, and some deep-sea individuals are thought to be more than 10,000 years old.

name: Glass squid
fact: Glass squid are almost completely transparent and keep their one opaque organ, the digestive gland, pointed vertically so it casts the smallest shadow.

name: Glasseye
fact: The glasseye is a nocturnal reef fish with huge eyes that can switch between a red coat and a silvery one.

name: Glassy sweeper
fact: Glassy sweepers pack Caribbean caves in coppery schools by day and stream out at night to feed on plankton.

name: Glaucilla
fact: Glaucilla floats at the sea surface and preys on other drifting animals such as blue buttons.

name: Glaucus
fact: Glaucus was a Greek fisherman who ate a magical herb, leapt into the sea and became a prophetic sea god.

name: Globe skimmer dragonfly
fact: The globe skimmer dragonfly crosses the Indian Ocean between India and East Africa on the monsoon winds, a multi-generation round trip of about 14,000 to 18,000 kilometres.

name: Glomar Challenger
fact: The drilling ship Glomar Challenger took cores from the Atlantic floor in 1968 that confirmed sea-floor spreading and plate tectonics.

name: Gloomy octopus
fact: Gloomy octopuses off eastern Australia gather at sites nicknamed Octopolis and Octlantis, where they have been filmed throwing shells and silt at each other.

name: Glorious First of June
aliases: Battle of the Glorious First of June
fact: The Glorious First of June in 1794 was fought to stop a French grain convoy from America reaching France.

name: Glover's Reef
fact: Glover's Reef is an atoll off Belize named after the pirate John Glover and is a marine reserve known for its sheer outer walls.

name: Glowing sucker octopus
fact: The glowing sucker octopus has suckers that no longer grip but glow blue-green, probably to lure the tiny copepods it eats.

name: Glowlight tetra
fact: The glowlight tetra is a 3-to-4-centimetre fish from Guyana with a glowing orange-red stripe down its side.

name: Goatfish
fact: Goatfish dig through sand with a pair of chin barbels used like fingers, and some change from yellow to red in seconds when resting or being cleaned.

name: Goblin shark
fact: The goblin shark shoots its jaws forward to snatch prey, and its pink skin comes from blood vessels showing through.

name: Goby
fact: Gobies are tiny bottom-living fish whose pelvic fins are fused into a sucker that holds them onto rocks in surging water.

name: Gold Beach
fact: Gold Beach was the central British landing beach on D-Day, next to the village of Arromanches where an artificial Mulberry harbour was built.

name: Gold coral
fact: Deep-sea gold corals have been dated at over 2,700 years old, among the oldest living things on Earth.

name: Gold nugget pleco
fact: The gold nugget pleco comes from Brazil's Xingu River and is named for the golden spots on its dark body.

name: Golden dorado
fact: The golden dorado of South American rivers is a brilliant gold predator that fly anglers travel to Argentina and Bolivia to catch.

name: Golden Gate
fact: The Golden Gate is the strait connecting San Francisco Bay to the Pacific, and its famous bridge was for decades the longest suspension bridge in the world.

name: Golden Globe Race
fact: The 1968 Golden Globe Race was the first solo non-stop round-the-world yacht race, and Robin Knox-Johnston was the only finisher.

name: Golden king crab
fact: Golden king crabs live on the cold continental slope of the North Pacific and are caught in deep traps.

name: Golden star tunicate
fact: Colonies of the golden star tunicate form flower-like star shapes, each star made of many linked individuals.

name: Golden trevally
fact: Young golden trevally swim beside sharks and other large animals like pilot fish, looking like a striped escort.

name: Golden trout
fact: The golden trout, with its brilliant gold and red colours, lives in the high Sierra Nevada and is the state freshwater fish of California.

name: Goldentail moray
fact: The goldentail moray is a small Caribbean moray, about 60 centimetres long, with a dark body speckled with yellow.

name: Goldfish
fact: Goldfish were bred from dull carp in China about a thousand years ago, and released pets now grow huge and invasive in lakes around the world.

name: Goldsinny
fact: The goldsinny is a small orange-brown wrasse of European rocky shores, now farmed as a cleaner fish to eat lice off farmed salmon.

name: Golfo Nuevo
fact: Golfo Nuevo is a sheltered gulf on Argentina's Valdes Peninsula where southern right whales gather to breed.

name: Goliath grouper
fact: The Atlantic goliath grouper can reach 2.5 metres and over 300 kilograms, and makes a booming sound to warn off divers.

name: Goliath tigerfish
fact: The goliath tigerfish of the Congo River has 32 dagger-like teeth and has been known to attack crocodiles.

name: Gonate squid
fact: Brooding female gonate squid of the species Gonatus onyx carry their eggs in their arms for months at depth.

name: Goonch
fact: The goonch, or giant devil catfish, is a huge, mottled catfish of South Asian rivers, blamed in reports from the Kali River for attacks on bathers.

name: Goose barnacle
fact: Goose barnacles, percebes in Spain, are gathered from wave-battered rocks and are among the most expensive seafood in Europe; medieval writers thought geese hatched from them.

name: Gorgonian
fact: Gorgonians are soft corals with a flexible, horn-like skeleton, growing as sea fans, whips and bushes.

name: Gough Island
fact: Gough Island is a remote South Atlantic island and nature reserve, home to enormous seabird colonies.

name: Gould's squid
fact: Gould's squid is an arrow squid of southern Australian waters that is fished commercially.

name: Gourami
fact: Gouramis have a labyrinth organ that lets them breathe air from the surface, so they thrive in warm, stagnant water.

name: Gozo
fact: Gozo is the smaller sister island of Malta and has the Ġgantija temples, built around 3600 BC.

name: GPS
fact: The Global Positioning System uses signals from satellites to tell a ship its position almost anywhere on Earth.

name: Gqeberha
fact: Gqeberha, formerly Port Elizabeth, was officially renamed in 2021 and is a major South African port on Algoa Bay.

name: Grace Bay
fact: Grace Bay on Providenciales in the Turks and Caicos Islands is a long beach sheltered by a barrier reef.

name: Grace Hopper
fact: Grace Hopper was a rear admiral in the United States Navy and a computing pioneer who helped develop the COBOL programming language.

name: Grace O'Malley
fact: Grace O'Malley was a sixteenth-century Irish clan leader and sea captain who met Queen Elizabeth I in 1593.

name: Gracilaria
fact: Gracilaria is a red seaweed farmed widely around the world as a source of agar.

name: Grand Banks
fact: The Grand Banks off Newfoundland are shallow underwater plateaus whose cod fishery fed Europe for centuries before collapsing in 1992.

name: Grand Canal of China
fact: China's Grand Canal, about 1,800 kilometres long, is the longest canal in the world and has been built up over more than a thousand years.

name: Grande Comore
fact: Grande Comore is the largest island of the Comoros and is dominated by the active volcano Mount Karthala.

name: Grass carp
fact: The grass carp is the most farmed fish on Earth by weight, raised in Chinese ponds on grass and water plants.

name: Gravlax
fact: Gravlax is a Nordic dish of salmon cured with salt, sugar and dill, and the name comes from words meaning buried salmon.

name: Gray angelfish
fact: The gray angelfish is a large, drab Caribbean angelfish that often follows divers; its juveniles are black with yellow bars.

name: Grayling
fact: The grayling, 'lady of the stream', carries a tall sail-like dorsal fin and lives only in clean, cold rivers.

name: Gray's beaked whale
fact: Gray's beaked whale, named after British zoologist John Edward Gray, is the beaked whale most often stranded in New Zealand and is seen in cold Southern Ocean waters.

name: Graysby
fact: The graysby is a small Caribbean grouper, about 30 centimetres long, covered in dark spots, and it hides in reef crevices.

name: Great Astrolabe Reef
fact: The Great Astrolabe Reef is a large barrier reef surrounding the Fijian island of Kadavu.

name: Great auk
fact: The great auk, a flightless North Atlantic seabird, was the original 'penguin', and the last known pair was killed on an Icelandic island in 1844.

name: Great Bahama Bank
fact: The Great Bahama Bank is a vast limestone platform so shallow that its turquoise waters are plainly visible from space, with the Tongue of the Ocean cut into it.

name: Great Barrier Reef
fact: The Great Barrier Reef stretches more than 2,300 kilometres along Australia's north-east coast and is the largest structure ever built by living things.

name: Great Barrier Reef Marine Park
fact: The Great Barrier Reef Marine Park protects about 344,000 square kilometres of reef off Queensland, the largest coral reef system on Earth.

name: Great Belt
fact: The Great Belt in Denmark separates Zealand from Funen and has been crossed by the Great Belt Bridge since 1998.

name: Great Blue Hole
fact: The Great Blue Hole off Belize is a near-circular sinkhole about 300 metres across and 120 metres deep that was a dry cave before the sea rose.

name: Great Britain
fact: Great Britain is the largest island in Europe and was joined to the continent by dry land until rising seas flooded Doggerland about 8,000 years ago.

name: Great Chagos Bank
fact: The Great Chagos Bank in the Indian Ocean is the largest atoll structure in the world and is almost entirely submerged.

name: Great cormorant
fact: The great cormorant dives after fish, and because its feathers soak up water it perches with wings spread to dry.

name: Great hammerhead
fact: The great hammerhead, the largest hammerhead at up to about 6 metres, uses its head to pin stingrays to the seabed.

name: Great lanternshark
fact: The great lanternshark is a deep North Atlantic shark with light-producing organs on its underside, found thousands of metres down.

name: Great Meteor Seamount
fact: The Great Meteor Seamount is a flat-topped underwater mountain in the north-east Atlantic, whose summit lies a few hundred metres below the surface.

name: Great Northern Expedition
fact: The Great Northern Expedition of 1733 to 1743 was a huge Russian effort that mapped Siberia's Arctic coast and took Vitus Bering to Alaska.

name: Great Sea Reef
fact: Fiji's Great Sea Reef, known locally as Cakaulevu, is the third-longest continuous barrier reef in the world.

name: Great seahorse
fact: The great seahorse is one of the biggest seahorses, growing to about 28 centimetres in Indo-Pacific waters.

name: Great skua
fact: The great skua, nicknamed the bonxie in Shetland, catches fish itself but is better known for robbing gannets and puffins of theirs.

name: Great white shark
fact: Great white sharks can sense the faint electrical fields given off by the muscles and heartbeat of hidden prey.

name: Greater amberjack
fact: The greater amberjack, kanpachi in Japan, is a fast, powerful hunter of the open water, farmed in sea pens and served as firm, mild sashimi.

name: Greater blue-ringed octopus
fact: Despite its name the greater blue-ringed octopus is only about 10 centimetres across; it is the size of its rings that is greater than its relatives'.

name: Greater forkbeard
fact: The greater forkbeard is a deep-water cod relative of the eastern Atlantic with long, forked pelvic fins used to feel for food.

name: Greater pipefish
fact: The greater pipefish of European coasts grows to about 45 centimetres, and the male broods the eggs in a pouch under his tail.

name: Green anaconda
fact: The green anaconda is the heaviest snake in the world and spends most of its life in or beside slow water in the Amazon basin.

name: Green bomber worm
fact: Green bomber worms drop glowing green "bombs" from their bodies to distract predators in the deep sea.

name: Green-lipped mussel
fact: The green-lipped mussel is found only in New Zealand, where it is farmed on ropes and exported worldwide, including as a joint supplement.

name: Green moray
fact: The green moray of the Caribbean is actually brown; a coat of yellow mucus over its skin makes it look green.

name: Green neon tetra
fact: The green neon tetra is a 2.5-centimetre relative of the neon tetra from the upper Orinoco and Rio Negro with a blue-green stripe.

name: Green sawfish
fact: The green sawfish is one of the largest sawfish, reported at over 7 metres long, and is now critically endangered.

name: Green sea urchin
fact: The green sea urchin lives in cold northern waters of both the Atlantic and the Pacific and is harvested for its roe.

name: Green spotted puffer
fact: The green spotted puffer lives in brackish South-East Asian estuaries and is a common, if demanding, aquarium fish.

name: Green sturgeon
fact: The green sturgeon of the North Pacific is a bony-plated fish from a lineage dating back to the age of the dinosaurs.

name: Green turtle
fact: Adult green sea turtles graze on seagrass and algae, which stains their fat green and gives them their name; they may live for 70 years or more.

name: Greenback cutthroat trout
fact: The greenback cutthroat trout is the state fish of Colorado and has been the focus of long conservation efforts after it nearly vanished.

name: Greenback flounder
fact: The greenback flounder is a flatfish of southern Australia and New Zealand that lives in estuaries and shallow bays.

name: Greenland
fact: Greenland is the largest island in the world, lying between the Atlantic and Arctic oceans, and about 80 per cent of it is buried under an ice sheet.

name: Greenland cod
fact: The Greenland cod is a dark, slow-growing cod of Arctic coastal waters, caught by Inuit through holes in the ice.

name: Greenland halibut
fact: The Greenland halibut's migrating eye stops at the top edge of its head, so it can swim upright as well as lie flat.

name: Greenland right whale
fact: Greenland right whale is an old name for the bowhead, an Arctic giant that can live for around two centuries.

name: Greenland shark
fact: Greenland sharks grow about a centimetre a year and may live for several centuries, longer than any other known vertebrate.

name: Greenpeace
fact: Greenpeace was founded in Vancouver in 1971 and campaigns against whaling, overfishing and ocean pollution, with ships such as the Rainbow Warrior.

name: Grenada
fact: Grenada is nicknamed the Spice Isle for the nutmeg and mace it grows and exports.

name: Grenadier
fact: Grenadiers, or rattails, are the commonest fish on the deep seabed, with big heads and whip-like tails, and have been seen about 7,000 metres down.

name: Grey bamboo shark
fact: The grey bamboo shark is a slim, nocturnal shark that rests on shallow Indo-Pacific reefs and sandy seabeds by day.

name: Grey mangrove
fact: The grey mangrove has the widest range of any mangrove, growing from East Africa to New Zealand and south-eastern Australia.

name: Grey mullet
fact: The grey mullet grazes algae and mud in estuaries and harbours around the world, and its roe is pressed into bottarga.

name: Grey reef shark
fact: Grey reef sharks warn off intruders with a hunched, exaggerated swimming display before they attack.

name: Grey seal
fact: Grey seal pups are born with white fur and are weaned in under three weeks, after which the mother leaves them to fend for themselves.

name: Grey snapper
fact: The mangrove snapper, or gray snapper, grows up among mangrove roots and is one of the most commonly caught snappers in Florida.

name: Grey triggerfish
fact: The grey triggerfish is found on both sides of the Atlantic, from the Gulf of Mexico to the Mediterranean, and is increasingly seen off Britain.

name: Grey whale
fact: Grey whales feed unlike any other whale, rolling on their sides to suck up mouthfuls of mud and straining out tiny amphipods through their baleen.

name: Grilling
fact: Grilling cooks fish over or under direct heat, and whole sardines grilled over charcoal are a classic Portuguese dish.

name: Grog
fact: Grog was the daily rum ration mixed with water that was given to sailors in the Royal Navy from 1740 until 1970.

name: Grouper
fact: Groupers are big-mouthed reef predators that suck in prey whole, and some species have been seen hunting together with moray eels.

name: Grunion
fact: Grunion ride the highest tides onto Californian beaches at night to spawn in the sand, and crowds come to catch them by hand.

name: Grunt
fact: Grunts are named for the sound they make by grinding their throat teeth together, amplified by the swim bladder, especially when caught.

name: Grunt sculpin
fact: The grunt sculpin of the Pacific Northwest hops along the bottom on its fins and hides inside empty giant barnacle shells.

name: Guadalupe fur seal
fact: The Guadalupe fur seal was thought to be extinct until a small colony was rediscovered at Guadalupe Island, Mexico, in the 1950s.

name: Guadeloupe
fact: Guadeloupe is shaped like a butterfly, with two main islands, Basse-Terre and Grande-Terre, split by a narrow channel.

name: Guam
fact: Guam is the largest of the Mariana Islands and lies close to the Mariana Trench, the deepest part of the ocean.

name: Guanabara Bay
fact: Guanabara Bay is the great bay on which Rio de Janeiro stands, named River of January by Portuguese sailors who reached it in January 1502 and, by tradition, took it for a river mouth.

name: Guanaja
fact: Guanaja is the easternmost of Honduras's Bay Islands and was visited by Christopher Columbus in 1502.

name: Guanay cormorant
fact: The guanay cormorant of Peru eats anchovies from the Humboldt Current, and its droppings built the guano deposits that made 19th-century fortunes.

name: Guatemala
fact: Guatemala has a Pacific coast of dark volcanic sand backed by a chain of volcanoes.

name: Guatemala Trench
fact: The Guatemala Trench is the section of the Middle America Trench off the Pacific coast of Guatemala.

name: Guayaquil
fact: Guayaquil, on the Guayas River estuary, is Ecuador's largest city and its main port.

name: Guiana Current
fact: The Guiana Current flows north-west along the north-east coast of South America, carrying Amazon water and sediment.

name: Guiana dolphin
fact: The Guiana dolphin lives in estuaries and bays along the Atlantic coast of South and Central America and can sense electric fields with its snout.

name: Guided missile cruiser
fact: A guided missile cruiser is a modern large warship built around missile systems for air defence and attack, such as the American Ticonderoga class.

name: Guinea
fact: Guinea's capital, Conakry, sits on the Atlantic coast, and the Niger, Senegal and Gambia rivers all rise in its highlands.

name: Guinea-Bissau
fact: Guinea-Bissau's Atlantic coast includes the Bijagós Archipelago, which has more than 80 islands.

name: Guinea Current
fact: The Guinea Current flows eastward along the coast of West Africa into the Gulf of Guinea.

name: Guineafowl puffer
fact: The guineafowl puffer is black with tiny white spots like the bird, and some individuals are entirely golden-yellow instead.

name: Guitarfish
fact: Guitarfish are rays shaped like a guitar, with a flattened shark-like body, and they give birth to live young.

name: Gulf corvina
fact: Gulf corvinas gather by the million in the Colorado River delta to spawn, and their chorus is loud enough to damage the hearing of nearby dolphins.

name: Gulf flounder
fact: The gulf flounder lives on sandy and muddy seabeds from the Carolinas to the Gulf of Mexico.

name: Gulf menhaden
fact: The Gulf menhaden is the biggest fishery by weight in the Gulf of Mexico and the main food of its pelicans, dolphins and redfish.

name: Gulf of Alaska
fact: The Gulf of Alaska is a wide arm of the Pacific along Alaska's southern coast where glaciers meet the sea and ferocious winter storms are born.

name: Gulf of Antalya
fact: The Gulf of Antalya on Turkey's southern coast is a wide bay of the Levantine Sea backed by the Taurus Mountains.

name: Gulf of Bothnia
fact: The Gulf of Bothnia, the northern arm of the Baltic, is so fresh and cold that it is largely frozen for months each winter.

name: Gulf of Cádiz
fact: The Gulf of Cádiz lies off south-west Spain and Portugal just outside the Strait of Gibraltar, where salty Mediterranean water pours out into the Atlantic.

name: Gulf of California
fact: The Gulf of California, also called the Sea of Cortez after the conquistador Hernán Cortés, separates Baja California from mainland Mexico and is home to the vaquita.

name: Gulf of Carpentaria
fact: The Gulf of Carpentaria in northern Australia is named after Pieter de Carpentier, a governor-general of the Dutch East Indies, and hosts the Morning Glory cloud.

name: Gulf of Corinth
fact: The Gulf of Corinth nearly cuts the Peloponnese off from mainland Greece, and the Corinth Canal, finished in 1893, links it to the Saronic Gulf.

name: Gulf of Finland
fact: The Gulf of Finland is the easternmost arm of the Baltic Sea, with St Petersburg at its head and Helsinki and Tallinn on its shores.

name: Gulf of Gabès
fact: The Gulf of Gabès off Tunisia has the largest tides in the Mediterranean, up to about 2 metres, in a sea where tides are usually tiny.

name: Gulf of Gaeta
fact: The Gulf of Gaeta is a gulf of the Tyrrhenian Sea in central Italy, with the town of Gaeta on its shore.

name: Gulf of Genoa
fact: The Gulf of Genoa is the northernmost part of the Ligurian Sea, with the port of Genoa, birthplace of Christopher Columbus, at its head.

name: Gulf of Gokova
fact: The Gulf of Gokova is a long, sheltered gulf on Turkey's south-west coast, popular for sailing and protected as a marine area.

name: Gulf of Guayaquil
fact: The Gulf of Guayaquil is a large gulf on the Pacific coast of South America, shared by Ecuador and Peru.

name: Gulf of Guinea
fact: The Gulf of Guinea is the great bend of the African coast where the equator and the prime meridian cross in open water.

name: Gulf of Hammamet
fact: The Gulf of Hammamet is a bay on Tunisia's east coast lined with beach resorts.

name: Gulf of Honduras
fact: The Gulf of Honduras is a Caribbean inlet bordered by Belize, Guatemala and Honduras at the southern end of the Mesoamerican Reef.

name: Gulf of İskenderun
fact: The Gulf of İskenderun in the far north-east corner of the Mediterranean is where the Turkish coast turns south towards Syria, near the ancient battlefield of Issus.

name: Gulf of Izmir
fact: The Gulf of Izmir is a long inlet of the Aegean on Turkey's coast, with the city of Izmir at its head.

name: Gulf of La Spezia
fact: The Gulf of La Spezia is a deep natural harbour on the Ligurian coast, nicknamed the Gulf of Poets.

name: Gulf of Lion
fact: The Gulf of Lion on the south coast of France is swept by the mistral wind and receives the waters of the Rhône.

name: Gulf of Maine
fact: The Gulf of Maine is one of the fastest-warming bodies of water in the world and borders the famous Georges Bank fishing grounds.

name: Gulf of Manfredonia
fact: The Gulf of Manfredonia is a gulf of the Adriatic on the south side of the Gargano peninsula in Italy.

name: Gulf of Maracaibo
fact: The Gulf of Maracaibo is a Caribbean inlet of Venezuela that connects with Lake Maracaibo, and the region is rich in oil.

name: Gulf of Mexico
fact: The Gulf of Mexico is an ocean basin of the Atlantic almost encircled by Mexico, Cuba and the United States, and the Mississippi River drains into it.

name: Gulf of Naples
fact: The Gulf of Naples is overlooked by Mount Vesuvius, whose eruption in AD 79 buried Pompeii, and holds the islands of Capri and Ischia.

name: Gulf of Nicoya
fact: The Gulf of Nicoya is a large gulf on the Pacific coast of Costa Rica, fringed with mangroves.

name: Gulf of Orosei
fact: The Gulf of Orosei on the east coast of Sardinia is lined with limestone cliffs and hidden coves.

name: Gulf of Palermo
fact: The Gulf of Palermo is the bay on Sicily's north coast in which the island's capital sits.

name: Gulf of Panama
fact: The Gulf of Panama is the Pacific entrance to the Panama Canal and has some of the largest tides in the tropics, unlike the tiny tides on the Caribbean side.

name: Gulf of Paria
fact: The Gulf of Paria is a shallow inlet between Trinidad and Venezuela, fed by the muddy waters of the Orinoco delta.

name: Gulf of Patras
fact: The Gulf of Patras in western Greece opens to the Ionian Sea, and the port of Patras sits on its shore.

name: Gulf of Riga
fact: The Gulf of Riga is a bay of the Baltic Sea enclosed by Latvia and Estonia and nearly cut off from the open sea by the island of Saaremaa.

name: Gulf of Salerno
fact: The Gulf of Salerno, south of the Amalfi Coast, was where Allied troops landed in Italy in September 1943.

name: Gulf of San Jorge
fact: The Gulf of San Jorge is a wide bay on the Patagonian coast of Argentina, open to the South Atlantic.

name: Gulf of Sidra
fact: The Gulf of Sidra on the coast of Libya was claimed by Gaddafi as Libyan waters behind a Line of Death, leading to clashes with the US Navy in the 1980s.

name: Gulf of St Lawrence
fact: The Gulf of St Lawrence, where the St Lawrence River meets the Atlantic, is one of the largest estuarine systems in the world, and ice covers the whole gulf in January and February.

name: Gulf of Taranto
fact: The Gulf of Taranto is the large bay in the instep of Italy's boot, opening onto the Ionian Sea.

name: Gulf of Tehuantepec
fact: The Gulf of Tehuantepec off southern Mexico is famous for violent gap winds that blast through the mountains and far out to sea.

name: Gulf of Thailand
fact: The Gulf of Thailand is a shallow inlet of the South China Sea, bordered by Thailand, Cambodia, Vietnam and Malaysia.

name: Gulf of Tonkin
fact: The Gulf of Tonkin, between northern Vietnam and China, holds Halong Bay and gave its name to the 1964 incident that drew the United States deeper into the Vietnam War.

name: Gulf of Trieste
fact: The Gulf of Trieste is the northernmost point of the Adriatic and of the whole Mediterranean, shared by Italy, Slovenia and Croatia.

name: Gulf of Tunis
fact: The Gulf of Tunis is a bay of the Mediterranean on which the ruins of ancient Carthage stand, near the modern city of Tunis.

name: Gulf of Valencia
fact: The Gulf of Valencia is a broad gulf on Spain's east coast, with the city of Valencia on its shore.

name: Gulf of Venezuela
fact: The Gulf of Venezuela opens off the Caribbean and connects through a narrow channel to Lake Maracaibo, one of the world's oldest oil regions.

name: Gulf of Venice
fact: The Gulf of Venice is the northern end of the Adriatic Sea, so shallow that Venice floods whenever strong winds push water into it.

name: Gulf Stream
fact: The Gulf Stream carries warm water from the Gulf of Mexico up the US east coast and across the Atlantic, keeping north-west Europe far milder than its latitude suggests.

name: Gulf sturgeon
fact: The Gulf sturgeon spends summers in rivers such as the Suwannee and winters in the Gulf of Mexico, and leaping fish have injured boaters.

name: Gull
fact: Gulls are the ocean's opportunists, snatching fish from the surface, raiding fishing boats and stealing catches from other seabirds.

name: Gulper eel
fact: The gulper eel's mouth is bigger than the rest of its body, and it can balloon out like a pelican's pouch to swallow prey larger than itself.

name: Gulper shark
fact: Gulper sharks live on deep slopes and have only one or two pups every couple of years, so their populations collapse quickly under fishing.

name: Gumboot chiton
fact: The gumboot chiton is the largest chiton in the world, a reddish-brown lump up to about 36 centimetres long nicknamed the wandering meatloaf.

name: Gunboat
fact: A gunboat is a small armed vessel built to carry heavy guns, and it was used for centuries to patrol rivers and coasts.

name: Gunther Lutjens
fact: Gunther Lutjens commanded the German fleet in Operation Rheinubung and died when the Bismarck sank in 1941.

name: Gunwale
fact: The gunwale, pronounced gunnel, is the upper edge of the side of a boat.

name: Guppy
fact: The guppy, the classic beginner's aquarium fish, now lives wild on every continent except Antarctica after releases to control mosquitoes.

name: Gurnard
fact: Gurnards grunt and growl by vibrating their swim bladder, which gave the fish its name from an old French word for grunting.

name: Gutweed
fact: Gutweed is a bright green, tube-shaped seaweed of upper shores and estuaries, named for its hollow, gut-like fronds.

name: Guyana
fact: Guyana's low, flat Atlantic coast is where most of its people live, many of them below sea level.

name: Gwadar
fact: Gwadar in Pakistan's Balochistan province is a deep-sea port on the Arabian Sea developed with Chinese investment.

name: Gymnarchus
fact: Gymnarchus, an African freshwater fish, makes weak electric pulses and senses their distortion to find its way and prey in murky water.

name: Gymnote
fact: The Gymnote was an experimental electric submarine launched in France in 1888.

name: Gyrocompass
fact: A gyrocompass uses a fast-spinning gyroscope to find true north, so it is not thrown off by a ship's metal or magnetic fields.

name: Haddock
fact: Haddock, with a black 'thumbprint' behind the gill, is the favourite fish-and-chips fish in Scotland and northern England and is smoked as finnan haddie.

name: Hafgufa
fact: The hafgufa is a gigantic sea monster described in the Old Norse King's Mirror, so huge that sailors might mistake it for an island.

name: Hagfish
fact: A hagfish can turn a bucket of water into slime in seconds, ties itself in a knot to wipe it off, and feeds on carcasses thousands of metres down.

name: Haida Gwaii
fact: Haida Gwaii is an archipelago off the coast of British Columbia, the homeland of the Haida people.

name: Haifa
fact: Haifa is Israel's largest port and home to the terraced Bahai Gardens, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

name: Hainosaurus
fact: Hainosaurus was a giant mosasaur of the Late Cretaceous, named after the Hainaut region of Belgium where its fossils were found.

name: Hairy vent snail
fact: Alviniconcha vent snails have bristly shells and gills packed with bacteria that feed them, so they barely need to eat.

name: Haiti
fact: Haiti occupies the western third of Hispaniola, with coasts on both the Atlantic Ocean and the Caribbean Sea.

name: Hakarl
fact: Hakarl is an Icelandic dish of Greenland shark, which is poisonous when fresh and is cured by fermenting and hanging to dry.

name: Hake
fact: Hake is a slim relative of cod and the favourite fish of Spain, which eats more of it than any other country.

name: Hakodate
fact: Hakodate in Hokkaido was among the first Japanese ports opened to foreign ships, in 1859.

name: Halfbeak
fact: Halfbeaks are slender surface fish with a long lower jaw; many species feed on seagrass and floating algae.

name: Halibut
fact: Halibut are the largest flatfish, and Atlantic halibut can grow to over 2 metres long and more than 300 kilograms.

name: Halifax
fact: Halifax, Nova Scotia, has one of the largest natural harbours in the world, and many of the Titanic's victims are buried in the city's cemeteries.

name: Halimeda
fact: Halimeda is a green seaweed built from chalky segments; its dead flakes make up much of the white sand on tropical beaches.

name: Halloween crab
fact: The Halloween crab is a black-and-orange land crab of Pacific Central America that returns to the sea to release its eggs.

name: Hallucigenia
fact: Hallucigenia, a spiny Cambrian worm from the Burgess Shale, was so strange that scientists first reconstructed it upside down.

name: Halong Bay
fact: Halong Bay in northern Vietnam is studded with about 1,600 limestone islands and is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

name: Paddle grass
fact: Paddle grass can grow in deeper, dimmer water than most seagrasses.

name: Halophila stipulacea
fact: Halophila stipulacea, native to the Red Sea and Indian Ocean, has spread to the Mediterranean and Caribbean.

name: Halosaur
fact: Halosaurs are long-tailed, eel-like fish of the deep seabed, swimming slowly over abyssal mud below 1,000 metres with a snout that overhangs the mouth.

name: Halyard
fact: A halyard is a rope used to hoist a sail or flag.

name: Hammer coral
fact: Hammer coral's tentacles end in hammer or anchor-shaped tips, and it sends out long sweeper tentacles to sting neighbouring corals.

name: Hammerhead shark
fact: A hammerhead's wide head spreads its eyes and electrical sensors across a broad span, helping it sweep the seabed for buried rays.

name: Hanauma Bay
fact: Hanauma Bay on Oahu is a flooded volcanic crater that became Hawaii's first marine life conservation district in 1967.

name: Hangzhou Bay
fact: Hangzhou Bay in eastern China produces the world's largest tidal bore, a wall of water that surges up the Qiantang River.

name: Hanno's voyage
fact: The Carthaginian Hanno led a fleet down the west coast of Africa, and a Greek version of his account survives as the Periplus of Hanno.

name: Hans Hass
fact: Hans Hass was an Austrian diving pioneer who made some of the first underwater films of sharks and manta rays in the 1940s and 1950s.

name: Hapuku
fact: The hapuku, or groper, is a large deep-water fish of New Zealand's rocky reefs and continental slope.

name: Harbo and Samuelsen's Atlantic row
fact: In 1896 George Harbo and Frank Samuelsen became the first people to row across the Atlantic, from New York to the Isles of Scilly, in about 55 days.

name: Harbour master
fact: A harbour master oversees the safe movement of vessels in a port and enforces its rules.

name: Harbour pilot
fact: A harbour pilot is a local expert who boards a ship to guide it safely into and out of port.

name: Harbour porpoise
fact: The harbour porpoise is the smallest cetacean in European waters and must feed almost constantly to stay warm.

name: Harbour seal
fact: Harbour seals are the most widespread pinniped, hauling out on coasts all around the Northern Hemisphere.

name: Hardhead catfish
fact: The hardhead catfish is a sea catfish of the Gulf of Mexico whose males carry the marble-sized eggs in their mouths for about two months.

name: Harlequin filefish
fact: The harlequin filefish eats only Acropora coral polyps and ends up smelling like the coral it eats, which hides it from predators that hunt by scent.

name: Harlequin rasbora
fact: The harlequin rasbora, with a black triangle on its side, lays its eggs on the underside of leaves in Malaysian and Thai streams.

name: Harlequin shrimp
fact: Harlequin shrimp hunt in pairs and eat only starfish, flipping their prey over and feeding on it alive for days.

name: Harlequin tuskfish
fact: The harlequin tuskfish has bright blue tusk-like teeth and orange bands, and uses the teeth to crush shellfish on Indo-Pacific reefs.

name: Harmony of the Seas
fact: Harmony of the Seas, which entered service in 2016, is the third of Royal Caribbean's Oasis-class cruise ships.

name: Harold Edgerton
fact: Harold Edgerton was an American engineer who perfected the electronic flash and worked with Jacques Cousteau on underwater photography and sonar.

name: Harp seal
fact: Harp seal pups are born on the sea ice with fluffy white coats, and the species was the focus of the famous Canadian seal hunt protests.

name: Harp sponge
fact: The harp sponge, found 3,300 metres down off California in 2012, is a carnivore: it snags tiny crustaceans on Velcro-like hooks along its harp-shaped branches.

name: Harpooner
fact: A harpooner threw the harpoon at a whale, and on a whaleship he was an officer in the whaleboat crew.

name: Hatchetfish
fact: Hatchetfish are silver, blade-thin fish with photophores on their bellies that match the faint light from above, making them invisible from below.

name: Hauraki Gulf
fact: The Hauraki Gulf is the island-studded gulf beside Auckland in New Zealand, and home to Bryde's whales.

name: Haus des Meeres
fact: Haus des Meeres in Vienna is an aquarium and terrarium housed in a Second World War anti-aircraft flak tower.

name: Havana
fact: Havana's sheltered harbour on the Straits of Florida was the gathering point for Spain's treasure fleets before they crossed the Atlantic.

name: Hawaii
fact: The Hawaiian Islands are the tops of volcanoes built over a hotspot, and Mauna Kea is the tallest mountain on Earth measured from its base on the sea floor.

name: Hawaiian bobtail squid
fact: The Hawaiian bobtail squid hosts glowing bacteria in a special organ that lets it hide its shadow from predators on moonlit nights.

name: Hawaiian-Emperor seamount chain
fact: The Hawaiian-Emperor seamount chain is a line of drowned volcanoes stretching about 6,000 kilometres across the Pacific, built as the plate moved over a hotspot.

name: Hawaiian monk seal
fact: The Hawaiian monk seal is one of the rarest seals, with only around 1,500 left, and its Hawaiian name means 'dog that runs in rough water'.

name: Hawke Bay
fact: Hawke Bay is a wide bay on the east coast of New Zealand's North Island, with Napier on its shore.

name: Hawkfish
fact: Hawkfish perch on coral heads using their thick pectoral fins, watching for prey like a hawk before darting out to grab it.

name: Hawksbill turtle
fact: Hawksbill turtles eat sea sponges that are toxic to most animals, and their patterned shells were the source of 'tortoiseshell'.

name: Hawkwing conch
fact: The hawkwing conch is a small Caribbean conch whose shell lip flares out like a wing.

name: Hawser
fact: A hawser is a thick rope or cable used for mooring or towing a ship.

name: Hayreddin Barbarossa
fact: Hayreddin Barbarossa was an Ottoman corsair who became the sultan's grand admiral and won the Battle of Preveza in 1538.

name: Headless chicken monster
fact: The headless chicken monster is a translucent pink sea cucumber that swims with a webbed collar and sheds a sticky glowing skin onto anything that touches it.

name: Heard Island
fact: Heard Island is a glaciated Australian sub-Antarctic island with an active volcano, Big Ben, the highest mountain in Australian territory.

name: Heart urchin
fact: The heart urchin, or sea potato, is a burrowing urchin with a heart-shaped shell that lives hidden in sand below the low-tide mark.

name: Heaviside's dolphin
fact: Heaviside's dolphin, found only off Namibia and South Africa, is named after the wrong man: its specimen came from a Captain Haviside, but was credited to a surgeon called Heaviside.

name: Heavy cruiser
fact: A heavy cruiser was defined by the 1922 Washington Naval Treaty as a cruiser with guns of more than six inches.

name: Hebrides
fact: The Hebrides off Scotland's west coast include Skye, Mull, Lewis and Harris, and the tiny island of Staffa with its basalt Fingal's Cave.

name: Heceta Head Lighthouse
fact: Heceta Head Lighthouse sits on a headland on the Oregon coast and was first lit in 1894.

name: Hector's beaked whale
fact: Hector's beaked whale is a small, rarely seen Southern Hemisphere beaked whale named after James Hector, a New Zealand scientist.

name: Hector's dolphin
fact: Hector's dolphin of New Zealand is one of the smallest dolphins, about 1.4 metres long, with a rounded dorsal fin like a Mickey Mouse ear.

name: Hedgehog seahorse
fact: The hedgehog seahorse is a spiny Indo-Pacific species that lives on sandy and muddy bottoms, often beside sponges, and is caught in trawls.

name: HELCOM
fact: HELCOM is the governing body of the Helsinki Convention, which protects the marine environment of the Baltic Sea.

name: Helicoprion
fact: Helicoprion was a shark relative with a spiral 'buzzsaw' of teeth in its lower jaw that puzzled scientists for more than a century.

name: Helicopter carrier
fact: A helicopter carrier is a ship designed to operate helicopters from its deck, and many are also used to land troops.

name: Heligoland
fact: Heligoland is a small red-sandstone German island in the North Sea.

name: Hellenic Trench
fact: The Hellenic Trench, curving south of Greece and Crete, contains the Calypso Deep, the deepest point in the Mediterranean at about 5,100 metres.

name: Helm
fact: The helm is the steering gear of a ship, meaning its wheel or tiller.

name: Helmet jellyfish
fact: The helmet jellyfish lives in deep water and in dark Norwegian fjords, where it has multiplied so much that it has displaced the fish.

name: Helmsman
fact: A helmsman is the sailor who steers the ship.

name: Henry Every
fact: Henry Every captured the Mughal treasure ship Ganj-i-Sawai in 1695, in one of the richest pirate hauls ever.

name: Henry Hudson
fact: Henry Hudson explored the river, strait and bay that now bear his name while seeking a northern route to Asia, and was cast adrift by his crew in 1611.

name: Henry Jennings
fact: Henry Jennings was a Jamaican privateer turned pirate who raided the camp of Spanish salvors working the wrecked 1715 treasure fleet.

name: Henry Morgan
fact: Henry Morgan was a Welsh privateer who sacked Panama in 1671 and later became lieutenant governor of Jamaica.

name: Heraklion
fact: Heraklion is the largest city on Crete and is guarded by a Venetian sea fortress called Koules.

name: Herbert Nitsch
fact: Herbert Nitsch, the deepest man on Earth, free-dived to 214 metres on a single breath in 2007.

name: Hermit crab
fact: Hermit crabs have soft abdomens and move into empty snail shells, swapping for larger ones as they grow.

name: Heron
fact: Herons stalk the shallows of estuaries and mangrove channels, striking fish with a lightning jab of their dagger-like bill.

name: Herring
fact: Herring feed on copepods and krill in schools of millions, and communicate at night with bursts of bubbles from their vents.

name: Hesperornis
fact: Hesperornis was a flightless, toothed seabird of the Cretaceous that swam with powerful legs.

name: Heteropod
fact: Heteropods are swimming sea snails whose glassy transparent bodies are almost invisible in open water.

name: High Seas Treaty
aliases: Agreement on Biodiversity Beyond National Jurisdiction
fact: The High Seas Treaty, adopted at the United Nations in 2023, provides for protecting marine life in waters beyond any country's control.

name: Hijiki
fact: Hijiki is a brown seaweed eaten in Japan, usually dried and black; it is known for holding unusually high levels of arsenic.

name: Hikurangi Trench
fact: The Hikurangi Trench off the east coast of New Zealand's North Island is where the Pacific Plate dives beneath the Australian Plate.

name: Hilsa
fact: The hilsa is a shad that lives in the Bay of Bengal and swims up the Ganges and other rivers to spawn, and it is the national fish of Bangladesh.

name: Himono
fact: Himono is Japanese fish that is split, salted and dried, usually in the open air, before being grilled.

name: Hirondellea gigas
fact: Hirondellea gigas amphipods swarm at the bottom of the Challenger Deep and make enzymes that digest sunken wood and plant debris.

name: Hispaniola
fact: Hispaniola is shared by Haiti and the Dominican Republic and is the second-largest island in the Caribbean.

name: Hjort Trench
fact: The Hjort Trench south of New Zealand and Macquarie Island is one of the southernmost trenches in the world, reaching about 6,700 metres.

name: H. L. Hunley
fact: The Confederate submarine H. L. Hunley sank in 1864 shortly after becoming the first submarine to sink an enemy warship.

name: HMAS Sydney
fact: HMAS Sydney was lost with all 645 crew after a battle with the German raider Kormoran in 1941, and was found in 2008 about 2,500 metres down off Western Australia.

name: HMS Affray
fact: HMS Affray was lost in the English Channel in 1951 with all 75 men aboard, the last Royal Navy submarine lost at sea.

name: HMS Beagle
fact: HMS Beagle carried the young Charles Darwin on a five-year surveying voyage around the world from 1831 to 1836 that led to his theory of evolution.

name: Bounty
fact: After the famous mutiny, the Bounty was burned and sunk by the mutineers at Pitcairn Island in 1790.

name: HMS Challenger
fact: HMS Challenger sailed around the world from 1872 to 1876 on the first great oceanographic expedition, sounding the deep that now bears its name.

name: HMS Conqueror
fact: HMS Conqueror sank the Argentine cruiser General Belgrano in 1982, the only time a nuclear-powered submarine has sunk a ship in wartime.

name: HMS Erebus
fact: HMS Erebus, one of the ships of Franklin's lost Arctic expedition, sank in the Canadian Arctic and was found in shallow water in 2014.

name: HMS Holland 1
fact: HMS Holland 1 was the Royal Navy's first submarine, launched in 1901, and it is now preserved at the Royal Navy Submarine Museum.

name: HMS Hood
fact: HMS Hood blew up and sank in three minutes after a hit from the Bismarck in 1941, with only 3 of 1,418 men surviving; the wreck lies about 2,800 metres down.

name: HMS Prince of Wales
fact: The battleship HMS Prince of Wales was sunk by Japanese aircraft off Malaya in December 1941, days after the attack on Pearl Harbor.

name: HMS Repulse
fact: The battlecruiser HMS Repulse was sunk by Japanese aircraft off Malaya in December 1941, along with HMS Prince of Wales.

name: HMS Royal Oak
fact: The battleship HMS Royal Oak was torpedoed by a U-boat at Scapa Flow in 1939, and her wreck is now a protected war grave.

name: HMS Terror
fact: HMS Terror, Franklin's second ship, was found almost intact in 2016 in Terror Bay, off King William Island in the Canadian Arctic.

name: HMS Thetis
fact: HMS Thetis sank in Liverpool Bay during trials in 1939 with the loss of 99 lives, was raised and later served as HMS Thunderbolt.

name: Hoff crab
fact: The Hoff crab, named for its hairy chest after actor David Hasselhoff, crowds by the thousand onto hot vent chimneys on the Antarctic East Scotia Ridge.

name: Hogchoker
fact: The hogchoker is a small American sole that swims up rivers and got its name because pigs fed on the rough-skinned fish supposedly choked on them.

name: Hogfish
fact: The hogfish of the western Atlantic roots in sand with its long pig-like snout and is prized by spearfishers for its taste.

name: Hoki
fact: Hoki is a deep-water cod relative of New Zealand's biggest fishery, and ends up in fish fingers and fast-food fish sandwiches.

name: Hokule'a voyage to Tahiti
fact: In 1976 the double-hulled canoe Hokule'a sailed from Hawaii to Tahiti using traditional navigation without instruments.

name: Honduras
fact: Honduras has a short Pacific coast of about 150 kilometres on the Gulf of Fonseca, though most of its coast faces the Caribbean.

name: Honeycomb coral
fact: Honeycomb corals form rounded colonies whose polyps share thin walls, giving a honeycomb pattern.

name: Honeycomb cowfish
fact: The honeycomb cowfish of Caribbean reefs has two horns over its eyes and a boxy body patterned like a honeycomb.

name: Honeycomb moray
fact: The honeycomb moray, or laced moray, is a large white moray covered in black honeycomb spots, common on Indo-Pacific reefs.

name: Honeycomb stingray
fact: The honeycomb stingray has a tail up to three times its body length and a net-like pattern on its back.

name: Honeycomb worm
fact: The honeycomb worm builds reefs from sand grains cemented into honeycomb-like tubes.

name: Honiara
fact: Honiara on Guadalcanal is the capital of the Solomon Islands and was the site of fierce fighting in the 1942 Guadalcanal campaign.

name: Honolua Bay
fact: Honolua Bay on Maui is a right-hand point break inside a marine life conservation district.

name: Honolulu
fact: Honolulu on Oahu is the main harbour of the Hawaiian Islands and lies close to Pearl Harbor.

name: Hooded nudibranch
fact: The hooded nudibranch spreads a large, fringed hood like a net to trap small crustaceans drifting past.

name: Hooded seal
fact: Male hooded seals inflate a bright red nasal balloon from one nostril to impress rivals, and pups are weaned in only four days.

name: Hook Lighthouse
fact: Hook Lighthouse in County Wexford, Ireland, dates from the 13th century and is often described as the oldest operating lighthouse in the world.

name: Ho'okipa
fact: Ho'okipa on Maui's north shore is both a surfing break and one of the world's best-known windsurfing beaches.

name: Hopkins' rose nudibranch
fact: Hopkins' rose is a bright pink, fuzzy-looking sea slug of the Pacific coast of North America that feeds on bryozoans.

name: Horatio Hornblower
fact: Horatio Hornblower is C. S. Forester's naval hero, who first appeared in a 1937 novel and was later played by Ioan Gruffudd in a 1998 television series.

name: Horatio Nelson
fact: Horatio Nelson won the Battle of Trafalgar in 1805 and was killed by a French sniper's bullet during the fighting.

name: Horn shark
fact: The horn shark has a sharp spine in front of each dorsal fin and crushes sea urchins and molluscs with flat, molar-like back teeth.

name: Horned puffin
fact: The horned puffin of the North Pacific has a small fleshy 'horn' above each eye and catches small fish underwater.

name: Horned sea snake
fact: The horned sea snake has small spines over its eyes and is the only sea snake with spiny scales on its head.

name: Hornwrack
fact: Hornwrack is a bryozoan that forms leaf-like colonies, often washed ashore, with a faint lemon scent.

name: Horse mackerel
fact: Horse mackerel, or scad, are not true mackerel but jacks with a row of bony scales along the lateral line, and they school in vast numbers.

name: Horse mussel
fact: Horse mussels form dense beds in cold northern seas that shelter many other animals.

name: Horsehair crab
fact: The horsehair crab of Hokkaido is covered in short bristles and is prized in Japan for its sweet meat and rich crab liver.

name: Horseshoe crab
fact: Horseshoe crabs have blue, copper-based blood that is harvested to test medicines and vaccines for bacterial contamination.

name: Hossegor
fact: Hossegor in south-west France is known for powerful sand-bottomed barrels at La Graviere and has long hosted a world tour contest.

name: Hot smoking
fact: Hot smoking cooks fish at higher temperatures while smoking it, as with the Scottish Arbroath smokie.

name: Houndfish
fact: The houndfish is a 1.5-metre needlefish that leaps from the water at speed and has impaled fishermen with its beak.

name: Hourglass dolphin
fact: The hourglass dolphin is the only small dolphin found regularly in Antarctic waters, and its bold black-and-white pattern gives it its name.

name: Houston Ship Channel
fact: The Houston Ship Channel in Texas runs inland for roughly 80 kilometres and serves one of the busiest ports in the United States.

name: Howell Davis
fact: Howell Davis was a Welsh pirate who captured ships off West Africa by trickery, and Bartholomew Roberts took over his crew after he died in 1719.

name: Hubbs' beaked whale
fact: Hubbs' beaked whale is known mostly from strandings on the US west coast and Japan, and males carry a white cap on their heads.

name: Huchen
fact: The huchen, or Danube salmon, is a giant trout relative of the Danube basin that can grow to more than a metre long and never goes to sea.

name: Hudson Bay
fact: Hudson Bay is a vast inland sea in Canada named after the English explorer Henry Hudson, who was set adrift there by mutineers in 1611 and never seen again.

name: Hudson Canyon
fact: Hudson Canyon is the largest submarine canyon on the US Atlantic coast, continuing the course of the Hudson River across the seabed off New York.

name: Hudson Strait
fact: Hudson Strait links Hudson Bay to the Labrador Sea and the Atlantic and is named after the English explorer Henry Hudson.

name: Henry Hudson's last voyage
fact: In 1610 Henry Hudson sailed into what is now Hudson Bay, and after a mutiny in 1611 his crew set him adrift in a small boat.

name: Hull
fact: The hull is the main body of a ship, the shell that keeps it afloat.

name: Humboldt Current
fact: The Humboldt Current carries cold, nutrient-rich water north along the coast of Chile and Peru, feeding the world's largest anchovy fishery.

name: Humboldt penguin
fact: The Humboldt penguin lives along the cold Humboldt Current coasts of Peru and Chile and hunts anchovies and sardines.

name: Humboldt squid
fact: Humboldt squid hunt in packs of hundreds and flash red and white across their skin, earning the nickname 'red devil' from fishermen.

name: Humbug dascyllus
fact: The humbug dascyllus is a small black-and-white banded damselfish that lives in tight groups inside branching Acropora corals.

name: Humpback anglerfish
fact: The humpback anglerfish is the classic toothy black seadevil of the deep; females reach about 15 centimetres while the males are only around 2 centimetres long.

name: Humpback dolphin
fact: Humpback dolphins live in shallow coastal waters and estuaries and have a distinctive hump beneath the dorsal fin.

name: Humpback grouper
fact: The humpback grouper, or panther grouper, is a polka-dotted, small-headed grouper that swims head-down and is farmed as a luxury fish in Asia.

name: Humpback red snapper
fact: The humpback red snapper is a snapper with a forked tail and a hump on its forehead, found in groups on Indo-Pacific reefs.

name: Humpback whale
fact: Male humpbacks sing long, complex songs, and the scientific name Megaptera novaeangliae means 'big-winged New Englander'.

name: The Hunt for Red October
fact: The Hunt for Red October is Tom Clancy's 1984 novel, filmed by John McTiernan in 1990, about a Soviet submarine captain who may be defecting.

name: Huntington Beach
fact: Huntington Beach in California calls itself Surf City USA and hosts the annual US Open of Surfing beside its pier.

name: Hurricane
fact: Hurricanes are intense tropical storms that gather energy from warm ocean water, and they are called typhoons in the western Pacific.

name: Hvar
fact: Hvar is a Croatian island in the Adriatic Sea known for its lavender fields and sunshine.

name: Hyams Beach
fact: Hyams Beach in Jervis Bay, New South Wales, is famed for sand so white and fine that it squeaks underfoot.

name: Hybodus
fact: Hybodus was an early shark relative of Triassic to Cretaceous seas that carried a spine in front of each dorsal fin.

name: Green-lined paper bubble
fact: The green-lined paper bubble is a sea slug with a thin, delicate bubble-like shell marked with fine green lines.

name: Hydra
fact: Hydra is a Greek island in the Saronic Gulf where cars are largely banned and donkeys and boats are the main transport.

name: Hydractinia
fact: Hydractinia is a colonial hydroid that coats hermit crab shells in a fuzzy fur and helps defend the crab.

name: Hydrographer
fact: Hydrographers survey and map the seabed and coasts so that nautical charts are accurate.

name: Hydroid
fact: Hydroids are plant-like colonies of stinging polyps, the attached stage of many jellyfish, and have been dredged from more than 8,200 metres in the Kermadec Trench.

name: Hydrophone
fact: A hydrophone is an underwater microphone used to record whales, ships and other sounds in the sea.

name: Hyman Rickover
fact: Hyman Rickover drove the development of nuclear-powered ships and is known as the father of the nuclear navy.

name: Bullock's nudibranch
fact: Bullock's nudibranch is a purple Indo-Pacific sea slug with orange gills that feeds on sponges.

name: I-400
fact: The Japanese I-400 submarines were the largest built before nuclear boats, and each carried three folding seaplanes in a hangar.

name: Ibiza
fact: Ibiza is a Balearic island famed for its clubs, and its old walled town, Dalt Vila, is a World Heritage Site.

name: Ibo Island
fact: Ibo Island lies in Mozambique's Quirimbas Archipelago and has an old Portuguese fort and a tradition of silverwork.

name: Icarian Sea
fact: The Icarian Sea is the part of the Aegean around the island of Icaria, where in legend Icarus fell into the sea after flying too close to the sun.

name: ICCAT
aliases: International Commission for the Conservation of Atlantic Tunas
fact: ICCAT is the commission formed in 1969 to manage tuna and tuna-like fish in the Atlantic Ocean.

name: Icebreaker
fact: An icebreaker is a ship with a strengthened hull that smashes a channel through sea ice.

name: Iceland
fact: Iceland sits astride the Mid-Atlantic Ridge, where the North American and Eurasian plates pull apart, which is why it is so volcanic.

name: Iceland catshark
fact: The Iceland catshark is a pale, slender shark of the North Atlantic that lives on deep slopes far below the reach of sunlight.

name: Ichthyosaur
fact: Ichthyosaurs were dolphin-shaped reptiles that gave birth to live young at sea, and Mary Anning found the first complete skeleton in 1811.

name: Icon of the Seas
fact: Icon of the Seas entered service in 2024 as the world's largest cruise ship by gross tonnage.

name: Ictineo II
fact: Ictineo II was an early Spanish submarine designed by Narcis Monturiol and launched in 1864.

name: Ifremeria snail
fact: Ifremeria snails cluster in dense beds at western Pacific vents and brood their young inside a pouch in the foot.

name: Ijima's sea snake
fact: Ijima's turtle-headed sea snake feeds on fish eggs and lives around reefs of the Ryukyu Islands and Taiwan.

name: Immortal jellyfish
fact: The immortal jellyfish can turn its adult body back into a juvenile polyp when injured or starving, restarting its life cycle indefinitely.

name: Imperial shag
fact: The imperial shag, with a blue ring around its eye, nests on Antarctic and subantarctic coasts and dives for fish.

name: In the Heart of the Sea
fact: In the Heart of the Sea is Nathaniel Philbrick's 2000 book about the whaleship Essex, sunk by a sperm whale in 1820, and Ron Howard filmed it in 2015.

name: Inanga
fact: The inanga of New Zealand and Australia lays its eggs on grasses flooded by spring tides, and the larvae are swept out to sea before returning as whitebait.

name: Inca tern
fact: The Inca tern of the Humboldt Current coast of Peru and Chile sports a dashing white moustache and snatches anchovies from the surface.

name: India
fact: India has a coastline of more than 7,000 kilometres on the Arabian Sea, the Bay of Bengal and the Indian Ocean itself.

name: Indian mackerel
fact: The Indian mackerel is the everyday fish of South and Southeast Asia, caught in huge numbers and fried, curried or dried.

name: Indian Ocean Dipole
fact: The Indian Ocean Dipole is a swing in sea surface temperatures between the western and eastern Indian Ocean that affects rainfall around it.

name: Indian Ocean humpback dolphin
fact: The Indian Ocean humpback dolphin has a pronounced hump under its dorsal fin and lives in estuaries and shallow coasts from South Africa to India.

name: Indian oil sardine
fact: The Indian oil sardine is the most important fish of India's west coast, caught by the hundreds of thousands of tonnes in the monsoon season.

name: Indo-Pacific beaked whale
fact: The Indo-Pacific beaked whale was known for decades only from two skulls and is still one of the rarest large whales.

name: Indo-Pacific bottlenose dolphin
fact: Indo-Pacific bottlenose dolphins in Shark Bay, Australia, carry sponges on their beaks as tools to protect them while foraging on the seabed.

name: Indo-Pacific finless porpoise
fact: The Indo-Pacific finless porpoise lives in estuaries and shallow coasts from the Persian Gulf to the Taiwan Strait, including the Pearl River estuary.

name: Indo-Pacific humpback dolphin
fact: Chinese white dolphins of the Pearl River estuary are actually pink as adults, and Hong Kong adopted them as its 1997 handover mascot.

name: Indo-Pacific king mackerel
fact: The Indo-Pacific king mackerel is a large, fast mackerel of the Indian Ocean and western Pacific and an important food fish.

name: Indo-Pacific tarpon
fact: The Indo-Pacific tarpon gulps air at the surface, which lets it live in low-oxygen mangrove pools and ponds.

name: Indonesia
fact: Indonesia is an archipelago of about 17,000 islands with coasts on both the Pacific and Indian oceans.

name: Indonesian Throughflow
fact: The Indonesian Throughflow carries warm water from the Pacific into the Indian Ocean through the seas of Indonesia.

name: Indus river dolphin
fact: The Indus river dolphin often swims on its side in the shallow, muddy Indus and was long trapped between irrigation barrages.

name: INS Dakar
fact: The Israeli submarine Dakar vanished in 1968 and was found in 1999 about 2,900 metres down between Crete and Cyprus.

name: Internal wave
fact: Internal waves travel along boundaries between layers of different density deep within the ocean, and they can be hundreds of metres high.

name: International Seabed Authority
fact: The International Seabed Authority, based in Kingston, Jamaica, regulates mineral activities on the seabed beyond national waters.

name: International Whaling Commission
fact: The International Whaling Commission was set up in 1946 and agreed a moratorium on commercial whaling that took effect in 1986.

name: Ionian Sea
fact: The Ionian Sea lies between southern Italy and western Greece and holds the deepest point in the Mediterranean, the Calypso Deep at about 5,100 metres.

name: Ipanema
fact: Ipanema Beach in Rio de Janeiro inspired the bossa nova song The Girl from Ipanema, written in 1962.

name: International Pacific Halibut Commission
fact: The International Pacific Halibut Commission, founded by the United States and Canada in 1923, manages halibut stocks in the north-eastern Pacific.

name: Iquique
fact: Iquique in northern Chile was the site of a naval battle on 21 May 1879 during the War of the Pacific.

name: Iran
fact: Iran has coasts on the Caspian Sea in the north and on the Persian Gulf and the Gulf of Oman in the south.

name: Iraq
fact: Iraq's coast on the Persian Gulf is only about 58 kilometres long, and its main port there is Umm Qasr.

name: Ireland
fact: Ireland is the second-largest island of the British Isles, and the Gulf Stream keeps its climate mild enough for subtropical gardens to thrive on its west coast.

name: Irish moss
fact: Irish moss, or carrageen, is a small red seaweed whose extract carrageenan thickens ice cream, toothpaste and plant milks.

name: Irish Sea
fact: The Irish Sea separates Ireland from Great Britain and opens to the Atlantic through the North Channel and St George's Channel.

name: Irminger Current
fact: The Irminger Current is a warm branch of the North Atlantic Drift that flows west past Iceland towards Greenland.

name: Ironclad
fact: Ironclads were steam warships protected by iron armour plates, and they appeared in the 1850s and 1860s.

name: Irrawaddy dolphin
fact: Irrawaddy dolphins in Myanmar herd fish towards fishermen's nets and are rewarded with part of the catch.

name: Irukandji jellyfish
fact: The Irukandji jellyfish is barely the size of a fingernail and transparent, yet its sting causes hours of agony, vomiting and a feeling of impending doom.

name: Ischia
fact: Ischia is a volcanic island in the Bay of Naples that is famous for its thermal springs.

name: Ise Bay
fact: Ise Bay is a large bay on the Pacific coast of Japan, with the port of Nagoya at its head.

name: Isla de la Juventud
fact: The Isla de la Juventud is Cuba's largest offshore island and was once called the Isle of Pines.

name: Isla Margarita
fact: Isla Margarita is Venezuela's largest island and was a centre of pearl fishing in the sixteenth century.

name: Isle of Man
fact: The Isle of Man sits in the Irish Sea between Britain and Ireland and is famous for its Tourist Trophy motorcycle races.

name: Isle of Wight
fact: The Isle of Wight lies off the south coast of England beside the Solent and is rich in dinosaur fossils.

name: Isles of Scilly
fact: The Isles of Scilly lie about 45 kilometres off Cornwall and are warmed by the Gulf Stream so that subtropical plants grow in their gardens.

name: Isopod
fact: Isopods, the group that includes woodlice, are found in every ocean habitat, including trench floors deeper than 6,000 metres.

name: Isoroku Yamamoto
fact: Isoroku Yamamoto planned the attack on Pearl Harbor and was killed in 1943 when American fighters shot down his aircraft.

name: Israel
fact: Israel has a Red Sea coast at Eilat as well as a Mediterranean coast.

name: Israel Hands
fact: Israel Hands was Blackbeard's gunner or captain who was shot in the knee by him in 1718, and Treasure Island borrowed his name.

name: Istanbul Aquarium
fact: Istanbul Aquarium in the Florya district opened in 2009 under the name Turkuazoo.

name: Ithaca
fact: Ithaca is the Ionian island usually identified as the home of Odysseus in Homer's epic.

name: Ivory Coast
fact: Ivory Coast has a coast on the Gulf of Guinea, where Abidjan is one of West Africa's major ports.

name: Ivory gull
fact: The ivory gull is a pure-white gull that lives year-round among Arctic pack ice and scavenges polar bear kills.

name: Ivory tree coral
fact: Ivory tree coral forms fragile branching thickets in deep water off Florida and is protected in the Oculina Banks reserve.

name: Iwo Jima
fact: Iwo Jima is a small volcanic island south of Japan where US Marines raised the flag on Mount Suribachi in 1945.

name: Izmir
fact: Izmir in Turkey was the ancient city of Smyrna and is one of the great Aegean ports.

name: Izu-Ogasawara Trench
fact: The Izu-Ogasawara Trench runs south from Japan to join the Mariana Trench and reaches more than 9,700 metres deep.

name: Jack Dempsey
fact: The Jack Dempsey cichlid from Central America was named after the boxer for its aggressive temper and strong-jawed face.

name: Jack mackerel
fact: The Pacific jack mackerel is a schooling jack, not a true mackerel, caught off California and Chile in enormous quantities.

name: Captain Jack Sparrow
fact: Captain Jack Sparrow is the fictional pirate of the Pirates of the Caribbean films, played by Johnny Depp.

name: Jack Ward
fact: Jack Ward was an English pirate who turned to the Barbary coast and became a leading corsair at Tunis in the early seventeenth century.

name: Jacksmelt
fact: The jacksmelt is a schooling silverside of the American Pacific coast that grows to about 40 centimetres.

name: Jacksonville
fact: Jacksonville in Florida sits on the St Johns River close to the Atlantic and has a major deepwater port and naval base.

name: Jacky Fisher
fact: Jacky Fisher was the First Sea Lord who drove the building of HMS Dreadnought in 1906 and modernised the Royal Navy.

name: Jacques Cartier
fact: Jacques Cartier was a French navigator who explored the Gulf of St Lawrence and sailed up the great river in the 1530s.

name: Jacques Cousteau
fact: Jacques Cousteau co-invented the Aqua-Lung in 1943, the first successful open-circuit scuba gear, and brought the undersea world to television aboard Calypso.

name: Jacques Mayol
fact: Jacques Mayol was the free diver who first dived below 100 metres on a single breath in 1976 and inspired the film The Big Blue.

name: Jacques Piccard
fact: Jacques Piccard and Don Walsh reached the bottom of the Challenger Deep in the bathyscaphe Trieste in 1960, the first humans ever to do so.

name: Jamaica
fact: Jamaica is the third-largest island of the Greater Antilles and the birthplace of reggae music.

name: James Bay
fact: James Bay, the southern arm of Hudson Bay, is named after Thomas James, the Welsh captain who wintered on its shore in 1631.

name: James Cameron
fact: The film director James Cameron made a solo dive to the bottom of the Challenger Deep in 2012 and has visited the Titanic wreck more than 30 times.

name: James Clark Ross
fact: James Clark Ross discovered the Ross Sea and Ross Ice Shelf in 1841 and made some of the first soundings of the deep ocean, reaching below 4,000 metres.

name: James Cook
fact: Captain James Cook charted more of the Pacific than any navigator before him, crossed the Antarctic Circle, and kept his crews free of scurvy on three great voyages.

name: Janolus cristatus
fact: Janolus cristatus is a sea slug with a bushy crest on its head that feeds on bryozoans.

name: Japan
fact: Japan is an archipelago of thousands of islands in the western Pacific, dominated by the four large islands of Honshu, Hokkaido, Kyushu and Shikoku.

name: Japan Trench
fact: The Japan Trench runs off north-east Honshu, and the 2011 Tōhoku earthquake that caused the Fukushima disaster ruptured along it.

name: Japan Trench snailfish
fact: The Japan Trench snailfish is a soft-bodied fish that lives in the Japan Trench at depths of more than 6,000 metres.

name: Japanese anchovy
fact: The Japanese anchovy is one of the largest catches in the northwest Pacific, eaten dried as niboshi and as tiny boiled whitebait, shirasu.

name: Japanese eel
fact: The Japanese eel, the unagi of Japanese cooking, spawns near the Mariana Islands and its young drift thousands of kilometres back to East Asian rivers.

name: Japanese eelgrass
fact: Japanese eelgrass is native to East Asia and has spread to the Pacific coast of North America.

name: Japanese flying squid
fact: The Japanese flying squid supports one of the biggest squid fisheries in the world and can glide briefly above the waves by jetting water.

name: Japanese horse mackerel
fact: Horse mackerel, aji, is one of the most common fish in Tokyo sushi bars, served raw with grated ginger and spring onion.

name: Japanese ivory shell
fact: The salivary glands of this edible sea snail contain surugatoxin, which caused outbreaks of poisoning in Japan in the 1960s.

name: Japanese pygmy seahorse
fact: The Japanese pygmy seahorse, nicknamed 'japapigu' or 'Japan pig', was known to local divers for years before being named as a new species in 2018.

name: Japanese sardine
fact: The Japanese sardine catch rose above 4 million tonnes in the 1980s before collapsing, one of the most dramatic booms and busts in fishing.

name: Japanese sea bass
fact: Japanese sea bass, suzuki, is a summer sashimi fish that changes its name as it grows, a 'success fish' in Japanese tradition.

name: Japanese sea cucumber
fact: The Japanese sea cucumber is farmed and dried as a luxury food across East Asia and is known in Japan as namako.

name: Japanese sea lion
fact: The Japanese sea lion bred on beaches of Japan and Korea until hunting wiped it out; the last reliable sightings were in the 1950s, with a final juvenile reported in 1974.

name: Japanese Spanish mackerel
fact: The Japanese Spanish mackerel, sawara, is a spring fish in Japan, grilled with miso or served as lightly seared sashimi.

name: Japanese spider crab
fact: The Japanese spider crab has the largest leg span of any arthropod, up to about 3.7 metres, and lives on the seabed off Japan down to about 600 metres.

name: Japanese spiny lobster
fact: The Japanese spiny lobster, Ise-ebi, is a celebration food in Japan, served grilled or raw at New Year and at weddings.

name: Japanese wireweed
fact: Japanese wireweed is a fast-growing brown seaweed from the Pacific that has invaded the coasts of Europe and North America.

name: Jason
fact: Jason is a remotely operated vehicle of Woods Hole that explores hydrothermal vents and wrecks from a ship at the surface.

name: Java
fact: Java is the most populous island in the world and is home to Jakarta, the capital of Indonesia.

name: Java Sea
fact: The Java Sea is a shallow sea between Java and Borneo, where a major naval battle was fought in 1942.

name: Java Trench
fact: The Java Trench, also called the Sunda Trench, is the deepest point in the Indian Ocean at more than 7,000 metres, and the 2004 tsunami began along it.

name: Jaws
fact: Jaws is Steven Spielberg's 1975 film, based on Peter Benchley's novel, about a great white shark terrorising a seaside town.

name: Jaws
fact: Jaws, or Peahi, on Maui's north shore is where tow-in surfing into giant waves was pioneered in the 1990s.

name: Jean-Baptiste Charcot
fact: Jean-Baptiste Charcot led French Antarctic expeditions aboard the ships Français and Pourquoi-Pas? and charted long stretches of the Antarctic Peninsula.

name: Jean Bart
fact: Jean Bart was a Dunkirk privateer who became a celebrated French naval officer under Louis XIV.

name: Jean Lafitte
fact: Jean Lafitte was a privateer based in Louisiana who helped Andrew Jackson defend New Orleans in 1815.

name: Jean-Michel Cousteau
fact: Jean-Michel Cousteau, Jacques Cousteau's elder son, founded the Ocean Futures Society and has spent his life making ocean documentaries.

name: Jeannette expedition
fact: The Jeannette expedition of 1879 to 1881 was an American Arctic voyage that ended when the ship was crushed by ice and most of the crew died.

name: Jebel Ali Port
fact: Jebel Ali Port near Dubai opened in 1979 and is the largest man-made harbour in the world.

name: Jeddah
fact: Jeddah on the Red Sea is Saudi Arabia's main commercial port and the gateway for pilgrims travelling to Mecca.

name: Jeddah Light
fact: Jeddah Light in Saudi Arabia is about 133 metres tall and is among the tallest traditional lighthouses in the world.

name: Jeffreys Bay
fact: Jeffreys Bay in South Africa's Eastern Cape is famed for Supertubes, one of the longest and fastest right-hand waves in the world.

name: Jellied eels
fact: Jellied eels are chopped eel set in cold jelly, a traditional dish of London's East End.

name: Jellyfish
fact: Jellyfish have no brain, heart or blood and are more than 95 per cent water, yet they have drifted the oceans for more than 500 million years.

name: Jerdon's sea snake
fact: Jerdon's sea snake is a true sea snake of Indo-Pacific coastal waters that spends its whole life in the sea.

name: Jericho worm
fact: The Jericho worm is a tube worm with a ringed tube like a crumbling wall, and it is usually the first tube worm to colonise a brand-new vent.

name: Jet skiing
fact: Jet skiing is riding a small, motorised personal watercraft across the water.

name: Jewel damselfish
fact: The jewel damselfish of Indo-Pacific reefs is spangled with tiny blue spots as a juvenile, and the adult farms a turf of red algae.

name: Jiaolong
fact: China's submersible Jiaolong dived to more than 7,000 metres in the Mariana Trench in 2012.

name: Jib
fact: The jib is the triangular sail at the front of a sailing boat.

name: Jingle shell
fact: Jingle shells are thin, translucent bivalves that cement themselves to rocks and other shells and chime when they are strung together.

name: John Dory
fact: John Dory has a dark spot on each flank said to be St Peter's thumbprint, and its sweet white fillets are prized by chefs.

name: John Jellicoe
fact: John Jellicoe commanded the British Grand Fleet at the Battle of Jutland in 1916.

name: John Jervis
fact: John Jervis won the Battle of Cape St Vincent in 1797 and gave Nelson his first chance to shine.

name: John Murray
fact: John Murray was a Scottish-Canadian oceanographer who served on the Challenger expedition and edited its reports.

name: John Paul Jones
fact: John Paul Jones, a founder of the American navy, captured HMS Serapis in 1779 in a battle in which he is said to have vowed that he had not yet begun to fight.

name: Johnson Sea Link
fact: The Johnson Sea Link was a research submersible, and two men died in 1973 when it became entangled in a wreck off Key West.

name: Johnson's seagrass
fact: Johnson's seagrass, found only on Florida's east coast, was the first marine plant listed as threatened under the United States Endangered Species Act.

name: JOIDES Resolution
fact: The drilling ship JOIDES Resolution spent decades recovering sediment cores from the deep sea floor that record millions of years of Earth's climate.

name: Jonah crab
fact: The Jonah crab of the north-west Atlantic was once lobster-pot bycatch but is now fished in its own right for its large claws.

name: Jordan
fact: Jordan's only coast, about 26 kilometres on the Gulf of Aqaba, gives it a port on the Red Sea.

name: Jormungandr
