fact: Jormungandr is the Norse serpent so huge that it lies in the ocean and encircles the whole world, biting its own tail.

name: Joseph Bonaparte Gulf
fact: The Joseph Bonaparte Gulf in northern Australia was named by the French explorer Nicolas Baudin after Napoleon's elder brother Joseph.

name: Joshua Slocum
fact: Joshua Slocum was the first person to sail alone around the world, finishing the voyage in 1898 in the sloop Spray.

name: Jost Van Dyke
fact: Jost Van Dyke is a small British Virgin Island famed for its beach bars, such as the Soggy Dollar Bar.

name: Juan de Fuca Ridge
fact: The Juan de Fuca Ridge off the Pacific Northwest is a spreading ridge whose vents are wired to shore by a cabled seafloor observatory.

name: Juan Fernandez fur seal
fact: The Juan Fernandez fur seal was believed extinct after heavy hunting until it was found again in the 1960s on Chile's Juan Fernandez Islands.

name: Juan Fernández Islands
fact: The Juan Fernández Islands off Chile include Robinson Crusoe Island, where the marooned sailor Alexander Selkirk survived alone for four years and inspired Defoe's novel.

name: Julidochromis
fact: Julidochromis are small, striped cichlids that live and breed in rocky crevices in Lake Tanganyika.

name: Junk
fact: The Chinese junk, with its battened sails, was sailing the seas centuries before similar rigs appeared in Europe, and Zheng He's treasure fleet used giant junks.

name: Juno Beach
fact: Juno Beach was the D-Day landing beach assigned to Canadian forces on 6 June 1944.

name: K-129
fact: The Soviet missile submarine K-129 sank in 1968 about 4,900 metres down in the Pacific; the CIA's Glomar Explorer secretly lifted part of it in 1974 and the rest still lies there.

name: K-19
fact: K-19 was a Soviet nuclear submarine whose reactor coolant system failed in 1961, earning it the nickname Hiroshima and inspiring a 2002 film.

name: Kaga
fact: The Japanese carrier Kaga, sunk at the Battle of Midway in 1942, was the first Midway carrier wreck found, in October 2019, more than 5,000 metres down.

name: Kaiko
fact: Kaiko was a Japanese robotic vehicle that in 1995 became the second craft to reach the bottom of the Challenger Deep, and it was lost at sea in 2003.

name: Kaiser Wilhelm der Grosse
fact: Kaiser Wilhelm der Grosse of 1897 was the first liner with four funnels and won the Blue Riband.

name: Kaiyukan
fact: Kaiyukan in Osaka, opened in 1990, centres on a Pacific Ocean tank of about 5,400 cubic metres that includes whale sharks.

name: Kaluga
fact: The kaluga of the Amur river basin is one of the largest freshwater fish in the world and is critically endangered.

name: Kamal
fact: The kamal is a simple Arab navigation tool of a card on a knotted string, used to find latitude from the height of a star.

name: Kamchatka Current
fact: The Kamchatka Current is a cold current flowing south-west along the Kamchatka coast that feeds the Oyashio.

name: Kamchatka flounder
fact: The Kamchatka flounder is a large flatfish of the deep North Pacific and Bering Sea.

name: Kampango
fact: The kampango is a large catfish of Lake Malawi and its rivers.

name: Kanaloa
fact: Kanaloa is a major Hawaiian god associated with the ocean and ocean winds, and the island of Kahoolawe is linked to him.

name: Kanmon Strait
fact: The Kanmon Strait between Japan's Honshu and Kyushu islands is only about 600 metres wide at its narrowest yet carries heavy shipping beneath its bridge and tunnels.

name: Kapenta
fact: Kapenta are tiny sardine-like fish from Lake Tanganyika that were introduced to Lake Kariba in the 1960s, where they now support a large fishery.

name: Karachi
fact: Karachi on the Arabian Sea is Pakistan's largest city and its principal port.

name: Karenia brevis
fact: Karenia brevis is the microscopic dinoflagellate behind Florida's red tides and produces toxins that kill fish.

name: Karl Donitz
fact: Karl Donitz directed Germany's U-boat campaign in the Second World War and briefly led Germany after Hitler's death in 1945.

name: Karpathos
fact: Karpathos is a long, rugged Greek island between Crete and Rhodes known for its traditional mountain villages.

name: Kastellorizo
fact: Kastellorizo is Greece's easternmost inhabited island and lies just off the Turkish coast.

name: Kathryn Sullivan
fact: Kathryn Sullivan was the first American woman to walk in space, and in 2020 became the first woman to reach Challenger Deep.

name: Katsuobushi
fact: Katsuobushi is skipjack tuna that has been cooked, smoked and fermented until as hard as wood, then shaved into flakes for Japanese stock.

name: Kattegat
fact: The Kattegat is the sea between Denmark and Sweden that connects the Baltic Sea to the North Sea through the Skagerrak.

name: Kauai
fact: Kauai is the oldest of the main Hawaiian islands and has one of the wettest spots on Earth, Mount Waialeale.

name: Kawakawa
fact: The kawakawa, or mackerel tuna, is a small coastal tuna of the Indo-Pacific with wavy stripes on its back and dark spots under its pectoral fins.

name: Kayak
fact: The kayak was developed by Inuit and other Arctic peoples as a sealed one-person hunting boat for seals and other sea animals.

name: Kayaking
fact: Kayaking uses a double-bladed paddle to move a covered boat, a design that began with Arctic peoples.

name: Kedge
fact: A kedge is a light anchor used to pull a ship through a narrow channel or off the shore, and to kedge means to move a ship this way.

name: Kedgeree
fact: Kedgeree is a dish of rice, smoked haddock and boiled eggs that British colonials adapted from the Indian dish khichdi.

name: Keel
fact: The keel is the long structural beam along the bottom of a ship's hull, which keeps the vessel stable.

name: Keelhaul
fact: To keelhaul was a naval punishment of dragging a sailor under a ship's keel, and it is now used to mean being severely reprimanded.

name: Kefalonia
fact: Kefalonia is the largest of the Greek Ionian Islands and the setting of the novel Captain Corelli's Mandolin.

name: Kelp
fact: Kelps are large brown seaweeds that form underwater forests along cold, rocky coasts, anchored by a root-like holdfast rather than true roots.

name: Kelp bass
fact: The kelp bass, or calico bass, is a mottled sea bass of California's kelp forests and one of the state's most popular sport fish.

name: Kelp crab
fact: The kelp crab lives in kelp forests of the Pacific coast of North America, where it feeds mostly on the kelp itself.

name: Kelp fly
fact: Kelp flies lay their eggs in rotting seaweed on the strandline, and their larvae feed on it, becoming food for shore birds.

name: Kelp goose
fact: The kelp goose of southern South America feeds on seaweed along rocky shores, and the male is white while the female is dark.

name: Kelp greenling
fact: The kelp greenling of the North Pacific hides among kelp, and its males and females look so different that they were once described as separate species.

name: Kelp gull
fact: The kelp gull is a black-backed gull of Southern Hemisphere coasts, including the Antarctic Peninsula.

name: Kelp perch
fact: The kelp perch is a small surfperch of California kelp beds that picks parasites off other fish and gives birth to fully formed young.

name: Kelp rockfish
fact: The kelp rockfish rests motionless among kelp fronds, often head-down, and gives birth to live young like all rockfishes.

name: Kelvin wave
fact: Kelvin waves are huge, slow ocean waves that travel along the equator or the coast and help trigger El Nino.

name: Kemp's ridley sea turtle
fact: Kemp's ridley is the rarest sea turtle and nests in mass daytime arrivals called arribadas, mostly on one Mexican beach, Rancho Nuevo.

name: Kenya
fact: Kenya's Indian Ocean coast includes the old port of Mombasa and the Swahili town of Lamu.

name: Kerguelen Islands
fact: The Kerguelen Islands are a remote French sub-Antarctic archipelago in the southern Indian Ocean, sometimes called the Desolation Islands.

name: Kerguelen Plateau
fact: The Kerguelen Plateau in the southern Indian Ocean is one of the largest submerged volcanic plateaus on Earth, with only a few island peaks breaking the surface.

name: Kermadec snailfish
fact: The Kermadec snailfish lives only in the Kermadec Trench off New Zealand, where it has been filmed feeding in groups about 7,500 metres down.

name: Kermadec Trench
fact: The Kermadec Trench north-east of New Zealand plunges to about 10,000 metres and is home to huge swarms of amphipods and snailfish.

name: Ketch
fact: A ketch is a two-masted sailing boat whose shorter mizzen mast stands forward of the rudder post.

name: Kiel Canal
fact: The Kiel Canal in Germany, opened in 1895, links the North Sea and the Baltic and is one of the busiest artificial waterways in the world.

name: Kilka
fact: Kilka are tiny sprats of the Caspian and Black seas that once made up most of the Caspian catch before the comb jelly invasion.

name: Killer shrimp
fact: The killer shrimp, a large amphipod from the Black Sea region, has spread through Europe's canals to Britain, killing far more prey than it eats.

name: Killifish
fact: Some killifish live in puddles that dry up each year, surviving as eggs in the mud that hobbyists can buy and post in the mail.

name: Kina
fact: Kina is New Zealand's native sea urchin, a kelp grazer whose roe is a traditional Māori delicacy.

name: King angelfish
fact: The king angelfish, dark blue with a white bar and orange tail, runs cleaning stations for hammerheads around the Galápagos.

name: King crab
fact: Red king crabs of the Bering Sea can span 1.5 metres across the legs and are actually closer relatives of hermit crabs than of true crabs.

name: King eider
fact: Male king eiders have a bright orange shield on the bill, and the species dives for food in cold Arctic seas.

name: King George whiting
fact: King George whiting is a prized food fish of southern Australia, named after King George Sound in Western Australia.

name: King helmet
fact: The king helmet is a heavy-shelled Caribbean sea snail that feeds on sea urchins and sand dollars.

name: King mackerel
fact: The king mackerel, or kingfish, is a big, fast Spanish mackerel of the western Atlantic, chased by anglers off Florida and known to leap clear of the water.

name: King penguin
fact: King penguins dive to over 300 metres for lanternfish and take more than a year to raise a chick, the longest breeding cycle of any penguin.

name: King prawn
fact: King prawns such as the western king prawn are large, commercially important prawns of Australian waters.

name: King ragworm
fact: The king ragworm is a large marine worm that can grow well over half a metre long and is dug by anglers for bait.

name: King scallop
fact: King scallops have a row of tiny eyes along the edge of their mantle and swim by clapping their two shells together.

name: King shag
fact: The king shag is a rare cormorant that breeds only in the Marlborough Sounds of New Zealand.

name: King threadfin
fact: The king threadfin of northern Australia begins life as a male and changes into a female as it grows older.

name: King tide
fact: A king tide is an especially high tide that occurs when the Moon is closest to Earth at new or full Moon.

name: Kingklip
fact: Kingklip is a long, slender cusk-eel of southern African waters that is prized as food.

name: Kingman Reef
fact: Kingman Reef is a nearly submerged coral atoll in the central Pacific with almost no dry land, yet its reef is one of the most pristine on Earth.

name: Kinilaw
fact: Kinilaw is a Filipino dish of raw fish cured in vinegar with ginger, onion and chilli.

name: Kinnaird Head Lighthouse
fact: Kinnaird Head at Fraserburgh was lit in 1787 as the first lighthouse built by the Northern Lighthouse Board in Scotland.

name: Kippering
fact: Kippering splits a herring, soaks it in brine and cold smokes it, and the result is called a kipper.

name: Kiribati
fact: Kiribati is spread across 33 islands straddling the equator and the International Date Line, and includes Kiritimati, the largest coral atoll by land area.

name: Kirra
fact: Kirra at the southern end of the Gold Coast is renowned for a fast, hollow right-hand barrel.

name: Kissing gourami
fact: Kissing gouramis press their lips together in a test of strength, and like other gouramis they breathe air with a labyrinth organ.

name: Kitefin shark
fact: The kitefin shark, found down to around 1,800 metres, is the largest known glowing vertebrate at up to about 1.8 metres long.

name: Kitesurfing
fact: Kitesurfing uses a large controllable kite to pull a rider on a board across the water.

name: Kittiwake
fact: The kittiwake is a small, truly oceanic gull that spends the winter far out at sea and nests on sheer cliff ledges.

name: Klaus Stortebeker
fact: Klaus Stortebeker was a leader of the Victual Brothers, northern German pirates, said to have been executed in Hamburg around 1401.

name: Knarr
fact: The knarr was the broad Viking cargo ship that carried settlers and livestock across the open North Atlantic to Iceland, Greenland and Vinland.

name: Kneeboarding
fact: Kneeboarding is being towed behind a boat while kneeling on a board.

name: Knifetooth dogfish
fact: The knifetooth dogfish has blade-like lower teeth for cutting chunks from its prey and lives on deep slopes of the eastern Atlantic.

name: Knorr
fact: The research vessel Knorr was the ship from which Robert Ballard's team found the wreck of the Titanic in 1985.

name: Knot
fact: A knot is a speed of one nautical mile per hour, about 1.85 kilometres per hour.

name: Knotted wrack
fact: Knotted wrack, or egg wrack, is a long-lived brown seaweed with single egg-shaped air bladders along its fronds, harvested for alginate and fertiliser.

name: Knysna seahorse
fact: The Knysna seahorse lives only in a few estuaries on South Africa's southern coast and is listed as endangered.

name: Kobe
fact: Kobe's port was badly damaged by the Great Hanshin earthquake of January 1995 and rebuilt in the years that followed.

name: Kochi
fact: Kochi in Kerala was a centre of the spice trade, and the Portuguese explorer Vasco da Gama died there in 1524.

name: Koi
fact: Koi are ornamental common carp bred in Japan, and prized fish have sold for more than a million dollars.

name: Kokoda
fact: Kokoda is a Fijian dish of raw fish marinated in lime juice and served in coconut cream.

name: Kole tang
fact: The kole tang, or goldring bristletooth, is a Hawaiian surgeonfish with a gold ring around each eye and comb-like teeth for brushing up algae and detritus.

name: Kolkata
fact: Kolkata's port stands on the Hooghly River, making it India's only major river port.

name: Kombu
fact: Kombu is dried kelp, the seaweed that gives Japanese dashi stock its savoury umami taste; monosodium glutamate was first isolated from it in 1908.

name: Kommetjie
fact: Kommetjie near Cape Town has several surf breaks including the Outer Kom, a big-wave spot on the Atlantic coast.

name: Komodo
fact: Komodo is the Indonesian island that gave its name to the Komodo dragon, the largest living lizard.

name: Komodo National Park
fact: Komodo National Park in Indonesia protects not only its dragons but strong-current reefs where manta rays gather to be cleaned.

name: Komsomolets
fact: The Soviet nuclear submarine Komsomolets sank in the Norwegian Sea in 1989 and lies about 1,700 metres down with its reactor and two nuclear torpedoes.

name: Kon-Tiki
fact: Kon-Tiki is Thor Heyerdahl's 1948 book about his 1947 balsa-raft voyage across the Pacific, and its 1950 documentary won an Academy Award.

name: Kon-Tiki expedition
fact: In 1947 Thor Heyerdahl and five companions sailed a balsa raft from Peru across the Pacific to the Tuamotu islands.

name: Koran angelfish
fact: The koran angelfish gets its name from the arabesque markings on the tail of some adults, said to resemble Arabic script; juveniles are blue with white arcs.

name: Korčula
fact: Korčula is a Croatian island whose walled old town is claimed as the birthplace of the explorer Marco Polo.

name: Korea Strait
fact: The Korea Strait between South Korea and Japan links the East China Sea to the Sea of Japan, and the Russian fleet was destroyed there at Tsushima in 1905.

name: Korean mackerel
fact: The Korean mackerel is a Spanish mackerel found from the Indian Ocean to the seas around Korea and China.

name: Kos
fact: Kos is the Greek island traditionally regarded as the birthplace of Hippocrates, the father of medicine.

name: Kotor
fact: Kotor in Montenegro stands at the head of a deep fjord-like bay and its old town is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

name: Kraken
fact: The kraken is a giant sea monster of Scandinavian legend, said to drag whole ships down into the deep.

name: Krill
fact: Antarctic krill swarms can stretch for kilometres, and their total weight of several hundred million tonnes is among the largest of any animal species.

name: Krk
fact: Krk is one of the two largest islands in the Adriatic Sea and is joined to the Croatian mainland by a bridge.

name: Kronosaurus
fact: Kronosaurus was a Cretaceous pliosaur from Queensland, Australia, whose skull alone is estimated at over 2 metres long.

name: Kubotai rasbora
fact: The Kubotai rasbora is a tiny Thai and Myanmar minnow that reaches only about 2 centimetres.

name: Kuhli loach
fact: The kuhli loach is a striped eel-like fish from South-east Asia that burrows into aquarium sand and comes out at night.

name: Kure Atoll
fact: Kure Atoll, at the northern end of the Hawaiian chain, is the northernmost coral atoll in the world.

name: Kuril Islands
fact: The Kuril Islands are a volcanic chain between Kamchatka and Japan, still disputed between Russia and Japan since the end of the Second World War.

name: Kuril-Kamchatka Trench
fact: The Kuril-Kamchatka Trench runs south from Kamchatka past the Kuril Islands and reaches more than 9,000 metres deep.

name: Kuroshio Current
fact: The Kuroshio, or Black Stream, is the Pacific's counterpart to the Gulf Stream, carrying warm water north past Japan.

name: Kursk
fact: The Russian submarine Kursk sank in the Barents Sea in August 2000 after torpedo explosions, with the loss of all 118 aboard.

name: Kuruma prawn
fact: The kuruma prawn, with its banded tail, is one of the most expensive prawns in Japan and the first prawn ever reared in a hatchery, in the 1930s.

name: Kusaya
fact: Kusaya is a fermented and dried fish from Japan's Izu Islands, made in a brine that has been reused for generations.

name: Kuwait
fact: Kuwait lies at the head of the Persian Gulf.

name: Kuwait City
fact: Kuwait City is the capital of Kuwait and sits on the shore of the Persian Gulf.

name: Kvarner Gulf
fact: The Kvarner Gulf is a bay of the northern Adriatic in Croatia, sheltered by the islands of Krk, Cres and Rab, with the port of Rijeka at its head.

name: Kwajalein Atoll
fact: Kwajalein Atoll in the Marshall Islands encloses one of the largest lagoons in the world, about 2,000 square kilometres.

name: La Concha
fact: La Concha in San Sebastian, Spain, takes its name from the scallop-shell shape of the bay it curves around.

name: La Désirade
fact: La Désirade, a dry narrow island east of Guadeloupe, was the first land Columbus sighted on his second voyage in 1493.

name: La Digue
fact: La Digue in the Seychelles is a small island where bicycles and ox carts are still common, and it is known for its granite boulder beaches.

name: La Jument Lighthouse
fact: La Jument Lighthouse off Ushant became world famous from a 1989 photograph by Jean Guichard showing a keeper at its door as a huge wave engulfed the tower.

name: La Maddalena
fact: La Maddalena is the main island of an archipelago national park off the north coast of Sardinia.

name: La Nina
fact: La Nina is the cool phase of the Pacific climate cycle, when the eastern Pacific becomes unusually cold.

name: La Pérouse Strait
fact: The La Pérouse Strait separates Hokkaido from the Russian island of Sakhalin, linking the Sea of Japan and the Sea of Okhotsk.

name: La Rochelle
fact: La Rochelle is a French Atlantic port whose old harbour is guarded by medieval towers.

name: La Spezia
fact: La Spezia in Liguria is a naval base and the usual gateway to the Cinque Terre villages.

name: Labrador Current
fact: The Labrador Current carries cold Arctic water and icebergs south past Newfoundland, and it was one of its icebergs that sank the Titanic.

name: Labrador duck
fact: The Labrador duck, a sea duck of the North American Atlantic coast, was the first bird endemic to North America to go extinct, last seen in 1878.

name: Labrador Sea
fact: The Labrador Sea between Canada and Greenland is one of the few places where surface water sinks to the deep ocean, helping drive global circulation.

name: Ladyfish
fact: The ladyfish is a slim silver fish of warm estuaries that leaps and skips repeatedly across the surface when hooked.

name: Lae
fact: Lae in Papua New Guinea is the country's largest cargo port and was the last departure point of Amelia Earhart in 1937.

name: Lagos
fact: Lagos, Nigeria's largest city, grew around a lagoon opening onto the Atlantic, and its name is Portuguese for 'lakes'.

name: Lagundri Bay
fact: Lagundri Bay on the Indonesian island of Nias has a famous right-hand point break found by travelling surfers in the 1970s.

name: Lahille's dolphin
fact: Lahille's dolphin is a large bottlenose dolphin of estuaries and coasts in southern Brazil, Uruguay and Argentina.

name: Lahinch
fact: Lahinch in County Clare is one of the best-known surf beaches on Ireland's Atlantic coast.

name: Lahontan cutthroat trout
fact: The Lahontan cutthroat is the largest subspecies of cutthroat trout, native to Nevada's Pyramid Lake, and is the state fish of Nevada.

name: Lake sturgeon
fact: The lake sturgeon of the Great Lakes and Mississippi can live for more than 100 years and does not breed until it is about 20.

name: Lake trout
fact: Lake trout are big, slow-growing char of cold northern lakes that can live for more than 25 years.

name: Lakshadweep
fact: Lakshadweep is an Indian archipelago of coral islands in the Arabian Sea off the coast of Kerala.

name: Lamp shell
fact: Lamp shells look like clams but belong to a separate ancient group, the brachiopods, and filter food with a coiled, tentacled organ called the lophophore.

name: Lampedusa
fact: Lampedusa is Italy's southernmost island and lies closer to Tunisia than to Sicily.

name: Lamprey
fact: Lampreys are jawless fish with a sucker mouth ringed with teeth, and several species fasten on to other fish to feed.

name: Lamu
fact: Lamu is a Kenyan island with a World Heritage old Swahili town where there are almost no cars and donkeys carry goods.

name: Lancaster Sound
fact: Lancaster Sound, the eastern entrance to the Northwest Passage, is named after Sir James Lancaster, a sponsor of William Baffin's 1616 voyage.

name: Lancastria
fact: The troopship Lancastria was bombed and sunk off Saint-Nazaire in June 1940, Britain's worst ever maritime disaster.

name: Lancelet
fact: The lancelet, a finger-length fish-like animal that burrows in sand, has a body plan close to the ancestor of all vertebrates.

name: Lancetfish
fact: The lancetfish is a 2-metre deep-sea predator with a huge sail fin and fangs, and its watery flesh is so flabby that it is rarely eaten.

name: Landlubber
fact: A landlubber is the sailors' term for someone who is inexperienced at sea.

name: Lane snapper
fact: The lane snapper is a pink-and-yellow striped Caribbean snapper with a black spot on its side, common on grass flats and reefs.

name: Langkawi
fact: Langkawi is an archipelago of about 100 islands in the Andaman Sea off the north-west coast of Malaysia.

name: Langoustine
fact: Langoustines live in burrows in muddy seabeds and are one of the most valuable catches landed in Britain, where they are sold as scampi.

name: Lanikai Beach
fact: Lanikai Beach on Oahu looks out over the twin Mokulua islands off the windward coast.

name: Lanterna of Genoa
fact: The Lanterna of Genoa, rebuilt in 1543 and about 77 metres tall, is one of the oldest working lighthouses in the world.

name: Lanternfish
fact: Lanternfish may make up more than half of all deep-sea fish by weight, and their nightly rise towards the surface is the largest animal migration on Earth.

name: Lanternshark
fact: Lanternsharks are small deep-sea sharks that glow along their bellies, hiding their silhouettes from predators looking up.

name: La Perouse expedition
fact: The French expedition of La Perouse left in 1785 and vanished in the Pacific, and its wrecks were found at Vanikoro in the following century.

name: Laptev Sea
fact: The Laptev Sea off Siberia is named after the Russian explorer cousins Dmitry and Khariton Laptev, who charted the Arctic coast in the 1730s and 1740s.

name: Large-leafed orange mangrove
fact: Bruguiera gymnorrhiza sends knee-like roots looping up out of the mud so that the tree can take in air.

name: Largehead hairtail
fact: The largehead hairtail is a ribbon-like, silver predator with fangs that is one of the largest fish catches in the world, mostly off China.

name: Largemouth bass
fact: The male largemouth bass sweeps out a nest in the shallows and guards the eggs and fry for weeks, attacking anything that comes near.

name: Larger Pacific striped octopus
fact: The larger Pacific striped octopus is unusually social: pairs share dens and mate beak to beak, and the female lays several clutches instead of dying after one.

name: Largetooth sawfish
fact: The largetooth sawfish can live in fresh water and has been caught hundreds of kilometres up rivers in Australia and Central America.

name: Larvacean
fact: Larvaceans are tadpole-shaped, transparent animals that build a disposable mucus 'house' around themselves to filter food, discarding it several times a day.

name: Las Palmas
fact: Las Palmas de Gran Canaria is a major Atlantic port where Columbus's ships stopped for repairs in 1492 before crossing to the Americas.

name: The Last Voyage of the Demeter
fact: The Last Voyage of the Demeter is a 2023 horror film by Andre Ovredal, adapted from a chapter of Bram Stoker's Dracula about a doomed ship.

name: Latakia
fact: Latakia is Syria's main seaport on the Mediterranean.

name: Laurens de Graaf
fact: Laurens de Graaf was a Dutch buccaneer who sacked Veracruz in 1683 and later served the French Crown.

name: Lawnmower blenny
fact: The lawnmower blenny is named for its habit of cropping algae, which makes it a popular cleaner for reef aquariums.

name: Laysan albatross
fact: A Laysan albatross named Wisdom, ringed on Midway Atoll in 1956, was still hatching chicks in her seventies, the oldest known wild bird.

name: Lazarev Sea
fact: The Lazarev Sea off Antarctica is named after the Russian admiral Mikhail Lazarev, who sailed on Bellingshausen's Antarctic voyage.

name: Le Maire Strait
fact: The Le Maire Strait, between Tierra del Fuego and Isla de los Estados, is named after the Dutch navigator Jacob Le Maire.

name: Lead line
fact: A lead line is a weighted rope marked in fathoms that sailors dropped to measure depth and sample the seabed.

name: Leaf-scaled sea snake
fact: The leaf-scaled sea snake vanished from Ashmore Reef and was feared extinct until it turned up again off Western Australia in 2015.

name: Leaf sheep
fact: The leaf sheep is a tiny sea slug that keeps chloroplasts from the algae it eats, and its green gills give it the look of a miniature sheep.

name: Leafscale gulper shark
fact: The leafscale gulper shark, named for its leaf-shaped scales, lives on continental slopes down to about 2,400 metres.

name: Leafy sea dragon
fact: The leafy sea dragon's leaf-like flaps are camouflage only; it swims with tiny transparent fins, and the male carries the eggs under his tail.

name: League
fact: A league is an old unit of distance, about three nautical miles at sea, which is why Jules Verne's novel measures twenty thousand of them.

name: Leaping bonito
fact: The leaping bonito is a small tuna relative of northern Australian waters.

name: Least darter
fact: The least darter is one of the smallest freshwater fish in North America, a 4-centimetre perch relative of weedy streams and lakes.

name: Least killifish
fact: The least killifish is one of the smallest fish in North America, a 2-to-3-centimetre livebearer of the southeastern United States, and not a true killifish.

name: Leather coral
fact: Leather corals are soft corals shaped like a toadstool with a leathery surface, and they shed a waxy film to clean themselves.

name: Leather star
fact: The leather star has a smooth, leathery skin and is said to smell of garlic when it is lifted from the water.

name: Leatherback turtle
fact: Leatherback turtles have been tracked crossing the entire Pacific, more than 10,000 kilometres, from Indonesian nesting beaches to feeding grounds off California.

name: Leatherjacket
fact: Leatherjackets are a family of filefishes with tough, rough skin, found in warm and temperate seas.

name: Leedsichthys
fact: Leedsichthys was a Jurassic filter-feeding fish perhaps 16 metres long, the largest bony fish known to have lived.

name: Leeuwin Current
fact: The Leeuwin Current flows south along the coast of Western Australia, carrying warm tropical water that lets corals grow as far south as the Abrolhos Islands.

name: Lefkada
fact: Lefkada is a Greek Ionian island joined to the mainland by a causeway and a short floating bridge.

name: Leif Eriksson's voyage to Vinland
fact: Around the year 1000 the Norse explorer Leif Eriksson sailed to North America from Greenland and named it Vinland.

name: Lemnos
fact: Lemnos is a northern Aegean island whose harbour at Moudros was a key Allied base in the Gallipoli campaign.

name: Lemon damselfish
fact: The lemon damselfish is a bright yellow damselfish that shelters among branching corals on Indo-Pacific reefs.

name: Lemon peel angelfish
fact: The lemon peel angelfish takes its name from its bright lemon-yellow body, which is marked with a blue ring around the eye.

name: Lemon shark
fact: Lemon sharks return to the same mangrove nurseries where they were born to give birth to their own pups.

name: Lemon sole
fact: Despite its name, the lemon sole is not a true sole but a right-eyed flounder found around the British Isles.

name: Lemon tetra
fact: The lemon tetra is a small, yellow South American fish that grows to only about 4 centimetres.

name: Lemonpeel angelfish
fact: The lemonpeel angelfish is a small, bright yellow angelfish with blue rings around its eyes, found on Indo-Pacific reefs.

name: Lenok
fact: The lenok, sometimes called the Asiatic trout, lives in the cold rivers of Siberia, Mongolia, China and Korea.

name: Leopard coral grouper
fact: The leopard coral grouper is a red, blue-spotted predator of the Great Barrier Reef and a major target of its reef fishery.

name: Leopard seal
fact: Leopard seals are the Antarctic's top seal predator, hunting penguins and the pups of other seals.

name: Leopard shark
fact: Leopard sharks gather in warm shallows off California each summer, with pregnant females basking in the waters off La Jolla.

name: Leopard whipray
fact: The leopard whipray has a leopard-like pattern of dark rings and was only separated from the honeycomb stingray as a species in 2008.

name: Leptocephalus
fact: The leptocephalus is the leaf-shaped, see-through larva of eels, tarpon and bonefish, which drifts in the current for months before changing shape.

name: Les Eclaireurs Lighthouse
aliases: Lighthouse at the End of the World
fact: Les Eclaireurs Lighthouse, built in 1920 in the Beagle Channel near Ushuaia, is popularly known as the Lighthouse at the End of the World.

name: Les Saintes
fact: Les Saintes are a cluster of small islands south of Guadeloupe, where the Battle of the Saintes was fought in 1782.

name: Lesbos
fact: Lesbos is the third-largest Greek island and the birthplace of the ancient poet Sappho.

name: Lesser electric ray
fact: The lesser electric ray of the western Atlantic is small enough to hold in two hands yet can deliver a shock of around 14 to 37 volts.

name: Lesser flying squid
fact: The lesser flying squid lives in the north-east Atlantic and the Mediterranean, mostly close to the seabed.

name: Lettuce coral
fact: Lettuce coral grows in thin, ruffled plates like the leaves of a lettuce and is common on Caribbean reef slopes.

name: Lettuce sea slug
fact: The lettuce sea slug eats green algae and keeps their chloroplasts alive inside its frilly body, where they go on making sugar from sunlight.

name: Leucothea
fact: Leucothea was a Greek sea goddess, formerly the mortal Ino, who gave Odysseus a veil that saved him from drowning.

name: Levantine Sea
fact: The Levantine Sea is the easternmost part of the Mediterranean, off Turkey, Syria, Lebanon, Israel and Egypt, and the saltiest part of the whole sea.

name: Leviathan
fact: Leviathan is a vast sea monster described in the Hebrew Bible, and the word later came to mean any enormous creature of the sea.

name: Leyte Gulf
fact: Leyte Gulf in the Philippines saw the largest naval battle of the Second World War in October 1944.

name: Liberia
fact: Liberia's capital, Monrovia, is an Atlantic port named after the US president James Monroe.

name: Liburna
fact: The liburna was a light, fast Roman warship modelled on the vessels of the Liburnian pirates of the Adriatic.

name: Libyan Sea
fact: The Libyan Sea is the stretch of the Mediterranean between Crete and the coast of Libya.

name: The Life Aquatic with Steve Zissou
fact: The Life Aquatic with Steve Zissou is Wes Anderson's 2004 comedy about an oceanographer and filmmaker in the style of Jacques Cousteau.

name: Life of Pi
fact: Life of Pi is Yann Martel's 2001 novel, filmed by Ang Lee in 2012, about a boy stranded in a lifeboat with a Bengal tiger.

name: Lifeguard
fact: Lifeguards watch over swimmers on beaches and in the sea, and they train in rescue and first aid.

name: Light-bulb tunicate
fact: The light-bulb tunicate lives in clusters of transparent, bulb-shaped bodies attached to rocks and docks.

name: Light cruiser
fact: A light cruiser was a cruiser with lighter armour and guns than a heavy cruiser, mainly used for scouting and leading destroyers.

name: Light-mantled albatross
fact: The light-mantled albatross is a slender, grey-backed albatross that glides around the Southern Ocean and even reaches Antarctic coasts.

name: Lighthouse keeper
fact: Lighthouse keepers once tended the lamp and lived at remote towers, a role largely ended by automation in the twentieth century.

name: Lighthouse Reef
fact: Lighthouse Reef is an atoll off Belize whose lagoon contains the Great Blue Hole, a sinkhole about 125 metres deep made famous by Jacques Cousteau.

name: Ligurian Sea
fact: The Ligurian Sea, between the Italian Riviera and Corsica, is part of the Pelagos Sanctuary, a protected area rich in fin whales and dolphins.

name: Orange-clubbed sea slug
fact: The orange-clubbed sea slug of North Atlantic shores has orange-tipped, club-shaped projections along its body.

name: Limassol
fact: Limassol is the main commercial port of Cyprus.

name: Limiting Factor
fact: Limiting Factor is the submersible in which Victor Vescovo became the first person to dive to the deepest point of all five oceans, in 2018 and 2019.

name: Limpet
fact: Limpets clamp their cone-shaped shells to rocks and return to the exact same 'home scar' after every grazing trip.

name: Lincoln Sea
fact: The Lincoln Sea, north of Greenland and Ellesmere Island, is named after Robert Todd Lincoln, US Secretary of War and son of Abraham Lincoln.

name: Lined butterflyfish
fact: The lined butterflyfish is the largest butterflyfish, growing to about 30 centimetres, with thin vertical lines and a black band through the eye.

name: Lined seahorse
fact: The lined seahorse is the seahorse of the western Atlantic, found from Nova Scotia to Venezuela, including the eelgrass beds of Chesapeake Bay.

name: Lined surgeonfish
fact: The lined surgeonfish, also called the clown surgeonfish, defends grazing territories on shallow Indo-Pacific reefs with sharp spines at the base of its tail.

name: Ling
fact: The ling is a long, slender cod relative of deep North Atlantic waters that can reach 2 metres; its salted, dried flesh is a traditional Norwegian export.

name: Lingcod
fact: The male lingcod guards the egg mass on the kelp-forest floor through winter, and its flesh is sometimes blue-green, fading to white when cooked.

name: Lingula
fact: Lingula, a burrowing brachiopod on a fleshy stalk, looks much like fossils more than 450 million years old and was one of Darwin's original examples of a living fossil.

name: Lionfish
fact: Lionfish have 18 venomous spines and, released from aquariums, have invaded the Caribbean and western Atlantic, where they have no natural predators.

name: Lion's mane jellyfish
fact: The lion's mane jellyfish of cold northern seas is the largest known jellyfish, with tentacles that can trail over 30 metres.

name: Lion's paw scallop
fact: The lion's paw scallop is a large, ridged scallop of the eastern Pacific, prized as seafood.

name: Liopleurodon
fact: Liopleurodon was a Jurassic pliosaur of European seas with a skull well over a metre long, far smaller than the 25-metre giant once shown on television.

name: Lipari
fact: Lipari is the largest of the Aeolian Islands off the north coast of Sicily.

name: Lisbon
fact: Lisbon sits where the Tagus meets the Atlantic, and Vasco da Gama sailed from here in 1497 on the first voyage from Europe to India.

name: Little auk
fact: The little auk is one of the most numerous seabirds in the Arctic, breeding in colonies of millions in Greenland and Svalbard.

name: Little Cayman
fact: Little Cayman is the smallest of the three Cayman Islands and has very few residents.

name: Little Kern golden trout
fact: The Little Kern golden trout is native to a single river basin in California's southern Sierra Nevada.

name: Little Neptune grass
fact: Little Neptune grass forms seagrass meadows in the Mediterranean and along the neighbouring Atlantic coast.

name: Little penguin
fact: The little penguin of Australia and New Zealand stands only about 30 centimetres tall and is the smallest penguin.

name: Little piked whale
fact: Little piked whale is an old name for the minke, one of the smallest of the great rorqual whales.

name: Little skate
fact: The little skate is a small, common skate of the north-west Atlantic that walks along the seabed on modified pelvic fins.

name: Little tunny
fact: The little tunny, or false albacore, is the most common tuna in the Atlantic, a small, fast, scribble-patterned fish loved by fly anglers but rarely eaten.

name: Littoral combat ship
fact: The littoral combat ship is a modern, fast American warship class designed to operate in shallow coastal waters.

name: Livorno
fact: Livorno, known in English as Leghorn, is the main seaport of Tuscany.

name: Livyatan
fact: Livyatan was a sperm whale of about 12 million years ago with teeth more than 30 centimetres long, named after Moby-Dick's author.

name: Lizardfish
fact: Lizardfish are toothy ambush hunters that sit on the sand, often with most of the body buried, and dart up to grab passing fish.

name: Lobster
fact: Lobsters keep growing throughout their lives by moulting their shells, and some may live for decades.

name: Lobster Newburg
fact: Lobster Newburg is an American dish of lobster in a sauce of cream, butter, egg yolks and sherry.

name: Lobster roll
fact: A lobster roll is a toasted bun filled with lobster meat, and it is a New England speciality.

name: Lobster thermidor
fact: Lobster thermidor is a French dish of lobster meat in a creamy sauce, returned to its shell and browned under the grill.

name: Lobsterman
fact: Lobstermen set baited traps called pots on the seabed to catch lobsters, especially around New England and Maine.

name: Lofoten
fact: The Lofoten islands lie off northern Norway and are known for steep peaks and winter cod fishing.

name: Loggerhead turtle
fact: The loggerhead sea turtle has a huge head and powerful jaws for crushing conchs and crabs, and can live for 70 years or more.

name: Lohikeitto
fact: Lohikeitto is a creamy Finnish salmon soup with potatoes and dill.

name: Loihi Seamount
fact: Loihi, now officially Kamaʻehuakanaloa, is an active undersea volcano south-east of Hawaii that may one day grow into the next Hawaiian island.

name: Lollipop catshark
fact: The lollipop catshark is a small deep-water shark of the eastern Pacific with a broad, rounded head like a lollipop.

name: Lombok
fact: Lombok lies just east of Bali across the Lombok Strait and is dominated by the volcano Mount Rinjani.

name: Lombok Strait
fact: The Lombok Strait between Bali and Lombok marks part of the Wallace Line, the boundary between Asian and Australian wildlife.

name: Lomonosov Ridge
fact: The Lomonosov Ridge crosses the Arctic Ocean floor near the North Pole and is claimed by Russia, Canada and Denmark in competing seabed submissions.

name: London Convention
aliases: London Convention on the Prevention of Marine Pollution by Dumping of Wastes
fact: The London Convention of 1972 was an early treaty restricting the dumping of wastes at sea.

name: Long Beach
fact: The Port of Long Beach in California is one of the two busiest container ports in the United States, alongside Los Angeles.

name: Long-beaked common dolphin
fact: The long-beaked common dolphin hugs the coasts of California, Peru and West Africa and has a noticeably longer snout than its short-beaked cousin.

name: Long-finned pilot whale
fact: Long-finned pilot whales are the target of the Faroe Islands' drive hunt, and their pods follow a leader so closely that they strand together.

name: Long Island
fact: Long Island stretches about 190 kilometres east from New York City into the Atlantic and is the largest island in the contiguous United States.

name: Long John Silver
fact: Long John Silver is the one-legged pirate cook of Robert Louis Stevenson's Treasure Island, who is usually shown with a parrot on his shoulder.

name: Long-nosed chimaera
fact: Long-nosed chimaeras are deep-sea ghost sharks with a long pointed snout covered in electric-sensing pores.

name: Long-snouted seahorse
fact: The long-snouted seahorse lives in seagrass meadows from the British Isles to the Mediterranean and Black Sea, and often grows a mane of skin filaments.

name: Long-spine porcupinefish
fact: The long-spine porcupinefish has spines that lie flat until it inflates, when they stand straight out, and it is found in warm seas worldwide.

name: Long-spined sea urchin
fact: The mass die-off of long-spined sea urchins in the Caribbean in 1983 let algae overgrow many reefs, showing how important their grazing was.

name: Longbill spearfish
fact: The longbill spearfish is a slender Atlantic billfish with a long, rounded bill.

name: Longfin bannerfish
fact: The longfin bannerfish is a black-and-white butterflyfish with a long white dorsal banner, often mistaken for the Moorish idol.

name: Longfin damselfish
fact: The longfin damselfish is a Caribbean damselfish that defends its small territory of algae-covered reef.

name: Longfin inshore squid
fact: The longfin inshore squid of the US Atlantic coast is a workhorse of neuroscience: its giant nerve fibre helped reveal how nerves fire.

name: Longfin mako
fact: The longfin mako has much longer pectoral fins than its shortfin cousin and is far more rarely seen.

name: Longhorn cowfish
fact: The longhorn cowfish is a boxfish with two horns over its eyes and can release a toxin into the water when it is stressed.

name: Longjaw mudsucker
fact: The longjaw mudsucker is a Pacific coast goby that can breathe air and survive for hours out of water on mudflats.

name: Longliner
fact: A longliner fishes with a main line that can stretch for tens of kilometres, hung with thousands of baited hooks.

name: Longman's beaked whale
fact: Longman's beaked whale was known only from two skulls for most of the 20th century and lives in warm Indo-Pacific waters.

name: Longnose batfish
fact: The longnose batfish walks across the seabed on arm-like fins, has a pointed snout, and dangles a tiny lure from beneath it to attract prey.

name: Longnose butterflyfish
fact: The longnose butterflyfish, or forcepsfish, uses its tweezer-like snout to pick tiny animals from coral crevices; it is Hawaii's lauwiliwilinukunukuoioi.

name: Longnose emperor
fact: The longnose emperor is an Indo-Pacific reef fish with a long, pointed snout.

name: Longnose gar
fact: The longnose gar gulps air at the surface and has a long, narrow snout filled with needle-like teeth.

name: Longnose hawkfish
fact: The longnose hawkfish perches on deep gorgonian sea fans wearing a red check pattern, with a long snout for plucking tiny shrimps.

name: Longnose skate
fact: The longnose skate of the North American Pacific coast has a long pointed snout and lays eggs in leathery cases known as mermaid's purses.

name: Longnose stingray
fact: The longnose stingray has a long pointed snout and lives in coastal waters of the western Atlantic from the Gulf of Mexico to Brazil.

name: Longnose velvet dogfish
fact: The longnose velvet dogfish lives on the continental slopes of the Atlantic, Indian and Pacific oceans, hundreds of metres below the surface.

name: Longship
fact: Viking longships were long, narrow and shallow-draughted, able to cross open sea and yet be rowed up shallow rivers to raid inland.

name: Longshore drift
fact: Longshore drift is the movement of sand and shingle along a beach by waves that arrive at an angle.

name: Longstone Lighthouse
fact: In 1838 Grace Darling and her father rowed out from Longstone Lighthouse in the Farne Islands to rescue survivors of the wrecked steamship Forfarshire.

name: Longtail tuna
fact: The longtail tuna is a coastal tuna of the Indo-Pacific that stays in shallow seas rather than roaming the open ocean.

name: Looe Key reef
fact: Looe Key reef in the Florida Keys is named after HMS Looe, a British warship wrecked on it in 1744.

name: Lookdown
fact: The lookdown has a steeply sloping, flattened forehead and a deep, silvery, disc-shaped body.

name: Loop Current
fact: The Loop Current curls up into the Gulf of Mexico and back out past Florida, and its deep warm water can strengthen hurricanes passing over it.

name: Lophelia
fact: Lophelia is a cold-water coral that builds reefs in the dark, hundreds of metres down, from Norway to the Gulf of Mexico.

name: Lord Howe Island reef
fact: The reef around Lord Howe Island, between Australia and New Zealand, is the southernmost coral reef in the world.

name: Los Angeles
fact: The Port of Los Angeles, with neighbouring Long Beach, forms the busiest container port complex in the United States.

name: Lost City hydrothermal field
fact: The Lost City is a field of pale carbonate chimneys up to 60 metres tall on the Atlantis Massif in the mid-Atlantic, venting warm alkaline fluid rather than black smoke.

name: Louis Mountbatten
fact: Louis Mountbatten was an Admiral of the Fleet and the last Viceroy of India, and he was killed by an IRA bomb in 1979.

name: Louvar
fact: The louvar is a rare open-ocean fish that looks like a tuna but is related to surgeonfish and feeds on jellyfish.

name: Trestles
fact: Trestles near San Clemente, California, is a cobblestone point break that has hosted the World Surf League Finals.

name: Luanda
fact: Luanda, Angola's capital, is a major Atlantic port whose bay is sheltered by the long sand island of Ilha de Luanda.

name: Luderick
fact: The luderick is a common Australian estuary fish that grazes mostly on green algae.

name: Luff
fact: The luff is the forward edge of a sail, and to luff means to turn a sailing boat into the wind so that its sails flap.

name: Lugger
fact: A lugger is a small sailing vessel rigged with lugsails, once widely used for fishing and smuggling around Britain.

name: Lugworm
fact: Lugworms live in U-shaped burrows in sand and mud, and leave coiled casts on the beach at low tide.

name: Lumpsucker
fact: The male lumpsucker, or lumpfish, clings to a rock with a sucker on its belly and guards a pink mass of eggs through the spring tides.

name: Lundy
fact: Lundy is a granite island in the Bristol Channel and the site of Britain's first marine nature reserve.

name: Lungfish
fact: Lungfish have true lungs as well as gills and are the closest living fish relatives of land animals.

name: Lusitania
fact: The Lusitania was torpedoed by a German U-boat off Ireland in 1915 and lies on its side in about 93 metres of water, slowly collapsing.

name: Lusitanian toadfish
fact: The Lusitanian toadfish of Portuguese estuaries hums and 'boat-whistles' from its nest, and larger males even sing in choruses to attract females.

name: Lutefisk
fact: Lutefisk is dried whitefish rehydrated with lye and then boiled, a traditional Scandinavian Christmas dish.

name: Luzon Strait
fact: The Luzon Strait between Taiwan and the Philippines connects the South China Sea with the Pacific Ocean.

name: Lye soaking
fact: Lye soaking rehydrates dried whitefish in an alkali solution, as in the Scandinavian dish lutefisk.

name: Lyngbakr
fact: The lyngbakr is a giant whale-like sea creature from the Norse Orvar-Odds saga that sailors mistook for an island.

name: Lyretail anthias
fact: Lyretail anthias live in large shoals over reefs, and every fish starts life as a female, with the dominant ones later changing into males.

name: Lyttelton
fact: Lyttelton, set in an extinct volcanic crater on New Zealand's South Island, is the main port for Christchurch.

name: Maarten Tromp
fact: Maarten Tromp was a Dutch admiral who destroyed a large Spanish fleet at the Battle of the Downs in 1639.

name: Macaroni penguin
fact: Macaroni penguins are the most numerous penguin and together eat more krill than any other seabird species.

name: Macaronis
fact: Macaronis is a fast left-hand wave in Indonesia's Mentawai Islands, west of Sumatra.

name: Machher jhol
fact: Machher jhol is a light, spiced Bengali fish curry, usually made with freshwater fish such as rohu.

name: Mackerel
fact: Mackerels are fast, striped schooling fish with tiny finlets before the tail; they spoil quickly, so for sushi (saba) they are cured in salt and vinegar.

name: Mackerel icefish
fact: The mackerel icefish has no red blood cells, so its blood runs clear, and it feeds almost entirely on Antarctic krill.

name: Mackerel scad
fact: The mackerel scad is a small schooling jack of tropical waters that is a staple bait and food fish from Hawaii to the Caribbean.

name: Macquarie Island
fact: Macquarie Island is a remote sub-Antarctic island between Tasmania and Antarctica, breeding ground for king penguins and elephant seals.

name: Macquarie Trench
fact: The Macquarie Trench lies south of New Zealand along the Macquarie Ridge, where two tectonic plates meet.

name: Madagascar
fact: Madagascar is the fourth-largest island in the world, and every species of lemur lives only there.

name: Madagascar anemonefish
fact: The Madagascar anemonefish is a clownfish found around Madagascar and the Comoros.

name: Madeira
fact: Madeira is a Portuguese volcanic island in the Atlantic north of the Canaries, famous for its fortified wine and the laurel forests that once covered it.

name: Madrid Protocol
aliases: Protocol on Environmental Protection to the Antarctic Treaty
fact: The Madrid Protocol of 1991 designates Antarctica a natural reserve and bans mining there.

name: Madtom
fact: Madtoms are tiny North American catfish, mostly under 10 centimetres, with venom glands at the base of their pectoral spines that give a painful sting.

name: Maelstrom
fact: A maelstrom is a powerful whirlpool, and the word comes from Dutch and was long linked to the tidal currents off northern Norway.

name: Maerl
fact: Maerl is a free-living coralline seaweed that grows into gravel-like nodules, forming seabed beds that take centuries to build up.

name: Mafia Island
fact: Mafia Island, off Tanzania, has a marine park where whale sharks gather in season.

name: Magadi tilapia
fact: The Magadi tilapia lives in hot, caustic soda lagoons beside Kenya's Lake Magadi, where the water can exceed 35 degrees Celsius and is highly alkaline.

name: Magellan's circumnavigation
fact: Magellan's expedition of 1519 to 1522 was the first to sail around the world, though Magellan died in the Philippines and only one of five ships returned.

name: Magellanic penguin
fact: Magellanic penguins breed in huge colonies along the coasts of Argentina, Chile and the Falkland Islands.

name: Magister armhook squid
fact: The magister armhook squid is an abundant squid of the North Pacific, eaten by seals, seabirds and fish.

name: Magnificent sea anemone
fact: The magnificent sea anemone is a favourite host of clownfish on Indo-Pacific reefs.

name: Mahakam river dolphin
fact: The Mahakam river dolphin is a tiny, critically endangered freshwater population of Irrawaddy dolphins in the Mahakam River of Borneo.

name: Mahé
fact: Mahé is the largest island of the Seychelles and is home to its capital, Victoria.

name: Mahi-mahi
fact: Mahi-mahi, or dorado, is a fast-growing, brilliantly coloured open-ocean fish that is among the fastest swimmers in the sea and a popular restaurant catch.

name: Mahseer
fact: The golden mahseer of Himalayan rivers was the prized game fish of British India and is now endangered.

name: Majestic angelfish
fact: The majestic angelfish is a blue, yellow and orange Indo-Pacific angelfish that grows to about 25 centimetres.

name: Makara
fact: The makara is a sea creature of Hindu mythology with parts of a crocodile and an elephant, and it is the vehicle of the god Varuna.

name: Makassar Strait
fact: The Makassar Strait between Borneo and Sulawesi is deep enough for very large ships and lies along the biological Wallace Line.

name: Mako shark
fact: Makos are widely regarded as the fastest sharks, built for speed with a crescent-shaped tail and a torpedo-shaped body.

name: Makran Trench
fact: The Makran Trench in the Arabian Sea, off Pakistan and Iran, is a shallow trench where the Arabian Plate slides beneath Eurasia.

name: Malaga
fact: Malaga on Spain's Costa del Sol was the birthplace of the painter Pablo Picasso in 1881.

name: Malaspina expedition
fact: The Malaspina expedition of 1789 to 1794 was a Spanish scientific voyage around the Americas and the Pacific.

name: Malaysia
fact: Malaysia has coasts on the Strait of Malacca and the South China Sea, with the Malaysian part of Borneo facing the Pacific side.

name: Maldive anemonefish
fact: The Maldive anemonefish is a clownfish found around the Maldives and Sri Lanka.

name: Maldives
fact: The Maldives are about a thousand coral islands grouped into atolls, and the country is the lowest-lying on Earth.

name: Male
fact: Male is the capital of the Maldives and one of the most densely populated cities on Earth.

name: Malibu
fact: Malibu's Surfrider Beach in California helped launch the 1950s surf craze and inspired the novel and film Gidget.

name: Mallorca
fact: Mallorca is the largest of Spain's Balearic Islands, and its Serra de Tramuntana mountains are a World Heritage Site.

name: Malpelo Island
fact: Malpelo, a bare rock in the Colombian Pacific, is a sanctuary where hundreds of hammerheads and silky sharks gather around its steep walls.

name: Malta
fact: Malta's prehistoric stone temples are older than both Stonehenge and the pyramids of Egypt.

name: Mami Wata
fact: Mami Wata is a water spirit worshipped across West, Central and Southern Africa and the African diaspora, often pictured as a mermaid-like woman.

name: Man-of-war
fact: A man-of-war was a large armed sailing ship of a navy, from which the name for the jellyfish-like Portuguese man o' war was borrowed.

name: Man-of-war fish
fact: The man-of-war fish lives among the deadly tentacles of the Portuguese man o' war, nibbling on them while sheltering from predators.

name: Manannan mac Lir
fact: Manannan mac Lir is the Irish sea god and son of Lir, associated with the Isle of Man, which is said to be named after him.

name: Manatee
fact: Manatees are gentle plant-eaters whose closest living relatives on land are elephants.

name: Manatee grass
fact: Manatee grass has round, noodle-like leaves and is grazed by manatees and sea turtles in the Caribbean.

name: Manchester Ship Canal
fact: The Manchester Ship Canal, opened in 1894, is about 58 kilometres long and turned Manchester into an inland seaport.

name: Mandarinfish
fact: The mandarinfish is one of only two vertebrates known to make a true blue pigment, and it has no scales but a bitter, toxic coating.

name: Manefish
fact: Manefish are deep-sea fish with a tall, mane-like dorsal fin, and they are sometimes found close to siphonophores and jellyfish.

name: Mangalore
fact: Mangalore in Karnataka, India, has a major port that handles much of the country's coffee and iron ore trade.

name: Mangrove
fact: Mangroves are trees that grow in salt water along tropical shores, with tangled stilt roots that trap mud and shelter young fish.

name: Mangrove apple
fact: Sonneratia alba is a pioneer mangrove whose flowers open at night and are pollinated by bats and moths.

name: Mangrove fern
fact: The mangrove fern is a tall fern that grows at the edges of mangrove forests and can reach several metres in height.

name: Mangrove horseshoe crab
fact: The mangrove horseshoe crab can carry tetrodotoxin and has caused fatal poisonings when eaten in South-East Asia.

name: Mangrove jack
fact: The mangrove jack is a snapper that lurks among mangrove roots in Australia and Asia when young and moves offshore to reefs as it matures.

name: Mangrove killifish
fact: The mangrove killifish can live for weeks out of water inside rotting logs, flipping itself across land with its tail, and most are self-fertilising hermaphrodites.

name: Mangrove monitor
fact: The mangrove monitor is a lizard of Australia and the western Pacific that swims through mangrove swamps and has a salt-excreting gland in its nose.

name: Mangrove tree crab
fact: The mangrove tree crab climbs the roots and branches of mangroves, where it feeds on leaves.

name: Mangrove tunicate
fact: The mangrove tunicate is the natural source of trabectedin, a compound developed into an anti-cancer drug.

name: Mangrove whipray
fact: The mangrove whipray spends its youth in mangroves and lagoons of the Indo-Pacific and has a white-spotted dark back.

name: Manila Bay
fact: Manila Bay is a large natural harbour on the Philippine island of Luzon, known for its sunsets and the 1898 battle fought there.

name: Manila clam
fact: The Manila clam is the most farmed clam in the world and reached North America by accident, mixed in with oyster seed shipped from Japan.

name: Manila Trench
fact: The Manila Trench lies west of Luzon in the South China Sea and reaches about 5,400 metres deep.

name: Manta ray
fact: Manta rays filter plankton through their gills and somersault repeatedly to stay in a dense patch of food.

name: Manta trawl
fact: A manta trawl is a net with a wide mouth towed along the sea surface to collect floating microplastics.

name: Mantis shrimp
fact: A mantis shrimp strikes with the acceleration of a bullet and sees with up to 16 types of light-sensing cell, compared with our three.

name: Manu Bay
fact: Manu Bay at Raglan in New Zealand is one of the longest left-hand point breaks in the world and appeared in the 1966 film The Endless Summer.

name: Manzanillo
fact: Manzanillo in the state of Colima is Mexico's busiest container port.

name: Maori octopus
fact: The Maori octopus is a large octopus of New Zealand and southern Australian waters.

name: Map puffer
fact: The map puffer is named for the maze of dark lines over its body, which look like the contour lines on a map.

name: Maputo
fact: Maputo, the capital of Mozambique, stands on Delagoa Bay and was called Lourenco Marques until 1976.

name: Mar del Plata
fact: Mar del Plata is Argentina's main seaside resort and its biggest fishing port.

name: Marathon swimming
fact: Marathon swimming is open water swimming over very long distances, such as crossing the English Channel.

name: Marble trout
fact: The marble trout of Slovenia and northern Italy has a marbled pattern instead of spots and can grow to well over a metre long.

name: Marbled electric ray
fact: The marbled electric ray of the eastern Atlantic and Mediterranean stuns its prey with powerful electric shocks.

name: Marbled lungfish
fact: The marbled lungfish breathes air with paired lungs and has one of the largest genomes known, roughly 40 times the size of a human's.

name: Marbled murrelet
fact: The marbled murrelet fishes at sea but nests on mossy branches high in old-growth conifers, sometimes far inland; its nest was not found until 1974.

name: Marbled rockcod
fact: The marbled rockcod is an Antarctic fish with antifreeze proteins in its blood, heavily overfished in the 1970s.

name: Marbled sea snake
fact: The marbled sea snake feeds almost entirely on fish eggs and has tiny fangs compared with most other sea snakes.

name: Marc Mitscher
fact: Marc Mitscher led the American fast carrier task force in the Pacific in the Second World War.

name: Marcus Agrippa
fact: Marcus Agrippa was the admiral of Octavian who defeated Antony and Cleopatra at the Battle of Actium in 31 BC.

name: Margaret River Main Break
fact: The Main Break at Margaret River in Western Australia is a powerful reef wave that has hosted the Margaret River Pro.

name: Mariana snailfish
fact: The Mariana snailfish, named in 2017, has been collected from nearly 8,000 metres and has a see-through pink body with no scales.

name: Mariana Trench
fact: The Mariana Trench holds the Challenger Deep, the deepest known point in the ocean at about 10,935 metres.

name: Marianas Trench Marine National Monument
fact: The Marianas Trench Marine National Monument protects the waters and seabed around the deepest trench on Earth and its mud volcanoes.

name: Marie-Galante
fact: Marie-Galante is a round island of Guadeloupe that was once covered in sugar mills and is known for its rum.

name: Marie Tharp
fact: Marie Tharp drew the first map of the entire ocean floor and spotted the rift valley running down the Mid-Atlantic Ridge, key evidence for continental drift.

name: Marine archaeologist
fact: Marine archaeologists excavate and study shipwrecks and drowned settlements.

name: Marine biologist
fact: Marine biologists study life in the sea, from plankton to whales.

name: Marine Conservation Society
fact: The Marine Conservation Society is a British charity founded in 1983 that runs the Good Fish Guide and the Great British Beach Clean.

name: Marine engineer
fact: A marine engineer runs and maintains a ship's engines and machinery.

name: Marine flatworm
fact: Marine flatworms cut into pieces can regrow into complete animals, and some are decorated as brightly as the nudibranchs they mimic.

name: Marine geologist
fact: Marine geologists study the rocks, sediments and structure of the ocean floor.

name: Marine heatwave
fact: A marine heatwave is a long period of unusually warm sea temperatures that can kill kelp, corals and fish.

name: Marine iguana
fact: The marine iguana of the Galápagos is the only lizard that feeds in the sea, grazing algae underwater and sneezing out salt.

name: Marine Mammal Commission
fact: The Marine Mammal Commission is an independent United States agency created by the Marine Mammal Protection Act of 1972.

name: Marine mammal trainer
fact: Marine mammal trainers work with dolphins, seals and other sea mammals in aquariums and research programmes.

name: Marine otter
fact: The marine otter, or chungungo, of Chile and Peru is the smallest marine mammal, weighing about 4 kilograms, and lives along rocky shores.

name: Marine snow
fact: Marine snow is the steady fall of dead plankton, faecal pellets and other debris from the upper ocean to the deep seafloor.

name: Marine Stewardship Council
fact: The Marine Stewardship Council runs a certification scheme that labels sustainably caught wild fish with a blue tick.

name: Marine virus
fact: Marine viruses are the most numerous biological entities in the sea, around 10 million in every millilitre of seawater, and they kill about a fifth of the ocean's microbes every day.

name: Marion Island
fact: Marion Island is a South African sub-Antarctic island with a weather station and large colonies of seabirds and seals.

name: Market squid
fact: Market squid gather in vast spawning schools off California, supporting one of the state's most valuable fisheries.

name: Marlin
fact: Marlins are big, spear-nosed billfish among the fastest fish in the ocean; Hemingway's The Old Man and the Sea is the story of a fight with a giant marlin.

name: Marlinspike
fact: A marlinspike is a pointed metal tool used by sailors to open the strands of rope for splicing.

name: Maroon clownfish
fact: The maroon clownfish is the largest clownfish, up to about 17 centimetres, with cheek spines and a female far bigger and more aggressive than her mate.

name: MARPOL
aliases: International Convention for the Prevention of Pollution from Ships
fact: MARPOL is the main international treaty against pollution from ships, adopted in 1973 and modified in 1978.

name: Marquesas Islands
fact: The Marquesas are rugged volcanic islands in French Polynesia without protecting reefs, where the painter Paul Gauguin spent his last years.

name: Marrella
fact: Marrella is one of the most common fossils of the Cambrian Burgess Shale, an arthropod with long, backward-pointing head spines.

name: Marron
fact: The marron of Western Australia is one of the largest freshwater crayfish, reaching more than 2 kilograms, and is farmed for restaurants.

name: Marseille
fact: Marseille was founded around 600 BC by Greek colonists from Phocaea and is France's largest port.

name: Marshall Islands
fact: The Marshall Islands are 29 low coral atolls in the central Pacific, including Bikini and Enewetak, where the United States tested nuclear weapons.

name: Martha's Vineyard
fact: Martha's Vineyard is a Massachusetts island south of Cape Cod and a popular summer retreat.

name: Martinique
fact: Martinique is a French island where the eruption of Mont Pelée destroyed the town of Saint-Pierre in 1902.

name: Mary Celeste
fact: The Mary Celeste was found drifting and abandoned in the Atlantic in 1872, and her crew and passengers were never found.

name: Mary Read
fact: Mary Read was an English pirate who disguised herself as a man for much of her life and sailed in Calico Jack's crew.

name: Mary Rose
fact: Henry VIII's warship Mary Rose sank in the Solent in 1545 and was raised in 1982; its hull is now displayed in Portsmouth.

name: Masirah Island
fact: Masirah is an Omani island that hosts one of the largest nesting populations of loggerhead turtles in the world.

name: Masked angelfish
fact: The masked angelfish lives only on the deep reefs of the Northwestern Hawaiian Islands and is pure white with a black mask as a female.

name: Masked booby
fact: The masked booby plunge-dives into the sea from a height to catch fish and flying fish.

name: Masked butterflyfish
fact: The masked butterflyfish lives only in the Red Sea and Gulf of Aden, where it is usually seen in pairs sheltering under table corals.

name: Masked crab
fact: The masked crab buries itself in sand and breathes through a snorkel made of its two long antennae pressed together.

name: Massachusetts Bay
fact: Massachusetts Bay is the broad bay on the Gulf of Maine that holds Boston Harbor and, at its mouth, Stellwagen Bank.

name: Massawa
fact: Massawa is Eritrea's main Red Sea port and sits on a coral island linked to the mainland by causeways.

name: Mast
fact: A mast is the tall vertical pole that holds up a ship's sails and rigging.

name: Master and Commander
aliases: Master and Commander The Far Side of the World
fact: Master and Commander is the 1969 first novel of Patrick O'Brian's Aubrey and Maturin series, and Peter Weir's 2003 film is based on the series.

name: Masu salmon
fact: The masu or cherry salmon is the Pacific salmon of Japan, Korea and the Russian Far East, and some populations never leave their rivers.

name: Matamata
fact: The matamata looks like a pile of bark and leaves on the river bed and gulps down fish by suddenly opening its mouth to create suction.

name: Match racing
fact: Match racing is a form of sailing in which two boats race directly against each other, as in the America's Cup.

name: Matira Beach
fact: Matira Beach is the main public beach on Bora Bora in French Polynesia, a long white strip with a shallow lagoon.

name: Matjes
fact: Matjes is young, fat herring lightly salt-cured, a speciality of the Netherlands, Germany and Scandinavia.

name: Matthew Flinders
fact: Matthew Flinders was the first to sail right around Australia, from 1801 to 1803, and popularised the continent's name.

name: Matthew Fontaine Maury
fact: Matthew Fontaine Maury, known as the Pathfinder of the Seas, compiled ships' logs into the first charts of ocean winds and currents in the 1840s and 1850s.

name: Matthew Perry
fact: Commodore Matthew Perry led a United States naval squadron into Tokyo Bay in 1853, pressing Japan to open its ports.

name: Maui
fact: Maui is the Hawaiian island whose waters host breeding humpback whales each winter.

name: Maui Ocean Center
fact: Maui Ocean Center, opened in 1998, is a Hawaiian marine park and aquarium built around the sea life of the Hawaiian Islands.

name: Māui dolphin
fact: The Māui dolphin, a subspecies of Hector's dolphin off New Zealand's North Island, is among the rarest dolphins with only around 50 adults left.

name: Mauna Kea
fact: Measured from its base on the Pacific seabed to its summit, Mauna Kea in Hawaii rises about 10,200 metres, taller than Everest above sea level.

name: Maurice Ewing
fact: Maurice Ewing founded the Lamont Geological Observatory and led research into the structure of the ocean floor.

name: Mauritania
fact: Mauritania's Atlantic coast includes the Banc d'Arguin National Park, where millions of migratory birds spend the winter.

name: Mauritius
fact: Mauritius was the only home of the dodo, a flightless bird that was extinct by the late seventeenth century.

name: Mauve stinger
fact: The mauve stinger glows when disturbed at night and has caused mass stingings on Mediterranean beaches; one swarm wiped out a salmon farm in Northern Ireland.

name: Mavericks
fact: Mavericks breaks about half a mile offshore near Half Moon Bay, California, and produces huge cold-water winter waves.

name: Mawson Sea
fact: The Mawson Sea off Antarctica is named after the Australian explorer Douglas Mawson.

name: Maximilian von Spee
fact: Maximilian von Spee commanded the German East Asia Squadron and died when it was destroyed at the Falkland Islands in 1914.

name: Maya Bay
fact: Maya Bay on Ko Phi Phi Leh in Thailand starred in the film The Beach, and was closed to visitors from 2018 until January 2022 to let its coral recover.

name: Mayflower voyage
fact: The Mayflower carried about 100 passengers from Plymouth, England, in 1620 and reached Cape Cod after crossing the Atlantic.

name: Mayotte
fact: Mayotte is a French island in the Comoros archipelago that is encircled by a large coral lagoon.

name: Mayreau
fact: Mayreau is a tiny Grenadine island with no airport and only a few hundred residents.

name: Mazatlan
fact: Mazatlan on Mexico's Pacific coast is known for its long seafront promenade and its big annual carnival.

name: Mazu
fact: Mazu is the Chinese goddess of the sea who protects sailors and fishermen, widely worshipped along the coasts of China and Taiwan.

name: Mbu puffer
fact: The mbu puffer of the Congo River is a freshwater giant that can reach about 67 centimetres long.

name: Mbuna
fact: Mbuna are the colourful, rock-dwelling cichlids of Lake Malawi, a lake that holds hundreds of cichlid species.

name: McCulloch's anemonefish
fact: McCulloch's anemonefish is a dark clownfish with a white face found only at Lord Howe and Norfolk Islands, one of the most restricted ranges of any clownfish.

name: McMurdo Sound
fact: McMurdo Sound in Antarctica is named after Lieutenant Archibald McMurdo of HMS Terror and lies off the main US research station.

name: Meagre
fact: The meagre is a big croaker that forms spawning groups and makes a loud drumming noise, audible from boats.

name: Medaka
fact: The medaka, or Japanese rice fish, is a 3-centimetre fish that became the first vertebrate to mate and lay eggs in space, aboard the space shuttle in 1994.

name: Mediterranean damselfish
fact: The Mediterranean damselfish is the only native damselfish in the Mediterranean, a dark fish whose juveniles are brilliant blue, common in shoals above rocks.

name: Mediterranean monk seal
fact: The Mediterranean monk seal gives birth in sea caves and numbers fewer than a thousand, most of them in Greece and off Mauritania.

name: Mediterranean moray
fact: The Mediterranean moray was a Roman delicacy, kept in seaside fish ponds by wealthy Romans.

name: Mediterranean mussel
fact: The Mediterranean mussel has spread to coasts around the world and is widely farmed for food.

name: Mediterranean parrotfish
fact: The Mediterranean parrotfish is the only native parrotfish in the Mediterranean, prized by the Romans, and is spreading north as the sea warms.

name: Mediterranean Sea
fact: The Mediterranean is almost landlocked, connected to the Atlantic only through the Strait of Gibraltar, and evaporates far more water than its rivers bring in.

name: Mediterranean spearfish
fact: The Mediterranean spearfish is a streamlined billfish whose slender build suits fast open-water hunting.

name: Megalodon
fact: Megalodon, a shark perhaps 15 to 20 metres long, died out roughly 3.6 million years ago, and its teeth are the size of a human hand.

name: Megamouth shark
fact: The megamouth shark was unknown to science until 1976, when one was hauled up tangled in a US Navy sea anchor off Hawaii.

name: Megrim
fact: The megrim is a slender, left-eyed flatfish of deep European slopes that was long overlooked by British diners and sold mostly to Spain.

name: Mekong dolphin
fact: The Mekong dolphin is a critically endangered freshwater population of Irrawaddy dolphins that lives in a stretch of the Mekong between Cambodia and Laos.

name: Mekong freshwater stingray
fact: The Mekong freshwater stingray lives in the Mekong river system of south-east Asia.

name: Mekong giant catfish
fact: The Mekong giant catfish is one of the largest freshwater fish on Earth, reaching about 3 metres and 300 kilograms, and is critically endangered.

name: Melilla
fact: Melilla is a Spanish port city on the North African coast and has been Spanish since 1497.

name: Melon-headed whale
fact: Melon-headed whales travel in pods of hundreds and are actually dolphins, despite their name.

name: Menai Strait
fact: The Menai Strait separates the island of Anglesey from mainland Wales and is crossed by Telford's suspension bridge.

name: Menhaden
fact: Menhaden are oily filter-feeding fish of the American Atlantic coast, caught in huge numbers for fish oil and fish meal.

name: Menorca
fact: Menorca is the quieter, easternmost island of the Balearics and is a UNESCO biosphere reserve.

name: Mermaid's glove
fact: Mermaid's glove is a branching sponge of North Atlantic shores whose finger-like lobes give it its name.

name: Mermaid's wineglass
fact: Mermaid's wineglass is a single-celled green alga shaped like a tiny goblet that grows several centimetres tall.

name: Merrow
fact: The merrow is the mermaid of Irish folklore, said to wear a magical cap that lets her breathe underwater.

name: Mersin
fact: Mersin is one of Turkey's main Mediterranean ports, on the Cilician coast.

name: Mesoamerican Reef
fact: The Mesoamerican Reef runs about 1,000 kilometres from Mexico's Yucatán to Honduras and is the largest barrier reef in the Western Hemisphere.

name: Messmate pipefish
fact: The messmate pipefish is a slender, banded pipefish of Indo-Pacific reefs and sandy flats.

name: Meteor
fact: The German ship Meteor criss-crossed the South Atlantic from 1925 to 1927 using echo sounding to produce the first detailed picture of a whole ocean basin's floor.

name: Meteotsunami
fact: A meteotsunami is a tsunami-like wave caused by a rapid change in air pressure, such as from a storm front, rather than an earthquake.

name: Mexican golden trout
fact: The Mexican golden trout lives in mountain streams of the Sierra Madre Occidental and is one of the southernmost native trout in North America.

name: Mexico
fact: Mexico has a long Pacific coast, as well as coasts on the Gulf of Mexico and the Caribbean Sea.

name: Miami
fact: The Port of Miami on Biscayne Bay calls itself the cruise capital of the world and handles more cruise passengers than any other port.

name: Miami Beach
fact: Miami Beach lies on a barrier island in Florida and is known for the Art Deco buildings of its South Beach district.

name: Michiel de Ruyter
fact: Michiel de Ruyter was the Dutch admiral who led the daring raid up the River Medway in 1667.

name: Federated States of Micronesia
fact: The Federated States of Micronesia are more than 600 islands scattered across the western Pacific.

name: Mid-Atlantic Ridge
fact: The Mid-Atlantic Ridge is a chain of underwater volcanoes where new seafloor forms as Europe and Africa drift away from the Americas.

name: Mid-ocean ridge
fact: The mid-ocean ridge is a continuous chain of underwater mountains, about 65,000 kilometres long, making it the longest mountain range on Earth.

name: Middle America Trench
fact: The Middle America Trench runs along the Pacific coast of Central America from Mexico to Costa Rica and reaches about 6,600 metres deep.

name: Middleton Reef
fact: Middleton Reef is a remote coral reef in the Tasman Sea, north of Lord Howe Island, with several shipwrecks.

name: Midnight parrotfish
fact: The midnight parrotfish is a dark blue Caribbean parrotfish with bright blue markings on its head that often grazes in schools with other species.

name: Midshipman
fact: The plainfin midshipman has rows of photophores like the buttons on a naval uniform, and the humming of the males keeps houseboat residents awake in Sausalito.

name: Midway Atoll
fact: Midway Atoll lies near the end of the Hawaiian chain and gave its name to the 1942 battle that turned the Pacific War.

name: Milkfish
fact: Milkfish is the national fish of the Philippines, farmed in coastal ponds for centuries and eaten despite its many fine bones.

name: Milky mangrove
fact: The milky mangrove has a sap that can badly irritate the eyes, which earned it the nickname blind-your-eye.

name: Milky sea
fact: A milky sea is a rare sight in which the ocean glows white over a huge area at night, probably from luminous bacteria, and it can even be seen from satellites.

name: Milos
fact: Milos is the Greek island where the famous statue of Venus de Milo was found in 1820.

name: Mimic filefish
fact: The mimic filefish copies the look of the poisonous saddled toby so closely that predators leave it alone, though it is not toxic itself.

name: Mimic octopus
fact: The mimic octopus of Indonesia impersonates lionfish, flatfish and sea snakes by changing its shape, colour and the way it moves.

name: Mindanao Current
fact: The Mindanao Current flows south along the east coast of the Philippines, carrying warm Pacific water towards Indonesia.

name: Minelayer
fact: A minelayer is a ship built to lay sea mines in advance of an enemy fleet or to defend a harbour.
