name: Minerva Reefs
fact: The Minerva Reefs are two remote atolls south of Fiji, claimed by Tonga, that briefly hosted a self-declared micronation in 1972.

name: Minesweeper
fact: Minesweepers clear sea mines and are often built with wooden or plastic hulls so that magnetic mines do not detect them.

name: Minke whale
fact: Minke whales are the smallest of the rorquals and the main target of whaling by Norway, Japan and Iceland today.

name: Minot's Ledge Lighthouse
fact: Minot's Ledge Lighthouse off Massachusetts flashes in a 1-4-3 pattern, earning it the nickname the I Love You Light.

name: Mir
fact: The Russian submersibles Mir-1 and Mir-2 filmed the Titanic wreck for James Cameron's 1997 film and in 2007 planted a flag on the sea floor at the North Pole.

name: Mirocaris fortunata
fact: Mirocaris fortunata is a small shrimp that swarms around hydrothermal vents on the Mid-Atlantic Ridge.

name: Missile boat
fact: Missile boats are small, fast craft carrying anti-ship missiles, first used to dramatic effect when Egyptian-launched missiles sank the Israeli destroyer Eilat in 1967.

name: Mission Blue
fact: Mission Blue was founded by Sylvia Earle in 2009 and promotes marine protected areas it calls Hope Spots.

name: Mizzen
fact: The mizzen is the mast behind the main mast on a ship with two or more masts, and the sail set on it.

name: Mljet
fact: Mljet is a Croatian island whose western end is a national park with two saltwater lakes.

name: Moana
fact: Moana is Disney's 2016 animated film, directed by Ron Clements and John Musker, about a Polynesian girl who sails across the ocean to save her island.

name: Mobile Bay
fact: Mobile Bay is the Alabama inlet of the Gulf of Mexico, where a famous naval battle was fought in 1864.

name: Moby-Dick
fact: Moby-Dick is Herman Melville's 1851 novel about Captain Ahab's obsessive hunt for a white sperm whale.

name: Mogadishu
fact: Mogadishu is the capital of Somalia and has been a trading port on the Indian Ocean since medieval times.

name: Mohéli
fact: Mohéli is the smallest of the Comoros islands and has a marine park where green turtles nest.

name: Mohinga
fact: Mohinga is a Burmese fish soup with rice noodles, often described as the national dish of Myanmar.

name: Molasses Reef
fact: Molasses Reef off Key Largo, Florida, lies inside the Florida Keys National Marine Sanctuary and is one of the most popular dive and snorkel sites in the Keys.

name: Mole crab
fact: Mole crabs burrow backwards into the sand of surf beaches and filter food from the receding waves with their feathery antennae.

name: Molly
fact: Mollies are hardy livebearers from Central America that thrive in anything from fresh to fully salty water.

name: Molly miller
fact: The molly miller is a small blenny that lives in tide pools and on shallow rocky shores of the Atlantic.

name: Molokini
fact: Molokini is a crescent-shaped volcanic crater off Maui whose sheltered inner reef is one of Hawaii's most visited snorkelling spots.

name: Molucca Sea
fact: The Molucca Sea lies between Sulawesi and the Maluku Islands, the Spice Islands that drew European traders to Indonesia.

name: Mombasa
fact: Mombasa is Kenya's main port, and Fort Jesus, built by the Portuguese in the 1590s, guards its old harbour.

name: Mona Island
fact: Mona Island lies in the Mona Passage between Puerto Rico and Hispaniola and is a nature reserve with giant Mona iguanas.

name: Mona Passage
fact: The Mona Passage between Hispaniola and Puerto Rico is a main route for ships running between the Atlantic and the Panama Canal.

name: Monitor
fact: Monitors were low-freeboard warships with a few big guns, named for USS Monitor of 1862, and they were used for shore bombardment.

name: Monk seal
fact: Monk seals are the only seals adapted to warm tropical and subtropical waters, and only two species survive today.

name: Monkfish
fact: Monkfish lie flattened on the seabed and twitch a fleshy lure on their heads to draw fish into their enormous mouths.

name: Monrovia
fact: Monrovia is the capital and main port of Liberia, on the Atlantic coast of West Africa.

name: Montauk Point Lighthouse
fact: Montauk Point Lighthouse on Long Island, New York, was authorised during George Washington's presidency and is among the oldest in the country.

name: Montecristo
fact: Montecristo is a small Italian island that gave its name to Alexandre Dumas's novel The Count of Monte Cristo.

name: Monterey Bay
fact: Monterey Bay in California lies above a submarine canyon as deep as the Grand Canyon and is a sanctuary for sea otters and whales.

name: Monterey Bay Aquarium
fact: Monterey Bay Aquarium opened in 1984 in a former sardine cannery on Cannery Row, California, and is famed for its giant kelp forest exhibit.

name: Monterey Bay National Marine Sanctuary
fact: Monterey Bay National Marine Sanctuary stretches along central California and shelters kelp forests, sea otters and a submarine canyon deeper than the Grand Canyon.

name: Monterey Canyon
fact: Monterey Canyon off California is a submarine canyon comparable in scale to the Grand Canyon, plunging to more than 3,000 metres.

name: Monterey Spanish mackerel
fact: The Monterey Spanish mackerel is named after Monterey Bay in California, where it was once abundant.

name: Montevideo
fact: Montevideo, Uruguay's capital and main port, lies on the Río de la Plata near where the Graf Spee was scuttled in 1939.

name: Montipora
fact: Montipora corals grow as plates, crusts and branches and are popular in reef aquariums for their bright colours.

name: Montserrat
fact: Montserrat is called the Emerald Isle of the Caribbean, and its Soufrière Hills volcano buried the capital, Plymouth, in the 1990s.

name: Moon jellyfish
fact: The moon jellyfish is see-through with four horseshoe-shaped gonads visible through its bell, and its sting is too weak to hurt most people.

name: Moon snail
fact: Moon snails plough through sand on a huge foot, drilling neat round holes in clam shells, and lay their eggs in a collar of sand.

name: Moon wrasse
fact: The moon wrasse, or lunar wrasse, is a green-and-blue wrasse with a yellow crescent on the tail, common on reefs across the Indo-Pacific.

name: Moonlight gourami
fact: The moonlight gourami is a silvery fish of Southeast Asia that gulps air at the surface with a labyrinth organ.

name: Moorea
fact: Moorea is a heart-shaped volcanic island in French Polynesia, a short ferry ride from Tahiti.

name: Moorish idol
fact: The Moorish idol, with its long trailing dorsal fin, is notoriously hard to keep in aquariums because it feeds mainly on sponges.

name: Moqueca
fact: Moqueca is a Brazilian fish stew, made in the state of Bahia with coconut milk and palm oil and in Espirito Santo with tomato and annatto.

name: Moray eel
fact: Moray eels have a second set of jaws in their throat that shoots forward to drag prey down the gullet.

name: Moreton Bay
fact: Moreton Bay lies off Brisbane in Australia and is a marine park with dugongs, turtles and great sand islands.

name: Morocco
fact: Morocco has coasts on both the Atlantic Ocean and the Mediterranean Sea, and sits just across the Strait of Gibraltar from Spain.

name: Morro Castle
fact: The Morro Castle was an American liner that caught fire off New Jersey in 1934, killing 137 people.

name: Morwong
fact: Morwongs are a family of reef fish of the Southern Hemisphere, caught commercially and by anglers off Australia and New Zealand.

name: Mosasaur
fact: Mosasaurs were giant sea lizards related to monitor lizards and snakes that ruled the late Cretaceous seas until the asteroid struck.

name: Moses sole
fact: The Moses sole of the Red Sea oozes a milky, soap-like toxin from its fins that makes sharks spit it out, and the toxin was studied as a shark repellent.

name: Mosquitofish
fact: The mosquitofish was released worldwide to eat mosquito larvae and has instead wiped out native fish and frogs from Australia to Spain.

name: Mosshead warbonnet
fact: The mosshead warbonnet is a small north Pacific fish with a crest of branching, moss-like tentacles on its head.

name: Mote Aquarium
fact: Mote Aquarium in Sarasota, Florida, grew out of a laboratory founded in 1955 by the shark scientist Eugenie Clark.

name: Motor torpedo boat
fact: Motor torpedo boats were small, fast, wooden or light-alloy craft that attacked larger ships with torpedoes in the Second World War.

name: Mototi octopus
fact: The mototi octopus is a small Indo-Pacific octopus that lives on shallow, silty seabeds.

name: Moules marinieres
fact: Moules marinieres is a French dish of mussels steamed in white wine with shallots and parsley.

name: Moustache conger
fact: The moustache conger is an Indo-Pacific eel named for the whisker-like flaps above its mouth and can grow longer than a metre.

name: Mozambique
fact: Mozambique has about 2,500 kilometres of Indian Ocean coastline, one of the longest in Africa.

name: Mozambique Channel
fact: The Mozambique Channel separates Madagascar from the African mainland, and the coelacanth was found alive in the Comoros at its northern end.

name: Mozambique Current
fact: The Mozambique Current flows south through the Mozambique Channel in a chain of large eddies and helps feed the Agulhas Current.

name: Mozambique tilapia
fact: The Mozambique tilapia can tolerate salt water as well as fresh, which has helped it spread to rivers and coasts around the world.

name: Mozuku
fact: Mozuku is a slimy brown seaweed farmed in Okinawa and eaten with vinegar.

name: Estonia
fact: The ferry Estonia sank in a Baltic storm in September 1994 with the loss of 852 lives, and lies on the seabed at about 80 metres.

name: Muckle Flugga Lighthouse
fact: Muckle Flugga Lighthouse in the Shetland Islands, first lit in 1858, is the northernmost lighthouse in the United Kingdom.

name: Mud crab
fact: The giant mud crab of mangrove estuaries has claws strong enough to crack a mussel shell or a careless finger, and is the crab in Singapore chilli crab.

name: Mud lobster
fact: The mud lobster of Indo-Pacific mangroves builds volcano-shaped mounds of mud over a metre high, which other mangrove animals use as homes.

name: Mudskipper
fact: Mudskippers are fish that walk and skip across mud flats, breathe through their skin, and retreat into burrows they dig in the mud.

name: Muertos Trough
fact: The Muertos Trough is a seabed trench in the Caribbean, south of Puerto Rico and Hispaniola.

name: Muizenberg Beach
fact: Muizenberg Beach near Cape Town is known for its colourful Victorian-style bathing huts and its gentle, beginner-friendly surf.

name: Mull of Galloway Lighthouse
fact: Mull of Galloway Lighthouse, built by Robert Stevenson in 1830, marks the southernmost point of Scotland.

name: Mullaghmore Head
fact: Mullaghmore Head in County Sligo, Ireland, breaks into giant slab waves in winter swells and is Ireland's best-known big-wave spot.

name: Mullet
fact: Mullet feed on algae and detritus in estuaries and mangrove creeks and are famous for leaping clear of the water for no obvious reason.

name: Mulloway
fact: The mulloway is a large, silvery Australian fish, long prized by anglers, that can grow to well over a metre.

name: Multibeam echosounder
fact: A multibeam echosounder sends a fan of sound beams beneath a ship to map a wide strip of the seabed at once.

name: Mumbai
fact: Mumbai on the Arabian Sea is India's gateway city, where the Gateway of India arch was completed in 1924, and the nearby Nhava Sheva port is the country's biggest for containers.

name: Mundaka
fact: Mundaka in Spain's Basque Country is a left-hand river-mouth wave in the Urdaibai estuary, often called the best in Europe.

name: Mundra
fact: Mundra in Gujarat, India, is the country's largest privately owned commercial port.

name: Munk's devil ray
fact: Munk's devil rays gather in schools of thousands off Baja California and the Galápagos and leap metres into the air, landing with a slap.

name: Murex
fact: Murex are spiny sea snails whose glands gave the ancient Phoenicians the precious purple dye of Tyre, worn by emperors.

name: Murray cod
fact: The Murray cod is Australia's largest freshwater fish, growing well over a metre in the Murray-Darling rivers.

name: Musashi
fact: The battleship Musashi, sister of the Yamato, was sunk in the Sibuyan Sea in 1944 and found by Paul Allen's team in 2015 more than 1,000 metres down.

name: Muscat
fact: Muscat, the capital of Oman, has been a seafaring port on the Gulf of Oman for many centuries.

name: Mushroom coral
fact: Mushroom corals are single large polyps that live unattached on the sea floor and can creep slowly across the sand.

name: Muskellunge
fact: The muskellunge, 'fish of ten thousand casts', is the largest pike and can top 1.5 metres in the lakes of the Great Lakes region.

name: Musky octopus
fact: The musky octopus of the Mediterranean gives off a distinct musky smell and has a single row of suckers on each arm.

name: Mussau Trench
fact: The Mussau Trench north of Papua New Guinea is a young, short trench reaching about 7,000 metres deep.

name: Mussel
fact: Mussels anchor themselves to rocks with tough byssal threads, which have inspired new surgical glues.

name: Mustard hill coral
fact: Mustard hill coral forms yellow-brown mounds and is one of the most common reef-building corals of the Caribbean.

name: Mustique
fact: Mustique is a small privately owned island in the Grenadines that is popular with celebrities.

name: Mutiny on the Bounty
fact: Mutiny on the Bounty is a 1932 novel by Charles Nordhoff and James Norman Hall, and the 1935 film starred Charles Laughton as Captain Bligh.

name: Mutton snapper
fact: The mutton snapper is a large Caribbean snapper with a black spot on its side and blue lines on its face, prized for the table.

name: MV Derbyshire
fact: The bulk carrier Derbyshire, the largest British ship ever lost at sea, went down in a typhoon in 1980 with 44 people and was found in 1994 about 4,200 metres down.

name: MS Prinsendam
fact: The Prinsendam caught fire in the Gulf of Alaska in 1980, and all 520 people aboard were rescued before she sank.

name: MS Stockholm
fact: The Stockholm was the Swedish liner whose bow collided with the Andrea Doria off Nantucket in 1956.

name: Myanmar
fact: Myanmar has a long coastline on the Bay of Bengal and the Andaman Sea.

name: Mykonos
fact: Mykonos is a Cycladic island famous for its whitewashed windmills and lively nightlife.

name: Myrtle Beach
fact: Myrtle Beach is the centre of South Carolina's Grand Strand, a roughly 60-mile stretch of continuous beach resorts.

name: Myrtoan Sea
fact: The Myrtoan Sea is the part of the Aegean between the Cyclades and the eastern coast of the Peloponnese.

name: Mystic Aquarium
fact: Mystic Aquarium in Connecticut opened in 1973 and is known for its beluga whales.

name: Nacala
fact: Nacala in Mozambique has one of the deepest natural harbours on the east coast of Africa.

name: Nagoya
fact: The Port of Nagoya is Japan's largest port by total cargo handled.

name: Namibia
fact: Namibia's Atlantic coast is the Skeleton Coast, where the Namib Desert meets the sea.

name: Nankai Trough
fact: The Nankai Trough off southern Japan is a subduction trench feared for the huge earthquakes it produces roughly every 100 to 150 years.

name: Nantucket
fact: Nantucket is a small island off Cape Cod that was one of the leading whaling ports of the 1800s.

name: Naples
fact: Naples sits on a bay beneath Mount Vesuvius and began as the ancient Greek colony of Neapolis.

name: Stazione Zoologica Anton Dohrn aquarium
fact: The aquarium of the Stazione Zoologica Anton Dohrn in Naples opened in 1874 and is among the oldest public aquariums still operating.

name: Napoleon wrasse
fact: The Napoleon wrasse can grow to about 2 metres long and is one of the few fish that eats the toxic crown-of-thorns starfish.

name: Nares Strait
fact: Nares Strait between Greenland and Ellesmere Island is named after George Nares, the British admiral who led an expedition towards the North Pole in 1875.

name: Narezushi
fact: Narezushi is the ancient form of sushi, in which fish is fermented for months with rice, and the rice was originally thrown away.

name: Narrow-barred Spanish mackerel
fact: The narrow-barred Spanish mackerel is a big, fast Indo-Pacific fish with wavy bars on its flanks, a prize of Australian and Gulf fishing.

name: Narrow sawfish
fact: The narrow sawfish, or knifetooth sawfish, has a slimmer snout than other sawfish and is the only member of its genus, Anoxypristis.

name: Narrowleaf seagrass
fact: Narrowleaf seagrass has three-pointed leaf tips and is an important food of dugongs.

name: Narwhal
fact: The narwhal's spiral tusk is actually a tooth that can grow to about 3 metres and is packed with nerve endings.

name: NASCO
fact: NASCO, based in Edinburgh, is an intergovernmental body created in 1984 to conserve wild Atlantic salmon.

name: Naso tang
fact: The naso tang, or orangespine unicornfish, has bright orange tail spines like a lipstick, and the males trail a long filament from each tail lobe.

name: Nassau
fact: Nassau, capital of the Bahamas, was a notorious pirate haven in the early 1700s, home to Blackbeard and Charles Vane.

name: Nassau grouper
fact: The Nassau grouper gathers in huge spawning groups at the same Caribbean sites each winter full moon, which made it easy to overfish; it is now endangered.

name: Natalia Molchanova
fact: Natalia Molchanova was the most decorated free diver in history, holding dozens of world records, before disappearing on a dive off Ibiza in 2015.

name: National Aquarium
fact: The National Aquarium in Baltimore opened in 1981 on the city's Inner Harbor.

name: National Marine Aquarium
fact: The National Marine Aquarium in Plymouth opened in 1998 and is the largest aquarium in the United Kingdom.

name: Nauru
fact: Nauru is a single raised coral island in the Pacific, the smallest island nation in the world, once rich from mining phosphate formed from seabird droppings.

name: Nausicaa
aliases: Nausicaa Centre National de la Mer
fact: Nausicaa in Boulogne-sur-Mer, France, opened in 1991 and was later expanded into one of the largest aquariums in Europe.

name: Nautical mile
fact: A nautical mile is 1,852 metres, roughly one minute of latitude, and it is used for distances at sea.

name: Nautile
fact: Nautile is the French crewed submersible that explored the wreck of the Titanic and recovered thousands of artefacts from it.

name: Nautilocaris saintlaurentae
fact: Nautilocaris saintlaurentae is a shrimp that lives around hydrothermal vents in the Lau Basin of the south-west Pacific.

name: Nautilus
fact: The nautilus controls its buoyancy by adjusting gas in the chambers of its spiral shell, and its lineage has changed little in hundreds of millions of years.

name: Nautilus
fact: The Nautilus is Captain Nemo's fictional electric-powered submarine in Jules Verne's 1870 novel Twenty Thousand Leagues Under the Seas.

name: Navaga
fact: The navaga is a small Arctic cod of the White and Barents Seas, fished through the ice in Russia in winter.

name: Navagio Beach
fact: Navagio Beach on Zakynthos in Greece is enclosed by cliffs and holds the rusting wreck of a freighter that ran aground in 1980.

name: Naval architect
fact: A naval architect designs ships and boats, working out their shape, strength and stability.

name: Navanax
fact: The navanax hunts other sea slugs by following their slime trails across the seabed.

name: Navassa Island
fact: Navassa Island is an uninhabited Caribbean island between Jamaica and Haiti that is administered by the United States and claimed by Haiti.

name: Navigator
fact: A navigator plots a ship's position and course, once with stars and a sextant, today often with satellite systems.

name: Naxos
fact: Naxos is the largest island of the Cyclades and has the Portara, a huge marble doorway left from an unfinished temple.

name: Nazare
fact: Nazare in Portugal produces some of the biggest waves ever surfed, driven by a huge underwater canyon that focuses the swell.

name: Neap tide
fact: Neap tides are the smallest tides, which occur at the first and last quarter of the Moon.

name: Nearchus's voyage
fact: In 325 to 324 BC Alexander the Great's admiral Nearchus led a fleet from the Indus River to the Persian Gulf.

name: Needlefish
fact: Needlefish have long beak-like jaws full of teeth and skim the surface at speed, occasionally spearing boaters when they leap.

name: Nematode
fact: Nematodes are the most abundant animals in deep-sea mud, including the sediments of the Challenger Deep, nearly 11 kilometres down.

name: Crested nembrotha
fact: The crested nembrotha is a large, boldly coloured Indo-Pacific sea slug that feeds on sea squirts.

name: Neomphalus
fact: Neomphalus fretterae is a limpet-like snail that grazes on bacteria around vents of the Galapagos Rift and East Pacific Rise.

name: Neon damselfish
fact: The neon damselfish is a bright blue and yellow damselfish common on Indo-Pacific reefs.

name: Neon flying squid
fact: Neon flying squid have been photographed gliding about 30 metres through the air, spreading their fins and arms like wings.

name: Neon goby
fact: The neon goby is a 4-centimetre Caribbean cleaner fish with a blue stripe that picks parasites from much larger fish at cleaning stations.

name: Neon tetra
fact: The neon tetra, with its electric blue stripe over red, grows to only about 3 centimetres and is one of the most popular aquarium fish, with millions bred each year.

name: Neopilina
fact: Neopilina, a limpet-like deep-sea mollusc dredged up in 1952, belongs to a group thought extinct for 350 million years.

name: Neptune
fact: The Roman god of the sea, Neptune was identified with the Greek Poseidon and gave his name to the eighth planet.

name: Neptune grass
fact: Neptune grass, Posidonia oceanica, forms vast Mediterranean meadows; one clone off Ibiza is thought to be up to about 100,000 years old.

name: Neptune's necklace
fact: Neptune's necklace is a seaweed of strings of water-filled beads, common on rocky shores of Australia and New Zealand.

name: Nereids
fact: The Nereids were fifty sea nymphs of Greek myth, daughters of the sea god Nereus, who helped sailors in storms.

name: Nereus
fact: Nereus was a hybrid robot submarine that reached the Challenger Deep in 2009 and was lost in the Kermadec Trench in 2014 when it imploded at nearly 10,000 metres.

name: Nereus (sea god)
fact: Nereus was the Greek Old Man of the Sea, a wise and truthful sea god who fathered the fifty Nereids.

name: Nevis
fact: Nevis is a round volcanic island whose peak is often wreathed in cloud, and Alexander Hamilton was born there.

name: New Bedford
fact: New Bedford, Massachusetts, was the whaling capital of the world in the 1800s and is today the highest-value fishing port in the United States.

name: New Britain Trench
fact: The New Britain Trench off Papua New Guinea drops to about 9,000 metres and has been explored by robotic landers dropped from the surface.

name: New Caledonia
fact: New Caledonia is a French territory in the south-west Pacific whose main island is ringed by one of the longest barrier reefs in the world.

name: New Caledonia Barrier Reef
fact: The New Caledonia Barrier Reef is the second-longest double barrier reef in the world and encloses one of the largest lagoons on Earth.

name: New Caledonian sea krait
fact: The New Caledonian sea krait hunts eels on coral reefs but returns to land to rest, digest and lay its eggs.

name: New England Aquarium
fact: The New England Aquarium in Boston opened in 1969 and is built around a huge cylindrical Giant Ocean Tank.

name: New England Seamounts
fact: The New England Seamounts are a chain of extinct volcanoes running south-east from Georges Bank into the deep Atlantic, home to cold-water coral gardens.

name: New Guinea
fact: New Guinea is the second-largest island in the world and is home to the birds of paradise and more than 800 languages.

name: New Hebrides Trench
fact: The New Hebrides Trench near Vanuatu reaches about 7,600 metres, and a 2013 expedition found it full of cusk eels and prawns rather than the snailfish seen in other trenches.

name: New York
fact: New York Harbour is one of the great natural harbours of the world and was the main gateway for immigrants arriving in the United States.

name: New Zealand
fact: New Zealand's two main islands sit alone in the South Pacific, and their isolation produced flightless birds like the kiwi and the extinct giant moa.

name: New Zealand arrow squid
fact: The New Zealand arrow squid is the target of one of the country's biggest squid fisheries.

name: New Zealand fur seal
fact: The New Zealand fur seal, or kekeno, was hunted almost to extinction in the nineteenth century but has since recovered around New Zealand's coasts.

name: New Zealand longfin eel
fact: The New Zealand longfin eel is one of the largest and longest-lived freshwater eels; females can live for more than 60 years before heading to sea to spawn once.

name: New Zealand mud snail
fact: The tiny New Zealand mud snail spreads on anglers' boots and can reach hundreds of thousands per square metre in rivers of the western USA and Europe.

name: New Zealand sea lion
fact: The New Zealand sea lion, or Hooker's sea lion, is one of the rarest sea lions and breeds mainly on the remote Auckland Islands.

name: Newcastle
fact: The Port of Newcastle in New South Wales is the largest coal export port in the world.

name: Newfoundland
fact: Newfoundland is a large island off eastern Canada where Vikings landed around the year 1000 and whose Grand Banks were once the richest cod fishery on Earth.

name: Nias
fact: Nias is an Indonesian island off the west coast of Sumatra that is known for its world-class surf breaks.

name: Nicaragua
fact: Nicaragua has coasts on both the Pacific and the Caribbean, and Lake Nicaragua lies close to its Pacific shore.

name: Nice
fact: Nice on the French Riviera is known for the Promenade des Anglais, which curves along its bay.

name: Nicobar Islands
fact: The Nicobar Islands are an Indian chain lying south of the Andaman Islands, not far from the northern tip of Sumatra.

name: Nigeria
fact: Nigeria's southern coast lies on the Gulf of Guinea, an arm of the Atlantic, where the Niger river builds a huge delta.

name: Night shark
fact: The night shark has large green eyes and lives along the edge of the continental shelf in the Atlantic, rising to feed at night.

name: Nile perch
fact: The Nile perch, introduced to Lake Victoria in the 1950s, grows to about 2 metres and drove hundreds of native cichlid species to extinction.

name: Nile tilapia
fact: The Nile tilapia is a mouthbrooding fish native to Africa and is now one of the most widely farmed freshwater fish in the world.

name: Nimrod expedition
fact: On the Nimrod expedition of 1907 to 1909 Ernest Shackleton's party turned back only about 97 nautical miles short of the South Pole.

name: Ninety East Ridge
fact: The Ninety East Ridge is a remarkably straight underwater mountain chain in the Indian Ocean, named because it follows the 90th meridian east.

name: Ningaloo Marine Park
fact: Ningaloo Reef in Western Australia is a fringing reef you can swim to from the beach, famous for whale sharks that gather every autumn.

name: Ningaloo Reef
fact: Ningaloo Reef in Western Australia is a fringing reef that hugs the shore so closely you can swim to it from the beach, and whale sharks gather there each year.

name: Ninja lanternshark
fact: The ninja lanternshark, a black glowing shark described in 2015, was named by the describer's young cousins, and its species name honours Jaws author Peter Benchley.

name: Nipa palm
fact: The nipa palm is a mangrove palm with a creeping, partly underground trunk whose sap is tapped to make sugar and vinegar.

name: Niskin bottle
fact: A Niskin bottle is a tube that closes at both ends at a chosen depth to collect a water sample.

name: Niue
fact: Niue is a single raised coral island in the South Pacific and one of the largest of its kind in the world.

name: Njord
fact: Njord is the Norse god of the sea, seafaring and fishing, as well as of the wind, and father of Freyr and Freyja.

name: No-limits freediving
fact: No-limits freediving is diving as deep as possible on one breath using a weighted sled to descend and a lift bag to ascend.

name: Noble pen shell
fact: The noble pen shell is a metre-long fan mussel of Mediterranean seagrass meadows whose silky threads were once woven into 'sea silk', and a parasite has nearly wiped it out since 2016.

name: Noctiluca
fact: Noctiluca, the 'sea sparkle', is a bubble-like dinoflagellate that lights up breaking waves at night with blue bioluminescence.

name: Nocturnal
fact: A nocturnal was a medieval tool that used the position of stars near the Pole Star to tell the time at night.

name: Nomura's jellyfish
fact: Nomura's jellyfish can weigh 200 kilograms and measure 2 metres across, and swarms drifting from China into Japanese waters have capsized a fishing boat.

name: Noodle seagrass
fact: Noodle seagrass has round, needle-like leaves and grows in meadows across the Indo-Pacific.

name: Noosa First Point
fact: First Point at Noosa Heads in Queensland is a gentle right-hand point break popular with longboarders.

name: Norfolk
fact: Norfolk, Virginia, at the mouth of Chesapeake Bay, is home to the largest naval base in the world.

name: Norfolk Island
fact: Norfolk Island is a small Australian territory in the south-west Pacific, once a penal colony and famous for its tall Norfolk pines.

name: Nori
fact: Nori is dried, pressed sheets of the red seaweed laver, grown on nets in shallow Japanese bays and used to wrap sushi rolls.

name: Norris's top snail
fact: Norris's top snail crawls up giant kelp to graze, then lets go and sinks when it senses a sea star hunting it.

name: North Atlantic Drift
fact: The North Atlantic Drift is the continuation of the Gulf Stream that carries warm water towards Britain, Norway and the Arctic.

name: North Atlantic Gyre
fact: The North Atlantic Gyre is the clockwise loop formed by the Gulf Stream, North Atlantic Drift, Canary Current and North Equatorial Current, enclosing the Sargasso Sea.

name: North Atlantic right whale
fact: The North Atlantic right whale is one of the most endangered great whales, with only around 370 left off eastern North America.

name: North Brazil Current
fact: The North Brazil Current flows north-west along the coast of Brazil and sheds huge rings of water that drift into the Caribbean.

name: North Equatorial Current
fact: The North Equatorial Current flows westward just north of the equator in both the Atlantic and the Pacific, driven by the trade winds.

name: North Korea
fact: North Korea has a Pacific coastline on the Sea of Japan to the east and the Yellow Sea to the west.

name: North Pacific Current
fact: The North Pacific Current is the broad eastward continuation of the Kuroshio across the North Pacific.

name: North Pacific Gyre
fact: The North Pacific Gyre is the huge clockwise circulation of the North Pacific whose calm centre collects floating plastic in the Great Pacific Garbage Patch.

name: North Pacific right whale
fact: The North Pacific right whale is one of the rarest whales, with perhaps only about 30 animals left in the eastern North Pacific.

name: North Ronaldsay sheep
fact: North Ronaldsay sheep live almost entirely on seaweed, kept off the grass of their Orkney island by a long stone wall.

name: North Sea
fact: The North Sea is a shallow arm of the Atlantic between Britain and mainland Europe, averaging only about 90 metres deep.

name: Northern anchovy
fact: The northern anchovy schools along the North American Pacific coast and feeds everything from humpback whales to brown pelicans.

name: Northern bottlenose whale
fact: Northern bottlenose whales were heavily hunted in the North Atlantic for their oil and are famously curious about boats.

name: Northern elephant seal
fact: Northern elephant seals were hunted to the brink of extinction in the 19th century, with perhaps fewer than 100 left, and now number well over 100,000.

name: Northern fulmar
fact: The northern fulmar defends itself and its chick by spitting a foul-smelling stomach oil at intruders.

name: Northern fur seal
fact: Most of the world's northern fur seals breed on the Pribilof Islands in the Bering Sea, where they were once hunted by the hundreds of thousands.

name: Northern gannet
fact: Northern gannets plunge-dive from up to 30 metres, hitting the water at around 100 kilometres per hour, with air sacs under the skin to cushion the impact.

name: Northern kingfish
fact: The northern kingfish is a bottom-feeding member of the drum family found along the Atlantic coast of North America.

name: Northern pike
fact: Northern pike lunge at prey from cover and leap clear of the water when hooked, and they can reach well over a metre long.

name: Northern pipefish
fact: The northern pipefish lives in eelgrass beds along the western Atlantic coast, often alongside the lined seahorse.

name: Northern prawn
fact: The northern prawn starts life as a male and changes into a female after a few years, and is the cold-water prawn in most prawn cocktails.

name: Northern puffer
fact: The northern puffer of the US east coast is sold as 'sea squab', its flesh being far less toxic than that of tropical puffers.

name: Northern right whale dolphin
fact: The northern right whale dolphin of the North Pacific has no dorsal fin and skims along the surface in low, long leaps.

name: Northern royal albatross
fact: Taiaroa Head near Dunedin hosts the only mainland breeding colony of royal albatrosses in the world.

name: Northern Sea Route
fact: The Northern Sea Route runs along Russia's Arctic coast, and the ship Vega made the first full passage of it in 1878 and 1879.

name: Northern searobin
fact: The northern searobin makes croaking and grunting sounds by drumming muscles against its swim bladder.

name: Northern shortfin squid
fact: The northern shortfin squid of the north-west Atlantic lives only about a year and is fished in large numbers.

name: Northwest Passage
fact: The Northwest Passage through the Arctic was first fully sailed by Roald Amundsen's ship Gjoa between 1903 and 1906.

name: Norway
fact: Norway's coast is cut by deep fjords and faces the North Atlantic and the Norwegian Sea.

name: Norway pout
fact: The Norway pout is a small cod relative of the North Sea caught almost entirely for fishmeal and oil.

name: Norwegian Current
fact: The Norwegian Current carries warm Atlantic water north along the coast of Norway, keeping its harbours ice-free even beyond the Arctic Circle.

name: Norwegian Sea
fact: The Norwegian Sea lies between Norway and Iceland, and warm Atlantic water flowing through it keeps Norway's coast ice-free.

name: Nosy Be
fact: Nosy Be is an island off north-west Madagascar known for its ylang-ylang perfume plantations.

name: Nothosaurus
fact: Nothosaurus was a long-necked, fish-eating marine reptile of the Triassic that probably hunted in shallow seas and rested on shores.

name: Noumea
fact: Noumea is the capital and main port of the French territory of New Caledonia.

name: Nuckelavee
fact: The nuckelavee is a skinless horse-like demon of Orcadian folklore that lived in the sea and brought plague and blight on land.

name: Nudibranch
fact: Nudibranchs are sea slugs, and some steal the stinging cells from the anemones they eat and reuse them for their own defence.

name: Nuestra Señora de Atocha
fact: The Spanish treasure galleon Nuestra Señora de Atocha sank in a hurricane off the Florida Keys in 1622; its gold and silver were found in 1985.

name: Numbfish
fact: The Australian numbfish is a flabby electric ray that lies buried in sand and can deliver a strong shock, and it is sometimes stranded alive on beaches.

name: Nurse shark
fact: Nurse sharks rest in groups on the seabed by day and suck prey out of crevices with a powerful vacuum-like gulp.

name: Nursehound
fact: The nursehound is a large spotted catshark of the eastern Atlantic that lays its eggs in tough cases attached to seaweed.

name: Nurseryfish
fact: The male nurseryfish of northern Australia and New Guinea carries the egg cluster hooked onto a bony hook on his forehead until the eggs hatch.

name: Nuuk
fact: Nuuk, Greenland's capital, lies on the Labrador Sea and is one of the smallest capital cities in the world.

name: Oahu
fact: Oahu is the Hawaiian island that holds Honolulu, Pearl Harbor and Waikiki.

name: Oakland
fact: The Port of Oakland on San Francisco Bay was an early West Coast pioneer of container shipping in the 1960s.

name: Oarfish
fact: The giant oarfish is the longest bony fish, reaching about 8 metres, and its rare strandings probably inspired sea-serpent legends.

name: Oarweed
fact: Oarweed is a common European kelp with a thick stem and a blade split into fingers, exposed only at the lowest tides.

name: Oasis of the Seas
fact: Oasis of the Seas, which entered service in 2009, was the world's largest passenger ship when she was built.

name: Oasisia tube worm
fact: Oasisia is a slender tube worm that grows in tangles among giant tube worms at East Pacific vents and, like them, feeds through bacteria instead of a mouth.

name: Ocean acidification
fact: Ocean acidification is the fall in the sea's pH as it absorbs carbon dioxide from the atmosphere, which harms shell-building animals.

name: Ocean Alliance
fact: Ocean Alliance is a whale research and conservation group founded by Roger Payne, who helped to discover that humpbacks sing.

name: Ocean Beach
fact: Ocean Beach in San Francisco is a cold, powerful beach break that faces the open Pacific beside the Golden Gate.

name: Ocean bottom seismometer
fact: An ocean bottom seismometer sits on the seabed to record earthquakes, from nearby tremors to those on the other side of the world.

name: Ocean Conservancy
fact: Ocean Conservancy is an American non-profit group that organises the annual International Coastal Cleanup.

name: Ocean current
fact: An ocean current is a continuous, directed flow of seawater, driven by wind, temperature and salinity differences.

name: Ocean eddy
fact: An ocean eddy is a swirling loop of water that breaks off from a current and can carry heat and marine life across the sea.

name: Ocean gyre
fact: An ocean gyre is a huge system of rotating currents, such as the North Pacific Gyre where floating rubbish gathers.

name: Ocean quahog
fact: An ocean quahog dredged up off Iceland in 2006 was 507 years old, the oldest known individual animal ever found.

name: Ocean rowing
fact: Ocean rowing is crossing an ocean in a rowing boat, and hundreds of people have rowed across the Atlantic.

name: Ocean sunfish
fact: The ocean sunfish, or mola, is the heaviest bony fish, weighing over 2 tonnes, and drifts the open ocean eating jellyfish.

name: Ocean surgeonfish
fact: The ocean surgeonfish is a western Atlantic surgeonfish that grazes algae on reefs in large groups.

name: Ocean triggerfish
fact: The ocean triggerfish is a pelagic triggerfish often found under floating objects far from land.

name: Wave
fact: Most ocean waves are made by wind blowing over the water surface, and bigger waves come from stronger wind blowing for longer.

name: Oceana
fact: Oceana is an international ocean conservation group, founded in 2001, that campaigns on fishing, pollution and protecting marine habitats.

name: Oceanario de Lisboa
fact: The Oceanario de Lisboa opened in 1998 for Expo 98 and is built around a central tank of about five million litres.

name: Oceanic Preservation Society
fact: The Oceanic Preservation Society, led by Louie Psihoyos, made the Oscar-winning documentary The Cove about dolphin hunting in Japan.

name: Oceanic whitetip shark
fact: Oceanic whitetips were blamed for many of the deaths of USS Indianapolis sailors adrift in the Pacific in 1945.

name: L'Oceanografic
fact: L'Oceanografic in Valencia, opened in 2003 as part of the City of Arts and Sciences, is the largest aquarium in Europe.

name: Oceanographer
fact: Oceanographers study the physical, chemical and biological workings of the ocean, including currents, waves and the seafloor.

name: Oceanographic Museum of Monaco
fact: The Oceanographic Museum of Monaco was opened in 1910 by Prince Albert I and houses a large public aquarium in its cellars.

name: Oceanus
fact: In Greek myth Oceanus was a Titan who personified the great river thought to encircle the whole world.

name: Ocellaris clownfish
fact: The ocellaris clownfish is the orange, three-barred fish made famous as Nemo; the film's success made it one of the most traded reef fish in the world.

name: Ocellate river stingray
fact: The ocellate river stingray lives in the Amazon and Paraná river systems and is one of the few rays found only in fresh water.

name: Ochre sea star
fact: The ochre sea star comes in purple or orange and is a keystone predator that stops mussels from taking over the rocky shore.

name: Octant
fact: The octant was an eighteenth-century navigation instrument that measured angles using mirrors and was the forerunner of the sextant.

name: Octopus
fact: An octopus has three hearts and blue, copper-based blood, and about two-thirds of its neurons sit in its eight arms rather than its brain.

name: Odd bobtail squid
fact: The odd bobtail squid defends itself by squirting a glowing cloud of luminous mucus instead of dark ink.

name: Odobenocetops
fact: Odobenocetops was a Pliocene whale from the coasts of Peru and Chile with a walrus-like face and two tusks, one far longer than the other in males.

name: Offshore powerboat racing
fact: Offshore powerboat racing is a high-speed race in powerful boats over open sea courses.

name: Ohrid trout
fact: The Ohrid trout lives only in Lake Ohrid, one of the oldest lakes in Europe, on the border of North Macedonia and Albania.

name: Oil tanker
fact: The largest oil tankers ever built, the ultra-large crude carriers, could carry more than 500,000 tonnes of oil in a single voyage.

name: Oilfish
fact: The flesh of the oilfish is rich in waxy esters that humans cannot digest, causing oily diarrhoea, and its sale is banned in Japan.

name: Oithona
fact: Oithona is a tiny copepod, about a millimetre long, and one of the most abundant animals in the sea.

name: Okeanos Explorer
fact: Okeanos Explorer is a US government ship dedicated entirely to exploring unknown parts of the ocean, broadcasting its dives live online.

name: Okinawa
fact: Okinawa is the largest of Japan's Ryukyu Islands, in the East China Sea, and was the site of the last great battle of the Second World War in 1945.

name: Okinawa Churaumi Aquarium
fact: The Kuroshio Sea tank at Okinawa Churaumi Aquarium holds about 7,500 cubic metres of water and has long been home to whale sharks and manta rays.

name: The Old Man and the Sea
fact: The Old Man and the Sea is Ernest Hemingway's 1952 novella about an old Cuban fisherman's struggle with a giant marlin.

name: Olive flounder
fact: The olive flounder, or hirame, is the most widely farmed flatfish in Japan and South Korea and is served raw as sashimi.

name: Olive-headed sea snake
fact: The olive-headed sea snake is a true sea snake of the coral reefs and seagrass beds of northern Australia and New Guinea.

name: Olive ridley sea turtle
fact: Olive ridleys nest in arribadas of tens of thousands of females on single beaches in Costa Rica, Mexico and India.

name: Olive sea snake
fact: The olive sea snake of Australian reefs has light-sensing cells in its tail, so it can keep its tail hidden in a crevice.

name: Olivier Levasseur
fact: Olivier Levasseur, known as La Buse, was hanged on Reunion Island in 1730 and is said to have thrown a coded treasure clue into the crowd.

name: Olokun
fact: Olokun is a Yoruba and Benin deity of the ocean, honoured in Nigeria and in the Caribbean and the Americas.

name: Olympia oyster
fact: The Olympia oyster is a small, coin-sized oyster native to the Pacific coast of North America.

name: Omaha Beach
fact: Omaha Beach in Normandy was one of the five landing beaches of the Allied invasion on 6 June 1944.

name: Oman
fact: Oman's long coast on the Arabian Sea and the Gulf of Oman includes its capital, Muscat.

name: Oman anemonefish
fact: The Oman anemonefish is found only along the coast of Oman, where it lives in anemones on rocky reefs.

name: Omura's whale
fact: Omura's whale was only recognised as a species in 2003 and was first filmed alive off Madagascar in 2015.

name: Barnacle-eating nudibranch
fact: The barnacle-eating nudibranch specialises in feeding on acorn barnacles in cold northern seas.

name: One Piece
fact: One Piece is Eiichiro Oda's manga, begun in 1997, about a boy called Luffy and his pirate crew searching the Grand Line for treasure.

name: Opabinia
fact: Opabinia, a Cambrian sea creature with five eyes and a clawed trunk, reportedly drew laughter when first shown to scientists in 1972.

name: Opah
fact: The opah, or moonfish, is the only fish known to keep its whole body warm, circulating heated blood through its gills.

name: Opalescent nudibranch
fact: The opalescent nudibranch of Pacific Northwest tide pools stores stinging cells from the hydroids it eats in the orange tips of its back.

name: Opaleye
fact: The opaleye is a Californian kelp-forest fish with bright blue-green eyes that feeds mainly on seaweed.

name: Open brain coral
fact: The open brain coral is a large, fleshy single-polyp stony coral that lives unattached on sandy seabeds.

name: Open Water
fact: Open Water is Chris Kentis's 2003 thriller about two scuba divers accidentally left behind in shark-filled seas, inspired by a real incident.

name: Open water swimming
fact: Open water swimming takes place in the sea, rivers or lakes rather than in a pool, and it is an Olympic event over ten kilometres.

name: Ophioctenella acies
fact: Ophioctenella acies is a brittle star that gathers in dense swarms around hydrothermal vents of the Mid-Cayman Rise in the Caribbean.

name: Ophthalmosaurus
fact: Ophthalmosaurus was a dolphin-shaped Jurassic ichthyosaur with some of the largest eyes, relative to body size, of any known vertebrate.

name: Opossum shrimp
fact: Opossum shrimp carry their young in a pouch like a possum and swarm in glassy clouds in caves, estuaries and the deep sea.

name: Oran
fact: Oran is the second-largest city in Algeria and a major Mediterranean port.

name: Orange clownfish
fact: The orange clownfish, or percula, looks almost identical to the ocellaris but has thicker black edges to its white bars, and lives around New Guinea and the Great Barrier Reef.

name: Orange-lined triggerfish
fact: The orange-lined triggerfish is dark green with curving orange lines and is notoriously aggressive, both on the reef and in aquariums.

name: Orange peel nudibranch
fact: The orange peel nudibranch is a large, bumpy orange sea slug of the north-eastern Pacific.

name: Orange puffball sponge
fact: The orange puffball sponge is a round, orange sponge with a tough surface covered in tiny bumps.

name: Orange roughy
fact: The orange roughy lives at 500 to 1,500 metres, does not breed until its twenties and can live for about 150 years, which is why it was so easily overfished.

name: Orange skunk clownfish
fact: The orange skunk clownfish has a single white stripe down its back, like a skunk's, and lives in anemones.

name: Orange-spotted grouper
fact: The orange-spotted grouper, or estuary cod, is a brown grouper with orange spots that is farmed widely in Southeast Asia for live-fish restaurants.

name: Orange-striped emperor
fact: The orange-striped emperor is an Indo-Pacific reef fish marked with orange stripes along its flanks.

name: Orangeshoulder tang
fact: The orangeshoulder tang has an orange patch behind its eye and grazes algae in large schools on Indo-Pacific reefs.

name: Orca
fact: Orcas are actually the largest dolphins, and different populations have their own dialects and hunting traditions.

name: Oregon Coast Aquarium
fact: The Oregon Coast Aquarium in Newport, opened in 1992, was home to Keiko, the orca star of the film Free Willy, from 1996 to 1998.

name: Oresund
fact: The Oresund between Denmark and Sweden is one of the three Danish straits linking the Baltic to the North Sea, now spanned by the Oresund Bridge.

name: Organ pipe coral
fact: Organ pipe coral has a bright red skeleton of parallel tubes like organ pipes, hidden under greyish-green polyps.

name: Oriental sweetlips
fact: The oriental sweetlips of Indian Ocean reefs hangs under ledges in striped schools by day, and its juveniles wriggle like poisonous flatworms.

name: Orinoco river dolphin
fact: The Orinoco river dolphin is the pink river dolphin of the Orinoco basin in Venezuela and Colombia.

name: Orkney
fact: Orkney, just north of mainland Scotland, is home to Skara Brae, a stone village older than the pyramids, and the natural harbour of Scapa Flow.

name: Ormer
fact: The ormer is the European abalone, gathered by hand on Channel Island beaches at low tide on a handful of strictly controlled days each year.

name: Ornate bichir
fact: The ornate bichir is a primitive-looking African fish that has lungs and can gulp air at the surface.

name: Ornate ghost pipefish
fact: In ornate ghost pipefish it is the female, not the male, that broods the eggs, in a pouch formed by her enlarged pelvic fins.

name: Ornate octopus
fact: The ornate octopus is a night-active Indo-Pacific octopus marked with pale stripes.

name: Ornate sea snake
fact: The ornate sea snake lives on reefs and sandy flats around northern Australia and feeds on fish and fish eggs.

name: Ornate wobbegong
fact: The ornate wobbegong is a carpet shark of eastern Australian reefs that lies camouflaged on the bottom by day and hunts at night.

name: Ornate wrasse
fact: The ornate wrasse is a bright Mediterranean wrasse, and many females later change sex to become males.

name: Osaka
fact: Osaka on Osaka Bay has been Japan's great merchant port for centuries and is a major container hub.

name: Oscar
fact: The oscar is a big Amazon cichlid that recognises its owner, begs at the glass and rearranges the gravel in its tank.

name: OSPAR Convention
fact: The OSPAR Convention of 1992 protects the marine environment of the north-east Atlantic.

name: Osprey
fact: The osprey hits the water feet-first and has a reversible outer toe and spiny foot pads to grip slippery fish.

name: Osprey Reef
fact: Osprey Reef is a submerged atoll in the Coral Sea off Queensland whose walls plunge about 1,000 metres and attract shark-diving expeditions.

name: Ostracod
fact: Ostracods, or seed shrimps, are tiny crustaceans sealed in a hinged shell, and some species flash blue light to attract mates.

name: Ostreococcus
fact: Ostreococcus is a green alga less than a micrometre wide, among the smallest known free-living cells with a nucleus.

name: Otis Barton
fact: Otis Barton designed and paid for the bathysphere in which he and William Beebe dived in the 1930s, and in 1949 reached about 1,370 metres alone in his benthoscope.

name: Otocinclus
fact: Otocinclus, or 'otos', are tiny suckermouth catfish from South America, kept in aquariums to graze algae and barely 4 centimetres long.

name: Otodus
fact: Otodus obliquus was a giant mackerel shark of about 50 million years ago whose lineage led to megalodon.

name: Outer Banks
fact: The Outer Banks are a long chain of barrier islands off North Carolina, where the Wright brothers first flew and the pirate Blackbeard was killed.

name: Outrigger canoe
fact: An outrigger canoe has a float lashed alongside the hull for stability, and such canoes carried Austronesian peoples across the Pacific and Indian Oceans.

name: Outrigger canoe racing
fact: Outrigger canoe racing uses long canoes with a float attached on one side, a sport popular across Polynesia and especially in Hawaii and Tahiti.

name: Owl limpet
fact: The owl limpet tends a private patch of algae on its rock and bulldozes away intruders that threaten it.

name: Oyashio Current
fact: The Oyashio is a cold current flowing south from the Bering Sea past Kamchatka, and where it meets the warm Kuroshio it creates rich fishing grounds off Japan.

name: Oyster
fact: A single oyster can filter up to around 190 litres of water a day, and oyster reefs once lined estuaries such as New York Harbour.

name: Oyster farmer
fact: Oyster farmers raise oysters in beds or racks in coastal waters until they are ready to eat.

name: Oyster toadfish
fact: The male oyster toadfish guards the eggs in a den and calls females with a foghorn-like 'boat whistle' that can be heard from boats above.

name: Oysters Rockefeller
fact: Oysters Rockefeller, created in New Orleans in 1899 at Antoine's restaurant, was named for the richness of its sauce.

name: Ozeaneum
fact: The Ozeaneum in Stralsund, Germany, opened in 2008 and focuses on the North Sea and Baltic Sea.

name: Pachycara thermophilum
fact: Pachycara thermophilum is an eelpout that lives around hot vents on the Mid-Atlantic Ridge.

name: Pacific angelshark
fact: The Pacific angelshark lies buried in sand off California and Mexico and snaps upward at passing fish faster than the eye can follow.

name: Pacific blackdragon
fact: Female Pacific blackdragons have a light-tipped chin barbel and rows of light organs along the body, while the males are tiny and toothless.

name: Pacific bluefin tuna
fact: The Pacific bluefin tuna is the species behind Tokyo's record new-year auctions; one sold for about 333 million yen in 2019.

name: Pacific cod
fact: The Pacific cod is a major fishery of the Bering Sea and Gulf of Alaska, with catches of several hundred thousand tonnes a year.

name: Pacific Decadal Oscillation
fact: The Pacific Decadal Oscillation is a long-lived pattern of Pacific sea surface temperatures that shifts over decades.

name: Pacific electric ray
fact: The Pacific electric ray hunts at night off California, enveloping fish in its disc and shocking them with up to about 45 volts.

name: Pacific gaper
fact: The Pacific gaper is a large clam whose long siphon is too big to pull back inside its shell.

name: Pacific hagfish
fact: The Pacific hagfish defends itself by releasing slime that swells into a choking gel in seawater.

name: Pacific hake
fact: The Pacific hake, also called Pacific whiting, is caught in huge numbers off the Pacific coast of North America.

name: Pacific halibut
fact: Pacific halibut are a mainstay of Alaskan fisheries, and anglers call the biggest ones, over 45 kilograms, barn doors.

name: Pacific herring
fact: The Pacific herring is fished mainly for its roe, sold to Japan as kazunoko, and its eggs laid on kelp are a traditional food of the Pacific Northwest.

name: Pacific lamprey
fact: The Pacific lamprey climbs waterfalls with its sucker mouth on its way up Columbia River tributaries and is a traditional food of Native peoples.

name: Pacific leaping blenny
fact: The Pacific leaping blenny of Guam lives entirely out of water on wave-splashed rocks, leaping between them by curling and flicking its tail.

name: Pacific Ocean
fact: The Pacific Ocean covers about 165 million square kilometres, more than all of Earth's land combined, making it the largest and deepest ocean.

name: Pacific ocean perch
fact: The Pacific ocean perch is a long-lived rockfish that can reach many decades of age.

name: Pacific oyster
fact: The Pacific oyster, native to Japan, is now the most farmed oyster in the world and grows on coasts from France to Australia.

name: Pacific Princess
fact: The Pacific Princess was the cruise ship featured in the television series The Love Boat, and the programme's opening credits showed her.

name: Pacific sand lance
fact: Pacific sand lance spend the night and much of the winter buried in coarse sand, which is why mapping their sand beds matters for salmon and seabirds.

name: Pacific sandfish
fact: The Pacific sandfish buries itself in sand with just its upturned mouth exposed, and is a key prey of seabirds and salmon in Alaska.

name: Pacific sardine
fact: The Pacific sardine fuelled Monterey's Cannery Row until the stock collapsed in the 1950s, and it still booms and busts with ocean cycles.

name: Pacific saury
fact: Pacific saury, sanma, is caught by the hundreds of thousands of tonnes in the northwest Pacific and is an autumn favourite grilled whole in Japan.

name: Pacific sea nettle
fact: The Pacific sea nettle is a large, long-armed jellyfish of the north-eastern Pacific with a golden-brown bell.

name: Pacific seahorse
fact: The Pacific seahorse is the only seahorse in the eastern Pacific, ranging from California to Peru and the Galápagos Islands.

name: Pacific sleeper shark
fact: The Pacific sleeper shark is a sluggish giant of cold northern waters that has been recorded at depths of around 2,000 metres.

name: Pacific spiny lumpsucker
fact: The Pacific spiny lumpsucker is a golf-ball-sized fish of the Pacific Northwest that sticks to eelgrass and rocks with a suction disc.

name: Pacific tomcod
fact: The Pacific tomcod is a small cod of North America's Pacific coast, closely related to the Atlantic tomcod.

name: Pacific viperfish
fact: The Pacific viperfish has fang-like teeth so long that they curve outside its closed mouth.

name: Pacific white-sided dolphin
fact: Pacific white-sided dolphins travel in boisterous groups of hundreds in the cool North Pacific and often ride the bow waves of ships.

name: Pack ice killer whale
fact: The pack ice killer whale, or Type B, hunts seals around Antarctic ice floes and often looks yellowish from a film of diatoms on its skin.

name: Pacu
fact: Pacu are relatives of piranhas with flat, human-like molars that they use to crush seeds and nuts.

name: Padang
fact: Padang is the largest city on the west coast of Sumatra and a port on the Indian Ocean.

name: Padang Padang
fact: Padang Padang on Bali's Bukit Peninsula, nicknamed the Balinese Pipeline, is a short, hollow and powerful left-hand reef wave.

name: Paddle steamer
fact: A paddle steamer is driven by a steam engine turning paddle wheels at its sides or stern.

name: Paddle weed
fact: Paddle weed has small, oval leaves on slender stalks and is a favourite food of dugongs.

name: Paddlefish
fact: The American paddlefish's long paddle-shaped snout is packed with tens of thousands of electroreceptors used to detect swarms of plankton.

name: Paedocypris
fact: Paedocypris progenetica, from the peat swamps of Sumatra, matures at under 8 millimetres and is among the smallest fish known.

name: Paella
fact: Paella is a rice dish from Valencia in Spain, cooked in a wide shallow pan, and the seafood version is known across the world.

name: Pagasetic Gulf
fact: The Pagasetic Gulf is an almost enclosed bay of the Aegean in Thessaly from whose shore, in legend, Jason and the Argonauts set sail for the Golden Fleece.

name: Painted frogfish
fact: The painted frogfish can alter its colour over time to match its surroundings and lures prey with a fishing-rod-like spine.

name: Painter
fact: The painter is the rope attached to the bow of a small boat, used to tie it up.

name: Paiute cutthroat trout
fact: The Paiute cutthroat trout is native to a single small stream system in California's Sierra Nevada.

name: Pajama cardinalfish
fact: Male pajama cardinalfish incubate the fertilised eggs in their mouths.

name: Pakistan
fact: Pakistan has an Arabian Sea coast of about 1,000 kilometres, where the port city of Karachi lies.

name: Palancar Reef
fact: Palancar Reef off Cozumel, Mexico, is part of the Mesoamerican Reef and became a famous dive site after Jacques Cousteau filmed it in the 1960s.

name: Palau
fact: Palau in the western Pacific is famous for its Rock Islands and for Jellyfish Lake, where millions of harmless jellyfish drift in a marine lake.

name: Palau National Marine Sanctuary
fact: Palau closed about 80 percent of its waters to fishing in 2020, creating one of the largest fully protected marine sanctuaries in the world.

name: Palau Trench
fact: The Palau Trench lies east of the islands of Palau in the western Pacific and reaches about 8,000 metres deep.

name: Pale octopus
fact: The pale octopus is a small octopus of the south-eastern Australian coast that lives on sandy and muddy seabeds.

name: Palermo
fact: Palermo, the capital of Sicily, was founded by the Phoenicians and later ruled by Arabs and Normans.

name: Palette surgeonfish
fact: The palette surgeonfish, a bright blue Indo-Pacific reef fish, became famous as Dory in the film Finding Nemo.

name: Palk Strait
fact: Palk Strait between India and Sri Lanka is so shallow that large ships cannot pass, and a chain of shoals called Adam's Bridge lies at its southern end.

name: Pallid sturgeon
fact: The pallid sturgeon of the Missouri and Mississippi rivers is a pale, shovel-snouted giant listed as endangered in the United States.

name: Palm worm
fact: The palm worm builds mucus tubes on Pacific vent chimneys and spreads a crown of tentacles like a palm tree to feed in the hot water.

name: Palma
fact: Palma is the capital and main port of the Spanish island of Mallorca.

name: Palmyra Atoll
fact: Palmyra Atoll, an uninhabited US territory south of Hawaii, has reefs so untouched that predators like sharks make up most of the fish biomass.

name: Pan-frying
fact: Pan-frying cooks fish in a little oil or butter in a shallow pan, giving the skin a crisp finish.

name: Panama
fact: Panama has coasts on both the Pacific Ocean and the Caribbean Sea, linked by the Panama Canal.

name: Panama Canal
fact: The Panama Canal, opened in August 1914, lifts ships through locks to cross the isthmus between the Atlantic and Pacific oceans.

name: Panama City
fact: Panama City sits at the Pacific entrance to the Panama Canal, where the port of Balboa receives ships coming through the locks.

name: Pancake batfish
fact: The pancake batfish is a round, flattened fish of the Gulf of Mexico seabed that hops along on arm-like fins.

name: Panda corydoras
fact: The panda corydoras, named for its black eye patches and tail spot, comes from the rivers of Peru and is about 5 centimetres long.

name: Pangasius
fact: Pangasius, sold as basa or river cobbler, is a Vietnamese Mekong catfish farmed in vast numbers and exported as cheap white fillets.

name: Pantelleria
fact: Pantelleria is a volcanic island between Sicily and Tunisia known for its sweet wine and its vines trained in sunken hollows.

name: Pantropical spotted dolphin
fact: Pantropical spotted dolphins swim above yellowfin tuna in the eastern Pacific, where millions died in tuna nets before dolphin-safe fishing.

name: Papahānaumokuākea Marine National Monument
fact: Papahānaumokuākea protects the uninhabited north-western Hawaiian Islands and is one of the largest marine protected areas in the world.

name: Papakolea Beach
fact: Papakolea on the Big Island of Hawaii has green sand because it contains crystals of the volcanic mineral olivine.

name: Papeete
fact: Papeete on Tahiti is the capital and main port of French Polynesia.

name: Paper nautilus
fact: Female paper nautiluses, which are in fact octopuses, make a thin papery egg case that they carry with them.

name: Papua New Guinea
fact: Papua New Guinea occupies the eastern half of the island of New Guinea and is bordered by the Pacific, and it has over 800 languages.

name: Paradise fish
fact: The paradise fish breathes air with a labyrinth organ and was one of the first tropical fish kept in home aquariums.

name: Parasailing
fact: Parasailing is a sport in which a person is towed behind a boat while attached to a parachute-like canopy.

name: Parasitic anemone
fact: The parasitic anemone rides on hermit crab shells, and in return stings the crab's enemies.

name: Paros
fact: Paros is a Cycladic island whose fine white marble was used to carve the Venus de Milo.

name: Parrotfish
fact: Parrotfish grind coral with beak-like teeth and excrete the remains as fine white sand, producing much of the sand on tropical beaches.

name: Partridge tun
fact: The partridge tun is a large sea snail with a thin, speckled shell patterned like a partridge's plumage.

name: Patagonian red octopus
fact: The Patagonian red octopus is fished along the coasts of Chile and Argentina and is a close relative of the giant Pacific octopus.

name: Patagonian squid
fact: The Patagonian squid is a major catch in the waters around the Falkland Islands.

name: Patagonian toothfish
fact: The Patagonian toothfish was renamed 'Chilean sea bass' by a fish wholesaler in 1977 to sell it, and lives down to about 3,800 metres.

name: Patmos
fact: Patmos is the Greek island where, by tradition, Saint John wrote the Book of Revelation.

name: Patong Beach
fact: Patong is the busiest resort beach on Phuket in Thailand, and it was struck by the 2004 Indian Ocean tsunami.

name: Patrol boat
fact: Patrol boats are small, fast naval or coastguard vessels used to guard coasts, harbours and rivers.

name: Pavel Nakhimov
fact: Pavel Nakhimov destroyed an Ottoman fleet at Sinop in 1853 and died defending Sevastopol in the Crimean War.

name: Payara
fact: The payara of the Orinoco and Amazon has two lower fangs so long that they fit into holes in its upper jaw.

name: Pea crab
fact: The pea crab is a tiny crab that lives inside the shells of living mussels and oysters, stealing food from its host's gills.

name: Pea puffer
fact: The pea puffer from the rivers of south-west India is one of the smallest pufferfish, about 3 centimetres long.

name: Peacock bass
fact: The peacock bass is an Amazon cichlid, not a bass, and was released in Florida canals, where anglers now chase it.

name: Peacock cichlid
fact: Male peacock cichlids of Lake Malawi flash vivid blue and gold colours as they court females over sandy lake floors.

name: Peacock flounder
fact: The peacock flounder is covered in bright blue rings and can change its pattern to match the reef in seconds.

name: Peacock hind
fact: The peacock hind is a blue-spotted Indo-Pacific grouper that was introduced to Hawaii to boost fisheries.

name: Peacock mantis shrimp
fact: The peacock mantis shrimp's club-like arms hit so hard they can crack aquarium glass and shatter crab shells in a single blow.

name: Peacock worm
fact: The peacock worm lives in a tube and spreads a fan of feathery tentacles to catch food particles from the water.

name: Peacock's tail
fact: Peacock's tail is a small fan-shaped brown seaweed of warm rock pools, banded with white lime and shimmering blue-green.

name: Peale's dolphin
fact: Peale's dolphin lives among the kelp beds and channels of Patagonia and the Falkland Islands and is named after artist Titian Peale.

name: Peanut worm
fact: When disturbed, a peanut worm pulls its narrow front end into its body, leaving a shape like a peanut.

name: Pearl diver
fact: Pearl divers gather oysters from the seabed by free-diving, hunting for natural pearls.

name: Pearlfish
fact: The pearlfish spends the day hiding inside the body of a sea cucumber, slipping in tail-first through its anus.

name: Pearlside
fact: Pearlsides are small fish with rows of light organs on their undersides that help them blend with the dim light from above.

name: Pearly razorfish
fact: The pearly razorfish is a wrasse with a blade-thin head that dives headfirst into sand in an instant to escape, and sleeps buried there.

name: Pederson's cleaner shrimp
fact: Pederson's cleaner shrimp is see-through with violet spots and lives on Caribbean anemones, where it cleans parasites from visiting fish.

name: Peggy's Point Lighthouse
fact: Peggy's Point Lighthouse perches on granite rocks at Peggy's Cove in Nova Scotia and is among the most photographed lighthouses in Canada.

name: Pelagibacter
fact: Pelagibacter ubique, from the SAR11 group, is probably the most abundant organism on Earth, a bacterium with hundreds of thousands in every millilitre of surface seawater.

name: Pelagic stingray
fact: The pelagic stingray is the only stingray that lives in the open ocean rather than on the seabed.

name: Pelagic thresher
fact: Pelagic threshers rise to a reef cleaning station at Malapascua in the Philippines each dawn to have parasites picked off by cleaner wrasses.

name: Pelagos Sanctuary
aliases: Pelagos Sanctuary for Mediterranean Marine Mammals
fact: The Pelagos Sanctuary is a marine mammal reserve between France, Monaco and Italy where fin whales and striped dolphins feed in the Ligurian Sea.

name: Pelican
fact: A pelican scoops fish in a throat pouch that can hold around 10 litres of water, which it drains before swallowing the catch.

name: Pelican eel
fact: The pelican eel, or gulper eel, has a vast pouch-like mouth on a thin body and lives in the deep sea, where it has been filmed ballooning its head.

name: Pelican's foot
fact: The pelican's foot is a small European sea snail whose shell lip spreads into webbed fingers like a pelican's foot.

name: Pelorus
fact: A pelorus is a compass-like ring with sighting vanes that measures the bearing of an object relative to the ship's heading.

name: Pemba Island
fact: Pemba Island lies north of Zanzibar off the coast of Tanzania and is known for its cloves.

name: Penang
fact: Penang is an island off the north-west coast of Malaysia, and its capital, George Town, is a World Heritage Site.

name: Penguin
fact: Penguins have backward-pointing spines on the tongue and roof of the mouth that stop slippery krill and fish escaping as they swallow.

name: Pennella
fact: Pennella is a parasitic copepod that buries its head in the flesh of whales and fish, trailing a long egg-bearing body.

name: Penteconter
fact: The penteconter was an early Greek warship rowed by fifty oarsmen in a single bank on each side.

name: Pentland Firth
fact: The Pentland Firth between mainland Scotland and Orkney has some of the fastest tidal currents in the world, used today to generate electricity.

name: Peppered corydoras
fact: The peppered corydoras is a mottled South American armoured catfish that has long been a favourite in aquariums.

name: Peppermint angelfish
fact: The peppermint angelfish, striped red and white, lives on deep reefs in the Cook Islands below 100 metres; one at Hawaii's Waikiki Aquarium drew offers of 30,000 dollars.

name: Peppermint shrimp
fact: The peppermint shrimp is stocked in reef aquariums because it eats the pest anemone Aiptasia.

name: Peral
fact: The Peral was an electric-powered Spanish submarine built by Isaac Peral and launched in 1888.

name: Perch
fact: European perch have dark vertical bars and a spiny dorsal fin, and hunt in shoals in lakes and slow rivers.

name: The Perfect Storm
fact: The Perfect Storm is Sebastian Junger's 1997 book about the loss of the fishing boat Andrea Gail, filmed by Wolfgang Petersen in 2000.

name: Periwinkle
fact: Periwinkles are small shore snails that seal themselves inside their shells with a trapdoor to survive hours out of water at low tide.

name: Permit
fact: The permit is a wary, deep-bodied flats fish of the Caribbean that fly anglers consider among the hardest to catch.

name: Peru
fact: Peru's Pacific coast is washed by the cold Humboldt Current, which feeds one of the world's richest fisheries.

name: Peru-Chile Trench
fact: The Peru-Chile Trench, or Atacama Trench, runs about 5,900 kilometres along South America's Pacific coast and reaches about 8,000 metres deep.

name: Peruvian anchoveta
fact: The Peruvian anchoveta is the most heavily fished species on Earth, with catches that have topped 10 million tonnes a year, nearly all ground into fishmeal.

name: Peruvian pelican
fact: The Peruvian pelican feeds mainly on anchoveta in the cold, productive Humboldt Current.

name: Peruvian scallop
fact: The Peruvian scallop is farmed along the coasts of Peru and Chile.

name: Petrale sole
fact: The petrale sole, a right-eyed flounder of the US and Canadian Pacific coast, is one of the most prized flatfish caught there.

name: Petrel
fact: Petrels are tube-nosed seabirds with a keen sense of smell that pick fish, squid and krill from the water, and the giant petrels also scavenge.

name: Petropavlovsk-Kamchatsky
fact: Petropavlovsk-Kamchatsky in Russia's Far East was founded in 1740 by Vitus Bering's expedition and sits on Avacha Bay.

name: Phaeocystis
fact: Phaeocystis is a colony-forming alga whose spring blooms whip up thick brown foam on North Sea beaches.

name: Phantom jelly
fact: The phantom jelly is a rarely seen deep-sea giant with ribbon-like oral arms that can stretch up to about 10 metres.

name: Pharaoh cuttlefish
fact: The pharaoh cuttlefish of the Indo-Pacific is one of the most heavily fished cuttlefish and is also bred in labs for research.

name: Pharos of Alexandria
fact: The Pharos of Alexandria was completed around 280 BC, stood roughly 100 metres tall, and was one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World.

name: Pheasant shell
fact: The pheasant shell is a glossy Australian sea snail whose colourful pattern resembles a pheasant's plumage.

name: Philippe Cousteau
fact: Philippe Cousteau, Jacques Cousteau's younger son, filmed and co-produced many of his father's undersea documentaries before dying in a seaplane crash in 1979.

name: Philippine Sea
fact: The Philippine Sea, east of the Philippines, is the largest sea in the world by area and contains the Mariana Trench.

name: Philippine Trench
fact: The Philippine Trench off Mindanao reaches about 10,500 metres at the Emden Deep, named after the German cruiser that sounded it in 1927.

name: Philippines
fact: The Philippines is an archipelago of more than 7,000 islands between the South China Sea and the Pacific.

name: Phoenix Islands Protected Area
fact: The Phoenix Islands Protected Area in Kiribati covers more than 400,000 square kilometres of the central Pacific around eight coral atolls.

name: Phorcys
fact: Phorcys was a Greek sea god who with his sister Ceto fathered many sea monsters.

name: Phronima
fact: Phronima is a transparent amphipod that hollows out a salp and lives inside the barrel, rearing its young there as it drifts.

name: Phuket
fact: Phuket is Thailand's largest island and lies in the Andaman Sea.

name: Varicose phyllidia
fact: The varicose phyllidia is a black sea slug with yellow-tipped bumps that makes toxic chemicals to deter predators.

name: Phyllodesmium longicirrum
fact: Phyllodesmium sea slugs feed on soft corals and house algae in their long, feathery gills.

name: Phyllosoma larva
fact: The phyllosoma larva of spiny and slipper lobsters is flat, leaf-shaped and as clear as glass while it drifts in the plankton.

name: Phytoplankton
fact: Phytoplankton are the drifting microscopic algae and bacteria that produce roughly half of the oxygen in Earth's atmosphere.

name: Picasso triggerfish
fact: The Picasso triggerfish wears a pattern of blue, black and yellow stripes that looks painted on, and it drums by beating its pectoral fins against its swim bladder.

name: Pickling
fact: Pickling preserves fish in vinegar or brine, as with the herring of northern Europe.

name: Pictus catfish
fact: The pictus catfish is a spotted, long-whiskered aquarium catfish from the Amazon and Orinoco whose barbels can be as long as its body.

name: Piddock
fact: The common piddock bores into soft rock and clay and is famously bioluminescent.

name: Pierre-Charles Villeneuve
fact: Pierre-Charles Villeneuve commanded the combined French and Spanish fleet defeated at Trafalgar in 1805.

name: Piet Heyn
fact: Piet Heyn was a Dutch privateer who captured a Spanish silver fleet at Matanzas Bay in 1628.

name: Pigeon Point Lighthouse
fact: Pigeon Point Lighthouse in California, about 35 metres tall, is among the tallest lighthouses on the United States west coast.

name: Pigfish
fact: The pigfish makes grunting noises by grinding its throat teeth, which gives it its name.

name: Piglet squid
fact: The piglet squid is a see-through, balloon-shaped deep-sea squid whose tuft of arms above a snout-like funnel gives it a comical piggy face.

name: Pikaia
fact: Pikaia is a Cambrian worm-like animal from the Burgess Shale that had a primitive stiffening rod and is thought to be an early relative of vertebrates.

name: Pike
fact: Pike are ambush predators with long, duck-bill-shaped snouts and are top freshwater hunters across the northern hemisphere.

name: Pike conger
fact: The daggertooth pike conger is a fanged eel of Indo-Pacific coasts eaten in Japan as hamo, famously in Kyoto in summer.

name: Pillar coral
fact: Pillar coral grows in tall columns up to about 3 metres high and, unlike most corals, extends its feeding polyps by day.

name: Pilot fish
fact: Pilot fish swim alongside sharks, rays and turtles, feeding on scraps and parasites, and are rarely attacked by their hosts.

name: Pilot whale
fact: Pilot whales are large dolphins that travel in tight-knit pods and are prone to mass strandings on beaches.

name: Pincushion starfish
fact: The pincushion starfish of Indo-Pacific reefs is so plump and rounded that its five arms are barely visible, making it look like a puffed-up pillow.

name: Pineapplefish
fact: The pineapplefish has yellow, black-edged scales that resemble a pineapple's skin and carries glowing bacteria in organs on its lower jaw.

name: Pinecone fish
fact: The pinecone fish is armoured in big plated scales and carries glowing bacteria in two light organs on its lower jaw to lure prey at night.

name: Pinfish
fact: The pinfish of the western Atlantic eats more and more seagrass as it grows, and is a common bait fish in Florida.

name: Ping-pong tree sponge
fact: The ping-pong tree sponge is a deep-sea carnivorous sponge with branches tipped by ball-shaped structures.

name: Pink ear emperor
fact: The pink ear emperor is a small emperor named for the pinkish patch on its gill cover.

name: Pink salmon
fact: Pink salmon are the smallest and most abundant Pacific salmon and live on a strict two-year cycle, so odd-year and even-year runs never mix.

name: Pink Sands Beach
fact: Pink Sands Beach on Harbour Island in the Bahamas gets its blush from the crushed shells of tiny red-shelled organisms.

name: Pink sea fan
fact: The pink sea fan is a branching gorgonian of British and Mediterranean waters, protected by law in the UK.

name: Pink skunk clownfish
fact: The pink skunk clownfish is a pale pink anemonefish with a white stripe along its back, like a skunk, living in magnificent anemones.

name: Pink vent fish
fact: The pink vent fish is an eelpout found only at East Pacific vents, where it lies among the tube worms and eats limpets and amphipods.

name: Pink whipray
fact: The pink whipray is a large Indo-Pacific stingray that often rests in piles of several individuals on sandy lagoon floors.

name: Pinktail triggerfish
fact: The pinktail triggerfish is a dark Indo-Pacific triggerfish with a pink tail, found on outer reef slopes.

name: Pipefish
fact: Pipefish are straightened-out relatives of seahorses, and the males carry the eggs on their belly or in a brood pouch until they hatch.

name: Pipehorse
fact: Pipehorses, relatives of seahorses and pipefish, have a horse-like head on a long straight body and a grasping tail.

name: Pipi
fact: Pipi are wedge-shaped surf clams dug from sandy beaches in Australia and New Zealand, traditionally found by twisting your feet into the wet sand.

name: Piraeus
fact: Piraeus is the port of Athens and was developed by the statesman Themistocles in the fifth century BC.

name: Piraíba
fact: The piraíba is the giant catfish of the Amazon, reaching about 3 metres and more than 150 kilograms, the largest catfish in the Americas.

name: Piranha
