fact: Piranhas bark, drum and croak by vibrating their swim bladder, with different sounds for warning, confronting and snapping at rivals.

name: Pirates of the Caribbean
fact: Pirates of the Caribbean began with Gore Verbinski's 2003 film The Curse of the Black Pearl, based on a Disney theme-park ride.

name: Pisces III
fact: Pisces III was a British submersible that sank off Ireland in 1973 and whose two crew were rescued after about three days on the seabed.

name: Pisces V
fact: Pisces V is a research submersible operated from Hawaii that has explored undersea volcanoes such as Loihi.

name: Pismo clam
fact: The Pismo clam is a large clam of the Californian coast named after Pismo Beach.

name: Pistol shrimp
fact: A pistol shrimp snaps its claw shut so fast it creates a collapsing bubble that briefly approaches the temperature of the Sun's surface and stuns prey.

name: Piston corer
fact: A piston corer is a long tube driven into the seabed to extract a column of sediment recording the history of the ocean.

name: Pitcairn Islands
fact: Pitcairn Island was settled in 1790 by the mutineers of HMS Bounty and remains one of the least populated territories on Earth.

name: Piure
fact: The piure is a red-fleshed sea squirt of the Chilean coast that is eaten as a local delicacy.

name: Pla ra
fact: Pla ra is a Thai condiment of fish fermented with salt and rice bran for months.

name: Placoderm
fact: Placoderms, the first jawed fish, wore bony armour on their heads and vanished entirely about 360 million years ago.

name: Plaice
fact: Plaice are easy to recognise by the bright orange spots scattered across their brown upper side.

name: Plain bonito
fact: The plain bonito is an unstriped, deep-bodied bonito of the eastern Atlantic and Mediterranean.

name: Planehead filefish
fact: The planehead filefish is a western Atlantic filefish that can change its colour pattern to blend in.

name: Plank cooking
fact: Plank cooking bakes or grills fish on a soaked wooden plank, a Pacific Northwest tradition used for salmon.

name: Plankton
fact: Plankton means 'wanderer' in Greek: it is every organism, from bacteria to jellyfish, that cannot swim against the current.

name: Plankton net
fact: A plankton net is a fine mesh net towed through the sea to collect tiny drifting organisms for study.

name: Platecarpus
fact: Platecarpus was a streamlined mid-sized mosasaur of the Late Cretaceous seas of North America and Europe.

name: Platy
fact: The platy is a small Mexican livebearer bred into dozens of colour forms and recommended for every beginner's tank.

name: Platypus
fact: The platypus hunts with its eyes, ears and nostrils closed, finding prey entirely with about 40,000 electric sensors in its rubbery bill.

name: Playa Flamenco
fact: Playa Flamenco on Culebra, Puerto Rico, is a horseshoe bay where rusting military tanks still sit on the sand.

name: Playa Hermosa
fact: Playa Hermosa near Jaco in Costa Rica is a fast, hollow beach break that has hosted international contests.

name: Pleco
fact: Plecos gulp air at the surface and absorb the oxygen through their stomach lining when the water runs low in oxygen.

name: Plesiosaur
fact: Plesiosaurs were long-necked marine reptiles that flew through the water on four flippers and vanished with the dinosaurs 66 million years ago.

name: California Pleurobranchaea
fact: The California Pleurobranchaea is a predatory sea slug studied for how a simple nervous system makes decisions.

name: Plimsoll line
fact: The Plimsoll line is a mark on a ship's hull showing the deepest it may safely be loaded, named after Samuel Plimsoll.

name: Pliny Trench
fact: The Pliny Trench is one of the deep trenches of the Hellenic subduction zone south of Crete in the eastern Mediterranean.

name: Pliosaur
fact: Pliosaurs were short-necked, huge-headed marine reptiles whose bite was among the most powerful of any animal that ever lived.

name: Plumose anemone
fact: The plumose anemone is a tall white or orange anemone with a feathery crown of hundreds of fine tentacles, common on wrecks and pier legs.

name: Poaching
fact: Poaching cooks fish gently in barely simmering liquid, such as a seasoned stock or milk.

name: Pocket battleship
fact: Pocket battleship was the British nickname for Germany's Deutschland class of the 1930s, which packed heavy guns into a hull limited by the Treaty of Versailles.

name: Pocket shark
fact: Only two pocket sharks have ever been found, and the tiny shark's pocket glands near its front fins are thought to squirt glowing fluid.

name: Poema del Mar
fact: Poema del Mar in Las Palmas on Gran Canaria opened in 2018 and recreates marine habitats from around the world.

name: Pohnpei
fact: Pohnpei is a high volcanic island in Micronesia, home to Nan Madol, a city built on coral reef islets.

name: Poisson cru
fact: Poisson cru is the national dish of Tahiti, raw fish marinated in lime juice and finished with coconut milk.

name: Poke
fact: Poke is a Hawaiian dish of cubed raw fish, usually tuna, seasoned with soy sauce and sesame oil.

name: Polar bear
fact: Polar bears are classed as marine mammals because they spend most of their lives on sea ice hunting seals, and they can swim for days.

name: Polarstern
fact: The German icebreaker Polarstern spent a year frozen into Arctic sea ice for the MOSAiC expedition of 2019 to 2020, the largest polar research expedition ever mounted.

name: Pollack
fact: The pollack is a golden-brown European cousin of cod with a jutting lower jaw, popular with sea anglers around rocky coasts and wrecks.

name: Pollock
fact: Pollock, a cod relative, produce thumping sounds with their swim bladder when handled or cornered, a trait shared with cod and haddock, which grunt during spawning.

name: Fourlined polycera
fact: The fourlined polycera is a small sea slug of North Atlantic shores that feeds on bryozoans.

name: Pom-pom crab
fact: The pom-pom crab holds a live sea anemone in each claw and waves them like boxing gloves; if it loses one it tears the other in half to grow a new pair.

name: Pompeii worm
fact: The Pompeii worm lives in tubes on vent chimneys with its tail in water of around 80 degrees Celsius, making it one of the most heat-tolerant animals known.

name: Ponta Delgada
fact: Ponta Delgada, the largest city of the Azores, sits on the island of São Miguel in the middle of the North Atlantic.

name: Pontoh's pygmy seahorse
fact: Pontoh's pygmy seahorse is a free-living pygmy seahorse of about 1.7 centimetres that clings to algae and hydroids rather than sea fans.

name: Pontus
fact: Pontus was the Greek primordial god of the sea, born of Gaia without a father, and he fathered many sea deities.

name: Ponyfish
fact: Ponyfish keep glowing bacteria in a ring-shaped organ around the throat and shine the light out through transparent windows in their bellies.

name: Ponyo
fact: Ponyo is Hayao Miyazaki's 2008 animated film about a goldfish princess who wants to become human, loosely inspired by The Little Mermaid.

name: Ponza
fact: Ponza is the largest of the Pontine Islands, which lie off the Italian coast between Rome and Naples.

name: Poop deck
fact: The poop deck is a raised deck at the stern of a ship, and the name comes from the Latin word for stern.

name: Poor cod
fact: The poor cod is a small, coppery cod relative of European coasts, too small to be worth eating but important food for larger fish.

name: Poor Knights Islands
fact: The Poor Knights Islands off New Zealand's North Island are a marine reserve that Jacques Cousteau rated among the best dive sites in the world.

name: Porbeagle
fact: The porbeagle, a cold-water cousin of the great white, keeps its muscles warm and ranges as far north as Iceland and Norway.

name: Porcelain crab
fact: Porcelain crabs are flat, fragile crab-like animals that filter plankton with feathery mouthparts and readily drop a leg to escape.

name: Porcupine Bank
fact: Porcupine Bank, west of Ireland, is a raised area of seabed named after HMS Porcupine, the survey ship that charted it in the 1860s.

name: Porcupine ray
fact: The porcupine ray has no stinging spine at all; instead its back is covered in sharp thorns.

name: Porcupinefish
fact: The porcupinefish inflates into a spiky ball when threatened, and its skin and organs carry tetrodotoxin, so it is poisonous to eat.

name: Porites
fact: Porites corals grow in massive domes so slowly and steadily that scientists drill cores from them to read centuries of ocean climate.

name: Porkfish
fact: The porkfish, a yellow-striped grunt with two black bars on its head, schools under Caribbean ledges by day and feeds at night.

name: Porpoise
fact: Porpoises are small toothed whales with spade-shaped teeth and blunt snouts, unlike the cone-shaped teeth and beaks of dolphins.

name: Port
fact: Port is the left-hand side of a ship when facing forward, and the word replaced larboard to avoid confusion with starboard.

name: Port Blair
fact: Port Blair is the capital of India's Andaman and Nicobar Islands in the Bay of Bengal.

name: Port Hedland
fact: Port Hedland in Western Australia ships iron ore from the Pilbara and handles more cargo by weight than any other port in Australia.

name: Port Jackson shark
fact: Port Jackson sharks lay spiral-shaped eggs that the mother wedges into rock crevices.

name: Port Louis
fact: Port Louis, the capital of Mauritius, was founded by the French in 1735 and remains the island's main port.

name: Port Moresby
fact: Port Moresby, the capital of Papua New Guinea, was named after the British naval officer John Moresby, who explored the coast in 1873.

name: Port Said
fact: Port Said was founded in 1859 at the Mediterranean entrance of the Suez Canal, which opened in 1869.

name: Port Sudan
fact: Port Sudan on the Red Sea was built in the early twentieth century to replace the old port of Suakin and is Sudan's main seaport.

name: Port Vila
fact: Port Vila on the island of Efate is the capital and main port of Vanuatu.

name: Portland Head Light
fact: Portland Head Light in Maine was first lit in 1791 and is one of the most photographed lighthouses in the United States.

name: Porto
fact: Porto, at the mouth of the Douro river, gave its name both to Portugal and to port wine.

name: Portugal
fact: The whole of mainland Portugal's coast faces the Atlantic, and its sailors launched the Age of Discovery from there.

name: Portugal Current
fact: The Portugal Current is a slow, cool current flowing south off Portugal as part of the North Atlantic gyre and feeding the Canary Current.

name: Portuguese dogfish
fact: The Portuguese dogfish has been caught at nearly 3,700 metres, deeper than any other shark known.

name: Portuguese man o' war
fact: The Portuguese man o' war is not a jellyfish but a colony of specialised animals under a gas-filled sail, trailing tentacles that can reach 30 metres.

name: Poseidon
fact: In Greek myth Poseidon ruled the sea and also caused earthquakes, and he carried a three-pronged trident.

name: The Poseidon Adventure
fact: The Poseidon Adventure is a 1972 film directed by Ronald Neame, from Paul Gallico's 1969 novel, about survivors of a liner capsized by a giant wave.

name: Potato cod
fact: The potato cod is a grouper of the Indo-Pacific covered in large dark blotches like potatoes; the tame giants of the Cod Hole on the Great Barrier Reef are famous among divers.

name: Potter's angelfish
fact: Potter's angelfish is a dwarf angelfish found only in Hawaii, orange with blue-black scribbles.

name: Pourquoi-Pas?
fact: Pourquoi-Pas? was Jean-Baptiste Charcot's polar research ship, which sank off Iceland in 1936.

name: Pouting
fact: The pouting, or bib, is a small, deep-bodied cod relative with coppery bands, common around piers and wrecks in European waters.

name: Powder blue tang
fact: The powder blue tang is a pale blue surgeonfish with a black face and yellow dorsal fin, found on Indian Ocean reefs, often in large grazing schools.

name: Powder monkey
fact: A powder monkey was a young boy on a warship who carried gunpowder from the magazine to the cannon.

name: Praia do Cassino
fact: Praia do Cassino in southern Brazil is often claimed as the longest uninterrupted beach in the world, at more than 200 kilometres.

name: Praslin
fact: Praslin in the Seychelles is home to the Vallée de Mai, where the coco de mer, the largest seed in the world, grows.

name: Prawn
fact: Prawn and shrimp are not scientific terms: Britain and Australia mostly say prawn and North America mostly says shrimp for the same animals.

name: Prawn cocktail
fact: Prawn cocktail is a starter of prawns in a pink sauce on lettuce, which was hugely popular in Britain in the 1960s and 1970s.

name: Pre-dreadnought
fact: Pre-dreadnoughts were the steel battleships built before HMS Dreadnought in 1906, with a mix of heavy and medium guns.

name: Predatory tunicate
fact: The predatory tunicate is a sea squirt anchored in deep-sea canyons that holds its hood open like a Venus flytrap and snaps it shut on passing animals.

name: Priapulid worm
fact: Priapulid worms burrow in cold seafloor mud and look much as their relatives did in the Cambrian, more than 500 million years ago.

name: Prickly redfish
fact: The prickly redfish is one of the largest sea cucumbers and is covered in spiky red-orange bumps.

name: Prickly shark
fact: The prickly shark is a bulky Pacific relative of the bramble shark, covered in thorn-like scales, and lives on deep slopes.

name: Prideaux's hermit crab
fact: Prideaux's hermit crab carries a cloak anemone on its shell, gaining protection while the anemone gets scraps and a ride.

name: Prince Albert I of Monaco
fact: Prince Albert I of Monaco spent his fortune on oceanographic cruises in the 1880s and 1890s and founded the Oceanographic Museum of Monaco.

name: Prince Edward Island
fact: Prince Edward Island is Canada's smallest province, a red-soiled island in the Gulf of St Lawrence.

name: Prince Rupert
fact: Prince Rupert in British Columbia is a deep-water port that is among the closest North American ports to Asia.

name: Prince William Sound
fact: Prince William Sound in Alaska was the scene of the 1989 Exxon Valdez oil spill.

name: Princess parrotfish
fact: The princess parrotfish is a Caribbean parrotfish whose males are blue-green with pink stripes, and it grazes in mixed schools over the reef.

name: Proa
fact: The proa is a Pacific sailing canoe with an outrigger float, famed for its speed.

name: Proboscis monkey
fact: The proboscis monkey lives only in Borneo's mangrove and riverside forests, swims well with partly webbed feet, and the male's huge nose amplifies its calls.

name: Prochlorococcus
fact: Prochlorococcus is the most abundant photosynthetic organism on Earth, yet this tiny ocean bacterium was not discovered until 1986.

name: Project AWARE
fact: Project AWARE is a non-profit working with the scuba diving community to protect the ocean, with a focus on marine debris and sharks.

name: Proteus
fact: Proteus was a Greek sea god and shepherd of Poseidon's seals who could change his shape, which is where the word protean comes from.

name: Providencia
fact: Providencia is a small volcanic Colombian island in the western Caribbean that was once used as a base by the pirate Henry Morgan.

name: Prydz Bay
fact: Prydz Bay in East Antarctica is named after the Norwegian whaling captain Olaf Prydz.

name: Pseudo-nitzschia
fact: Pseudo-nitzschia is a chain-forming diatom, and some species make the toxin domoic acid, which can poison shellfish and seabirds.

name: Ptychodus
fact: Ptychodus was a Cretaceous shark with flat, ridged, pavement-like teeth suited to crushing hard-shelled prey.

name: Puddingwife
fact: The puddingwife is a large Atlantic wrasse that can reach about 50 centimetres and changes colour as it matures.

name: Puerto Escondido
fact: Playa Zicatela at Puerto Escondido in Oaxaca, Mexico, is nicknamed the Mexican Pipeline for its heavy barrelling waves.

name: Puerto Rico
fact: Puerto Rico lies at the eastern end of the Greater Antilles, and just north of it the Puerto Rico Trench drops to the deepest point in the Atlantic.

name: Puerto Rico Trench
fact: The Puerto Rico Trench is the deepest point in the Atlantic Ocean, reaching about 8,400 metres at the Milwaukee Deep.

name: Puffadder shyshark
fact: The puffadder shyshark of South African kelp forests curls into a ring and covers its eyes with its tail when threatened, hence the name shyshark.

name: Pufferfish
fact: Pufferfish carry tetrodotoxin, a poison with no antidote that is about 1,200 times deadlier than cyanide, yet fugu is a Japanese delicacy.

name: Puget Sound
fact: Puget Sound is a deep, glacier-carved inlet of the Pacific in Washington state, named by George Vancouver after his lieutenant Peter Puget, with Seattle on its shore.

name: Pulley Ridge
fact: Pulley Ridge, off south-west Florida, is a drowned reef holding some of the deepest light-dependent coral in US waters.

name: Pulpo a la gallega
fact: Pulpo a la gallega is boiled octopus served with olive oil, paprika and salt, a traditional dish of Galicia in Spain.

name: Pumpkinseed
fact: The pumpkinseed sunfish is a brightly coloured pond fish of North America that has become invasive across Europe.

name: Punalu'u Beach
fact: Punalu'u Beach on Hawaii's Big Island has black sand made of fragmented basalt, and green sea turtles often haul out on it.

name: Hatshepsut's expedition to Punt
fact: Around 1470 BC the Egyptian queen Hatshepsut sent a fleet to Punt, and the voyage is shown in carvings at her temple at Deir el-Bahari.

name: Punta de Lobos
fact: Punta de Lobos near Pichilemu in Chile is a long left-hand point wave that was declared a World Surfing Reserve in 2013.

name: Puntarenas
fact: Puntarenas in Costa Rica is a port built on a long, narrow sandy spit that reaches into the Gulf of Nicoya.

name: Purple sea urchin
fact: Purple sea urchins can bore shallow pits into solid rock and, left unchecked, can mow down whole kelp forests.

name: Purple shore crab
fact: The purple shore crab of the Pacific coast has purple spots on its claws and hides under rocks in the intertidal zone.

name: Purple-striped jelly
fact: The purple-striped jelly of the Californian coast has long frilly arms and often lives alongside the jellies it feeds on.

name: Purple-striped jellyfish
fact: The purple-striped jellyfish of Monterey Bay feeds on other jellyfish, especially moon jellies.

name: Purple vase sponge
fact: The purple vase sponge grows in tall, vase-shaped tubes on Caribbean reefs.

name: Purpleback flying squid
fact: The purpleback flying squid has a glowing patch on its back and can glide above the surface of tropical seas.

name: Purse seiner
fact: A purse seiner surrounds a school of fish with a long wall of net, then draws the bottom closed like a purse; most tuna and sardines are caught this way.

name: Purser
fact: The purser is the ship's officer who manages money, passengers and supplies.

name: Puysegur Trench
fact: The Puysegur Trench off the south-west tip of New Zealand is where the Australian Plate begins to slide beneath the Pacific Plate.

name: Pygmy beaked whale
fact: The pygmy beaked whale is one of the smallest beaked whales and was first described from Peruvian waters in the early 1990s.

name: Pygmy blue whale
fact: The pygmy blue whale, a subspecies of the blue whale in the Indian Ocean and South Pacific, is shorter overall and has a proportionally shorter tail section than other blues.

name: Pygmy Bryde's whale
fact: The pygmy Bryde's whale, now often called Eden's whale, is a small baleen whale of warm Indo-Pacific coastal waters.

name: Pygmy corydoras
fact: The pygmy corydoras is a 2.5-centimetre armoured catfish from Brazil that, unlike its relatives, swims in mid-water in shoals.

name: Pygmy killer whale
fact: The pygmy killer whale is a small, little-known dark dolphin of tropical seas that was known only from two skulls until the 1950s.

name: Pygmy killifish
fact: The pygmy killifish of the south-eastern United States rarely grows beyond about 3 to 4 centimetres.

name: Pygmy right whale
fact: The pygmy right whale is the smallest and least-known baleen whale, rarely seen alive in the cool waters of the Southern Hemisphere.

name: Pygmy seahorse
fact: Pygmy seahorses are mostly under 2.5 centimetres long and so well camouflaged on sea fans and corals that the first was found only when its host fan was collected.

name: Pygmy sperm whale
fact: The pygmy sperm whale squirts a cloud of reddish-brown fluid to confuse predators, much as a squid uses ink.

name: Pygmy squid
fact: Pygmy squid are among the smallest cephalopods, about the size of a fingernail, and glue themselves to seagrass blades with a sticky patch on their back.

name: Pygmy sunfish
fact: Pygmy sunfishes of the southeastern United States are 2-to-3-centimetre swamp fish, not true sunfish, that flash iridescent blue when breeding.

name: Pyjama shark
fact: The pyjama shark, a striped catshark of South African kelp forests, starred in the film My Octopus Teacher and hunts at night.

name: Pyramid butterflyfish
fact: The pyramid butterflyfish has a yellow upper body with a white pyramid-shaped patch and gathers in big schools to feed on plankton above the reef.

name: Pyrosome
fact: A pyrosome is a hollow tube of thousands of cloned tunicates that glows blue-green, and some grow longer than a bus.

name: Pytheas's voyage
fact: Around 325 BC the Greek explorer Pytheas sailed from Massalia to northern Europe and described a distant land he called Thule.

name: Q-ship
fact: A Q-ship was a heavily armed warship disguised as a harmless merchant vessel to lure submarines into surface attack.

name: Qatar
fact: Qatar is a peninsula that juts out into the Persian Gulf.

name: Queen Elizabeth 2
fact: Queen Elizabeth 2 sailed for Cunard from 1969 to 2008 and has since become a floating hotel in Dubai.

name: Quadrant
fact: A quadrant measures the angle of a star or the sun above the horizon, and it was an early navigation tool used before the sextant.

name: Quagga mussel
fact: The quagga mussel followed the zebra mussel into the Great Lakes and has largely replaced it, carpeting the lake beds in their trillions.

name: Quahog
fact: The quahog is the hard clam of New England chowder, and its cousin the ocean quahog, dredged off Iceland, lived to 507 years, the oldest animal ever aged.

name: Quartermaster
fact: On a ship the quartermaster steers and helps with navigation, and in the navy the rank also covers stores and signals.

name: Queen angelfish
fact: The queen angelfish of the Caribbean wears a blue 'crown' ringed with spots on its forehead and feeds mostly on sponges.

name: Queen Anne's Revenge
fact: Blackbeard's flagship Queen Anne's Revenge ran aground and was lost off Beaufort, North Carolina, in 1718; its wreck was found in 1996.

name: Queen conch
fact: The queen conch has a heavy shell with a flared pink lip and has been a staple food of the Caribbean for centuries.

name: Queen coris
fact: The queen coris is an Indian Ocean wrasse whose colour and pattern change dramatically as it grows from juvenile to adult.

name: Queen helmet
fact: The queen helmet is a large sea snail that feeds on sea urchins and whose thick shell has been carved into cameos.

name: Queen Mary 2
fact: The Queen Mary 2 entered service in 2004 and is a Cunard ocean liner still running regular transatlantic crossings.

name: Queen parrotfish
fact: The queen parrotfish of the Caribbean sleeps at night inside a cocoon of mucus that it secretes, which may hide its scent from predators.

name: Queen scallop
fact: Queen scallops, smaller than king scallops, escape danger by clapping their shells to jet through the water.

name: Queen snapper
fact: The queen snapper is a bright red, large-eyed snapper of the deep Atlantic reef slope.

name: Queen triggerfish
fact: The queen triggerfish of the Caribbean and tropical Atlantic blows jets of water to flip sea urchins over and eat their soft undersides.

name: Queenfish
fact: The queenfish is a fast, silvery fish of Indo-Pacific shallows that often leaps clear of the water while chasing prey.

name: Quinquereme
fact: The quinquereme was the standard large warship of Carthage and Rome in the Punic Wars, rowed by crews of several hundred.

name: Ra expeditions
fact: On the Ra expeditions of 1969 and 1970 Thor Heyerdahl sailed papyrus reed boats across the Atlantic, and Ra II reached Barbados.

name: Rabaul
fact: Rabaul on New Britain in Papua New Guinea was largely buried in ash by the twin volcanic eruptions of 1994.

name: Rabbitfish
fact: Rabbitfish are harmless-looking reef grazers with venomous spines in their fins that cause an agonising sting if handled.

name: Raccoon butterflyfish
fact: The raccoon butterflyfish has a black mask across its eyes like a raccoon and feeds at night on coral polyps and small animals.

name: Rachel Carson
fact: Rachel Carson was a marine biologist whose book The Sea Around Us, published in 1951, introduced millions of readers to the science of the oceans.

name: Radar
fact: Radar bounces radio waves off objects, and ships use it to spot other vessels, land and storms in the dark or in fog.

name: Radiolarian
fact: Radiolarians are single-celled plankton with intricate glassy skeletons of silica, so beautiful that Ernst Haeckel drew hundreds of them in the 1800s.

name: Rainbow parrotfish
fact: The rainbow parrotfish is the largest parrotfish in the Atlantic, up to about 1.2 metres, with a coppery body and green fins, and its young grow up in mangroves.

name: Rainbow Reef
fact: Rainbow Reef in Fiji's Somosomo Strait is known for the Great White Wall, a drop-off draped in white soft coral.

name: Rainbow runner
fact: The rainbow runner is a fast, streamlined jack that roams the open tropical oceans in schools.

name: Rainbow smelt
fact: Rainbow smelt live in coastal seas and run up rivers to spawn in early spring, and freshly caught smelt smell faintly of cucumber.

name: Rainbow trout
fact: Rainbow trout that migrate to sea are called steelhead; they return silver and powerful to spawn in their home rivers and can spawn more than once.

name: Rainbow Warrior
fact: The Greenpeace ship Rainbow Warrior was sunk by bombs planted by French agents in Auckland harbour in 1985.

name: Rainbow wrasse
fact: The rainbow wrasse of the Mediterranean and eastern Atlantic is a small wrasse in which many females later change sex to become brightly striped males.

name: Rainbowfish
fact: Rainbowfish from New Guinea and Australia shimmer with shifting colours and are among the most peaceful community aquarium fish.

name: Raja Ampat
fact: The reefs of Raja Ampat in Indonesia hold more coral and reef-fish species than almost anywhere else on Earth, at the heart of the Coral Triangle.

name: Rakfisk
fact: Rakfisk is Norwegian trout that is salted and fermented for months and eaten uncooked.

name: Ram cichlid
fact: The ram cichlid is a small, brilliantly coloured dwarf cichlid from Venezuelan and Colombian streams that pairs up to guard its eggs.

name: Ramari's beaked whale
fact: Ramari's beaked whale, described in 2021, is named after Māori whale expert Ramari Stewart, the first cetacean named after an indigenous woman.

name: Ram's horn squid
fact: The ram's horn squid carries a coiled, chambered shell inside its body, and the little white shells wash up on beaches worldwide.

name: Ran
fact: Ran is the Norse sea goddess who was said to catch drowning sailors in her net and take them to her hall below the waves.

name: Rangiroa
fact: Rangiroa in French Polynesia is one of the largest atolls in the world, with a lagoon so big that the whole island of Tahiti would fit inside it.

name: Ras Mohammed National Park
fact: Ras Mohammed, Egypt's first national park, sits at the tip of the Sinai where the Red Sea's Shark Reef and Yolanda Reef draw divers from around the world.

name: Raymond Spruance
fact: Raymond Spruance commanded the American carrier forces at the Battle of Midway in 1942 and at the Battle of the Philippine Sea in 1944.

name: Razee
fact: A razee was a warship that had one deck cut away, converting a ship of the line into a faster frigate-like vessel.

name: Razor clam
fact: Razor clams can dig down through wet sand faster than a person can dig, which is why collectors sprinkle salt to make them pop up.

name: Razor surgeonfish
fact: The razor surgeonfish grazes the rocky shores of the Galápagos in huge grey schools with bright yellow tails.

name: Razorbill
fact: The razorbill is the closest living relative of the extinct great auk and chases fish underwater using its wings.

name: Recife
fact: Recife is a Brazilian Atlantic port city of rivers and bridges, built partly on islands.

name: Red bait
fact: Red bait is a sea squirt of rocky shores in southern Africa and Australia that anglers cut up and use as fishing bait.

name: Red bass
fact: The red bass is a big reef snapper that so often carries ciguatera poison that it is a no-take species in Queensland, banned from being kept or sold.

name: Red-bellied piranha
fact: The red-bellied piranha hunts in shoals and uses razor-sharp, interlocking teeth to slice flesh from its prey.

name: Red-billed tropicbird
fact: The red-billed tropicbird has two very long central tail feathers and plunge-dives for flying fish and squid.

name: Red cod
fact: The red cod of New Zealand is a morid cod, a distant relative of the Atlantic cod, with a single chin barbel and pinkish skin.

name: Red coral
fact: Red coral from the Mediterranean has been harvested for jewellery for thousands of years and grows only a few millimetres a year.

name: Red drum
fact: The red drum, or redfish, is farmed in ponds and cages in Texas and China after blackened redfish made the wild fish a craze in the 1980s.

name: Red-eared slider
fact: The red-eared slider, the pet-shop turtle, has been dumped into ponds worldwide and is now one of the most widespread invasive reptiles.

name: Red emperor
fact: The red emperor is a large, red Indo-Pacific snapper that can reach about a metre.

name: Red-footed booby
fact: The red-footed booby is the smallest booby and, unlike its relatives, usually nests in trees and bushes.

name: Red grouper
fact: The red grouper of the Gulf of Mexico digs and maintains pits in the seabed that become homes for many other reef animals.

name: Red gurnard
fact: The red gurnard walks over the North Sea floor on finger-like fin rays and grunts audibly when caught.

name: Red hake
fact: The red hake is a western Atlantic hake with long, thread-like pelvic fins that it uses to feel along the seabed.

name: Red hind
fact: The red hind is a small Caribbean grouper with red spots that gathers to spawn at traditional sites and is a staple catch in the Virgin Islands.

name: Red-lipped batfish
fact: The red-lipped batfish of the Galápagos is a poor swimmer and instead walks across the seabed on its stiff, limb-like fins.

name: Red mangrove
fact: The red mangrove stands on arching prop roots and drops long, pencil-shaped seedlings that float away to take root on other shores.

name: Red mullet
fact: Red mullet feel for prey with two chin barbels, and the ancient Romans paid fortunes for large ones and watched them change colour as they died.

name: Red October
fact: The Red October is the fictional Soviet missile submarine in Tom Clancy's 1984 novel The Hunt for Red October.

name: Red reef lobster
fact: Unlike true spiny lobsters, reef lobsters carry small pincers on their first three pairs of legs.

name: Red rock crab
fact: The red rock crab of the Pacific Northwest has big black-tipped claws strong enough to crush barnacles and snails.

name: Red scorpionfish
fact: The red scorpionfish, the rascasse, has venomous spines and is the essential fish of a true Marseille bouillabaisse.

name: Red Sea bannerfish
fact: The Red Sea bannerfish trails a long white dorsal filament like a pennant and lives only in the Red Sea and Gulf of Aden.

name: Red sea bream
fact: Red sea bream, tai, is Japan's celebration fish, served as sashimi at weddings and New Year because its name sounds like 'medetai', meaning happy.

name: Red sea urchin
fact: The red sea urchin of the Pacific coast can live for more than 100 years, and its roe is sold as uni in sushi restaurants.

name: Red snapper
fact: The northern red snapper of the Gulf of Mexico can live for over 50 years and is so popular that many cheaper fish are passed off as it in restaurants.

name: Red swamp crayfish
fact: The red swamp crayfish is the star of Louisiana crawfish boils and has spread as an invader to rivers and rice paddies across Europe, Africa and Asia.

name: Red tide
fact: A red tide is a bloom of algae that colours the water and can poison fish and shellfish.

name: Red tree coral
fact: Red tree coral forms branching colonies in cold deep water of the North Atlantic and can live for centuries.

name: Redband parrotfish
fact: The redband parrotfish grazes algae from Caribbean reefs and helps keep coral from being smothered.

name: Redband trout
fact: Redband trout are rainbow trout of the dry interior of western North America, adapted to warm and harsh streams.

name: Redtail catfish
fact: The redtail catfish of the Amazon has a bright orange-red tail and grows well over a metre, a giant that aquarists often regret buying.

name: Redtoothed triggerfish
fact: The redtoothed triggerfish is blue-black with red teeth and feeds on plankton in the water column above Indo-Pacific reefs.

name: Reef Check
fact: Reef Check is a volunteer-led programme in which trained divers survey coral reefs around the world to track their health.

name: Reef manta ray
fact: Reef mantas visit cleaning stations on coral reefs and can be told apart by the unique spot patterns on their bellies.

name: Reef shark
fact: Reef sharks are the sleek, mostly harmless sharks that patrol coral reefs, and their numbers are a good sign of a healthy reef.

name: Reef triggerfish
fact: The reef triggerfish is Hawaii's state fish, with the famous Hawaiian name humuhumunukunukuāpuaʻa, meaning roughly 'triggerfish with a snout like a pig'.

name: Regal angelfish
fact: The regal angelfish, striped in orange, white and blue, is a shy sponge-eater of Indo-Pacific reefs that is notoriously difficult to keep in aquariums.

name: Reinhard Scheer
fact: Reinhard Scheer led the German High Seas Fleet at the Battle of Jutland in 1916.

name: Remora
fact: Remoras hitch rides on sharks, whales, turtles and even ships using a suction disc on top of the head, eating scraps and parasites.

name: Republic of the Congo
fact: The Republic of the Congo has a short Atlantic coast around Pointe-Noire, its second city and main port.

name: Restaurants
fact: Restaurants is a fast left-hand reef wave on Tavarua in Fiji, close to Cloudbreak.

name: Resurgam
fact: Resurgam was a steam-powered submarine built by the Reverend George Garrett in 1879, and it sank under tow off Wales in 1880.

name: Reticulate dascyllus
fact: The reticulate dascyllus is a small damselfish that shelters among branching corals in large groups.

name: Réunion
fact: Réunion is a French island whose volcano, the Piton de la Fournaise, is one of the most active in the world.

name: Revillagigedo Archipelago
fact: The Revillagigedo Islands, often just called Socorro, are a Mexican national park where giant oceanic manta rays approach divers to be cleaned.

name: Rex sole
fact: The rex sole is a slender, thin-bodied flatfish of the North Pacific with a very small mouth, usually fried whole on the bone.

name: Reykjanes Ridge
fact: The Reykjanes Ridge is the stretch of the Mid-Atlantic Ridge that runs south-west from Iceland, where the ridge actually rises above sea level.

name: Reykjavik
fact: Reykjavik, the world's northernmost national capital, grew up around its harbour and Iceland's fishing fleet.

name: Reynisfjara
fact: Reynisfjara near Vik in Iceland is a black volcanic sand beach backed by basalt columns and watched over by the Reynisdrangar sea stacks.

name: Rhine-Main-Danube Canal
fact: The Rhine-Main-Danube Canal, opened in 1992, completed a continuous waterway between the North Sea and the Black Sea.

name: Rhinoceros auklet
fact: The rhinoceros auklet grows a pale horn on its bill in the breeding season and carries fish back to its burrow at night.

name: Rhodes
fact: Rhodes was home to the Colossus of Rhodes, a giant bronze statue counted among the Seven Wonders of the ancient world.

name: Rhomaleosaurus
fact: Rhomaleosaurus was a short-necked, big-headed plesiosaur of Early Jurassic Europe, around seven metres long.

name: Rhossili Bay
fact: Rhossili Bay on the Gower Peninsula in Wales is a three-mile beach where the wreck of the Helvetia, lost in 1887, still lies.

name: Atlantic ribbed mussel
fact: The Atlantic ribbed mussel lives in salt marshes, wedged among the roots of cordgrass.

name: Ribbon eel
fact: The ribbon eel lives in a burrow in sand or rubble and changes from black to blue to yellow as it turns from juvenile to male to female.

name: Ribbon Reefs
fact: The Ribbon Reefs are a chain of ten long, narrow reefs on the outer Great Barrier Reef, home to the famous Cod Hole dive site.

name: Ribbon seal
fact: Ribbon seals have striking white bands around the neck and flippers and spend most of the year in the open Bering Sea and Sea of Okhotsk.

name: Ribbon weed
fact: A meadow of ribbon weed in Shark Bay, Western Australia, has been found to be a single clone covering about 180 square kilometres.

name: Ribbon worm
fact: Ribbon worms fire a sticky proboscis to catch prey, and some species regrow a complete worm from a small fragment.

name: Ribboned pipehorse
fact: The ribboned pipehorse is an Australian relative of seahorses with a horse-like head and a straight, ribbon-shaped body.

name: Rice's whale
fact: Rice's whale, named in 2021 after biologist Dale Rice, lives only in the Gulf of Mexico and numbers only around 50 animals.

name: Richard Howe
fact: Richard Howe won the Glorious First of June in 1794 and was known to his sailors as Black Dick.

name: Richards Bay
fact: Richards Bay in South Africa is home to one of the largest coal export terminals in the world.

name: Richelieu Rock
fact: Richelieu Rock, a horseshoe-shaped pinnacle in the Andaman Sea off Thailand, is prized for whale shark sightings and purple soft corals.

name: Ridgeia tube worm
fact: Ridgeia tube worms blanket the vents of the Juan de Fuca Ridge off Canada, growing tall and thin or short and fat depending on how hot their spot is.

name: Rigger
fact: A rigger fits and maintains the ropes and spars of a sailing ship, working high above the deck.

name: Rigging
fact: Rigging is the system of ropes, wires and chains that supports a ship's masts and controls its sails.

name: Right whale
fact: Right whales got their name from whalers because they were the 'right' whale to hunt: slow, rich in oil, and floating when dead.

name: Riiser-Larsen Sea
fact: The Riiser-Larsen Sea off Antarctica is named after the Norwegian aviator and explorer Hjalmar Riiser-Larsen.

name: Rijeka
fact: Rijeka is Croatia's largest port.

name: Rimurehu
fact: Rimurehu is the Maori name for the eelgrass that forms the main seagrass meadows of New Zealand and southern Australia.

name: Rincon
fact: Rincon Point on the Santa Barbara and Ventura county line in California is nicknamed the Queen of the Coast for its long right-hand waves.

name: Ringed seal
fact: Ringed seals are the smallest and most common Arctic seal, keeping breathing holes open in the ice with their claws, and are the polar bear's main prey.

name: Rio de Janeiro
fact: Rio de Janeiro means 'River of January', the name given by Portuguese sailors who reached Guanabara Bay in January 1502.

name: Rio Grande cutthroat trout
fact: The Rio Grande cutthroat trout is the state fish of New Mexico and lives in cold mountain headwaters.

name: Rip current
fact: A rip current is a narrow, fast channel of water flowing away from the shore, and it is a leading danger to swimmers.

name: Ripley's Aquarium of Canada
fact: Ripley's Aquarium of Canada in Toronto opened in 2013 and has a moving walkway through its Dangerous Lagoon shark tunnel.

name: Risso's dolphin
fact: Risso's dolphins are born dark grey and turn almost white with age as they accumulate scars from fights and squid.

name: River dolphin
fact: River dolphins have long slender beaks, tiny eyes and flexible necks suited to hunting in murky, cluttered water.

name: River mangrove
fact: The river mangrove is a shrubby mangrove that excretes salt through its leaves and has curved, horn-shaped seedlings.

name: RMS Aquitania
fact: The Aquitania was a Cunard liner launched in 1913 that served in two world wars and sailed for around thirty-five years.

name: RMS Britannia
fact: The Britannia was the first Cunard steamship on the Atlantic route in 1840, and she carried Charles Dickens to America in 1842.

name: RMS Empress of Ireland
fact: The Empress of Ireland sank in the Saint Lawrence River in 1914 after a collision, with the loss of over 1,000 lives.

name: RMS Majestic
fact: The Majestic was launched in Germany as the Bismarck and completed for White Star in 1922, and she was the largest ship in the world until 1935.

name: RMS Mauretania
fact: The Mauretania was a Cunard liner of 1907 that held the Blue Riband for fastest Atlantic crossing for about two decades.

name: RMS Olympic
fact: The Olympic was the Titanic's older sister ship, and she served for twenty-four years from 1911 to 1935.

name: RMS Queen Elizabeth
fact: The Queen Elizabeth was the largest passenger liner in the world when she entered service in 1940, and she burned in Hong Kong harbour in 1972.

name: RMS Queen Mary
fact: The Queen Mary was a Cunard liner launched in 1934 that now serves as a hotel and museum in Long Beach, California.

name: RMS Rhone
fact: The steamer RMS Rhone sank in a hurricane off Salt Island in the British Virgin Islands in 1867 and is now a popular dive site.

name: Roach
fact: The roach, with its red fins and silver body, is the fish most often caught by beginners in European rivers and canals.

name: Roasting
fact: Roasting cooks whole fish or large cuts in an oven or over a fire, often with herbs and lemon.

name: Roatán
fact: Roatán is the largest of Honduras's Bay Islands and lies beside the Mesoamerican Barrier Reef.

name: Robben Island
fact: Robben Island in Table Bay off Cape Town is where Nelson Mandela was imprisoned for 18 of his 27 years in jail.

name: Robert Ballard
fact: Robert Ballard led the team that found the wreck of the Titanic in 1985 and also located the Bismarck and took part in the discovery of hydrothermal vents.

name: Robert Blake
fact: Robert Blake was a Commonwealth admiral who won victories against the Dutch and the Spanish in the 1650s.

name: Robert Surcouf
fact: Robert Surcouf was a French privateer who captured dozens of British ships in the Indian Ocean around 1800.

name: Robust ghost pipefish
fact: The robust ghost pipefish mimics a drifting leaf or seagrass blade, and the female, not the male, carries the eggs.

name: Rock beauty
fact: The rock beauty is a Caribbean angelfish, yellow at the front and black behind, that feeds mainly on sponges.

name: Rock-boring urchin
fact: Rock-boring urchins grind snug hollows into coral rock with their teeth and spines and sit inside them.

name: Rock Brasiliano
fact: Rock Brasiliano was a Dutch buccaneer who raided Spanish shipping out of Jamaica in the 1670s and was known for his cruelty.

name: Rock cook
fact: The rock cook is a small wrasse of European waters that cleans parasites from other fish, and is used to de-louse farmed salmon.

name: Rock hind
fact: The rock hind is a small, spotted grouper of the Atlantic that lives in rocky areas and can change colour.

name: Rock sole
fact: The rock sole is a Pacific flatfish that lives on gravelly and rocky seabeds from California to the Bering Sea.

name: Rockall
fact: Rockall is a lone granite rock about 20 metres high in the North Atlantic, west of Scotland, claimed by Britain and argued over for its fishing waters.

name: Rockall Bank
fact: Rockall Bank is a submerged plateau west of Scotland from which only the tiny granite islet of Rockall breaks the surface.

name: Rockfish
fact: Rockfishes of the North Pacific are among the longest-lived fish; several species live well past 100 years, and the rougheye may reach 200.

name: Rockhopper penguin
fact: Rockhopper penguins hop up cliffs with both feet together and feed on krill, squid and small fish.

name: Rockpool prawn
fact: The rockpool prawn is almost transparent, with fine brownish stripes, and is common in shallow rock pools around Europe.

name: Rodney Fox
fact: Rodney Fox survived a great white shark attack in 1963 and went on to pioneer shark cage diving.

name: Rodrigues
fact: Rodrigues is a small volcanic island that is part of Mauritius, about 560 kilometres east of the main island.

name: Rogue wave
fact: A rogue wave is an unusually large and unexpected wave, more than twice the height of the surrounding waves.

name: Rohu
fact: Rohu is a carp of South Asian rivers, the most popular eating fish in Bangladesh and eastern India.

name: Rollmops
fact: Rollmops are pickled herring fillets rolled around a pickle or onion, a German and Scandinavian speciality.

name: Romanche Trench
fact: The Romanche Trench is a deep fracture-zone trench in the equatorial Atlantic that cuts through the Mid-Atlantic Ridge.

name: Roosterfish
fact: The roosterfish of the eastern Pacific raises a comb of seven long dorsal spines and is caught from the beaches of Baja and Costa Rica.

name: Ropefish
fact: The ropefish has lungs as well as gills and can survive for a while out of water, slithering along like a snake.

name: Rorqual
fact: Rorquals, such as blue and fin whales, have throat pleats that expand to engulf huge mouthfuls of water, and most grow well beyond 8 metres.

name: Rose coral
fact: The rose coral is an Atlantic stony coral that lives loose on sand and seagrass rather than fixed to rock.

name: Roseate spoonbill
fact: The roseate spoonbill sweeps its flat bill from side to side through estuary shallows, snapping it shut on shrimps and small fish.

name: Rosette river stingray
fact: The rosette river stingray is a freshwater ray of the Amazon basin marked with a pattern of dark-edged rosettes.

name: Ross Antarctic expedition
fact: The Ross expedition of 1839 to 1843 sailed HMS Erebus and HMS Terror to discover the Ross Sea and the Ross Ice Shelf.

name: Ross Gyre
fact: The Ross Gyre is a large clockwise circulation in the Southern Ocean beside Antarctica's Ross Sea.

name: Ross Sea
fact: The Ross Sea is a deep bay of Antarctica named after James Clark Ross, who discovered it in 1841, and it is fringed by the Ross Ice Shelf, the largest in the world.

name: Ross Sea killer whale
fact: The Ross Sea killer whale, or Type C, is a small Antarctic form of killer whale that hunts Antarctic toothfish around the sea ice.

name: Ross Sea Marine Protected Area
fact: The Ross Sea Marine Protected Area in Antarctica, agreed in 2016, is among the largest protected areas on the planet and shelters Adélie penguins and toothfish.

name: Ross seal
fact: The Ross seal is the least-known Antarctic seal, living deep in the pack ice and making eerie siren-like calls.

name: Rossby wave
fact: Rossby waves are very large, slow waves in the ocean and atmosphere that arise from the rotation of the Earth.

name: Ross's gull
fact: Ross's gull is a small, pink-tinged Arctic gull that breeds in Siberia and spends the winter near the edge of Arctic pack ice.

name: Røst Reef
fact: Røst Reef off Norway's Lofoten islands is one of the largest known cold-water coral reefs, built by Lophelia coral.

name: Rosy feather star
fact: The rosy feather star is a crinoid of north-east Atlantic coasts that can swim by waving its ten feathery arms.

name: Rottnest Island
fact: Rottnest Island, off Perth in Western Australia, is home to the quokka, a small marsupial that appears to smile.

name: Rough-toothed dolphin
fact: The rough-toothed dolphin has a sloping, reptile-like head with no crease between beak and forehead, and finely ridged teeth.

name: Rougheye rockfish
fact: The rougheye rockfish is one of the longest-lived fish known, with individuals aged at more than 200 years from the growth rings in their ear bones.

name: Roughskin dogfish
fact: The roughskin dogfish is a small shark of the continental slopes that lives at depths of many hundreds of metres.

name: Roughtail stingray
fact: The roughtail stingray is one of the largest whiptail stingrays in the Atlantic, over 2 metres across, with rows of thorns on its tail.

name: Round goby
fact: The round goby from the Black and Caspian seas arrived in the Great Lakes in ballast water in 1990 and now numbers in the billions there and in the Baltic.

name: Round herring
fact: Round herrings are slim schooling fish of warm seas including the Gulf of Mexico, caught as bait and for fishmeal.

name: Round sardinella
fact: The round sardinella is a small schooling fish caught in huge numbers off West Africa, where it is a staple protein.

name: Round stingray
fact: Round stingrays cause most of the stingray injuries on southern California beaches, which is why bathers do the 'stingray shuffle'.

name: Roundnose grenadier
fact: The roundnose grenadier is a deep-sea cod relative trawled at over 1,000 metres in the North Atlantic that can live for more than 50 years.

name: Remotely operated vehicle
fact: A remotely operated vehicle is an unmanned underwater robot linked to a ship by a cable and used to explore and work at depth.

name: ROV pilot
fact: An ROV pilot flies a remotely operated underwater vehicle, a tethered robot used for survey, inspection and research.

name: Roving coralgrouper
fact: The roving coralgrouper hunts in partnership with giant morays, signalling to them with headstands and head shakes.

name: Rowing
fact: Rowing propels a boat using oars, and ocean rowers cross entire oceans in small boats.

name: Rowley Shoals
fact: The Rowley Shoals are three atolls off north-west Australia that rise steeply from deep water and are famous for strong tidal currents and clear water.

name: Royal gramma
fact: The royal gramma, or fairy basslet, is a purple-and-yellow Caribbean reef fish that often swims upside down beneath ledges.

name: Royal pleco
fact: The royal pleco is a South American armoured catfish that rasps wood with its spoon-shaped teeth, helping it digest fibre.

name: Royal tern
fact: The royal tern is a large crested tern that plunge-dives to catch small fish off warm coasts.

name: RRS Charles Darwin
fact: RRS Charles Darwin was a British ocean research ship, launched in 1984, used to study the deep sea.

name: RRS Discovery
fact: The Discovery was built for Scott's first Antarctic expedition in 1901, and three later British research ships of the same name have continued its work.

name: RRS James Clark Ross
fact: RRS James Clark Ross is a British polar research ship, launched in 1990 and named after the Antarctic explorer.

name: RRS Sir David Attenborough
fact: The polar research ship RRS Sir David Attenborough got its name after a 2016 public vote overwhelmingly chose Boaty McBoatface, a name given to one of its robot submarines instead.

name: Rubjerg Knude Lighthouse
fact: Rubjerg Knude Lighthouse in Denmark was lifted onto rails and moved about 70 metres inland in 2019 to save it from a crumbling cliff.

name: Ruby Princess
fact: The Ruby Princess was a cruise ship whose passengers disembarked in Sydney in March 2020, and COVID-19 cases were later traced to the voyage.

name: Ruby sea dragon
fact: The ruby sea dragon, deep red and living below the reach of most divers off Western Australia, was named as a new species only in 2015 and first filmed alive in 2016.

name: Rudder
fact: The rudder is the movable blade at the stern that steers the ship.

name: Rudist
fact: Rudists were strange cone-shaped clams that built reefs in Cretaceous seas and died out along with the dinosaurs.

name: Rummy-nose tetra
fact: The rummy-nose tetra has a bright red nose and swims in tight, synchronised shoals.

name: Russia
fact: Russia's Pacific coast includes the port of Vladivostok and the volcanic Kamchatka Peninsula.

name: Ryujin
fact: Ryujin is the Japanese dragon god of the sea, said to live in a coral palace under the waves and to control the tides with magical jewels.

name: Ryukyu Trench
fact: The Ryukyu Trench runs along the Ryukyu Islands between Japan and Taiwan and reaches about 7,500 metres deep.

name: Saba
fact: Saba is a tiny Dutch island that is the top of a single volcano, Mount Scenery, the highest point in the Kingdom of the Netherlands.

name: Sabertooth fish
fact: Sabertooth fish are small deep-sea hunters with upward-looking eyes and fangs that stick out past the jaw.

name: Sable Island
fact: Sable Island is a crescent of sand off Nova Scotia known as the Graveyard of the Atlantic for its hundreds of shipwrecks, and home to wild horses.

name: Sablefish
fact: Sablefish, sold as black cod, is a buttery deep-water fish of the North Pacific, famous miso-marinated, and it can live for more than 90 years.

name: Saddle wrasse
fact: The saddle wrasse is a colourful fish found only in the Hawaiian Islands and nearby Johnston Atoll, and it is one of the most common fish on Hawaiian reefs.

name: Saddleback clownfish
fact: The saddleback clownfish has a white saddle on its back rather than a full bar, and lives in anemones on open sand rather than on the reef.

name: Saddled butterflyfish
fact: The saddled butterflyfish has a big dark patch on its back edged with white, and it is common on Indo-Pacific reefs.

name: Saddled toby
fact: The saddled toby is so poisonous that the harmless mimic filefish has evolved to copy its black saddles and colours almost exactly.

name: Saffron cod
fact: The saffron cod is a small cod of the North Pacific and Arctic seas, fished by coastal communities in Alaska and Russia.

name: Sagami Bay
fact: Sagami Bay is a deep Japanese bay south of Tokyo, where deep-sea animals can be found close to shore.

name: Sagami Trough
fact: The Sagami Trough lies off the Pacific coast of Japan near Tokyo Bay, and is linked with the great Kanto earthquake of 1923.

name: Sailboat
fact: Sailboats are driven by the wind alone, and the oldest known picture of a sail, on an Egyptian pot, is more than 5,000 years old.

name: Sailfin pleco
fact: The sailfin pleco is an armoured South American catfish with a tall sail-like dorsal fin that has become an invasive pest in Florida and Asia.

name: Sailfin tang
fact: The sailfin tang raises enormous dorsal and anal fins to look twice its size, and is banded brown and yellow.

name: Sailfish
fact: The sailfish is widely held to be the fastest fish in the sea, raising its huge dorsal sail when it herds sardines into tight balls.

name: Sailing
fact: Sailing uses wind in sails to move a boat across the water, in recreation and in racing.

name: Sailmaker
fact: A sailmaker cuts and sews sails, and in the age of sail every large ship carried one.

name: Sailor
fact: Sailors work aboard ships, handling lines, steering and keeping watch.

name: Saimaa ringed seal
fact: The Saimaa ringed seal lives only in Finland's freshwater Lake Saimaa and numbers just a few hundred animals.

name: Saint Barthélemy
fact: Saint Barthélemy is a small French island that belonged to Sweden from 1784 to 1878.

name: Saint Croix
fact: Saint Croix is the largest of the US Virgin Islands and was once a Danish sugar colony.

name: Saint John
fact: Much of Saint John in the US Virgin Islands is protected as the Virgin Islands National Park.

name: Saint Kitts
fact: Saint Kitts is the larger island of Saint Kitts and Nevis, the smallest country in the Americas by area.

name: Saint Kitts and Nevis
fact: Saint Kitts and Nevis is a twin-island nation and the smallest country in the Americas by area.

name: Saint Lucia
fact: Saint Lucia's twin volcanic peaks, the Pitons, rise straight out of the sea and are a World Heritage Site.

name: Saint Martin
fact: The island of Saint Martin is divided between France and the Netherlands, who have shared it since a treaty in 1648.

name: Saint Thomas
fact: Saint Thomas is one of the US Virgin Islands and its capital, Charlotte Amalie, is a busy cruise port.

name: Saint Vincent
fact: Saint Vincent is a volcanic island where the La Soufrière volcano erupted in 2021.

name: Saint Vincent and the Grenadines
fact: Saint Vincent and the Grenadines is made up of the volcanic main island of Saint Vincent and a chain of small islands to its south.

name: Sainte-Marie
fact: Sainte-Marie, off eastern Madagascar, was a pirate base in the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries, and humpback whales gather there each year.

name: Saipan
fact: Saipan is the largest island of the Northern Mariana Islands and the site of a major battle in 1944.

name: Saithe
fact: Saithe, or coley, is a dark-fleshed cousin of cod caught in huge numbers in the North Atlantic; cheaper than cod, it is often used in fish pies.

name: Sakhalin taimen
fact: The Sakhalin taimen of Japan and the Russian Far East is a critically endangered giant that migrates between rivers and the sea.

name: Salalah
fact: Salalah in southern Oman is a major container transshipment port and lies in the historic frankincense-producing region.

name: Salema
fact: The salema, a striped Mediterranean bream, can cause vivid hallucinations lasting days when eaten, earning it the nickname 'the dreamfish'.

name: Salish Sea
fact: The Salish Sea, which includes Puget Sound and the Strait of Georgia, was only officially named in 2009, after the Coast Salish peoples.

name: Sally Lightfoot crab
fact: Sally Lightfoot crabs skitter over Galápagos lava rocks in bright red and blue, and pick ticks off basking marine iguanas.

name: Salmon
fact: Pacific salmon at sea feed heavily on krill, and the pigment from those crustaceans is what turns their flesh pink.

name: Salmon shark
fact: The salmon shark can hold its body temperature well above that of the cold North Pacific, letting it chase salmon in near-freezing seas.

name: Salp
fact: Salps are barrel-shaped, transparent relatives of vertebrates that pump water through their bodies, and can link into chains many metres long.

name: Salt baking
fact: Salt baking encases a whole fish in a crust of salt that traps moisture, and it is a classic way to cook sea bream.

name: Salt cod
fact: Salt cod is cod that has been salted and dried so that it keeps for months, and it is the basis of Portuguese bacalhau dishes.

name: Salting
fact: Salting draws water out of fish so that bacteria cannot thrive, and it was the key to the medieval cod trade.

name: Saltwater crocodile
fact: The saltwater crocodile is the largest living reptile, over 6 metres long, and swims between islands across hundreds of kilometres of open sea.

name: Salvador
fact: Salvador, Brazil's first capital, sits on the Bay of All Saints, one of the largest bays on the Atlantic coast of South America.

name: Sambro Island Lighthouse
fact: Sambro Island Light at the entrance to Halifax Harbour in Nova Scotia was first lit in 1758 and is one of the oldest in the Americas.

name: Samoa
fact: The Samoan Islands in the central Pacific are divided between the independent nation of Samoa and the US territory of American Samoa.

name: Samos
fact: Samos is the Greek island where the mathematician Pythagoras was born.

name: Samothrace
fact: Samothrace is the Greek island where the statue known as the Winged Victory was found in 1863.

name: Sampan
fact: The sampan is a flat-bottomed wooden boat of China and Southeast Asia, used for fishing and as a floating home in harbours and rivers.

name: Samuel Bellamy
fact: Samuel Bellamy captured the slave ship Whydah in 1717 and was lost when she wrecked off Cape Cod weeks later.

name: San Andrés
fact: San Andrés is a Colombian island that lies far closer to Nicaragua than to the Colombian mainland.

name: San Antonio
fact: San Antonio on Chile's central coast is among the country's busiest ports by cargo.

name: San Cristobal Trench
fact: The San Cristobal Trench runs south of the Solomon Islands and is part of the chain of trenches along the Pacific's Ring of Fire.

name: San Diego
fact: San Diego is home to Naval Base San Diego, one of the largest bases of the United States Pacific Fleet.

name: San Diego Bay
fact: San Diego Bay is a sheltered natural harbour in southern California and home to a major naval base.

name: San Francisco
fact: San Francisco grew from a small settlement into a major Pacific port during the 1849 California Gold Rush.

name: San Francisco Bay
fact: San Francisco Bay is the largest estuary on the Pacific coast of the Americas, entered through the Golden Gate strait.

name: San José
fact: The Spanish galleon San José, sunk by the British off Cartagena in 1708 with a cargo of gold, silver and emeralds, was located in 2015 about 600 metres down.

name: San Juan
fact: San Juan, Puerto Rico, is guarded by El Morro, a Spanish fortress begun in 1539 to protect the harbour entrance.

name: San Juan de Salvamento Lighthouse
aliases: Lighthouse at the End of the World Isla de los Estados
fact: The San Juan de Salvamento lighthouse on Staten Island, Argentina, was built in 1884 and inspired Jules Verne's novel The Lighthouse at the End of the World.

name: Sand bubbler crab
fact: Sand bubbler crabs sift sand for food and leave thousands of tiny sand balls radiating from their burrows on tropical beaches at low tide.

name: Sand dollar
fact: Sand dollars are flattened sea urchins, and the bleached white 'shell' found on beaches is the animal's skeleton, or test.

name: Sand eel
fact: Sand eels are slim silvery fish that dive headfirst into sand to hide, and puffins and kittiwakes depend on them to feed their chicks.

name: Sand hopper
fact: Sand hoppers are tiny shrimp-like crustaceans that live in and feed on rotting seaweed washed up along the strandline.

name: Sand tiger shark
fact: Sand tiger embryos eat their siblings in the womb, so only one pup from each uterus survives to birth.

name: Sandbar shark
fact: Sandbar sharks have an unusually tall dorsal fin and were once the mainstay of the shark fishery on the US east coast.

name: Sanddab
fact: Pacific sanddabs are small left-eyed flounders of the US west coast, pan-fried whole and a speciality of Monterey and San Francisco restaurants.

name: Sanganeb Atoll
fact: Sanganeb is the only atoll in the Red Sea, rising off the coast of Sudan and protected as a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

name: Santa Monica Beach
fact: Santa Monica State Beach in California is backed by a pier that opened in 1909 and carries a historic funfair.

name: Santorini
fact: Santorini is a crescent of islands around a flooded volcanic crater left by a huge eruption in the Bronze Age.

name: Santos
fact: Santos, near São Paulo, is the busiest port in Latin America and the main gateway for Brazil's coffee exports.

name: São Tomé and Príncipe
fact: São Tomé and Príncipe are two volcanic islands in the Gulf of Guinea that make up Africa's second-smallest country.

name: Sapphire damselfish
fact: The sapphire damselfish is a small reef fish with a vivid, electric-blue body that shelters among coral.

name: Sap-sucking slug
fact: The sap-sucking slug keeps the chloroplasts of the algae it eats and uses them to photosynthesise for weeks.

name: Sarcastic fringehead
fact: The sarcastic fringehead of the Californian coast defends its burrow by gaping an enormous fluorescent mouth at rivals.

name: Sardine
fact: Sardines filter copepods and krill from the water, and their immense schools off South Africa form the annual sardine run.

name: Sardinella
fact: Sardinellas are small sardine-like fish that support huge fisheries off West Africa, where they are smoked and dried for food.

name: Sardinia
fact: Sardinia is the second-largest island in the Mediterranean and is dotted with prehistoric stone towers called nuraghi.

name: Sargasso Sea
fact: The Sargasso Sea is the only sea with no coastline, bounded instead by Atlantic currents, and both European and American eels spawn there.

name: Sargassum
fact: Sargassum is a floating brown seaweed held up by gas-filled bladders; huge rafts of it give the Sargasso Sea its name and shelter young sea turtles.

name: Saronic Gulf
fact: The Saronic Gulf is the bay of the Aegean on which Athens and its port Piraeus stand, where the Greeks crushed the Persian fleet at Salamis in 480 BC.

name: Sashimi
fact: Sashimi is thin slices of very fresh raw fish or seafood, served without rice in Japanese cooking.

name: Satomi's pygmy seahorse
fact: Satomi's pygmy seahorse, from Indonesia, is about 1.4 centimetres long and is the smallest known seahorse.

name: Sato's beaked whale
fact: Sato's beaked whale is a rarely seen North Pacific species that was only formally described as new to science in 2019.

name: Saturation diver
fact: Saturation divers live in pressurised chambers for weeks so they can work at great depth without repeated decompression.

name: Saudi Arabia
fact: Saudi Arabia has coasts on both the Red Sea and the Persian Gulf.

name: Savannah
fact: Savannah is a historic Georgia port city, home to one of the busiest container ports on the US east coast.

name: Sawfish
fact: A sawfish's toothed snout is lined with sensors that detect prey, and it slashes sideways to stun fish.

name: Sawshark
fact: Sawsharks carry a long flat saw-like snout with a pair of trailing barbels, and unlike sawfish they have gills on the sides of the head.

name: Sawtooth eel
fact: Sawtooth eels are small deep-sea eels with saw-like rows of teeth, drifting in the midwater of all the oceans.

name: Sayyida al Hurra
fact: Sayyida al Hurra was the governor of Tetouan in Morocco who controlled piracy in the western Mediterranean in the 1500s, in alliance with Barbarossa.

name: Scaldfish
fact: The scaldfish is a small, translucent flatfish of European seas whose loose scales come off so easily that it looks scalded when caught.

name: Scallop
fact: Scallops have dozens of tiny blue eyes along the edge of their shells and can swim by clapping their shells together.

name: Scalloped hammerhead
fact: Scalloped hammerheads gather in schools of hundreds around seamounts such as Cocos Island and the Galápagos.

name: Scaly-foot snail
fact: The scaly-foot snail armours its foot with plates of iron sulphide and is the first species declared endangered because of deep-sea mining.

name: Scamp
fact: The scamp is a western Atlantic grouper that begins life as a female and some change sex to become male.

name: Scapa Flow
fact: Scapa Flow in Orkney is where the interned German High Seas Fleet was scuttled in 1919, leaving battleships and cruisers that divers still explore.

name: Scarlet badis
fact: The scarlet badis is a 2-centimetre fish from India with scarlet and blue bars, one of the smallest perch-like fish.

name: Scarlet cleaner shrimp
fact: The scarlet cleaner shrimp is a bright red reef shrimp that sets up cleaning stations and picks parasites off visiting fish.

name: Scarlet ibis
fact: The scarlet ibis gets its brilliant red colour from pigments in the crabs and shrimps it probes out of mangrove mud.

name: Scharnhorst
fact: The German battleship Scharnhorst was sunk off North Cape, Norway, in December 1943 after a battle with British warships.

name: Schoolmaster snapper
fact: The schoolmaster is a yellow-finned Caribbean snapper that gathers in daytime schools beneath elkhorn coral and mangroves.

name: Schooner
fact: A schooner is a sailing ship with two or more masts whose main sails run fore-and-aft, a rig that made it a favourite of fishermen and smugglers.

name: Scoresby Sound
fact: Scoresby Sound in east Greenland is named after the British whaler and explorer William Scoresby and is one of the largest fjord systems in the world.

name: Scorpionfish
fact: Scorpionfish are camouflaged ambush hunters with venomous fin spines, and the family includes the lionfish and the stonefish.

name: Scott Reef
fact: Scott Reef is a remote atoll system off north-west Australia that recovered remarkably after being devastated by coral bleaching in 1998.

name: Scrawled filefish
fact: The scrawled filefish has blue scribbles over an olive body that it can lighten, darken or mottle to match its surroundings.

name: Scroll coral
fact: Scroll corals grow as wavy, curled plates that can resemble cabbage leaves or vases.

name: Scuba diver
fact: Professional divers work underwater on tasks such as inspection, construction, salvage and research.

name: Scuba diving
fact: Scuba diving uses a self-contained breathing apparatus, a name that stands for self-contained underwater breathing apparatus, to explore underwater.

name: Sculpin
fact: Sculpins are spiny bottom fish of cold waters, and several species grunt and hum during territorial disputes and courtship.

name: Scupper
fact: A scupper is an opening in the side of a ship that lets water drain off the deck.

name: Scuttlebutt
fact: The scuttlebutt was the cask of drinking water on a ship, where sailors gathered and gossiped, so the word came to mean rumour.

name: Scylla
fact: In Greek myth Scylla was a many-headed sea monster who seized sailors from passing ships in a narrow strait, opposite Charybdis.

name: Sea anemone
fact: Sea anemones look like flowers but are predators armed with stinging tentacles, found from rock pools to the floors of ocean trenches.

name: Sea angel
fact: The sea angel is a tiny swimming sea slug of Arctic waters that flaps two wing-like lobes and preys only on sea butterflies.

name: Sea apple
fact: The sea apple is a brightly coloured sea cucumber that feeds with a crown of tentacles and can release a toxin that kills everything in an aquarium.

name: S.E.A. Aquarium
fact: S.E.A. Aquarium on Singapore's Sentosa island opened in 2012 and is one of the largest aquariums in the world.

name: Sea bass
fact: The European sea bass, sold as branzino, is a prized angling fish of the North Sea and Atlantic coasts and is widely farmed in the Mediterranean.

name: Sea biscuit
fact: A sea biscuit is a thick, domed relative of the sand dollar that burrows through sand on tropical sea floors.

name: Sea bream
fact: The gilthead sea bream, named for the gold bar between its eyes, is one of the most farmed fish in the Mediterranean.

name: Sea breeze
fact: A sea breeze is a cool wind that blows from the sea to the land during the day, as the land warms faster than the water.

name: Sea butterfly
fact: Sea butterflies are tiny swimming snails that flap wing-like flaps, and their thin shells are threatened by ocean acidification.

name: Sea chub
fact: Sea chubs, or rudderfish, are unusual among reef fish in eating mostly brown seaweeds such as sargassum, and they often follow boats.

name: Sea Cliff
fact: Sea Cliff was a US Navy deep-submergence submersible rated to roughly 6,000 metres.

name: Sea cow
fact: Sea cows, the manatees and dugong, are the only plant-eating marine mammals and are related to elephants rather than seals.

name: Sea cucumber
fact: Sea cucumbers breathe through their bottoms and can eject their sticky internal organs at attackers, growing them back within weeks.

name: Sea daisy
fact: Sea daisies are tiny disc-shaped echinoderms found on sunken wood in the deep sea and were only discovered in 1986.

name: Sea dragon
fact: Sea dragons are seahorse relatives found only in the coastal waters of southern Australia, where they drift among kelp and seagrass.

name: Sea fan
fact: A sea fan is a soft coral whose colony grows into a flat, lacy fan held side-on to the current to catch drifting plankton.

name: Sea firefly
fact: The sea firefly is a 3-millimetre ostracod that squirts glowing blue mucus; dried ones were used by Japanese soldiers as a dim reading light.

name: Sea fishing
fact: Sea fishing as a sport includes angling from shore and from boats for species such as marlin and tuna.

name: Sea fog
fact: Sea fog forms when warm moist air moves over cold water, and it is common off coasts like California and Newfoundland.

name: Sea gooseberry
fact: The sea gooseberry is a glassy, marble-sized comb jelly that trails two long sticky tentacles to snare copepods.

name: Sea grapes
fact: Sea grapes are a green seaweed with tiny bubble-like beads that pop in the mouth, eaten fresh in Okinawa and the Philippines.

name: Sea hare
fact: The sea hare is a large sea slug that squirts a cloud of purple ink when it is disturbed.

name: Sea krait
fact: Sea kraits are the only sea snakes that come ashore to lay eggs, and they have highly potent venom but rarely bite people.

name: Sea lamprey
fact: The sea lamprey grows up at sea clamped onto fish, rasping through their skin to feed on blood, then swims up rivers to spawn and die.

name: Sea Legacy
fact: Sea Legacy is a conservation group founded by photographers Paul Nicklen and Cristina Mittermeier that uses imagery to promote ocean protection.

name: Sea lemon
fact: The sea lemon is a yellow, warty nudibranch of Atlantic and Pacific shores that eats sponges, and the Pacific species gives off a fruity, citrus-like smell.

name: Sea lettuce
fact: Sea lettuce is a bright green seaweed with fronds only two cells thick, which can bloom into 'green tides' where sewage or farm runoff enriches the water.

name: Sea Life Brighton
fact: Sea Life Brighton opened in 1872 as the Brighton Aquarium and is the oldest operating aquarium in the world.

name: London Aquarium
fact: The London Aquarium opened in 1997 inside County Hall on the south bank of the Thames.

name: Sea Life Sydney Aquarium
fact: Sydney Aquarium at Darling Harbour opened in 1988 and is known for underwater tunnels that run through its shark and ray tanks.

name: Sea lily
fact: Sea lilies are animals, not plants: feathery filter feeders on a stalk that were common 300 million years ago and today live densely on rocks more than 9,000 metres down in the Izu-Ogasawara Trench.

name: Sea lion
fact: Sea lions differ from true seals in having small external ear flaps and in walking on all four flippers on land.

name: Sea louse
fact: Sea lice are tiny copepods that attach to salmon and feed on their skin and blood, and they are a major problem on salmon farms.

name: Sea mink
fact: The sea mink, a large coastal mink of New England and Atlantic Canada, was trapped to extinction for its fur by about 1900.

name: Sea moth
fact: Sea moths are small armoured fish of Indo-Pacific sand flats that walk on their pelvic fins and spread wing-like pectoral fins.

name: Sea mouse
fact: The sea mouse is a furry-looking marine worm whose iridescent bristles were among the first natural structures found to work like optical fibres.

name: Sea nettle
fact: Sea nettles are golden-brown jellyfish with long frilly oral arms whose sting feels like brushing a stinging nettle, hence the name.

name: Sea oak
fact: The sea oak is a brown seaweed of rock pools and shallow seas whose branches carry pod-like air bladders.

name: Sea of Azov
fact: The Sea of Azov, linked to the Black Sea by the Kerch Strait, is the shallowest sea in the world, averaging only about 7 metres deep.

name: Sea of Corsica
fact: The Sea of Corsica lies between the island of Corsica and the Tuscan Archipelago.

name: Sea of Crete
fact: The Sea of Crete is the southern part of the Aegean between Crete and the Cyclades, and is deeper than most of the Aegean.

name: Sea of Japan
fact: The Sea of Japan, called the East Sea in Korea, is a marginal sea of the Pacific nearly enclosed by Japan, Korea and Russia.

name: Sea of Marmara
fact: The Sea of Marmara is a small inland sea entirely within Turkey, linking the Black Sea to the Aegean through the Bosporus and Dardanelles.

name: Sea of Okhotsk
fact: The Sea of Okhotsk, off Russia's far east, is the coldest sea in East Asia and is covered by drifting ice for much of the winter.

name: Sea of Sardinia
fact: The Sea of Sardinia is the stretch of the western Mediterranean between Sardinia and the Balearic Islands.

name: Sea otter
fact: Sea otters have the densest fur of any animal and use rocks as tools to crack open shellfish.

name: Sea palm
fact: The sea palm looks like a tiny palm tree and lives only on the most wave-battered rocks of the Pacific coast of North America.

name: Sea pansy
fact: The sea pansy is a flat, purple soft coral colony on sand that glows green when touched, thanks to a protein now used in laboratories.

name: Sea peach
fact: The sea peach is a round, orange-red sea squirt of cold North Atlantic and Pacific waters, shaped like a peach.

name: Sea pen
fact: A sea pen is a colony of polyps shaped like an old quill pen, rooted in soft mud, and many species glow green when touched.

name: Sea pig
fact: Sea pigs are pink, pudgy sea cucumbers that walk on tube feet across abyssal plains, often in herds all facing the current, 1,000 to 6,000 metres down.

name: Sea pineapple
fact: The sea pineapple is a knobbly sea squirt farmed and eaten raw in Japan and Korea.

name: Sea pork
fact: Sea pork is a colonial sea squirt that forms fleshy lumps, and its name comes from a resemblance to salted pork.

name: Sea potato
fact: The sea potato is a heart urchin that lives buried in sand and is named for its rounded, potato-like shape.

name: Sea raven
fact: The sea raven is a lumpy, ragged-finned sculpin of the North American Atlantic coast that puffs itself up with water when caught.

name: Sea robin
fact: Sea robins 'walk' on finger-like fin rays and grunt or croak by vibrating their swim bladder, a sound anglers hear when they lift them from the water.

name: Sea sapphire
fact: The sea sapphire is a copepod whose males flash brilliant blue, then turn transparent and vanish as they tilt, thanks to crystal plates in their skin.

name: Sea scorpion
fact: Sea scorpions, or eurypterids, were armoured arthropods that died out about 250 million years ago, and the largest reached about 2.5 metres.

name: Sea Shepherd
fact: Sea Shepherd was founded by Paul Watson in 1977 and takes direct action against illegal whaling, fishing and sealing.

name: Sea slater
fact: The sea slater is a large woodlouse of the splash zone that hides in crevices by day and scavenges over the rocks at night.

name: Sea slug
fact: Sea slugs are marine snails that have lost or shrunk their shell, and many are brightly coloured to warn predators of their toxins.

name: Sea smoke
fact: Sea smoke is the wisps of fog that rise from relatively warm water when very cold air blows across it.

name: Sea snail
fact: Sea snails build their spiral shells from calcium carbonate drawn from seawater, adding to the opening as they grow.

name: Sea snake
fact: Sea snakes are venomous relatives of cobras with paddle-shaped tails, and most give birth to live young at sea.

name: Sea spider
fact: Sea spiders are not true spiders but leggy marine arthropods, and in Antarctic waters they grow as wide as a dinner plate.

name: Sea squirt
fact: A sea squirt starts life as a swimming tadpole-like larva, then glues itself to a rock and spends the rest of its life pumping water through its body to filter food.

name: Sea star
fact: Sea stars have no brain or blood, pumping seawater through their bodies to move hundreds of tiny tube feet.

name: Sea toad
fact: Sea toads, or coffinfish, are deep-sea anglerfish that can inflate their bodies with water and hold their breath for minutes to save energy.

name: Sea trout
fact: The sea trout is a brown trout that goes to sea to feed, and anglers fish for it at night in rivers draining into the North and Baltic seas.

name: Sea turtle
