fact: Thalassodendron ciliatum is a robust seagrass of the Indian Ocean with woody stems that can root into rock.

name: Thalassomedon
fact: Thalassomedon was a long-necked plesiosaur of the Cretaceous Western Interior Seaway whose neck made up roughly half of its body length.

name: Thasos
fact: Thasos is a Greek island in the northern Aegean that was famed in antiquity for its marble and gold.

name: The Abyss
fact: The Abyss is James Cameron's 1989 science-fiction film about an underwater drilling crew who encounter a mysterious intelligence on the seabed.

name: The Caine Mutiny
fact: The Caine Mutiny is Herman Wouk's 1951 novel, a Pulitzer Prize winner, about a naval mutiny against an unstable captain.

name: The Cruel Sea
fact: The Cruel Sea is Nicholas Monsarrat's 1951 novel about the crew of a British Royal Navy escort ship in the Battle of the Atlantic.

name: The Deep
fact: The Deep in Hull opened in 2002 at the point where the River Hull meets the Humber estuary.

name: The Little Mermaid
fact: The Little Mermaid is Hans Christian Andersen's 1837 fairy tale, and Disney's 1989 film by Ron Clements and John Musker is based on it.

name: The Love Boat
fact: The Love Boat was an American television series that began in 1977, following the crew and passengers of a cruise ship.

name: The Ocean Cleanup
fact: The Ocean Cleanup is a Dutch non-profit, founded by Boyan Slat in 2013, that develops systems to remove plastic from the oceans and rivers.

name: The Odyssey
fact: The Odyssey is Homer's ancient Greek epic poem about Odysseus's ten-year voyage home from Troy, much of it spent at sea.

name: The Pirates! In an Adventure with Scientists!
fact: The Pirates! In an Adventure with Scientists! is a 2012 stop-motion film from Aardman, directed by Peter Lord, featuring a bumbling pirate captain.

name: The Sea Beast
fact: The Sea Beast is a 2022 Netflix animated film directed by Chris Williams, about a monster hunter and a girl who befriend a sea creature.

name: The Sea-Wolf
fact: The Sea-Wolf is Jack London's 1904 novel about a scholar rescued by the brutal sealing-ship captain Wolf Larsen.

name: The Silent World
fact: The Silent World is Jacques Cousteau's 1953 book and the 1956 documentary film he co-directed with Louis Malle, which won the Palme d'Or at Cannes.

name: Themistocles
fact: Themistocles was the Athenian leader who built up Athens's navy and commanded the Greek fleet to victory at Salamis in 480 BC.

name: Thermaic Gulf
fact: The Thermaic Gulf is the arm of the Aegean at whose head stands Thessaloniki, Greece's second city.

name: Thermohaline circulation
fact: The thermohaline circulation is the global flow of ocean water driven by differences in temperature and salt content, which takes about a thousand years to complete.

name: Thick-billed murre
fact: Thick-billed murres of Arctic and sub-Arctic seas are among the deepest-diving flying birds, with dives recorded to 150 metres and beyond.

name: Thimble jellyfish
fact: The thumb-sized thimble jellyfish's larvae cause 'sea bather's eruption', an itchy rash under swimsuits along Florida and Caribbean beaches.

name: Thomas Anstis
fact: Thomas Anstis sailed under Bartholomew Roberts before breaking away to lead his own pirate crew around 1721.

name: Thomas Cavendish
fact: Thomas Cavendish was an English privateer who circumnavigated the globe in 1586 to 1588, raiding Spanish ships and settlements on the way.

name: Thomas Cochrane
fact: Thomas Cochrane commanded the Chilean, Brazilian and Greek navies as well as the Royal Navy, and he is said to be a model for fictional heroes like Hornblower.

name: Thomas Tew
fact: Thomas Tew pioneered the Pirate Round, sailing from the Americas to raid ships in the Red Sea in the 1690s.

name: Thongweed
fact: Thongweed, or sea spaghetti, grows from a small button into straps up to about 2 metres long and is sold fresh as a sea vegetable.

name: Thor Heyerdahl
fact: Thor Heyerdahl sailed the balsa raft Kon-Tiki about 8,000 kilometres across the Pacific in 1947 to show that ancient people could have made such voyages.

name: Thornback cowfish
fact: The thornback cowfish has a rigid boxy shell with horns and spines, protecting it from predators.

name: Thornback ray
fact: The thornback ray, the most common skate around Britain, is covered in thorny spines and lays egg cases known as mermaid's purses.

name: Thorntail stingray
fact: The thorntail stingray of Australia, New Zealand and South Africa carries rows of thorns along its tail and can reach 1.8 metres across.

name: Thorny oyster
fact: Thorny oysters are spiny, brightly coloured bivalves whose shells were treasured by ancient Andean peoples.

name: Thorny seahorse
fact: The thorny seahorse is covered in sharp spines and is found across the Indo-Pacific from the Red Sea to Hawaii.

name: Thracian Sea
fact: The Thracian Sea is the northernmost part of the Aegean, off the coasts of Greek Thrace and Macedonia and the island of Thasos.

name: Threadfin butterflyfish
fact: The threadfin butterflyfish has a trailing thread on its dorsal fin and a chevron pattern on its sides; it is one of the most widespread Indo-Pacific butterflyfish.

name: Three-band anemonefish
fact: The three-band anemonefish lives only in the Marshall Islands, where some individuals turn almost completely black.

name: Three-banded panther worm
fact: The three-banded panther worm, a small acoel flatworm, can regrow an entire new body from a fragment.

name: Three-spined stickleback
fact: Many three-spined sticklebacks live at sea and move into fresh water to breed, where the red-bellied male builds a nest and guards the eggs.

name: Threebeard rockling
fact: The threebeard rockling is a cod relative of north-east Atlantic coastal waters with three barbels on its head.

name: Threespot damselfish
fact: The threespot damselfish farms algae gardens on Caribbean reefs and chases away much larger fish.

name: Thresher shark
fact: Thresher sharks whip their enormous tails, which can be as long as their bodies, to stun fish before eating them.

name: Thumbprint emperor
fact: The thumbprint emperor carries a dark blotch on its flank and feeds on sandy flats and seagrass beds around reefs.

name: Thurso East
fact: Thurso East is a powerful reef break below Thurso Castle in northern Scotland and is widely seen as Scotland's best wave.

name: Thwart
fact: A thwart is a seat across a small boat that also strengthens the hull.

name: Tiamat
fact: In the Babylonian creation myth Enuma Elish, Tiamat is the primeval goddess of the salt sea, slain by the god Marduk.

name: Tidal bore
fact: A tidal bore is a wave that travels up a river against the current when a rising tide pushes into a narrowing estuary.

name: Tide
fact: Tides are the regular rise and fall of the sea, caused mainly by the gravity of the Moon and the Sun.

name: Tide gauge
fact: A tide gauge records the rise and fall of the sea level at a harbour or coast.

name: Tidepool sculpin
fact: The tidepool sculpin is a small camouflaged fish that can find its way back to its home pool after being carried to another one.

name: Tiger barb
fact: The tiger barb from Sumatra and Borneo is a striped aquarium favourite that nips fins unless kept in a school of six or more.

name: Tiger grouper
fact: The tiger grouper is a Caribbean grouper with diagonal tiger stripes that visits cleaning stations to have its gills picked clean by gobies.

name: Tiger prawn
fact: The giant tiger prawn grows to about 33 centimetres, one of the largest prawns, and has escaped from farms to invade the Gulf of Mexico.

name: Tiger puffer
fact: The tiger puffer, torafugu, is the most prized fugu; its liver and ovaries hold a deadly poison, so only licensed chefs in Japan may prepare it as sashimi.

name: Tiger shark
fact: Young tiger sharks carry the dark stripes that give them their name, and the stripes fade as the shark matures.

name: Tiger shovelnose catfish
fact: The tiger shovelnose catfish of South America has a long flat snout and bold black stripes, and can grow to over a metre long.

name: Tiger tail seahorse
fact: The tiger tail seahorse of South-East Asia is named for the dark bands on its tail and, with the common seahorse, makes up most of the Philippine seahorse catch.

name: Tigris expedition
fact: In 1977 and 1978 Thor Heyerdahl's reed boat Tigris sailed from Iraq to Djibouti, where he burned it in protest of regional wars.

name: Tilapia
fact: Tilapia is a freshwater fish farmed in warm ponds worldwide and is now one of the most eaten fish on earth; it was raised in ancient Egypt.

name: Tillamook Rock Lighthouse
fact: Tillamook Rock Lighthouse off Oregon, nicknamed Terrible Tilly, was lit in 1881 and sits on a wave-battered rock about a mile offshore.

name: Tiller
fact: A tiller is a lever attached to the rudder, used to steer small boats.

name: Timor-Leste
fact: Timor-Leste occupies the eastern half of the island of Timor, on the Timor Sea.

name: Timor Trough
fact: The Timor Trough is a deep seabed trench lying between the island of Timor and northern Australia.

name: Tinapa
fact: Tinapa is Filipino fish, often milkfish, that is brined and smoked.

name: Tinker's butterflyfish
fact: Tinker's butterflyfish is a deep-reef butterflyfish from Hawaii, white with a bold black triangle, so rare that it fetches high prices from aquarists.

name: Tirpitz
fact: The German battleship Tirpitz was sunk by RAF bombers near Tromso, Norway, in November 1944.

name: Titan
fact: Titan was a privately owned submersible that imploded in June 2023 during a dive to the wreck of the Titanic, killing all five people aboard.

name: Titan triggerfish
fact: The titan triggerfish guards its nest fiercely and will charge and bite divers who swim into the cone-shaped territory above its eggs.

name: Titanic
fact: The Titanic lies in two main pieces about 3,800 metres down in the North Atlantic, where Robert Ballard's team found it in 1985.

name: Titanic (1997 film)
fact: Titanic is James Cameron's 1997 film about a doomed love story aboard the liner that sank in 1912.

name: Toadfish
fact: Toadfish make loud grunting and boatwhistle calls by vibrating a muscle against their swim bladder.

name: Toamasina
fact: Toamasina, once known as Tamatave, is Madagascar's main seaport.

name: Tobago
fact: Tobago is the smaller island of Trinidad and Tobago and is known for the coral gardens of Buccoo Reef.

name: Togo
fact: Togo's coast on the Gulf of Guinea is only about 50 kilometres long.

name: Togo Heihachiro
fact: Togo Heihachiro led the Japanese fleet that destroyed the Russian fleet at Tsushima in 1905.

name: Toheroa
fact: The toheroa is a prized New Zealand surf clam that is now heavily protected.

name: Tokyo
fact: Tokyo sits on Tokyo Bay, an inlet of the Pacific, and was known as Edo until 1868.

name: Tokyo Bay
fact: Tokyo Bay, the harbour of Tokyo and Yokohama, is where Commodore Perry's black ships arrived in 1853 to open Japan to trade.

name: Tokyo Sea Life Park
fact: Tokyo Sea Life Park in Kasai Rinkai Park is known for a large doughnut-shaped tank of circling tuna.

name: Tom yum goong
fact: Tom yum goong is a hot and sour Thai soup with prawns, lemongrass, galangal and lime leaves.

name: Tomato clownfish
fact: The tomato clownfish is a red-orange anemonefish with a single white head bar that lives in bubble-tip anemones in the western Pacific.

name: Tomopteris
fact: Tomopteris is a transparent swimming worm of the open ocean and one of the very few animals able to make yellow light.

name: Tompot blenny
fact: The tompot blenny peers from rock crevices with branched tentacles above its eyes and fiercely defends its chosen hole.

name: Tonga
fact: Tonga is a kingdom of about 170 islands in the South Pacific, and the Tonga Trench off its coast is the second-deepest in the world.

name: Tonga Trench
fact: The Tonga Trench is the second-deepest trench on Earth, reaching about 10,800 metres at the Horizon Deep.

name: Tongue-eating louse
fact: The tongue-eating louse is an isopod that enters a fish through its gills, drains the blood from its tongue, and then takes the tongue's place.

name: Tonguefish
fact: Tonguefish are tongue-shaped flatfish with both eyes on the left side, and one species lives beside hydrothermal vents in the Pacific.

name: Top shell
fact: Top shells are cone-shaped grazing snails of rocky shores that scrape seaweed and algal film from the rocks.

name: Tope
fact: The tope, or school shark, was heavily fished for its vitamin-rich liver oil in the 1940s and can live for over 50 years.

name: Topknot
fact: The topknot is a small, rough-scaled flatfish of rocky shores that clings upside-down beneath ledges rather than lying on sand.

name: Topman
fact: A topman was a sailor stationed aloft to handle the upper sails of a square-rigged ship.

name: Topsmelt
fact: The topsmelt is a small silverside that schools in bays and estuaries of the American Pacific coast and is eaten by many predators.

name: Torch coral
fact: Torch coral has long, flowing tentacles tipped with glowing knobs and is a favourite of reef aquarists.

name: Torpedo boat
fact: Torpedo boats were small, fast craft armed with torpedoes, built in the late nineteenth century to threaten much larger warships.

name: Torres Strait
fact: Torres Strait between Australia and New Guinea is named after the Spanish navigator Luis Váez de Torres, who sailed through it in 1606.

name: Torrey's surfgrass
fact: Torrey's surfgrass grows on wave-washed rocky shores of the Pacific coast of North America.

name: Tortola
fact: Tortola is the largest of the British Virgin Islands.

name: Totoaba
fact: The totoaba, a drum of the Gulf of California, makes booming calls with its swim bladder, the organ now smuggled as a delicacy, which has driven it close to extinction.

name: Touch-me-not sponge
fact: Touching the touch-me-not sponge can cause a painful skin rash.

name: Toulon
fact: Toulon is the main base of the French Navy in the Mediterranean.

name: Tow-in surfing
fact: Tow-in surfing uses a personal watercraft to tow surfers into waves that are too big and fast to paddle into.

name: Tower of Hercules
fact: The Tower of Hercules at A Coruna in Spain is a Roman lighthouse from the first or second century that is still in use, and a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

name: Toxic reef crab
fact: Cooking does not destroy the saxitoxin and tetrodotoxin in this brightly marked Indo-Pacific reef crab, which has killed people who ate it.

name: Trahira
fact: The trahira is an ambush predator of South American rivers with strong jaws and large teeth.

name: Transom
fact: The transom is the flat surface across the stern of a boat.

name: Transparent goby
fact: The transparent goby is a see-through, finger-length fish of European coasts that lives only a year and is eaten by the plateful as whitebait in Italy and Spain.

name: Transpolar Drift
fact: The Transpolar Drift carries sea ice from Siberia across the North Pole towards Greenland, and it carried Nansen's ship Fram across the Arctic.

name: Traverse board
fact: A traverse board was a peg board on which sailors recorded the courses and times of each half-hour watch for dead reckoning.

name: Trawler
fact: A trawler catches fish by dragging a large net, the trawl, through the water or along the seabed behind it.

name: Trawlerman
fact: A trawlerman fishes by dragging a net behind a trawler, often on long voyages to distant fishing grounds.

name: Treasure Island
fact: Treasure Island is Robert Louis Stevenson's 1883 pirate adventure novel, introducing Long John Silver and the map marked with an X.

name: Trevally
fact: Trevally are powerful, fast-swimming reef and open-water predators, and the family also includes jacks and pompanos.

name: Tri-spine horseshoe crab
fact: The tri-spine horseshoe crab of Asian coasts belongs to a lineage that has barely changed in hundreds of millions of years.

name: Trichodesmium
fact: Trichodesmium, or sea sawdust, is a cyanobacterium that forms floating brown rafts and pulls nitrogen from the air to fertilise the tropical ocean.

name: Trieste
fact: The bathyscaphe Trieste carried Jacques Piccard and Don Walsh to the bottom of the Challenger Deep in 1960, the first crewed dive to the ocean's deepest point.

name: Triggerfish
fact: A triggerfish locks itself into a crevice at night by raising a dorsal spine that can only be released by a second, smaller trigger spine.

name: Trilobite
fact: Trilobites crawled the seafloor for about 270 million years and were among the first animals with complex eyes before dying out 252 million years ago.

name: Trimaran
fact: A trimaran is a boat with a central hull and two smaller hulls on either side.

name: Trimmatom nanus
fact: Trimmatom nanus, a goby of the Chagos Islands and Maldives, matures at under 1 centimetre and held the record as the smallest vertebrate from 1981 to 2004.

name: Trincomalee
fact: Trincomalee on Sri Lanka's north-east coast has one of the finest natural deep-water harbours in the world.

name: Trinidad
fact: Trinidad is the larger island of Trinidad and Tobago and lies only about 11 kilometres off the coast of Venezuela.

name: Trinidad and Tobago
fact: Trinidad and Tobago is a twin-island nation whose eastern shores face the open Atlantic, only a few kilometres off Venezuela.

name: Triops
fact: Triops tadpole shrimp hatch in temporary pools from eggs that can wait years in dry dust, and tadpole shrimp that look much like them were already around more than 200 million years ago.

name: Triplefin
fact: Triplefins are small reef fish named for their three separate dorsal fins and are especially diverse around New Zealand.

name: Tripletail
fact: The tripletail floats on its side under buoys and weed in the Gulf of Mexico, pretending to be a drifting leaf.

name: Tripod fish
fact: The tripod fish stands motionless on the abyssal floor on three stiff fin rays up to a metre long, facing the current with its mouth open.

name: Tripoli
fact: Tripoli, the capital of Libya, has a long history as a Mediterranean port and an old town dominated by the Red Castle.

name: Trireme
fact: The trireme was the ancient Greek warship rowed by three banks of oarsmen, which won the Battle of Salamis in 480 BC.

name: Tristan da Cunha
fact: Tristan da Cunha is the most remote inhabited island in the world, with about 250 people living more than 2,000 kilometres from the nearest inhabited land.

name: Triton
fact: Triton was the son of Poseidon and Amphitrite, a merman who calmed or raised the waves by blowing on a conch shell.

name: Homberg's tritonia
fact: Homberg's tritonia is a large cold-water sea slug of the north-east Atlantic that feeds on soft corals called dead man's fingers.

name: Triton's trumpet
fact: The Triton's trumpet is a huge sea snail that preys on crown-of-thorns starfish, and its shell has been blown as a horn for centuries.

name: Tromelin Island
fact: Tromelin is a tiny, flat island east of Madagascar where enslaved people were abandoned in 1761 and the few survivors were rescued about fifteen years later.

name: Tromso
fact: Tromso is a Norwegian port city north of the Arctic Circle and a base for polar expeditions.

name: Tropheus
fact: Tropheus are rock-dwelling cichlids of Lake Tanganyika that come in a remarkable variety of colour forms.

name: Trout
fact: Several trout, including brown and rainbow trout, have sea-run forms that feed in the ocean and return to rivers to spawn.

name: True's beaked whale
fact: True's beaked whale is named after Frederick True, an American museum curator, and was first filmed underwater in the Azores in 2017.

name: Trumpetfish
fact: The trumpetfish hangs vertically among sea fans and shadows larger fish to sneak up on its prey.

name: Tsugaru Strait
fact: The Tsugaru Strait separates Honshu from Hokkaido and is crossed by the Seikan Tunnel, one of the longest rail tunnels in the world.

name: Tsukudani
fact: Tsukudani is a Japanese method of simmering small fish, shellfish or seaweed in soy sauce and mirin until they keep for a long time.

name: Tsunami
fact: A tsunami is a series of enormous waves, usually triggered by an undersea earthquake, landslide or volcanic eruption.

name: Tsushima Current
fact: The Tsushima Current is a warm branch of the Kuroshio that flows through the Korea Strait into the Sea of Japan.

name: Tuamotu Islands
fact: The Tuamotus are the largest chain of coral atolls in the world, about 80 low islands strung across French Polynesia.

name: Tuatua
fact: The tuatua is a New Zealand surf clam traditionally gathered from sandy beaches.

name: Tubbataha Reef
fact: The Tubbataha Reefs in the Philippines' Sulu Sea are two coral atolls so rich in life that they were made a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

name: Tube anemone
fact: Tube anemones live inside a slimy tube buried in sand and can withdraw their two rings of long tentacles in a flash when disturbed.

name: Tubeshoulder
fact: Tubeshoulders are deep-sea fish that squirt a cloud of glowing fluid from a tube above each shoulder to confuse predators.

name: Tubicinella major
fact: Tubicinella major is a barnacle that burrows into the skin of southern right whales, leaving only its top exposed.

name: Tucuxi
fact: The tucuxi is a small grey dolphin that lives in the Amazon river system yet looks like a miniature bottlenose rather than a river dolphin.

name: Tufted puffin
fact: The tufted puffin breeds around the North Pacific and grows golden head plumes during the breeding season.

name: Tugboat
fact: Tugboats are small but extremely powerful, built to push and pull ships many times their own size in and out of harbours.

name: Tully monster
fact: The Tully monster was a soft-bodied animal about 30 centimetres long with eyes on stalks, known from Illinois fossils, and its place in the tree of life has long been debated.

name: Tuna
fact: Tunas are warm-blooded, torpedo-shaped sprinters among the fastest fish in the sea; in Japan tuna is maguro, the most popular sushi fish of all.

name: Turbot
fact: Turbot are prized food fish with a nearly circular body and can change their colour to match the gravel they lie on.

name: Turgut Reis
fact: Turgut Reis was an Ottoman corsair and admiral who was killed during the Great Siege of Malta in 1565.

name: Turkey wing ark
fact: The turkey wing ark is a zebra-striped bivalve that anchors itself to rocks with a tuft of tough threads.

name: Turneffe Atoll
fact: Turneffe Atoll off Belize is a large coral atoll whose mangrove islands and seagrass lagoons shelter manatees, crocodiles and bonefish.

name: Turquoise killifish
fact: The turquoise killifish lives in seasonal pools in Zimbabwe and Mozambique, and its eggs survive the dry season buried in mud.

name: Turtle
fact: The Turtle was a one-man, hand-cranked submersible built by David Bushnell that tried to attach a bomb to a British warship in New York harbour in 1776.

name: Turtle barnacle
fact: Turtle barnacles settle on the shells of sea turtles and ride with them, filtering food from the water as the turtle swims.

name: Turtle grass
fact: Turtle grass is the dominant seagrass of the Caribbean, grazed by green turtles and manatees.

name: Turtle-headed sea snake
fact: The turtle-headed sea snake has almost no teeth and feeds only on fish eggs, which it scrapes from the reef.

name: Tusk shell
fact: Tusk shells are molluscs with a tapering tubular shell open at both ends, living head-down in sand.

name: Tuvalu
fact: Tuvalu is a nation of nine low coral atolls in the Pacific whose highest point is only a few metres above sea level.

name: Twenty Thousand Leagues Under the Seas
fact: Twenty Thousand Leagues Under the Seas is Jules Verne's 1870 novel in which Captain Nemo takes a professor on a voyage aboard the submarine Nautilus.

name: Two-banded anemonefish
fact: The Red Sea clownfish, with two white bars on an orange body, is found only in the Red Sea and the Gulf of Aden.

name: Two Oceans Aquarium
fact: Two Oceans Aquarium at the V&A Waterfront in Cape Town opened in 1995 and has a large kelp forest exhibit.

name: Two Years Before the Mast
fact: Two Years Before the Mast is Richard Henry Dana Jr.'s 1840 memoir of his voyage as a common sailor from Boston to California.

name: Tylosaurus
fact: Tylosaurus, a mosasaur up to about 13 metres long, rammed prey with its bony snout in the shallow sea that once covered Kansas.

name: Typhoon-class submarine
fact: Soviet Typhoon-class submarines, about 175 metres long and roughly 48,000 tonnes submerged, are the largest submarines ever built.

name: Tyrrhenian Sea
fact: The Tyrrhenian Sea, between Italy's west coast, Sardinia, Corsica and Sicily, is named after the Tyrrhenians, the Greek name for the Etruscans.

name: U-505
fact: U-505 was a German submarine captured intact by the United States Navy in June 1944 and is now displayed at the Museum of Science and Industry in Chicago.

name: U-571
fact: U-571 is a 2000 film directed by Jonathan Mostow about American sailors who seize a German submarine to capture an Enigma machine.

name: Uluj Ali
fact: Uluj Ali was a Calabrian-born Ottoman corsair who became grand admiral and escaped the defeat at Lepanto in 1571.

name: Uluwatu
fact: Uluwatu on Bali's Bukit Peninsula is a long left-hand reef break beneath a clifftop sea temple.

name: Umiak
fact: The umiak is a large open skin boat of the Inuit, rowed or paddled by several people and used for hunting whales and moving families along the coast.

name: Umibozu
fact: The umibozu is a giant black sea spirit from Japanese folklore that rises from calm water and can wreck ships.

name: United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea
fact: UNCLOS, opened for signature in 1982, sets out the rules for the use of the oceans, including territorial waters and exclusive economic zones.

name: Underwater welder
fact: Underwater welders join and repair metal structures like pipelines and oil rigs beneath the sea.

name: Undulate ray
fact: The undulate ray is named for the wavy dark lines that run across the pale upper side of its body.

name: Undulated moray
fact: The undulated moray is a mottled Indo-Pacific moray that hunts mostly at night and can grow to about 1.5 metres.

name: Unicornfish
fact: Unicornfish are large surgeonfish with a horn on the forehead that graze on brown seaweeds on Indo-Pacific reefs.

name: Union Island
fact: Union Island is one of the Grenadines and a hub for sailors, with its main port at Clifton.

name: United Arab Emirates
fact: The United Arab Emirates has coasts on the Persian Gulf and the Gulf of Oman, with Dubai and Abu Dhabi on the Gulf shore.

name: United Kingdom
fact: The United Kingdom is made up of Great Britain, Northern Ireland and many smaller islands, and its western shores face the open Atlantic.

name: United States
fact: The United States has both Atlantic and Pacific coastlines, and Alaska and Hawaii extend its waters far into the northern and central Pacific.

name: Upside-down catfish
fact: The upside-down catfish of the Congo basin habitually swims belly-up to feed at the surface, and its belly is darker than its back as a result.

name: Upside-down jellyfish
fact: The upside-down jellyfish lies on its back in mangrove shallows so the algae in its arms get sunlight, and releases stinging blobs of mucus into the water.

name: Upwelling
fact: Upwelling brings cold, nutrient-rich water from the deep to the surface, and it supports some of the world's richest fisheries.

name: Urchin clingfish
fact: The urchin clingfish shelters among the long spines of sea urchins and hides there by day.

name: Uruguay
fact: Uruguay's coast runs from the Río de la Plata estuary out to the open Atlantic at the resort of Punta del Este.

name: Albatross (research ship)
fact: The Albatross, launched in 1882, is often called the first ship built specifically for marine research, and it dredged up thousands of new species.

name: USS Arizona
fact: The battleship USS Arizona exploded and sank during the attack on Pearl Harbor in December 1941, and its wreck still leaks oil today.

name: USS Holland
fact: USS Holland was the first submarine commissioned by the United States Navy, in 1900, and was designed by the Irish inventor John Philip Holland.

name: USS Hornet
fact: The carrier USS Hornet, which launched the Doolittle Raid, was sunk in 1942 and found in 2019 about 5,300 metres down near the Solomon Islands.

name: USS Indianapolis
fact: The USS Indianapolis, sunk by a Japanese submarine in 1945 after delivering atomic bomb parts, was found in 2017 about 5,500 metres down in the Philippine Sea.

name: USS Johnston
fact: The destroyer USS Johnston, sunk off Samar in 1944, was surveyed in 2021 at 6,469 metres, briefly the deepest shipwreck ever identified.

name: USS Juneau
fact: The US cruiser USS Juneau was sunk off Guadalcanal in 1942, and all five Sullivan brothers aboard were lost.

name: USS Lexington
fact: The carrier USS Lexington, scuttled after the Battle of the Coral Sea in 1942, was found in 2018 about 3,000 metres down with aircraft still intact on the seabed.

name: USS Liberty wreck
fact: The USS Liberty, torpedoed in 1942 and pushed into the sea by a volcanic eruption in 1963, lies just off the beach at Tulamben in Bali.

name: USS Maine
fact: USS Maine exploded and sank in Havana harbour in 1898, helping to spark the Spanish-American War.

name: USS Monitor
fact: The Civil War ironclad USS Monitor sank in a storm off Cape Hatteras on the last day of 1862; its turret was raised in 2002.

name: USS Nautilus
fact: USS Nautilus, launched in 1954, was the world's first nuclear-powered submarine and in 1958 made the first submerged crossing of the North Pole.

name: USS Samuel B. Roberts
fact: The destroyer escort USS Samuel B. Roberts, sunk off Samar in 1944, was surveyed in 2022 at 6,895 metres, the deepest shipwreck ever identified.

name: USS Saratoga
fact: The aircraft carrier USS Saratoga was sunk in the 1946 atomic bomb tests at Bikini Atoll and now lies upright in the lagoon as a dive site.

name: USS Scorpion
fact: The nuclear submarine USS Scorpion was lost with 99 crew in May 1968 and lies about 3,000 metres down south-west of the Azores.

name: USS Skate
fact: USS Skate was the first submarine to surface at the North Pole, which she did in March 1959.

name: USS Thresher
fact: The nuclear submarine USS Thresher was lost with 129 people during deep-diving tests in 1963, and its remains lie about 2,600 metres down off New England.

name: USS Triton
fact: USS Triton was an American nuclear submarine that made the first submerged circumnavigation of the globe in 1960.

name: USS Yorktown
fact: The aircraft carrier USS Yorktown, sunk at the Battle of Midway in 1942, was found by Robert Ballard in 1998 about 5,000 metres down.

name: Ustica
fact: Ustica is a volcanic island north of Sicily with Italy's first marine reserve, created in 1986.

name: Utah Beach
fact: Utah Beach was the westernmost of the D-Day landing beaches, where United States troops came ashore on 6 June 1944.

name: Utila
fact: Utila is one of Honduras's Bay Islands and is a popular place to learn to dive, with occasional whale shark sightings.

name: Valdivia
fact: The German steamship Valdivia carried the 1898 to 1899 Deep Sea Expedition, which collected animals from the deep ocean.

name: Valencia
fact: Valencia is one of the busiest container ports on the Mediterranean.

name: Valerie Taylor
fact: Valerie Taylor is an Australian diver, filmmaker and shark conservationist whose shark footage featured in the film Jaws.

name: Valettietta gracilis
fact: Valettietta gracilis is a slender amphipod that lives in trenches of the Pacific, far below the reach of sunlight.

name: Valletta
fact: Valletta, the capital of Malta, was founded in 1566 by the Knights of St John after the Great Siege of 1565.

name: Valparaiso
fact: Valparaiso in Chile was a key stop for ships rounding Cape Horn before the Panama Canal opened in 1914, and its historic quarter is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

name: Vampire squid
fact: The vampire squid lives in oxygen-poor water around 600 to 900 metres down and, instead of ink, squirts a cloud of glowing mucus at threats.

name: Vancouver
fact: The Port of Vancouver in British Columbia is the largest and busiest port in Canada.

name: Vancouver Aquarium
fact: Vancouver Aquarium in Stanley Park opened in 1956 and was Canada's first public aquarium.

name: Vancouver Island
fact: Vancouver Island off Canada's west coast is the largest island on the Pacific coast of the Americas.

name: Vanuatu
fact: Vanuatu is a chain of about 80 volcanic islands in the South Pacific, including Tanna with its easily visited active volcano, Mount Yasur.

name: Vaquita
fact: The vaquita, a tiny porpoise of the upper Gulf of California near the Colorado River delta, is the most endangered marine mammal, with perhaps only about 10 left.

name: Varied catshark
fact: The varied catshark hides among rocks and reefs off southern Australia and is patterned with dark spots and bands.

name: Varuna
fact: Varuna is a Hindu god of water and the ocean, who in later tradition became the guardian of the western quarter and of the seas.

name: Vasa
fact: The Swedish warship Vasa sank on its maiden voyage in 1628, minutes after leaving Stockholm, and was raised almost intact in 1961.

name: Vasco da Gama
fact: Vasco da Gama sailed around the Cape of Good Hope to reach India in 1498, opening the sea route from Europe to Asia.

name: Vase tunicate
fact: The vase tunicate is a see-through, vase-shaped sea squirt widely used in research and invasive in several regions.

name: Vega expedition
fact: The Vega expedition of 1878 to 1880, led by Adolf Nordenskiold, was the first to sail the Northeast Passage along Siberia's coast.

name: Veined rapa whelk
fact: The veined rapa whelk, a big predatory snail from Japan, invaded the Black Sea and later Chesapeake Bay, where it eats oysters and clams.

name: Veined squid
fact: The veined squid is one of the main squid caught around Britain and Ireland, and can hover in place and change colour in an instant.

name: Velvet belly lanternshark
fact: The velvet belly lanternshark glows along its underside and even on its dorsal spines, which may warn predators off.

name: Velvet crab
fact: The velvet crab of European shores has red eyes, a furry shell and a famously aggressive temper, and is caught for Spanish markets.

name: Vendee Globe
fact: The Vendee Globe is a solo, non-stop, unassisted round-the-world yacht race held every four years since 1989.

name: Venezuela
fact: Venezuela has a long coast on the Caribbean Sea and the Atlantic, where the Orinoco river forms a vast delta.

name: Venice
fact: Venice is built on more than a hundred small islands in a lagoon and was a great maritime republic for centuries.

name: Venice Beach
fact: Venice Beach in Los Angeles began in 1905 as a seaside resort founded by Abbot Kinney and modelled on Venice, Italy.

name: Vent amphipod
fact: Ventiella amphipods swarm in dense clouds around East Pacific vents, feeding on bacterial mats and dead tube worms.

name: Vent anemone
fact: Pale sea anemones fringe the cooler edges of hydrothermal vent fields, catching scraps carried past by the warm, murky water.

name: Vent barnacle
fact: Vent barnacles grow in dense clusters on vent chimneys, with long bristly feeding legs coated in filamentous bacteria that are thought to be part of their diet.

name: Vent clam
fact: The giant white vent clam grows to more than 25 centimetres, has bright red flesh full of haemoglobin, and gets its food from bacteria in its gills.

name: Vent copepod
fact: Dirivultid copepods are found only at hydrothermal vents, where they are often the most numerous animals crawling over tube worms and mussels.

name: Vent crab
fact: Bythograea vent crabs are the top scavengers and predators of East Pacific vent fields, picking over tube worms, mussels and dead fish.

name: Vent limpet
fact: Tiny Lepetodrilus limpets carpet tube worms and mussels at vents by the thousand, grazing the bacterial film that coats everything.

name: Vent mussel
fact: Vent mussels pack their gills with bacteria that feed them from the vent chemicals, forming beds thousands strong around warm vents and seeps.

name: Vent octopus
fact: The vent octopus is a small, pale, nearly blind octopus found only around hydrothermal vents on the East Pacific Rise.

name: Vent scale worm
fact: Branchipolynoe scale worms live inside the shells of living vent mussels, with special blood that stores oxygen for when the vent water turns foul.

name: Vent sea spider
fact: Sericosura sea spiders cluster by the hundred on vent chimneys, sucking up bacterial mats with a tube-like proboscis.

name: Vent shrimp
fact: Rimicaris vent shrimp swarm in thousands on Mid-Atlantic vent chimneys and have no normal eyes, only a light-sensing patch on the back that detects the vents' faint glow.

name: Vent spaghetti worm
fact: Vent spaghetti worms are acorn worms that drape themselves over rocks in tangled strands at the Galápagos Rift vents, mopping bacteria off the surface.

name: Vent squat lobster
fact: Munidopsis squat lobsters, pale and nearly blind, crawl in crowds around the cooler fringes of vent fields, scavenging whatever drifts their way.

name: Vent tonguefish
fact: Symphurus thermophilus is a flatfish that lives in crowds at volcanic vents of the western Pacific, resting on crusts of solid sulphur beside pools of the molten stuff.

name: Venus' flower basket
fact: The Venus' flower basket is a lattice-like glass sponge in which a pair of shrimp live trapped for life, which is why dried ones are given as wedding gifts in Japan.

name: Venus flower basket shrimp
fact: A pair of these shrimp lives inside a Venus flower basket sponge, growing too big to leave and spending their lives there together.

name: Venus flytrap anemone
fact: The deep-sea Venus flytrap anemone folds its tentacled disc shut around prey, like the plant it is named after.

name: Venus girdle
fact: The Venus girdle is a ribbon-shaped, transparent comb jelly up to about 1.5 metres long that ripples through the water like a strip of glass.

name: Vermilion snapper
fact: The vermilion snapper, or beeliner, is a slim red snapper relative of the southeastern US that often ends up sold as red snapper.

name: Vestas Sailrocket 2
fact: Vestas Sailrocket 2 set the world sailing speed record in 2012, reaching about 65 knots, or roughly 121 kilometres per hour, off Walvis Bay in Namibia.

name: Victor Vescovo
fact: Victor Vescovo became the first person to reach the deepest point of all five oceans, completing the Five Deeps Expedition in 2019.

name: Victoria
fact: Victoria, on the island of Mahe, is the capital of the Seychelles and one of the smallest capitals in the world.

name: Vieques
fact: Vieques, off Puerto Rico, is home to Mosquito Bay, whose water glows with bioluminescent plankton.

name: Vietnam
fact: Vietnam has an S-shaped coastline of more than 3,000 kilometres on the South China Sea.

name: Vigo
fact: Vigo, in Galicia, is one of the biggest fishing ports in the world, landing fish from fleets that work the Atlantic as far away as the Falklands.

name: Violet sea snail
fact: The violet sea snail cannot swim: it hangs upside down from a raft of mucus bubbles and drifts until it bumps into a by-the-wind sailor to eat.

name: Violet tunicate
fact: The violet tunicate forms bright, crust-like colonies and has spread as an invader to coasts around the world.

name: Viper dogfish
fact: The viper dogfish has needle-like fangs on jaws it can thrust forward, and it glows along its belly in the deep waters off Japan.

name: Viper moray
fact: The viper moray has long, curved, needle-like teeth that stick out even when its mouth is closed.

name: Viperfish
fact: The viperfish's fangs are so long they do not fit inside its mouth, and it has been recorded deeper than 4,000 metres.

name: Viperine sea snake
fact: The viperine sea snake is a true sea snake of Asian coastal waters with a flattened, paddle-like tail for swimming.

name: Virgin Gorda
fact: Virgin Gorda is home to the Baths, a beach of giant granite boulders that form sea-filled grottoes.

name: Vis
fact: Vis was closed to foreign visitors as a Yugoslav military base until 1989.

name: Visakhapatnam
fact: Visakhapatnam on India's east coast has a natural deep-water harbour and is one of the country's major ports.

name: Visayan Sea
fact: The Visayan Sea lies in the central Philippines and is an important fishing ground.

name: Vitus Bering
fact: Vitus Bering was a Danish-born Russian navigator who sailed through the strait now named after him in 1728.

name: Vityaz
fact: The Soviet research ship Vityaz took deep soundings of the Mariana Trench in 1957 and found a depth of around 11,000 metres.

name: Vityaz Trench
fact: The Vityaz Trench north of Fiji is named after the Soviet research ship Vityaz, which surveyed the Pacific's deepest trenches in the 1950s.

name: Viviparous eelpout
fact: The viviparous eelpout of the North and Baltic seas gives birth to fully formed live young, rare among bony fish.

name: Voyage of the Beagle
fact: The Voyage of the Beagle from 1831 to 1836 carried the young Charles Darwin around the world and shaped his later ideas on evolution.

name: Voyage to the Bottom of the Sea
fact: Voyage to the Bottom of the Sea was an Irwin Allen film in 1961 that became a television series from 1964, set aboard the research submarine Seaview.

name: Vulcano
fact: Vulcano is an Aeolian island whose name gave us the word volcano.

name: Vundu
fact: The vundu is a large catfish of central and southern African rivers such as the Zambezi, and it can grow well over a metre long.

name: Wadden Sea
fact: The Wadden Sea is a shallow, tidal stretch of the North Sea with the world's largest unbroken system of intertidal sand and mud flats.

name: Wahoo
fact: The wahoo is a long, razor-toothed member of the mackerel family and one of the fastest fish in the sea; Hawaiians call it ono, meaning delicious.

name: Waikiki
fact: Waikiki Beach in Honolulu was a playground of Hawaiian royalty, and a bronze statue of the surfer Duke Kahanamoku stands beside it.

name: Waimea Bay
fact: Waimea Bay on Oahu's North Shore hosts the Eddie Aikau big-wave invitational, held only when winter swells are large enough.

name: Wakame
fact: Wakame is the brown seaweed in miso soup and seaweed salad; outside Asia it is an invasive species that spread on the hulls of ships.

name: Wake Island
fact: Wake Island is a remote coral atoll in the north Pacific and the site of a fierce battle in 1941.

name: Wakeboarding
fact: Wakeboarding is riding a board across the water while towed behind a boat, using its wake to jump.

name: Walking catfish
fact: The walking catfish can breathe air and wriggle across land between ponds, which helped it spread as an invasive species in Florida.

name: Walking shark
fact: Walking sharks wriggle across reef flats and tide pools on their paired fins, and can even cross short stretches of exposed reef.

name: Wallago
fact: The wallago, or freshwater shark of South Asia, is a long, big-mouthed predatory catfish that can exceed 1.5 metres.

name: Walleye
fact: Walleye is the most popular eating fish of the Great Lakes region and the state fish of Minnesota.

name: Walleye pollock
fact: Walleye pollock, sold as Alaska pollock, is among the world's largest fisheries by volume and is the usual fish in fish fingers and imitation crab.

name: Walrus
fact: Walruses use their tusks to haul themselves onto ice, and a big male can weigh over 1,500 kilograms.

name: Walter Munk
fact: Walter Munk, called the Einstein of the oceans, predicted surf conditions for the D-Day landings and explained how ocean waves travel across whole oceans.

name: Walvis Bay
fact: Walvis Bay on the coast of Namibia is a natural deep-water harbour whose name means whale bay in Afrikaans.

name: Walvis Ridge
fact: The Walvis Ridge is a long volcanic ridge running from the Namibian coast towards Tristan da Cunha, formed by a hotspot as the South Atlantic opened.

name: Wandering albatross
fact: The wandering albatross has the longest wingspan of any living bird, up to about 3.5 metres, and can circle the Southern Ocean on a single foraging trip.

name: Warsaw grouper
fact: The Warsaw grouper is a huge grouper of deep rocky ledges in the western Atlantic, reaching over 2 metres, with an unusually tall second dorsal spine.

name: Warty comb jelly
fact: The warty comb jelly is a see-through, lobed predator that, carried in ships' ballast water, invaded the Black Sea in the 1980s.

name: Warty frogfish
fact: The warty frogfish dangles a lure on a modified fin spine to tempt prey within reach of its huge mouth.

name: Waspfish
fact: Waspfish carry venomous dorsal spines and rest camouflaged against the seabed.

name: Water polo
fact: Water polo is a team sport played in a pool in which two teams try to score by throwing a ball into the opposing goal, and it has been an Olympic sport since 1900.

name: Water skiing
fact: Water skiing is being towed behind a boat on skis, an idea first tried in 1922 by Ralph Samuelson in Minnesota.

name: Waterspout
fact: A waterspout is a spinning column of air and water vapour that forms over the sea, like a tornado over water.

name: Waterworld
fact: Waterworld is Kevin Reynolds's 1995 film, set in a future where the polar ice has melted and the Earth is covered by ocean.

name: Western and Central Pacific Fisheries Commission
fact: The Western and Central Pacific Fisheries Commission, established by a 2000 convention, manages tuna fisheries across a vast area of the Pacific.

name: Weakfish
fact: The weakfish is a drum of the US Atlantic coast that drums loudly during spawning; its name refers to its tender mouth, which tears on hooks.

name: Weasel shark
fact: Weasel sharks are a family of slender sharks found along warm Indo-Pacific and West African coasts.

name: Weather loach
fact: The weather loach burrows into mud to survive drought and gets its name from becoming restless when the air pressure drops before a storm.

name: Webfoot octopus
fact: The webfoot octopus is a small octopus of East Asian waters that is caught and eaten in Japan, Korea and China.

name: Weddell Gyre
fact: The Weddell Gyre is a huge clockwise circulation in the Southern Ocean off Antarctica, where cold dense bottom water forms.

name: Weddell Sea
fact: The Weddell Sea off Antarctica is named after the British sealer James Weddell, who sailed into it in 1823, and its pack ice crushed Shackleton's ship Endurance in 1915.

name: Weddell seal
fact: Weddell seals live further south than any other mammal, under the fast ice of Antarctica, and can dive for over an hour.

name: Wedge sea hare
fact: The wedge sea hare is a large Indo-Pacific sea slug that gave chemists dolastatins, compounds studied as anti-cancer drugs.

name: Wedge-tailed shearwater
fact: Wedge-tailed shearwaters nest in burrows on Pacific islands and make eerie moaning calls at night.

name: Wedgefish
fact: Wedgefish are shark-like rays with a rounded, wedge-shaped snout, and many species are critically endangered because their fins are highly prized.

name: Weedy sea dragon
fact: The male weedy sea dragon carries the pink eggs stuck to the underside of his tail, and the species is the marine emblem of the Australian state of Victoria.

name: Weever fish
fact: The weever fish buries itself in sand with only its venomous black dorsal fin showing, and is the most common cause of fish stings on British beaches.

name: Welland Canal
fact: The Welland Canal in Ontario, first opened in 1829, lets ships bypass Niagara Falls between Lake Ontario and Lake Erie.

name: Wellington
fact: Wellington, the capital of New Zealand, sits on a harbour that opens onto the windy Cook Strait.

name: Wels catfish
fact: The wels catfish of European rivers can grow to over 2.5 metres and has been filmed lunging onto the bank to snatch pigeons.

name: Wentletrap
fact: Wentletraps are sea snails with ladder-like spiral shells, and the name comes from the Dutch word for a spiral staircase.

name: West African manatee
fact: The West African manatee lives in coastal lagoons and rivers from Senegal to Angola and is the least-studied of the sirenians.

name: West African red mangrove
fact: Rhizophora racemosa is the dominant red mangrove along the coast of West Africa.

name: West Australian Current
fact: The West Australian Current is the cold northward flow on the eastern side of the Indian Ocean gyre, offshore of the warm Leeuwin Current.

name: West Greenland Current
fact: The West Greenland Current carries water north along Greenland's west coast towards Baffin Bay.

name: West Indian manatee
fact: West Indian manatees crowd into Florida's warm springs in winter because they cannot survive long in water below about 20 degrees Celsius.

name: Western blue groper
fact: The western blue groper is a very large wrasse of the reefs of southern Australia.

name: Western gray whale
fact: The western gray whale, a population of the north-west Pacific, is critically endangered, with only a few hundred animals left.

name: Western rock lobster
fact: The western rock lobster is a spiny lobster of Western Australia that supports one of the country's most valuable fisheries.

name: Western wobbegong
fact: The western wobbegong is a carpet shark of southern Western Australia whose fringed, mottled body camouflages it on the seabed.

name: Westslope cutthroat trout
fact: The westslope cutthroat trout lives on both sides of the northern Rocky Mountains and is the state fish of Montana.

name: Whale
fact: Baleen whales have no teeth; they gulp or skim water and strain out krill and small fish through fringed plates of keratin in their jaws.

name: Whale and Dolphin Conservation
fact: Whale and Dolphin Conservation is a charity that campaigns to protect whales and dolphins, and it is against keeping them in captivity.

name: Whale barnacle
fact: Whale barnacles grow embedded in the skin of humpback and grey whales, riding along for a free supply of plankton-rich water.

name: Whale louse
fact: Whale lice are not lice but crustaceans that cling to the skin folds and rough patches of whales, especially right whales.

name: Whale shark
fact: The whale shark is the largest fish alive, growing to over 12 metres while feeding on plankton and small fish.

name: Whaler shark
fact: Whaler shark is the Australian name for sharks of the genus Carcharhinus, which includes bull, blacktip and bronze whalers.

name: Essex
fact: The whaleship Essex was rammed and sunk by a sperm whale in the Pacific in 1820, inspiring Herman Melville's Moby-Dick.

name: International Convention for the Regulation of Whaling
fact: The International Convention for the Regulation of Whaling, signed in Washington in 1946, created the International Whaling Commission.

name: Whelk
fact: Common whelks are scavenging and predatory sea snails of the North Atlantic, and their spongy egg masses wash up as 'sea wash balls'.

name: Whip coral goby
fact: The whip coral goby is a tiny fish that spends its whole life clinging to a single strand of whip coral.

name: Whip-lash squid
fact: Whip-lash squid hover over the deep seabed and trail two long, sticky tentacles covered in tiny suckers to catch small prey.

name: Whirlpool
fact: A whirlpool is a rotating body of water, typically formed where opposing currents meet.

name: Whiskery shark
fact: The whiskery shark is a slender, bottom-feeding shark of southern Australia named for the barbels beside its nostrils.

name: White abalone
fact: The white abalone of California was the first marine invertebrate listed as endangered in the USA after divers stripped it from the reefs.

name: White bass
fact: White bass are silver schooling fish of North American lakes and rivers that boil at the surface when chasing shad.

name: White Beach, Boracay
fact: White Beach on Boracay in the Philippines stretches for roughly four kilometres along the island's west coast.

name: White-beaked dolphin
fact: The white-beaked dolphin is a robust cold-water dolphin that ranges north into Arctic waters off Greenland, Svalbard and Norway.

name: White-blotched river stingray
fact: The white-blotched river stingray lives only in Brazil's Xingu River and has a dark disc covered in pale blotches.

name: White-bonnet anemonefish
fact: The white-bonnet anemonefish, with a white cap on its head, is a natural hybrid between the orange skunk clownfish and the orange-fin anemonefish.

name: White catfish
fact: The white catfish lives in the brackish tidal rivers of the US east coast and has been introduced to California.

name: White-clawed crayfish
fact: The white-clawed crayfish, Britain's only native crayfish, is being wiped out by a fungal plague carried by invasive American signal crayfish.

name: White Cloud Mountain minnow
fact: The White Cloud Mountain minnow is a 4-centimetre fish discovered in 1932 on a mountain near Guangzhou, now almost extinct in the wild while thriving in aquariums.

name: White hake
fact: White hake is a long-bodied relative of the cod found over soft seabeds in the north-west Atlantic.

name: White mangrove
fact: White mangroves have two small glands at the base of each leaf stalk that secrete excess salt.

name: White marlin
fact: The white marlin is the smallest Atlantic marlin, a fast, acrobatic billfish prized by anglers off the US east coast.

name: White Sea-Baltic Canal
fact: The White Sea-Baltic Canal in Russia, opened in 1933, was dug largely by forced labour in the Soviet Gulag system.

name: White seabass
fact: The white seabass of the Californian coast is a large drum, not a bass, and is a prize for kayak anglers in the kelp beds.

name: White shark
fact: The white shark, better known as the great white, can sense the faint electrical fields given off by the muscles of hidden prey.

name: White-spotted bamboo shark
fact: The white-spotted bamboo shark is a small, slender Indo-Pacific reef shark that lays egg cases and is common in public aquariums.

name: White-spotted char
fact: The white-spotted char is a pale-spotted char of Japan, Korea and Russia, known as iwana in Japan.

name: White-spotted jellyfish
fact: The white-spotted jellyfish, native to the western Pacific, has spread to the Gulf of Mexico and elsewhere, where its blooms can clog fishing nets.

name: White-spotted octopus
fact: The white-spotted octopus hunts at night, flushing bright red with white spots and reaching its long arms deep into coral crevices.

name: White-spotted puffer
fact: The white-spotted puffer is a common Indo-Pacific puffer with white spots on a grey body and white stripes on the belly.

name: White sturgeon
fact: The white sturgeon of the Fraser and Columbia rivers is North America's largest freshwater fish, reaching about 6 metres.

name: White-tailed eagle
fact: The white-tailed eagle, one of Europe's largest birds of prey, snatches fish from the sea surface and was reintroduced to Scotland in the 1970s.

name: White whale
fact: White whale is another name for the beluga, whose calves are born dark grey and turn white as they reach adulthood.

name: Whitehaven Beach
fact: Whitehaven Beach on Whitsunday Island in Queensland runs for about seven kilometres and is famed for its very pure, bright silica sand.

name: Whiteleg shrimp
fact: The whiteleg shrimp is the most farmed shrimp in the world, raised in ponds from Ecuador to Vietnam and sold by the million as supermarket prawns.

name: Whitemouth moray
fact: The whitemouth moray is brown with white spots and has a pale inside to its mouth, which gives it its name.

name: White's seahorse
fact: White's seahorse, or Sydney seahorse, lives in New South Wales estuaries and clings to the shark nets of Sydney's swimming enclosures.

name: Whitetail dascyllus
fact: The whitetail dascyllus shelters in small groups among branching corals on Indo-Pacific reefs.

name: Whitetip reef shark
fact: Whitetip reef sharks can pump water over their gills while resting, so they spend the day lying motionless in reef caves.

name: Whiting
fact: Whiting is a small, soft-fleshed relative of cod that has long been a cheap staple of British chip shops.

name: Whydah Gally
fact: The pirate ship Whydah Gally sank in a storm off Cape Cod in 1717; its wreck, found in 1984, was the first authenticated pirate shipwreck.

name: Wide-band anemonefish
fact: The wide-band anemonefish lives only around Lord Howe Island and eastern Australia, with wide white bars that merge on some fish.

name: Widgeon grass
fact: Widgeon grass grows in salty and brackish water around the world and is eaten by waterfowl.

name: Wigeon
fact: The wigeon is a dabbling duck that grazes on eelgrass in estuaries in winter, often alongside brant geese.

name: Wilhelm Gustloff
fact: The German liner Wilhelm Gustloff was torpedoed in the Baltic in January 1945; with roughly 9,000 dead, it is the deadliest sinking in history.

name: Wilkes expedition
fact: The Wilkes expedition of 1838 to 1842 was a United States naval survey that charted a long stretch of the Antarctic coast.

name: William Beebe
fact: William Beebe descended more than 900 metres off Bermuda in the bathysphere in 1934 and was the first scientist to watch deep-sea animals alive in their own world.

name: William Dampier
fact: William Dampier was an English buccaneer and explorer who circumnavigated the globe three times and described parts of Australia.

name: William Fly
fact: William Fly was an English pirate who was hanged in Boston in 1726 after capturing several ships off the American coast.

name: William Halsey
fact: William Halsey commanded the United States Third Fleet in the Pacific in the Second World War and was nicknamed Bull.

name: William Trubridge
fact: William Trubridge is a New Zealand freediver who has set world records diving without fins or any pull on a rope.

name: Wilson's storm petrel
fact: Wilson's storm petrel patters across the water on dangling feet, picking krill and oil from the surface, and may be the most numerous wild bird on Earth.

name: Windfoiling
fact: Windfoiling is windsurfing on a board with a hydrofoil, which lifts the board clear of the water at speed.

name: Windlass
fact: A windlass is a winch used on a ship to raise the anchor.

name: Windowpane flounder
fact: The windowpane flounder is so thin that light passes through its body when it is held up to the sun.

name: Windowpane oyster
fact: The windowpane oyster has a thin, translucent shell that was once used in place of glass in windows in parts of Asia.

name: Windsurfing
fact: Windsurfing combines surfing with sailing, using a board with a hand-held sail.

name: Windward Passage
fact: The Windward Passage between Cuba and Haiti connects the Atlantic to the Caribbean and is the main shipping route from the US east coast to the Panama Canal.

name: Wineglass Bay
fact: Wineglass Bay in Freycinet National Park, Tasmania, is a near-perfect crescent of white sand reached only on foot or by boat.

name: Winged kelp
fact: Winged kelp, or alaria, has a long blade with a midrib and is farmed in the North Atlantic and eaten as 'Atlantic wakame'.

name: Wingfoiling
fact: Wingfoiling is a sport in which the rider holds a hand-held inflatable wing and rides a hydrofoil board.

name: Winghead shark
fact: The winghead shark has the widest head of any hammerhead, nearly half as wide as the shark is long.

name: Winter flounder
fact: Winter flounder move inshore in winter and carry antifreeze proteins in their blood to survive icy New England waters.

name: Winter skate
fact: The winter skate of the north-west Atlantic has an eye-like spot on each wing and lives on sandy and gravelly seabeds.

name: Wire coral
fact: Wire corals are black corals that grow as a single, unbranched, wire-like whip or spiral.

name: Wire weed
fact: Wire weed of southern Australia has woody stems topped with tufts of leaves and forms tall underwater meadows.

name: Witch
fact: The witch is a long, thin, right-eyed flounder of deep muddy seabeds, sold as Torbay sole in Britain and grey sole in North America.

name: Wiwaxia
fact: Wiwaxia was a Cambrian seafloor grazer from the Burgess Shale covered in overlapping scales and two rows of spines.

name: Wobbegong
fact: Wobbegongs are flattened, carpet-patterned sharks that lie in wait on reefs, with a fringe of skin flaps hiding their mouths.

name: Wolf eel
fact: Wolf eel pairs share a den for life, and both parents coil around their egg mass, guarding it for months.

name: Wolffish
fact: The Atlantic wolffish has a mouthful of fangs for crushing crabs and sea urchins, and makes its own antifreeze to live in near-freezing water.

name: Wonder of the Seas
fact: Wonder of the Seas entered service in 2022 as the largest cruise ship in the world at the time.

name: Woodes Rogers
fact: Woodes Rogers was an English privateer who rescued Alexander Selkirk in 1709 and later became governor of the Bahamas, cracking down on pirates.

name: Worm pipefish
fact: The worm pipefish is a short, thin pipefish that lives among seaweed on rocky shores around Europe.

name: Wrasse
fact: Many wrasses dive into the sand to sleep at night, and most species start life as females and later change into males.

name: Wreck diving
fact: Wreck diving is scuba diving to explore sunken ships and aircraft.

name: Wreckfish
fact: The Atlantic wreckfish, or stone bass, is a big deep-water sea bass whose young shelter under floating wreckage and driftwood.

name: Wrymouth
fact: The wrymouth is an eel-like fish of the north-west Atlantic that lives in burrows in muddy seabed.

name: Wunderpus
fact: The wunderpus of Indonesian sand flats has a pattern of white bands so individual that scientists can identify each animal by its markings.

name: WWF
fact: WWF is a global conservation charity founded in 1961 with a panda as its emblem, and it runs major marine programmes.

name: Xebec
fact: The xebec was a lateen-rigged Mediterranean ship used by Barbary corsairs and by European navies.

name: Xenia
fact: Xenia are soft corals whose feathery polyps pulse open and shut in a rhythmic, hand-clasping motion.

name: Xenobalanus
fact: Xenobalanus is a long-stalked barnacle that attaches to the fins and flukes of dolphins and whales.

name: Xenophyophore
fact: Xenophyophores are single cells up to about 10 centimetres across that build mud shells on the seabed, and were found at 10,641 metres in the Mariana Trench.

name: Xiphactinus
fact: Xiphactinus was a 5-metre fanged fish of the Cretaceous, and one famous fossil contains a whole 2-metre fish swallowed just before it died.

name: Yabby
fact: The yabby of Australian creeks and farm dams digs so deep into mud to survive drought that its scientific name means 'destroyer'.

name: Yacht
fact: The word yacht comes from the Dutch 'jacht', meaning hunt, from the fast, light ships once used to chase pirates.

name: Yam
fact: Yam is the Canaanite god of the sea and rivers, who in the Ugaritic Baal cycle is defeated by the storm god Baal.

name: Yamato
fact: The Yamato, the largest battleship ever built, was sunk by US aircraft in April 1945 and lies in two main pieces about 340 metres down off Kyushu.

name: Yangon
fact: Yangon, formerly Rangoon, is Myanmar's largest city and its main seaport on the Andaman Sea coast.

name: Yangtze finless porpoise
fact: The Yangtze finless porpoise is the only porpoise that lives entirely in fresh water and numbers only around a thousand.

name: Yap Trench
fact: The Yap Trench lies south-west of the Mariana Trench near the island of Yap and reaches about 8,500 metres deep.

name: Yawl
fact: A yawl is a two-masted sailboat whose small mizzen mast is stepped behind the rudder post.

name: Yellow-bellied sea snake
fact: The yellow-bellied sea snake is the most widespread snake on Earth, drifting across the Pacific and Indian Oceans and never coming ashore.

name: Yellow boxfish
fact: Young yellow boxfish are bright yellow cubes with black spots, and Mercedes-Benz modelled a concept car on their boxy shape in 2005.

name: Yellow clown goby
fact: The yellow clown goby is a 3.5-centimetre reef fish that lives among the branches of Acropora corals and produces a bitter skin mucus to deter predators.

name: Yellow-edged moray
fact: The yellow-edged moray is a large Indo-Pacific moray, up to about 1.2 metres long, with a yellow rim on its fins.

name: Yellow-eyed penguin
fact: The yellow-eyed penguin, or hoiho, is one of the world's rarest penguins and nests in coastal forest and scrub in southern New Zealand.

name: Yellow perch
fact: The yellow perch, with its dark vertical bars, is the fish most children in North America catch first from a lake.

name: Yellow Sea
fact: The Yellow Sea between China and Korea takes its name from the yellow silt carried into it by the Yellow River.

name: Yellow sea snake
fact: The yellow sea snake is a large, yellow-and-black banded sea snake of the Indian Ocean and western Pacific that gives birth to live young at sea.

name: Yellow-spotted river turtle
fact: The yellow-spotted river turtle is named for the bright yellow spots on the head of the young and of females.

name: Yellow stingray
fact: The yellow stingray is a small, speckled ray of the Caribbean that can change its colour to blend in with the sand.

name: Yellow Submarine
fact: The Yellow Submarine is the fictional vessel of the 1966 Beatles song and the 1968 animated film of the same name.

name: Yellow tang
fact: The yellow tang is a bright lemon-yellow surgeonfish from Hawaii, one of the most popular marine aquarium fish; Hawaii now breeds them in captivity.

name: Yellow tube sponge
fact: The yellow tube sponge forms bright yellow tubes on Caribbean reefs and filters large volumes of water through its body.

name: Yellowback stingaree
fact: The yellowback stingaree is a small stingray of the eastern Australian coast with a yellowish back.

name: Yelloweye rockfish
fact: The yelloweye rockfish of the North Pacific grows slowly and can live for more than 100 years, which makes it very easy to overfish.

name: Yellowfin grouper
fact: The yellowfin grouper is a big western Atlantic grouper that can grow to about a metre and can carry ciguatera toxin.

name: Yellowfin sole
fact: The yellowfin sole of the Bering Sea supports the largest flatfish fishery in the world by weight.

name: Yellowfin tuna
fact: Yellowfin tuna, sold as ahi, is a fast, warm-water tuna with long yellow fins that is the common tuna in poke and sushi outside Japan.

name: Yellowfish
fact: Yellowfish are large minnow relatives of southern African rivers that are prized by fly anglers.

name: Yellowhead jawfish
fact: The male yellowhead jawfish holds the eggs in his mouth for over a week, spitting them out briefly to turn them, and cannot eat until they hatch.

name: Yellowhead wrasse
fact: The yellowhead wrasse of the Caribbean changes from a yellow juvenile with a blue stripe to a grey-bodied, yellow-headed adult.

name: Yellowlip emperor
fact: The yellowlip emperor is a large Indo-Pacific emperor with bright yellow lips.

name: Yellowmargin triggerfish
fact: The yellowmargin triggerfish digs large nest pits in sand and guards them as fiercely as its cousin the titan triggerfish.

name: Yellowstone cutthroat trout
fact: Yellowstone cutthroat trout take their name from the red slash under the jaw and are native to the Yellowstone River basin.

name: Yellowtail
fact: Yellowtail, or hamachi, is a fast-swimming Japanese amberjack farmed in large numbers in Japan and served raw for its buttery flesh.

name: Yellowtail amberjack
fact: The yellowtail amberjack is a prized game fish off California, Baja and Australia and is served as hiramasa in sushi bars, distinct from the Japanese yellowtail sold as hamachi.

name: Yellowtail blue damsel
fact: The yellowtail blue damsel is a deep blue damselfish with a bright yellow tail, one of the most popular and peaceful damselfish for aquariums.

name: Yellowtail damselfish
fact: The juvenile yellowtail damselfish of the Caribbean is dark blue sprinkled with electric-blue spots, earning it the name jewelfish.

name: Yellowtail flounder
fact: The yellowtail flounder is a flatfish of the north-west Atlantic with rusty-red spots and a yellow edge to its tail.

name: Yellowtail kingfish
fact: Yellowtail kingfish are fast, powerful predators that are both farmed and prized by sport anglers in the southern hemisphere.

name: Yellowtail snapper
fact: The yellowtail snapper of the Caribbean has a yellow stripe running into a deeply forked yellow tail and often hovers in midwater above the reef.

name: Yemen
fact: Yemen has coasts on the Red Sea, the Gulf of Aden and the Arabian Sea, and it owns the island of Socotra.

name: Yemoja
fact: Yemoja is a Yoruba water goddess and mother of living things, worshipped in West Africa and in Brazil and Cuba as the goddess of the sea.

name: Yesso scallop
fact: The Yesso scallop is intensively farmed in Japan and China and is one of the most widely cultured scallops.

name: Yeti crab
fact: The yeti crab, discovered in 2005 at vents south of Easter Island, has hairy arms coated in bacteria that it is thought to feed on.

name: Yi Sun-sin
fact: Yi Sun-sin was a Korean admiral who defeated far larger Japanese fleets in the 1590s, partly with his armoured turtle ships.

name: Yokohama
fact: Yokohama was opened to foreign trade in 1859 and grew from a fishing village into one of Japan's largest ports.

name: Yucatán Channel
fact: The Yucatán Channel between Mexico and Cuba links the Caribbean Sea to the Gulf of Mexico and carries the current that becomes the Gulf Stream.

name: Zakynthos
fact: Zakynthos is a Greek island in the Ionian Sea whose beaches are nesting grounds for loggerhead turtles.

name: Zander
fact: The zander is Europe's largest perch relative and lives in rivers, lakes and the brackish Baltic Sea.

name: Zanzibar
fact: Zanzibar lies off the coast of Tanzania and was once a centre of the spice and slave trades.

name: Zanzibar Town
fact: Stone Town, the old quarter of Zanzibar Town, became a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2000 and was once a centre of the Indian Ocean spice and slave trades.

name: Zarzuela
fact: Zarzuela is a Catalan stew of fish and shellfish in a tomato and almond-thickened sauce.

name: Zealandia
fact: Zealandia is a continent-sized block of crust around New Zealand of which about 94 percent lies underwater, drowned after it split from Gondwana.

name: Zebra lionfish
fact: The zebra lionfish is a smaller lionfish with striped, feathery fins, and its dorsal spines carry a painful venom.

name: Zebra moray
fact: The zebra moray, banded in dark brown and white, has flat crushing teeth and feeds almost entirely on crabs and sea urchins.

name: Zebra mussel
fact: Zebra mussels arrived in the Great Lakes in ships' ballast water from the Black and Caspian seas in the 1980s and now clog pipes across North America.

name: Zebra pleco
fact: The zebra pleco, a striking black-and-white striped catfish, lives only in a stretch of Brazil's Xingu River and is threatened by the Belo Monte dam.

name: Zebra seahorse
fact: The zebra seahorse, striped black and white, is known only from the waters of northern Australia.

name: Zebra shark
fact: Zebra sharks are born with dark stripes that break up into leopard-like spots as they grow, so adults are often called leopard sharks in Australia.

name: Zebra urchin crab
fact: The zebra crab lives among the spines of sea urchins, where its bold black and white stripes hide it from predators.

name: Zebrafish
fact: The zebrafish, a striped minnow about 3 to 4 centimetres long, is one of science's favourite lab animals because its transparent embryos develop in full view.

name: Zheng He
fact: Zheng He commanded huge Chinese treasure fleets on seven voyages across the Indian Ocean between 1405 and 1433.

name: Zheng He's treasure voyages
fact: Between 1405 and 1433 Zheng He led seven huge Chinese treasure fleets across the Indian Ocean as far as East Africa.

name: Zombie worm
fact: Zombie worms have no mouth or stomach; they bore roots into whale bones on the seabed and let bacteria digest the fat, and the dwarf males live inside the females.

name: Berlin Zoo Aquarium
fact: The Aquarium at Berlin Zoo opened in 1913 and houses fish, reptiles and insects across several floors.

name: Zooplankton
fact: Zooplankton are the animal drifters of the sea, from copepods to jellyfish, and each night they rise towards the surface in the largest migration on Earth.
